\(Tf\). With a chosen \(\psi\), \(Tf[(x, \varphi, h)]\) is the class of the image tuple Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap, computable in any chart around \(f(x)\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap_mk. It covers \(f\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_tangentMap, maps \(T_xX\) into \(T_{f(x)}Y\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap_mapsTo_fiber, and in charts \(T\psi \circ Tf = T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ T\varphi\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentChartMap_tangentMap. \(T(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap_id, and the chain rule \(T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf\) holds: with charts \(\psi\) around \(f(x)\) and \(\chi\) around \(g(f(x))\) and the open set \(t = \operatorname{fdom}(\varphi, f, \psi) \cap f^{-1}(\operatorname{fdom}(\psi, g, \chi))\), the chain rule with locality gives \(T(\chi \circ g \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) = T(\chi \circ g \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})\) on \(T(\varphi(t))\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap_comp. \(Tf\) is continuous: near a class in \(TV\), the preimage of a generating set of \(TY\) contains the generating set of \(TX\) given by \(\varphi\) and the preimage under the continuous \(T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})\) Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.continuous_tangentMap; and \(Tf\) is sc-smooth \(TX \to TY\), its representation in the charts \(T\varphi\), \(T\psi\) being \(T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})\), sc-smooth by the tangent functor Chapter2/TangentMapMPolyfold.tangentMap_isScSmooth.

II.10 Sub-M-polyfolds (Definition 2.20, Proposition 2.21)

Definition 2.20. \(A \subseteq X\) is a sub-M-polyfold if every \(a \in A\) has an open \(V \ni a\) and a map \(r\) with \(r(V) \subseteq V\), sc-smooth on \(V\), idempotent on \(V\), with \(r(V) = A \cap V\) Chapter2/MPolyfoldMPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold; \(X\) is one Chapter2/MPolyfoldMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_univ. The data at a point are packaged Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold.data: \(r\) maps \(V\) into \(A\), fixes \(A \cap V\), and is continuous on \(V\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.apply_mem Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.apply_eq_self Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.continuousOn.

Proposition 2.21, the structure. Shrinking. For a chart \(\varphi\), put \(W := (V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi) \cap r^{-1}(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi)\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.shrink: open (continuity of \(r\)) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.isOpen_shrink, containing every \(a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.mem_shrink, with \(r(W) \subseteq W\) and \(r(W) = W \cap A\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.mapsTo_shrink Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.image_shrink. The retract. \(\rho := \varphi \circ r \circ \varphi^{-1}\) is sc-smooth from \(\varphi(W)\) to itself — Definition 2.14 for \(r\) in the charts \(\varphi\), \(\varphi\) — idempotent, and \(\rho(\varphi(W)) = \varphi(W \cap A)\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_isScSmooth Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_idem Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_image; so \(\varphi(W \cap A)\) is a retract by Proposition 2.10 (2) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.isScRetract_image. The chart. With the subspace topology on \(A\), \(\varphi\) restricted to \(W \cap A\) is a chart of \(A\) with model \((\varphi(W \cap A), C, E)\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subChart Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subChartInv. Compatibility. The overlap of two such charts is \(\varphi((W \cap W') \cap A)\), a subset of \(\varphi(V \cap V')\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subChart_overlap. An sc-smooth map between retracts is sc-smooth on every sub-retract \(O_1 \subseteq O\): for a retraction \(s\) onto \(O_1\), \(f \circ s = (f \circ r) \circ s\), sc-smooth by the chain rule Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldIsScSmoothRetractMap.mono_source — this is the text’s “\((\psi' \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ s'' = (\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ s''\)”. The transition maps of the sub-charts are restrictions of those of \(X\), hence sc-smooth Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subChart_compatible. They form an atlas Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subAtlas, and \(A\) is an M-polyfold Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold_isChart. The structure requires \(A\) to be paracompact (an instance argument); it is, as a subset of the metrizable \(X\) (§II.7), and for closed \(A\) also elementarily Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.paracompactSpace_of_isClosed.

(1) and (2). The inclusion \(A \to X\) is sc-smooth: in the sub-chart and \(\varphi\) it is the identity of \(\varphi(W \cap A)\) into \(O\); one pair of charts per point suffices Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold_inclusion_isScSmooth; it is a homeomorphism onto its image by the choice of topology. For any data \((V, r)\), the map \(i^{-1} \circ r\) (a total map with a junk value off \(V\)) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.retractInto Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.retractInto_val is sc-smooth on \(V\): near \(x \in V\) take a chart \(\varphi'\) around \(x\), a chart \(\varphi\) around \(r(x)\) and \(V_0 = V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi' \cap r^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi)\); on \(\varphi'(V_0)\) the representation in \(\varphi'\) and the sub-chart on \(\varphi\) is \(\varphi \circ r \circ \varphi'^{-1}\), sc-smooth by Definition 2.14 for \(r\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold_retraction_isScSmooth.

Proposition 2.21 (3), (4), in a chart. Let \(r\) be a retraction onto \(O\), \(s\) sc-smooth from \((O, C, E)\) to itself with \(s \circ s = s\), and \(t := s \circ r\), a retraction onto \(s(O)\) (Proposition 2.10 (2)) Chapter2/MetrizableScRetraction.compRetraction Chapter2/MetrizableScRetraction.compRetraction_retract. For \(a \in s(O)_1\) put \(P := Dr(a)\), \(Q := Dt(a) = D(s \circ r)(a)\) — the text’s “\(Ds(a)\)”. Both are idempotent (§II.2). From \(r \circ t = t\) and \(t \circ r = t\) on \(U\) (\(s\) takes values in \(O\), which \(r\) fixes; and \(r \circ r = r\)), the chain rule at the point \(a\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexscDeriv_comp_apply gives \(PQ = Q\) and \(QP = Q\). If \(a\) is smooth, \(P\) and \(Q\) are sc-operators (Part I, Proposition 1.16), and so is \(P - Q\); identities between base maps of sc-operators hold on every level Chapter2/MetrizableScOperator.lvl_comp_of_base Chapter2/MetrizableScOperator.lvl_comp_eq_zero_of_base Chapter2/MetrizableScOperator.lvl_eq_add_of_base. Then \(Q\) and \(P - Q\) are commuting idempotent sc-operators with \(Q(P - Q) = 0\), their ranges are sc-subspaces (Part I, §I.3: sc-splittings and sc-projections Chapter1/ExpositionLemmasScBanach.isScSplitting_of_idem), and on every level the level parts of \(QE\) and \((P - Q)E\) are disjoint with sum the level part of \(PE\). Since \(T_aO = PE\) and \(T_a s(O) = QE\) (§II.2), this is the sc-splitting \(T_aO = T_aA \oplus (Dr(a) - Dt(a))E\) Chapter2/Metrizableproposition_2_21_3. For (4), \(s\) is sc-smooth from \(O\) onto \(s(O)\) (shrinking the target), and \(Ts(a, h) = (a, Q h)\) for \(h \in T_aO\) because \(Q h = Q P h\); as \(Q\) maps \(PE\) onto \(QE = Q(PE)\), \(Ts(a)\) maps \(T_aO\) onto \(T_a s(O)\) Chapter2/Metrizableproposition_2_21_4. The transport to \(T_aX\) is not formalized.

II.12 The subspaces \(E_x\), the cones \(C_x\) and the sign arguments

Coordinates. For a presentation \(T\) of \(C\) and \(x \in E_0\), the coordinates vanishing at \(x\) form a continuous linear surjection \(E_0 \to \mathbb R^{I(x)}\), \(v \mapsto ((Tv)_i)_{i \in I(x)}\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexcoordProj Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexcoordMapL Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexcoordMapL_surjective. Its kernel is \(E_x\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexminimalSubspaceWith Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexmem_minimalSubspaceWith, closed Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexisClosed_minimalSubspaceWith, and by the first isomorphism theorem \(E_0/E_x \cong \mathbb R^{I(x)}\), so \(\dim(E_0/E_x) = d_C(x)\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexfinrank_quotient_minimalSubspaceWith. The cone \(C_x = \{v : (Tv)_i \ge 0 \text{ for } i \in I(x)\}\) Chapter2/TamepartialQuadrantAtWith is convex and closed and contains \(E_x\) Chapter2/Tameconvex_partialQuadrantAtWith Chapter2/BoundaryisClosed_partialQuadrantAtWith Chapter2/TameminimalSubspaceWith_subset_partialQuadrantAtWith. Approximation: if \(Tx = (a, w)\), the points \(T^{-1}(a, w')\) with \(w' \in W_1\) (resp. \(W_\infty\)) converge to \(x\) as \(w' \to w\) and have the same vanishing coordinates, so \(x\) is a limit of points on level \(1\) (resp. smooth points) of the same index, in \(C\) iff \(x\) is Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexexists_tendsto_lvl1_degIndexWith Chapter2/TameRetractsexists_tendsto_smooth_degIndexWith.

Density on level \(1\). For a continuous linear \(L : E_0 \to V\), \(V\) finite-dimensional, the level-\(1\) points of \(\ker L\) are dense in \(\ker L\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexScBanach.subset_closure_ker_inter_range_toBase. The image \(S\) of \(E_1\) is dense in \(E_0\); \(L\) maps \(S\) onto the finite-dimensional \(L(S)\), which has a linear, hence continuous, right inverse \(g\) with values in \(S\). For \(v \in \ker L\) take \(u_k \in S\) with \(u_k \to v\); then \(L(u_k) \to 0\), \(g(L(u_k)) \to 0\), and \(u_k - g(L(u_k)) \in S \cap \ker L\) converges to \(v\). This is the text’s “the closure of \((T^R_xO)_\infty\) is \(T^R_xO\)” in the form the proofs need; the level-\(1\) points of \(C_x\) are dense in \(C_x\) likewise Chapter2/BoundarypartialQuadrantAtWith_subset_closure.

The two-sided sign argument. Let \(f\) be sc¹ on \(U\) relatively open in \(C\), with values in \(C'\), \(x \in U_1\) and \(v \in E_1\) with \(\iota_1 v \in E_x\). Then \(x + tv \in U_1\) for \(|t|\) small: the coordinates in \(I(x)\) stay \(0\), the others stay positive, and \(U_1\) is relatively open Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexeventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet. For \(j\) with \((T'f(x))_j = 0\) the real function \(g(t) = (T'f(\iota_1(x + tv)))_j\) is \(\ge 0\) near \(0\) (values in \(C'\)), vanishes at \(0\), and has derivative \((T' Df(x)v)_j\) at \(0\) (Definition 1.14’s derivative along \(E_1\), composed with the path); a local minimum has zero derivative Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LocalExtr/BasicIsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero. So \(Df(x)v \in E'_{f(x)}\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexIsSc1With.deriv_mem_minimalSubspace_of_lvl1, and by density and continuity of \(Df(x)\) on \(E_0\), \(Df(x)\) maps \(E_x\) into \(E'_{f(x)}\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexIsSc1With.mapsTo_minimalSubspace.

The one-sided sign argument. For \(v \in E_1\) with \(\iota_1 v \in C_x\), \(x + tv \in U_1\) for small \(t \ge 0\) Chapter2/Boundaryeventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet_of_cone, the same \(g\) is \(\ge 0\) on \([0, \varepsilon)\) with \(g(0) = 0\), so its one-sided derivative is \(\ge 0\) Chapter2/Boundarynonneg_of_hasDerivWithinAt_Ici; hence \(Df(x)v \in C'_{f(x)}\) Chapter2/BoundaryIsSc1With.deriv_mem_partialQuadrant_of_lvl1, and \(Df(x)\) maps \(C_x\) into \(C'_{f(x)}\) Chapter2/BoundaryIsSc1With.mapsTo_partialQuadrant. These are the derivative-level content of Lemma 2.29 (1) and (2); the lemma itself, about sc-smooth paths, is not formalized.

The chain rule at a point. For sc¹ maps \(f\), \(g\) on relatively open sets with \(f(U) \subseteq U'\), \(Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = D(g \circ f)(x)\) at \(x \in U_1\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexscDeriv_comp_apply; if \(g \circ f = \mathrm{id}\) on \(U\) then \(g_1(f_1(x)) = x\) and \(Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = \mathrm{id}\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexlevelMap_comp_eq_self Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexscDeriv_comp_eq_self.

Germs between retracts. The core of Theorem 2.31. Along a germ \(F\), \(\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_{C'}(F(x))\) for \(x \in O_1\) Chapter2/BoundaryScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.quotDim_le. With \(P = Dr(x)\), \(P' = Dr'(y)\): \(D\) maps \(T_x = PE\) into \(T_y = P'E'\) and \(D'\) maps back, \(D'D = P\) is the identity on \(T_x\) and \(DD' = P'\) the identity on \(T_y\). The map \(\Phi : T_x \to T_y/(T_y \cap E'_y)\), \(v \mapsto [Dv]\), is onto (\([w] = \Phi(D'w)\)) with kernel \(T_x \cap E_x\) (\(Dv \in E'_y\) implies \(v = D'Dv \in E_x\)). Definition 2.33. \(C_e\) and \(E_e\) are the cone and subspace of §II.12 for the presentation \(T\). Proposition 2.35. \(Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x\) for every retraction at every \(x \in O_1\): the two-sided sign argument for \(r\), with \(r(x) = x\) Chapter2/TameRetractsScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace. Only condition (2) is used; the text uses condition (1) for \(Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x\). In coordinates: \(\lambda_j(Dr(x)v) = \lambda_j(v)\) for \(j \in I(x)\) Chapter2/TameRetractscoord_scDeriv_eq.

Proposition 2.36. (13) at smooth points. Proposition 2.36, the remaining statements Chapter2/PartialConeproposition_2_36_partialCone. Let \(r\) be tame for \(T\), \(x \in O_1\) smooth, \(P = Dr(x)\) and \(I(x) = \{i_1, \dots, i_d\}\). \(T_xO = PE\) is an sc-subspace, the range of the sc-projection \(P\) (Proposition 2.35 above) Chapter2/TameRetractsScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv. By definition \(T^R_xO = T_xO \cap \bigcap_k \ker \lambda_{i_k}\) Chapter2/TameRetractscoordL. \(T^R_xO\) is an sc-subspace. It is closed, as an intersection of closed subspaces Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexisClosed_minimalSubspaceWith. And \(\phi(w) = Pu = u\), since \(u \in T_xO\) and \(P\) is a projection Chapter2/RetractsScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self. As \(W_\infty\) is dense in \(W_m\), \(u\) lies in the closure of \(\phi(W_\infty) \subseteq T^R_xO \cap E_\infty\) (this is the exposition’s Lemma 3.A (1) in the case at hand). The quadrant. II.16 Faces are tame sub-M-polyfolds: Propositions 2.43, 2.44 and Theorem 2.45

The projection onto a face. \(P_i := T^{-1} \circ (a \mapsto a \text{ with } a_i = 0) \circ T\) is an sc-operator Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoordL Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoordModel Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoord which kills the \(i\)-th coordinate and keeps the others Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoord_coord Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoord_coord_self, fixes \(f_i\) Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoord_eq_self and maps \(C\) into \(C\) Chapter2/TameRetractskillCoord_mem.

Proposition 2.43, the retraction. Let \(F\) be a face of the retract, through \(x \in S\) with \(I(x) = \{i\}\), so \(F \subseteq f_i\) Chapter2/TameRetractsproposition_2_43. For each \(e \in F\), Lemma 4.C gives \(\varepsilon_e\) with \(B_e = B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap C \subseteq U\) and \(r(z) \in F\) for \(z \in B_e \cap f_i\) (the component of Lemma 4.C at \(e\) is the one of \(F\)). Put \(U^* := \bigcup_{e \in F} (B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap P_i^{-1}(B_{\varepsilon_e}(e))) \cap C\): relatively open in \(C\), contains \(F\) (as \(P_i e = e\)), and for \(z \in U^*\) the point \(P_i z\) lies in some \(B_e \cap f_i\), so \(r(P_i z) \in F\). Then \(s := r \circ P_i\) is sc-smooth on \(U^*\) (chain rule), maps \(U^*\) into \(F \subseteq U^*\), and fixes \(F\); so it is a retraction onto \(F\), and \(U^* \subseteq U\). The preimages under \(P_i\) are needed because \(P_i\) need not be norm-decreasing for the norm of \(E_0\); the exposition’s “\(|P_1 z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0\)” holds only for special norms. \(F\) is a sub-M-polyfold of \(O\): in the chart \(\mathrm{id}\) of \(O\), \(s\) restricted to \(O \cap U^*\) is an sc-smooth retraction onto \(F\) Chapter2/TameRetractsLocalModel.selfChart_symm_apply Chapter2/TameRetractsLocalModel.isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace.

The face as a model space. Insert and delete a coordinate: \(\mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^{k+1}\), \(b \mapsto (b_1, \dots, 0_i, \dots, b_k)\), and back Chapter2/TameFacesinsertCoordL Chapter2/TameFacesremoveCoordL, as sc-operators on \(\mathbb R^k \oplus W\) Chapter2/TameFacesinsertCoordModel Chapter2/TameFacesremoveCoordModel; composed with \(T\) they give \(\iota : \mathbb R^k \oplus W \to E\) onto \(f_i\) and \(\pi : E \to \mathbb R^k \oplus W\) Chapter2/TameFacesfaceIncl Chapter2/TameFacesfaceProj, with \(\pi\iota = 1\), \(\iota\pi = 1\) on \(f_i\) Chapter2/TameFacesfaceProj_faceIncl Chapter2/TameFacesfaceIncl_faceProj, \(\iota(C') \subseteq C\) and \(\pi(C) \subseteq C'\) for \(C' = [0, \infty)^k \oplus W\) Chapter2/TameFacesfaceIncl_mem Chapter2/TameFacesfaceProj_mem, and \(d_C(y) = d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1\) on \(f_i\) Chapter2/TameFacesdegIndexWith_eq_quadrantDeg_faceProj_add_one. The derivative of an sc-operator is itself Chapter2/TameFacesScOperator.scDeriv_eq, and the chain rule at a point holds between arbitrary sc-domains Chapter2/TameFacesscDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain.

Proposition 2.43, the tame model Chapter2/TameFacesproposition_2_43_tameModel. With \(U^*\) and \(s\) as above, put \(U' := \iota^{-1}(U^*)\) (relatively open in \(C'\)) and \(r' := \pi \circ r \circ \iota\) on \(U'\). Since \(r \circ \iota\) maps \(U'\) into \(F \subseteq f_i\), where \(\iota\pi = 1\), \(r'\) is an sc-smooth retraction with retract \(\pi(F)\), and \(\iota\) maps it back into \(F\). Tameness (1): for \(z \in U'\), \(d_{C'}(r'z) + 1 = d_C(r(\iota z)) = d_C(\iota z) = d_{C'}(z) + 1\). Tameness (2): at a smooth \(x \in \pi(F)\), \(\iota x\) is a smooth point of \(O\) and \(Dr'(x)v = \pi(Dr(\iota x)(\iota v))\) by the chain rule; for \(j\) with \(x_j = 0\) the coordinate \(j' = i.\mathrm{succAbove}(j)\) vanishes at \(\iota x\), and Proposition 2.35 for \(r\) gives \(\lambda_{j'}(Dr(\iota x)\iota v) = \lambda_{j'}(\iota v) = v_j\); so \(\lambda'_j \circ Dr'(x) = \lambda'_j\), and \((1 - Dr'(x))E'\) is an sc-complement of \(T_x\pi(F)\) inside \(E'_x\). The exposition instead intersects the complement \(A\) of \(T_xO\) with \(f_1\); that is not needed. And \(d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1 = d_C(y)\) on \(F\).

Proposition 2.43, faces are tame Chapter2/TameFacesLocalModel.proposition_2_43_isTame. For a face \(F\) of a tame retract \(O\) (paracompact, being closed), the chart \(\pi : F \to \pi(F)\) Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChart Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChartInv is compatible with the sub-charts of \(F\) built on the chart \(\mathrm{id}\) of \(O\), its transition maps being the sc-operators \(\iota\) and \(\pi\) Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart; a chart compatible with all sub-charts built on one chart of \(X\) is a chart of the induced structure, by locality of compatibility Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible. Its model is the tame retract \((\pi(F), C', E')\), so \(F\) is tame (a space all of whose points lie in tame charts is tame Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart), and the tame chart realizes the index: \(d_F(x) = d_{C'}(\pi x) = d_C(x) - 1 = d_O(x) - 1\) (equation (14) twice). The text calls this last statement obvious.

Proposition 2.44, first sentence Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.proposition_2_44. In a tame chart \(\varphi\) around \(x\): \(\varphi(x)\) lies in exactly \(d_X(x)\) faces of the M-polyfold \(O\) (Proposition 2.42 with Corollary 2.41), and each face of \(O\) is a tame sub-M-polyfold with \(d_F + 1 = d_O\), where \(d_O(\varphi x) = d_X(x)\).

The corner as a model space. The sc-projection \(P_\sigma = \iota_\sigma \circ \pi_\sigma\) Chapter2/CornerGermscornerKill sets the coordinates in \(\sigma\) to zero Chapter2/CornerGermscornerKill_coord_mem, fixes \(f_\sigma\) Chapter2/CornerGermscornerKill_eq_self and maps \(C\) into \(C\) Chapter2/CornerGermscornerKill_mem. For \(\sigma = \{i\}\) these are the \(\iota\), \(\pi\) and \(P_i\) of Proposition 2.43.

The retraction onto a corner Chapter2/CornerGermscorner_retraction. Let \(r\) be tame for \(T\), \(o \in O\) and \(\sigma \subseteq I(o)\). For each \(i \in \sigma\), Lemma 4.C at \(o\) Chapter2/TameRetractslocal_face_structure gives a face \(F_i\) of the retract with \(o \in F_i \subseteq f_i\), containing a point with \(d_C = 1\), and a ball around \(o\) in which \(r\) maps the points of \(C \cap f_i\) into \(F_i\). Distinct \(i\) give distinct faces: a point \(p \in F_i\) with \(d_C(p) = 1\) has \(I(p) = \{i\}\), so \(F_i = F_j\) forces \(i = j\) Chapter2/TameRetractszeroSet_eq_singleton. Take a ball \(B\) around \(o\) inside all these balls with \(B \cap C \subseteq U\), an open \(W_s\) with \(W_s \cap U = r^{-1}(B) \cap U\) (continuity of \(r\)), and put \(V := B \cap P_\sigma^{-1}(B \cap W_s)\), an open set containing \(o\) (since \(P_\sigma o = o = r(o)\)). On \(V \cap C\) the map \(s := r \circ P_\sigma\) is sc-smooth by the chain rule. For \(z \in V \cap C\), \(P_\sigma z \in C \cap f_\sigma \cap B\), so \(r(P_\sigma z) \in F_i \subseteq f_i\) for every \(i \in \sigma\): \(s(z) \in O \cap f_\sigma\). Moreover \(s(z) \in B\) (as \(P_\sigma z \in W_s\)), \(P_\sigma s(z) = s(z)\), and \(s(z) \in W_s\) (as \(r(s(z)) = s(z) \in B\)); so \(s\) maps \(V \cap C\) into itself. On \(f_\sigma \cap O\), \(P_\sigma\) and \(r\) are the identity, so \(s \circ s = s\): \(s\) is an sc-smooth retraction with retract \(O \cap V \cap f_\sigma\), and this set equals \(O \cap V \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i\) (a point of \(O \cap V \cap f_\sigma\) is fixed by \(r\), which maps it into each \(F_i\); conversely \(F_i \subseteq f_i\)). The exposition proceeds by induction on \(\#\sigma\), identifying the germ of \(F_1 \cap F_2\) with a face of \(F_1\); the formal proof removes all coordinates of \(\sigma\) at once.

The tame model of a corner Chapter2/CornerGermscorner_tameModel. Let \(s\) be an sc-smooth retraction on \(U_s \subseteq U\), equal to \(r \circ P_\sigma\) there, with retract \(F \subseteq O \cap f_\sigma\); write \(U_s = W_0 \cap C\) with \(W_0\) open, and put \(U' := \iota_\sigma^{-1}(W_0) \cap C'\) and \(r' := \pi_\sigma \circ r \circ \iota_\sigma\) on \(U'\). For \(z \in U'\), \(r(\iota_\sigma z) = s(\iota_\sigma z) \in F\) (as \(P_\sigma\iota_\sigma = \iota_\sigma\)), so \(r'\) maps \(U'\) into \(\pi_\sigma(F) \subseteq U'\); it is sc-smooth by the chain rule and idempotent because \(\iota_\sigma\pi_\sigma = 1\) on \(F\) and \(r = 1\) on \(F \subseteq O\); its retract is \(\pi_\sigma(F)\). Tameness (1): \(d_{C'}(r'z) + \#\sigma = d_C(r(\iota_\sigma z)) = d_C(\iota_\sigma z) = d_{C'}(z) + \#\sigma\) (the index formula on \(f_\sigma\) twice, and tameness (1) of \(r\)) Chapter1/DegeneracydegIndex_eq. Tameness (2): at a smooth \(x\) of the retract, \(\iota_\sigma x\) is a smooth point of \(O\), and \(Dr'(x)v = \pi_\sigma(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v)\) by the chain rule between sc-domains Chapter2/TameFacesscDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain Chapter2/TameFacesScOperator.scDeriv_eq; for \(j\) with \(x_j = 0\) the coordinate \(l_j\) vanishes at \(\iota_\sigma x\) Chapter2/CornerGermscoord_cornerIncl_idx, and Proposition 2.35 gives \(\lambda_{l_j}(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v) = \lambda_{l_j}(\iota_\sigma v) = v_j\) Chapter2/TameRetractscoord_scDeriv_eq; so \((1 - Dr'(x))E'\) lies in \(E'_x\) and is an sc-complement of \(T_x\pi_\sigma(F)\) Chapter2/TameRetractsScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv. And \(d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma = d_C(y)\) for \(y \in F\). This is the proof of the tame model of Proposition 2.43 with \(\sigma\) in place of \(\{i\}\).

Proposition 2.44, second sentence Chapter2/CornerGermsMPolyfold.proposition_2_44_corner. Let \(X\) be tame and \(x \in X\), and take a chart \(\varphi : V \to O\) of the structure around \(x\) with a tame retraction \(r\) onto \(O\), tame for a presentation \(T\) Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart. The face germs at \(x\) are the faces \(F_i\), \(i \in I(\varphi x)\), of the retract (Corollary 2.41: there are \(d_X(x)\) of them), and \(\sigma\) is a set of such indices. The retraction onto the corner gives the pairwise distinct faces \(F_i \ni \varphi(x)\), \(i \in \sigma\), an open \(B \ni \varphi(x)\) and \(s\) with retract \(O \cap B \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i\). Put \(A := \{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in B,\ \varphi(y) \in F_i\ \forall i \in \sigma\}\); its germ at \(x\) is the germ \(F^\sigma_x\). Since \(\varphi(A)\) is the retract of \(s\), \(A\) is a sub-M-polyfold by the local criterion of Theorem 2.45 Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local (paracompact as every subset Chapter2/MetrizableMPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype). The chart \(\pi_\sigma \circ \varphi\) of \(A\) onto the retract \(\pi_\sigma(\varphi(A))\) of \(r'\) Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChart is compatible with the sub-charts of \(A\) built on \(\varphi\), its transitions being \(\iota_\sigma\) and \(\pi_\sigma\) Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart, hence a chart of the induced structure Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible; its model is tame Chapter2/TameFacesScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame, so \(A\) is tame Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart. Both tame charts realize the index Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith, so for \(a \in A\): \(d_A(a) + \#\sigma = d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma\varphi(a)) + \#\sigma = d_C(\varphi(a)) = d_X(a)\); in particular \(d_A(x) = d_X(x) - \#\sigma\), and the codimension, the number of quadrant coordinates removed in the tame model, is \(\#\sigma\). The text states the proposition without proof.

Theorem 2.45. The interior of a face. \(F \cap \{d_X = 1\} = G\) for \(F = \overline G\) Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.theorem_2_45_interior: at \(y \in F\) with \(d_X(y) = 1\), in a tame chart with \(I(\varphi y) = \{i\}\), all points of \(\{d_X = 1\}\) near \(y\) lie in \(\varphi^{-1}(\hat F)\) for the single component \(\hat F\) of Lemma 4.C at \(\varphi(y)\), a connected subset of \(\{d_X = 1\}\) containing \(y\); it meets \(G\) (as \(y \in \overline G\)), hence lies in \(G\). A local criterion for sub-M-polyfolds Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local: if near each \(a \in A\), in a chart \(\varphi\), \(\varphi(A \cap V)\) agrees on an open \(B \ni \varphi(a)\) with the retract of an sc-smooth retraction \(s\) contained in \(O\), then \(A\) is a sub-M-polyfold, with the retraction \(\varphi^{-1} \circ s \circ \varphi\) on \(V' = \varphi^{-1}(B \cap W_0 \cap s^{-1}(B))\) — shrunk so that \(s\) maps it into itself, a step the exposition’s “transport by \(\varphi^{-1}\)” omits. \(G\) is a sub-M-polyfold Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isSubMPolyfold_interior: at \(y \in G\), the local face \(\overline{\hat F} \cap O\) agrees with \(\varphi(G)\) on the ball of Lemma 4.C (both consist of the points of \(S\) there), and Proposition 2.43 gives its retraction. The face-structured case. Near \(x \in F\), in a tame chart, \(\varphi(F)\) agrees on a ball with a face of the retract Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.exists_localFace_of_isFaceStructured: the map \(i \mapsto F_i\) (the closure of the component of \(\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_i)\)) from \(I(\varphi x)\) to the faces through \(x\) is onto (as in Proposition 2.42), and since there are exactly \(d_X(x) = \#I(\varphi x)\) faces through \(x\), it is injective; so the points of \(G\) near \(x\) lie in \(\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_j)\) for the one \(j\) with \(F = F_j\). Hence \(F\) is a sub-M-polyfold Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isSubMPolyfold_face, and with the charts \(\pi \circ \varphi\) onto the restrictions of the tame retractions \(r'\) it is tame with \(d_X(x) = d_F(x) + 1\) Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.theorem_2_45_isTame_face. The local and global face counts of the theorem are Proposition 2.42 and the definition of face-structured.

II.17 Products and fibred products: Lemma 4.D and Proposition 2.46

Products of partial quadrants. For presentations \(T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W\) and \(T' : E' \cong \mathbb R^{n'} \oplus W'\) of \(C\) and \(C'\), concatenating the coordinates (\(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^{n'} \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'}\) Chapter2/FibredProductfinAppendL) gives a presentation \(E \oplus E' \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'} \oplus (W \oplus W')\) Chapter2/FibredProductprodPresentation of \(C \times C'\) Chapter2/FibredProductprod_eq_prodPresentation, so \(C \times C'\) is a partial quadrant Chapter2/FibredProductIsPartialQuadrant.prod and \(U \times U'\) is relatively open in it Chapter2/FibredProductIsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod. The vanishing coordinates of \((x, x')\) are those of \(x\) followed by those of \(x'\), so \(d_{C \times C'}(x, x') = d_C(x) + d_{C'}(x')\) Chapter2/FibredProductdegIndexWith_prodPresentation Chapter2/FibredProductdegIndex_prod, and the minimal subspace is \(E_x \oplus E'_{x'}\) Chapter2/FibredProductminimalSubspaceWith_prodPresentation.

Products of retractions. \(f \times f'\) is sc-smooth when \(f\) and \(f'\) are Chapter2/FibredProductIsScSmooth.prodMap, with derivative \(Df(x) \times Df'(x')\) Chapter2/FibredProductscDeriv_prodMap; so \(r \times r'\) is an sc-smooth retraction Chapter2/FibredProductScRetraction.prod with retract \(O \times O'\) Chapter2/FibredProductScRetraction.prod_retract Chapter2/FibredProductIsScRetract.prod, and products of sc-smooth maps between retracts are sc-smooth Chapter2/FibredProductIsScSmoothRetractMap.prodMap. Products of sc-subspaces and of sc-splittings are again such Chapter2/FibredProductIsScSubspace.prod Chapter2/FibredProductIsScSplitting.prod; hence if \(r\), \(r'\) are tame for \(T\), \(T'\), then \(r \times r'\) is tame for the product presentation Chapter2/FibredProductScRetraction.IsTameWith.prod: (1) is the additivity of the index, and for (2) the complement of \(T_{(x, x')}(O \times O') = T_xO \oplus T_{x'}O'\) is \(A \oplus A'\) inside \(E_x \oplus E'_{x'}\).

Lemma 4.D (the product M-polyfold). \(X \times Y\) is paracompact, being metrizable by Theorem 2.16 Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.paracompactSpace_prod. The product charts Chapter2/FibredProductMChart.prod have the product retracts as models Chapter2/FibredProductLocalModel.prod, their overlaps are products Chapter2/FibredProductMChart.overlap_prod, and products of compatible charts are compatible Chapter2/FibredProductMChart.Compatible.prod; so they form an atlas of an M-polyfold structure on \(X \times Y\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.prod, in which products of charts of the factors are charts Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.IsChart.prod. In a product chart the index is additive Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.chartDegIndex_prod; choosing charts that realize \(d_X(x)\) and \(d_Y(y)\) gives \(d_{X \times Y}(x, y) \le d_X(x) + d_Y(y)\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le. If \(X\) and \(Y\) are tame, products of tame charts are tame charts, so \(X \times Y\) is tame, and since a tame chart realizes the index (§II.14), \(d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isTame_prod. The text’s “\(d_{X \times Y} = d_X + d_Y\)” is thus a statement about tame spaces. The projections are sc-smooth Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_fst Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_snd and so is the pairing \(z \mapsto (f(z), g(z))\) of sc-smooth maps Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.prodMk.

Proposition 2.46. A local sc-diffeomorphism \(f : X \to Z\) is read as: every point has an open neighbourhood \(U\) that \(f\) maps sc-diffeomorphically onto an open subset Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo; such an \(f\) is continuous and sc-smooth Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.continuous Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isScSmoothMap. The fibred product \(X {}_f\times_g Y = \{(x, y) : f(x) = g(y)\}\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.fibredProduct is closed in \(X \times Y\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isClosed_fibredProduct, hence paracompact, which the text does not mention. Sub-M-polyfold. Near \((x, y)\), with \(f|_U : U \to W\) an sc-diffeomorphism and \(V = g^{-1}(W)\), the map \(R(x', y') = ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')\) on \(U \times V\) is sc-smooth, idempotent, with image the fibred product near \((x, y)\); in a product chart it is an sc-smooth retraction Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.fibredSubDataL, and so the fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct (symmetrically when \(g\) is the local sc-diffeomorphism Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.fibredSubDataR Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct'). \(\pi_2\) is a local sc-diffeomorphism. On the fibred product near \((x, y)\), \(\pi_2\) is sc-smooth with inverse \(y' \mapsto ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')\), a pairing of sc-smooth maps with values in the fibred product, hence sc-smooth into the sub-M-polyfold by Proposition 2.21 (2) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_snd_fibredProduct; symmetrically for \(\pi_1\) when \(g\) is a local sc-diffeomorphism Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_fst_fibredProduct. The exposition factors this inverse through \(y' \mapsto (x, y')\), which is not sc-smooth unless \(x\) is a smooth point (a constant map is sc⁰ only when its value lies in \(X_\infty\)); the formula above has the same values and avoids it. The index. Proposition 2.24 along \(\pi_2\) gives \(d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_Y(y)\) for arbitrary \(Y\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_snd, and along \(\pi_1\), when \(g\) is a local sc-diffeomorphism, \(= d_X(x)\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_fst. Tameness. If \(Y\) is tame, the charts \(\psi \circ \pi_2\), \(\psi\) a tame chart of \(Y\) restricted to \(g^{-1}(W)\), are charts of the fibred product with tame models Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isTame_fibredProduct. Together: Proposition 2.46 Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.proposition_2_46, and in its last statement \(d = d_X = d_Y\) for arbitrary \(X\), \(Y\) and, for tame \(X\), \(Y\), \(2d = d_{X \times Y}\) by Lemma 4.D Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.proposition_2_46_of_isLocalScDiffeo.

II.18 Strong bundle retractions (Definitions 2.47–2.49)

\(U \triangleleft F\). The double filtration is \(U_m \times F_k\) Chapter2/TamedoubleLevel. \(C \times F_0\) is a partial quadrant in \(E \oplus F\), through \((\mathbb R^n \oplus W) \oplus F \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus (W \oplus F)\) Chapter2/StrongBundleprodQuadrantIso Chapter2/StrongBundleIsPartialQuadrant.prod_univ, and \(U \times F_0\) is relatively open in it Chapter2/StrongBundleIsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod_univ — so “sc-smooth on \((U \triangleleft F)[i] = U \oplus F^i\)” makes sense (exposition Lemma 1.B of Chapter 1). Definition 2.47. A strong bundle map maps \(U \times F_0\) into \(U' \times F'_0\), has first component independent of \(h\) and second linear in \(h\), maps \(U_m \times F_k\) into \(U'_m \times F'_k\) for \(k \le m + 1\), is sc-smooth on \(U \times F_0\), and its fibre-lifted map on \(U \times F_1\) Chapter2/TameshiftFiber is sc-smooth for \(E \oplus F^1\) Chapter2/TameIsStrongBundleMap; a strong bundle retraction is an idempotent one Chapter2/TameIsStrongBundleRetraction. Lemma 5.A. The base \(r(u) = R(u, 0)_1\) Chapter2/TameIsStrongBundleMap.base Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.apply_fst is an sc-smooth retraction on \(U\): sc-smooth as \(R\) composed with \(u \mapsto (u, 0)\) and the first projection, idempotent by the first component of \(R \circ R = R\) Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.baseRetraction. For \(u \in O\), \(R(u, h) = (u, \Gamma(u, h))\), so the second component of \(R \circ R = R\) reads \(\Gamma(u, \Gamma(u, h)) = \Gamma(u, h)\): \(\Gamma(u, \cdot)\) is a projection Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.fiber_idem. \(R\) is an sc-smooth retraction on \(U \times F_0\) in \(C \times F_0\) Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetraction and, through the lift of the fibre component to \(F_1\) (possible since \(R\) preserves the double filtration at \((0, 1)\) Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.snd_mem_range Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.toBase_shiftFiber_snd), on \(U \times F_1\) for \(E \oplus F^1\) Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetractionOne.

An sc-smooth section is sc-smooth from \((O, C, E)\) into \((K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)\) with \(f(x)_1 = x\) Chapter2/TameIsScSmoothSection; an sc⁺-section is sc-smooth into \(K[1]\) Chapter2/TameIsScPlusSection Chapter2/TameIsScPlusSection.mem. II.19 Strong bundles over M-polyfolds (Definitions 2.50–2.53)

Definition 2.50. For \(P : Y \to X\) with linear structures on the fibres, a strong bundle chart is a chart \(\varphi\) of \(X\) (of the structure — the text says only “a homeomorphism onto \(O\)”), a strong bundle retraction \(R\) on \(U \subseteq C\) with base retract \(O\), and a homeomorphism \(\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K\) with \(\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))\), linear on fibres Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.K. \(K\) is a local strong bundle retract and a retract on \([0]\) and \([1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.isStrongBundleRetract Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.isScRetract Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.isScRetract_one Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.model, the source \(P^{-1}(V)\) is open Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.isOpen_source, \(\Phi(P^{-1}(V)) = K\) and \(p(K) = O\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.image_source Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.base_K. “Bounded on the fibres” needs no hypothesis: the restriction of the continuous \(\Phi\) to a fibre is continuous Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.continuous_fiber. Two charts are compatible if the transitions \(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.overlap Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.transition and back are sc-smooth between the overlaps on \([0]\) and, fibre-lifted, on \([1]\), and carry fibre components in \(F_1\) to \(F'_1\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.Compatible Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.Compatible.symm; the last condition, implicit in the text, is what makes \((\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]\) the restriction of \(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}\). Atlases and their equivalence Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleAtlas Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleAtlas.Equiv; Banachable fibres Chapter2/StrongBundleIsBanachable.

Definition 2.51. A strong bundle is a continuous surjection with Banachable fibres and a strong bundle atlas, \(Y\) Hausdorff paracompact Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle. Each \(\Phi\) is a chart of \(Y\) with model \((K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.toMChart, compatibility of strong bundle charts on \([0]\) is compatibility of these charts Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.Compatible.toMChart, and they form the atlas of the M-polyfold \(Y[0]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.atlas0 Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.toMPolyfold0 Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.isChart_toMChart. \(P : Y[0] \to X\) is sc-smooth: in the charts \(\Phi\) and \(\varphi\) it is \(p : K \to O\) (Lemma 5.B), and one pair of charts per point suffices Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj. The double filtration \(Y_{m,k}\) is defined through all the charts of the atlas around a point Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.doubleLevel.

\(Y_{m,k}\) does not depend on the chart Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff. Let \(y\) lie in the domain of a chart \(\Phi\) of the atlas with \(\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k\), \(k \le m + 1\), and let \(\Phi'\) be another chart around \(y\); then \(\Phi'(y) = (\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})(\Phi(y))\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.transition_apply. The base component: \(\Phi'(y)_1 = \varphi'(\varphi^{-1}(\Phi(y)_1))\), and the base transition, sc-smooth and so \(\mathrm{sc}^0\), maps points of level \(m\) to points of level \(m\) Chapter2/MPolyfoldMChart.transition_apply. The fibre component, \(k \le m\): \(\Phi(y)\) lies on level \(k\) of \(E \oplus F\) (levels decrease Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.range_toBase_mono), and the \([0]\)-transition, \(\mathrm{sc}^0\) on the overlap retract Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap, keeps it on level \(k\). The case \(k = m + 1\): the fibre component of \(\Phi(y)\) lies in \(F_1\), so its lift \(\Phi(y)[1]\) to \(E_0 \times F_1\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundleChart.liftOne Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundleChart.toBase_liftOne is a point of level \(m\) of \(E \oplus F^1\) (level \(m\) of \(F^1\) is \(F_{m+1}\) Chapter1/ScBanachScBanach.shiftScale_toBase); the \([1]\)-transition, \(\mathrm{sc}^0\) for \(E \oplus F^1\) on the overlap Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap_one, keeps it on level \(m\), and its value is the lift \(\Phi'(y)[1]\), because the \(F_1\)-condition of compatibility puts the fibre component of \(\Phi'(y)\) in \(F'_1\). So \(\Phi'(y) \in E'_m \times F'_{m+1}\). The case \(k \le m\) uses the \([0]\)-transition only; the case \(k = m + 1\) uses exactly the \(F_1\)-condition made explicit in Definition 2.50.

The set \(Y[1]\) and its topology. \(Y_{0,1}\) is the set of points whose fibre component lies in \(F_1\) in every chart of the atlas around them Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneSet; by the \(F_1\)-condition one chart suffices Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff. \(Y[1]\) is \(Y_{0,1}\) as a type Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.One with the topology generated by the sets \(\{y \in \operatorname{dom}\Phi : \Phi(y)[1] \in W\}\), \(W\) open in \(E_0 \times F_1\), as for \(X_m\) in §2.2 Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.isOpen_one_basic. The inclusion \(Y[1] \to Y\) is continuous Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.continuous_oneVal: inside the domain of a chart \(\Phi\), an open subset of \(Y\) is the preimage under \(\Phi\) of an open \(W \subseteq E_0 \times F_0\) (\(\Phi\) is a homeomorphism onto \(K\) Chapter2/MPolyfoldMChart.exists_isOpen_image_eq), and its points in \(Y[1]\) form the basic set of \((1 \times \iota)^{-1}(W)\). A continuous injection into the Hausdorff space \(Y\) makes \(Y[1]\) Hausdorff Mathlib/Topology/Separation/HausdorffT2Space.of_injective_continuous.

The charts \(\Phi[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneChart. \(y \mapsto \Phi(y)[1]\) maps \(P^{-1}(V) \cap Y[1]\) into \(K[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundleChart.liftOne_mem, with inverse \(z \mapsto \Phi^{-1}(z_1, \iota z_2)\), a point of \(Y_{0,1}\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.symm_mem_oneSet Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneChartInv Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.liftOne_symm. It is continuous by the definition of the topology. Its inverse is continuous: a basic open set \(\{\Phi'(y)[1] \in W\}\) pulls back to the set of \(z \in K[1]\) in the \([1]\)-part of the overlap with \((\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1](z) \in W\); the overlap is \(K \cap W_0\) for an open \(W_0\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.overlap_eq_inter and the \([1]\)-transition is continuous on it, so this set is open in \(K[1]\). The overlap of \(\Phi[1]\) and \(\Phi'[1]\) is the \([1]\)-part of the overlap of \(\Phi\) and \(\Phi'\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneChart_overlap, and their transition map is the \([1]\)-transition \((\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneChart_transition, sc-smooth in both directions by Definition 2.50; so the charts \(\Phi[1]\) are compatible Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.oneChart_compatible and form an atlas of \(Y[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.atlas1. \(Y[1]\) is metrizable: \(P\) restricted to \(Y[1]\) is continuous into the paracompact Hausdorff \(X\), and over the domain \(V\) of a chart of \(X\) its preimage is the source of a chart \(\Phi[1]\), homeomorphic to a retract and so metrizable Chapter2/MetrizableMChart.metrizableSpace_source; the pull-back form of Smirnov’s theorem applies Chapter2/MetrizablemetrizableSpace_of_pullback Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.metrizableSpace_one. Hence \(Y[1]\) is paracompact Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.paracompactSpace_one, which an M-polyfold must be and the text does not mention, and \(Y[1]\) is an M-polyfold Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.toMPolyfold1 whose charts include the \(\Phi[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.isChart_oneChart.

\(P[1]\) and the inclusion \(Y[1] \to Y[0]\). In the charts \(\Phi[1]\) and \(\varphi\), \(P[1]\) is the projection \(K[1] \to O\) of Lemma 5.B Chapter2/StrongBundleIsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst_one, and one pair of charts per point suffices Chapter2/LevelPolyfoldMPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts; so \(P[1] : Y[1] \to X\) is sc-smooth Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj1. Definition 2.52. A section has \(P \circ f = \mathrm{id}\) Chapter2/StrongBundleIsSection; it is sc-smooth if sc-smooth into \(Y[0]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection, and an sc⁺-section if in every chart its fibre values lie in \(F_1\) and its fibre-lifted representative Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.localRepOne is sc-smooth into \(K[1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundle.IsScPlusSection. This is the text’s definition Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.isScPlusSection_iff: \(f\) is an sc⁺-section iff it is a section and \(f = \iota \circ g\) for an sc-smooth \(g : X \to Y[1]\), \(\iota\) the inclusion. Forward: the values of \(f\) lie in \(Y_{0,1}\) (one chart suffices), which defines \(g\); on the domain of a chart \(\varphi\) of \(X\) under a strong bundle chart \(\Phi\), \(g = \Phi[1]^{-1} \circ (\text{the local representative}) \circ \varphi\), which gives the continuity of \(g\), and the representative of \(g\) in the charts \(\varphi\), \(\Phi[1]\) is the chart-wise representative, sc-smooth by hypothesis. Backward: the fibre values lie in \(F_1\) because \(g\) takes values in \(Y_{0,1}\), and the chart-wise representative is the representative of \(g\) in \(\varphi\), \(\Phi[1]\), sc-smooth by Definition 2.14 (a chart with empty domain is handled separately).

II.20 Proposition 2.54: the pull-back strong bundle

The pulled-back retraction. For a retraction \(r'\) on \(U'\) and \(g : O' \to O\) sc-smooth between retracts, \(R_g(w, h) := (r'(w), \Gamma(g(r'(w)), h))\) Chapter2/StrongBundlepullbackRetraction, where \(g(r'(w)) \in O \subseteq U\) Chapter2/StrongBundlepullback_mem_O Chapter2/StrongBundlepullback_mem_U. It is a strong bundle retraction Chapter2/StrongBundleisStrongBundleRetraction_pullback: it maps \(U' \times F_0\) into itself; its first component does not depend on \(h\) and its second is linear in \(h\); it preserves the double filtration (\(r'\) and \(g \circ r'\) preserve levels, and \(R\) preserves the double filtration); on \([0]\) it is the pairing of \(r' \circ \mathrm{pr}_1\) with the second component of \(R \circ ((g \circ r') \circ \mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_2)\), sc-smooth by the chain rule and the pairing lemma, and likewise on \([1]\); and \(R_g \circ R_g = R_g\) because \(r' \circ r' = r'\) and \(\Gamma(o, \cdot)\) is a projection for \(o = g(r'(w)) \in O\) (Lemma 5.A). Its image is \(K_g = \{(w, h) : w \in O', (g(w), h) \in K\}\) Chapter2/StrongBundlepullback_image Chapter2/StrongBundleisStrongBundleRetract_pullback.

The fibres. \(P_f^{-1}(z) \to P^{-1}(f(z))\), \((z, y) \mapsto y\), is a bijection Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackpullbackFiberEquiv; transporting the linear structure along it Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackpullbackFiber_addCommGroup Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackpullbackFiber_module makes it a linear homeomorphism Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackpullbackFiberCLE, so the fibres of \(f^*Y\) are Banachable.

The charts. The data: a strong bundle chart \(c\) of \(Y\), a chart \(\psi\) of \(Z\) with \(f(\operatorname{dom}\psi) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi\), a retraction \(r_Z\) onto the model of \(\psi\), and the sc-smoothness of \(g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.g Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.g_smooth. The chart \(\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))\) maps \(P_f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)\) into \(K_g\) — because \(\Phi(y) = (g(\psi(z)), \cdot) \in K\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.g_apply Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.mem_Kg — with inverse \((w, h) \mapsto (\psi^{-1}(w), \Phi^{-1}(g(w), h))\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.symm_mem_pullback Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.invFun; both are continuous, it covers \(\psi\) and is linear on fibres, so it is a strong bundle chart of \(f^*Y\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.toChart Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.image_eq_Kg.

Compatibility. Sc-operators and pairings are sc-smooth between retracts Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackScOperator.isScSmoothRetractMap Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackIsScSmoothRetractMap.scPair Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackisScRetract_univ, and overlaps of strong bundle charts are retracts on \([0]\) and \([1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackStrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap_one. On the overlap of two pulled-back charts the transition map is \[(w, h) \mapsto \big(\psi_2\psi_1^{-1}(w),\ \mathrm{pr}_F(\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1})(g_1(w), h)\big)\] Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transitionFormula Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transition_eqOn: its first component is the transition of \(Z\) composed with the projection, its second the fibre component of the transition of \(Y\) composed with \((w, h) \mapsto (g_1(w), h)\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.gPair, which maps the overlap into the overlap of \(Y\)’s charts Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.gPair_mem. Each factor is sc-smooth between retracts, and Theorem 2.8 and the pairing lemma give the sc-smoothness on \([0]\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transition_isScSmooth; the same with \(F^1\) on \([1]\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transitionOne_eqOn Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transitionOne_isScSmooth; fibre components in \(F_1\) go to \(F_1\) because the transitions of \(Y\) have this property Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.transition_snd_mem_range. So any two pulled-back charts are compatible Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackPullbackChartData.compatible_toChart.

Proposition 2.54. \(f^*Y\) is paracompact: \(Z\) and \(Y[0]\) are metrizable (Theorem 2.16), so \(Z \times Y\) and its subspace \(f^*Y\) are metrizable, hence paracompact Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackparacompactSpace_pullbackSpace — a requirement of Definition 2.51 that the text does not mention. The pulled-back charts, built around every point from a chart of \(Y\)’s atlas and a chart of \(Z\) restricted to \(f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi)\), cover \(f^*Y\) and form an atlas Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackpullbackAtlas. With the continuous surjection \(P_f\) and its Banachable fibres this is a strong bundle structure on \(f^*Y \to Z\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackproposition_2_54 (“the easy proof is left to the reader”).

II.21 What the formalization taught us

  • Theorem 2.16 needs no added hypothesis, and not the text’s route. The text’s proof applies Proposition 2.57 to \(X_m\) without checking that \(X_m\) is regular. A partition of unity of \(X\), pulled back along the continuous inclusion, metrizes \(X_m\) directly Chapter2/MetrizablemetrizableSpace_of_pullback, and the same lemma proves Smirnov’s theorem Chapter2/MetrizablemetrizableSpace_of_locally, Proposition 2.19 (3) Chapter2/Metrizableproposition_2_19_3 and the paracompactness of \(f^*Y\) Chapter2/StrongBundlePullbackparacompactSpace_pullbackSpace. With it every paracompactness hypothesis carried by the constructions is discharged Chapter2/MetrizableMPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype.
  • Compatibility is local, and the text needs it. That the charts compatible with an atlas are compatible with each other is not in the text; it is the chain rule plus the locality of sc-smoothness Chapter2/MPolyfoldMChart.compatible_of_locally, and every chart-independence claim of §2.2 rests on it.
  • \(TO\) is a fixed-point set. Proposition 2.4 and Proposition 2.6 are one-line consequences of \(p \in Tr(TU) \iff Tr(p) = p\) Chapter2/RetractsScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff, which the text’s proofs use without stating.
  • The tangent bundle needs the locality of \(Tf\). That Definition 2.17’s relation is an equivalence relation needs the chain rule on the triple overlap and the agreement of \(Tf\) computed on an open subset with \(Tf\) computed on the whole retract Chapter2/TangentBundleretractTangentMap_inter_isOpen Chapter2/TangentBundleMPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_transport.
  • Level \(1\) suffices for §2.3. Proposition 2.30, Theorem 2.31 and Corollary 2.32 hold at points on level \(1\) and for sc¹ germs Chapter2/Boundaryproposition_2_30_reduced Chapter2/Boundarytheorem_2_31 Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexcorollary_2_32; the text’s “closure of \((T^R_xO)_\infty\)” is the density of level-\(1\) points in the kernel of a finite-rank map Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexScBanach.subset_closure_ker_inter_range_toBase.
  • Proposition 2.35 needs only tameness (2), and Lemma 2.40 needs (2) through it. \(Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x\) holds for every retraction Chapter2/TameRetractsScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace; that the retraction keeps points of a face in that face is the ray lemma Chapter2/TameRetractsray_zeroSet, which uses Proposition 2.35.
  • Three slips in the exposition. “\(|P_1 z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0\)” in the exposition’s proof of Proposition 2.43 is false for a general norm on \(E_0\); the formal neighbourhood intersects balls with their \(P_i\)-preimages Chapter2/TameRetractsproposition_2_43. The “transport by \(\varphi^{-1}\)” in Theorem 2.45 needs a shrinking so that the retraction maps its domain into itself Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local. In Proposition 2.46 the inverse of \(\pi_2\) cannot be factored through the constant-in-\(x\) map \(y' \mapsto (x, y')\), which is not sc-smooth at a non-smooth \(x\) Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_snd_fibredProduct.
  • Tameness is needed only for the additivity of the index under products. \(d_{X \times Y} \le d_X + d_Y\) in general Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le, with equality for tame factors Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.isTame_prod; the identities \(d = d_X = d_Y\) of Proposition 2.46 hold without tameness Chapter2/FibredProductMPolyfold.proposition_2_46_of_isLocalScDiffeo.
  • Definition 2.50 needs two explicit conditions. The base homeomorphism of a strong bundle chart must be a chart of \(X\), and the \([1]\)-transition must preserve fibre components in \(F_1\) Chapter2/StrongBundleStrongBundleChart.Compatible. The second condition is exactly what makes \(Y_{0,1}\), and so the M-polyfold \(Y[1]\), independent of the chart Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff Chapter2/StrongBundleOneStrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff.
  • Proposition 2.36 does not need the equality case of Theorem 2.31. For a tame retraction the smooth vectors of the splitting are \(Dr(x)T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)\), dual to the coordinates by Proposition 2.35, and \(T^R_xO\) is an sc-subspace because \(Dr(x)\) preserves \(E_x\) Chapter2/PartialConeproposition_2_36_partialCone.
  • Corners at once, not by induction. The intersections \(F^\sigma_x\) of Proposition 2.44 are retracts of \(r \circ P_\sigma\), by Lemma 4.C for each \(i \in \sigma\); no identification of the germ of \(F_1 \cap F_2\) with a face of \(F_1\) is needed Chapter2/CornerGermscorner_retraction.

Part III. Sc-Fredholm theory and the implicit function theorem (HWZ Chapter 3, §§3.1–3.8)

Chapter 3 is the reason for the first two chapters: it defines the sections of strong bundles to which an implicit function theorem applies, the sc-Fredholm sections, and proves that theorem. The engine is a fixed point problem with finitely many parameters, \(w = B(a, w)\), \(a \in \widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n\), \(w \in W\), where \(B(a, \cdot)\) contracts with an arbitrarily small constant near \(0\) on every level \(W_m\) of the scale. Its solution \(w = \delta(a)\) is the solution germ; the germ implicit function theorem (Theorem 3.33) says that \(\delta\) is as regular as \(B\). Around it the chapter builds: germs and their calculus (§III.1), sections of strong bundles in charts (§III.2), fillers (§§III.3–III.4), basic germs and their linearization (§III.5), sc-Fredholm germs and sections with the stability theorem 3.15 (§III.6); the germ implicit function theorem itself (§§III.7–III.11); local regularity and compactness, Theorems 3.40 and 3.12 (§§III.12–III.13); the finite-dimensional geometry of good position and the inverse and implicit function theorems in partial quadrants, which the formalization proved first and the rest uses (§§III.14–III.17); the basic class and local solvability (§§III.18–III.20); the linearization of an sc-Fredholm section at a zero, good position, and the graph description of the solution set of Theorem 3.54 (§§III.21–III.23); the tangent germ property, its invariance, and the manifold structure of solution sets (§III.24); and Lemmas 3.59–3.61 of the basic germ criterion (§III.25). Sections III.27–III.39 were added after the part was first assembled, for the Lean written since: tameness under sc-diffeomorphisms (§III.27), Corollary 3.39 (§III.28), good complements whose projection maps the quadrant into itself and local solvability with such a complement (§III.29), the index in Proposition 3.52 (§III.30), the linearization at a zero in charts and its chart independence (§III.31), Theorem 3.54 (1) at the nearby zeros (§§III.32–III.33), Theorem 3.54 (2) (§§III.34–III.36), the implicit function theorems 3.54, 3.23, 3.19, 3.24, 3.56, 3.57 assembled (§III.37), the basic germ criterion, Theorem 3.58 (§III.38), and what this addendum taught us (§III.39). Sections III.40–III.46 were added in a second addendum: Theorem 3.18 (§III.40); Theorem 3.54 (1) with the text’s hypotheses, by an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero (§§III.41–III.43); the dimension of the solution set as the Fredholm index and its local constancy (§III.44); the kernel as tangent space, good position at interior zeros, and the filler condition of §III.33 as a theorem (§III.45); and what the second addendum taught us (§III.46). Section III.47 repairs a tameness hypothesis, and §III.48 records the switch of Definition 3.11 to the text’s germ reading; the passages above that use the filling or the sc⁺-section have been rewritten for it.

What is proved, and what is not. The germ implicit function theorem is proved with the text’s hypotheses: no hypothesis had to be added to Theorems 3.29–3.35. What the formalization adds is precision about where the solution germ is regular. A germ is formalized as a fixed sequence of sets, and the proof shows that \(\delta\) is sc\(^k\) on the germ shifted by \(s_k = 2^k - 1\) levels; “if \(f\) is sc-smooth so is its solution germ” therefore holds for every \(k\) on a germ depending on \(k\) (§III.11). Elsewhere hypotheses had to be added: the good complement must be closed in Lemma 3.55 and in Definition 3.25; and Theorem 3.27 needs two regularity conditions on its data, each of which the text’s proof asserts and each of which fails in an example (§III.24) — for solution sets both are theorems (§§III.29, III.35–III.36). These are the only ones. Definition 3.11 is formalized as the text writes it, with the filling and the sc⁺-section sc-smooth germs whose levels may shrink, and every theorem built on it holds in that reading with the text’s conclusions (§§III.6, III.48); the first formalization’s whole-chart reading was narrower. Definition 6.1 (the index of the germ at a smooth point) and Proposition 6.2 (its constancy along sc-smooth paths), from Chapter 6 of the text, are proved with the text’s hypotheses — tame germ data, no bump functions, the locally defined sc⁺-sections of Definition 6.1 — for paths on \(\mathbb R\), by the text’s device run on the restriction of the bundle to a chart domain; the first proof, with global sections, assumed bump functions (§III.49). The implicit function theorems of §§III.23–III.45 were first stated with a tameness hypothesis that no strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies, and were vacuous; they now assume germ data and good position in tame charts, as the text does (§III.47). Theorem 3.54 (1) was first proved only under condition (3) of Definition 3.4 at the nearby zeros (§III.33); it is now proved with the text’s hypotheses, by an argument that is not the text’s (§§III.41–III.43), and the condition is a theorem (§III.45). The local solvability theorems 3.43 and 3.47 are proved in full, their clause (1) (“the solution map is an sc-smooth germ”) in the level-wise sense with \(k\)-dependent neighbourhoods (§III.20). Of Theorem 3.54 the graph description of the solution set near a zero in good position is §III.23. Its conclusion (2), the manifold structure, and the global Theorems 3.56, 3.57 and Corollary 3.24 are proved with the text’s hypotheses (§§III.34–III.37); its conclusion (1), good position at the nearby zeros, first under the added filler condition (§III.33), then with the text’s hypotheses (§III.43), and with it the local Theorems 3.54, 3.23 and 3.19 (§§III.37, III.43), with the dimension of the solution set equal to the Fredholm index (§III.44). Theorem 3.18 is §III.40. The basic germ criterion (Theorem 3.58) is proved in the coordinates of its proof (§III.38), with Lemmas 3.59–3.61 (§III.25).

Seven structural choices. (1) Germs are fixed sequences of sets, and the calculus the text uses on them silently is proved (§III.1). (2) Contraction germs carry explicit contraction regions instead of the text’s balls, because the regions of the iterated germ \(f^{(1)}\) must be unbounded in the tangent directions (§III.7). (3) “A strong bundle chart” in the definitions of §3.1 is a chart compatible with the atlas (§III.2). (4) Tameness, which the text assumes throughout, is used only in Theorem 3.54, and only for the chart of the germ data at the zero: through Proposition 2.35, \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\), and through the tameness of the model of the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) (§III.27). The theorems assume germ data and good position in tame charts, as Definitions 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53 do; the first formalization assumed every compatible chart tame, which cannot be met (§III.47). (5) The coordinate change of Theorem 3.38 is linear, which makes the transport of solution sets in §3.5 linear algebra. (6) Classical regularity in the appendix is Mathlib’s \(C^k\) within a set, and the iterations of the text’s Lemmas 3.76 and 3.82 are replaced by bootstrapping a derivative formula. (7) In Definition 3.11 the filling \(g\) and the sc⁺-section \(s\) are germs on germs of neighbourhoods of their own, and the basic germ is shrunk to the germ \(G''\) of the points that \(\psi^{-1}\) sends into both, so that the nearby zeros produced by the implicit function theorem are points where \(g\) and \(s\) are sc¹ (§§III.6, III.48).
