III.18 Weak stability of basic germs: Theorem 3.38

Theorem 3.38 (text): for a basic germ \(f\) and the principal part \(s\) of an sc⁺-section with \(s(0) = 0\) there is a strong bundle isomorphism \(\Phi\) covering an sc-diffeomorphism \(\varphi\) such that \((\Phi_*(f + s))^1\), with the levels raised by one, is a basic germ, and \(n - N = n' - N'\). The text’s proof: with \(A = P_W \circ D_2s(0)\), \(1 + A\) is sc-Fredholm of index \(0\), with sc-splittings \(W = C \oplus X = R \oplus Z\), \(C = \ker(1 + A)\), \(R = \mathrm{range}(1 + A)\); \(P_W \circ s(a, w) = Aw + S(a, w)\) with \(S\) a small contraction in \(w\) on every level \(m \ge 1\); and with \(L = (1 + A)|_X : X \to R\) the equation becomes \(x - L^{-1}P_2\bar B(a, c + x) = 0\) in the new parameters \((a, c)\) and the new fibre variable \(x\). The formal proof follows it with two observations: the coordinate change is linear, and the index raise is a change of sc-structure.

The linear part of \(s\). For an sc¹-germ \(s\) into \(W^1\), \(A = D_2s(0)\) is an sc⁺-operator whose level-\(m\) map is the level operator of Proposition 1.16 at \(0 \in U_{m+1}\) Chapter3/BasicClassscPlusOfDeriv. The remainder \(S(a, w) = s(a, w) - Aw\) on level \(m + 1\) Chapter3/BasicClassscPlusRemainder is, for \(a\) and \(w\) small depending on \(m\) and \(\varepsilon\), an \(\varepsilon\)-contraction in \(w\): \(D_2S(0) = 0\) on level \(m + 1\), the derivative of \(s : U_{m+1} \to W_{m+1}\) is continuous in the operator norm (§III.1), and the mean value inequality on a ball for fixed \(a\) concludes Chapter3/BasicClassscPlusRemainder_contraction. The partial derivative of \(S\) in \(a\) does not vanish and plays no role. The text gives this one sentence (“\(S\) is … an arbitrary small contraction on every level \(m \ge 1\)”).

The data and the splitting. The data of the theorem are the germ \(G\), the \(W\)-component \(s\) of the sc⁺-germ with \(s(0) = 0\), and an sc-Fredholm splitting \(W = C \oplus X = R \oplus Z\) of \(T = 1 + A\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData. Such data exist: the identity is sc-Fredholm of index \(0\) (the trivial splitting) Chapter3/BasicClassisScFredholm_id Chapter3/BasicClassscIndex_id, so \(1 + A\) is sc-Fredholm by Proposition 1.10 Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.exists_of_scPlus. With the projections \(P_1 : W_m \to X_m\) along \(C_m\), \(P_2 : W_m \to R_m\) along \(Z_m\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.projX Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.projR, \(L = T|_X : X_m \to R_m\) is bijective Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.Lm_bijective, a topological isomorphism by the open mapping theorem Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.Lequiv, and \(L^{-1}P_2\) is an sc-operator \(W \to X\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.LinvPOp. The finite-dimensional \(C\), \(Z \subseteq W_\infty\) lift to every level Chapter3/BasicClassScBanach.finLift.

The coordinate changes. On the index-raised spaces, the new source is \(E' = (P \oplus C) \oplus X^1\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.E' and the new target \(F' = (Q \oplus Z) \oplus X^1\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.F' — the text’s \(\tau : Z \to C\), making the new finite-dimensional target \(\mathbb R^N \oplus C\), is not applied. The base change \(\psi(a, w) = ((a, (1 - P_1)w), P_1w)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.split and its inverse \(\psi^{-1}((a, c), x) = (a, c + x)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.glue are sc-operators inverse to each other Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.glue_split Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.split_glue; so are the fibre change \(\Psi(q, w) = ((q, (1 - P_2)w), L^{-1}P_2w)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiber and \(\Psi^{-1}((q, z), x) = (q, z + (1 + A)x)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiberInv Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiber_fiberInv Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiberInv_fiber, and \(\Psi\) vanishes only at \(0\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiber_eq_zero_iff. No general strong bundle isomorphism is needed.

The push-forward. The perturbed germ is \(f + \iota s\) with the inclusion \(W^1 \to Q \oplus W\) Chapter3/BasicClassScBanach.inrOp Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fsum, sc-smooth by the pairing and operator rules Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fsum_isScSmoothGerm. Its germ of neighbourhoods on \(E'\) is \(\psi(U_{m+1})\), the preimage of \(U_{m+1}\) under \(\psi^{-1}\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushGerm Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.glue_mapsToGerm, and the push-forward is \((\Phi_*(f + s))^1 = \Psi \circ (f + \iota s)^1 \circ \psi^{-1}\) with the level-shifted operators Chapter3/BasicClassScOperator.shiftOp Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap. It is sc-smooth: \((f + \iota s)^1\) is sc-smooth on the shifted germ (Proposition 1.17 for germs) and \(\Psi\), \(\psi^{-1}\) are sc-operators Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap_isScSmoothGerm. With \(\bar B = B - S\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.Bbar, the \(W\)-component of \((f + \iota s)^1\) at a level-\(1\) point is \((1 + A)w - \bar B(a, w)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.snd_levelMap_fsum, so the \(X\)-component of the push-forward is \(x - \hat B((a, c), x)\) with \(\hat B((a, c), x) = L^{-1}P_2\bar B(a, c + x)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushB Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.snd_pushMap — the text’s “desired formula”. \(\hat B\) is an sc⁰-contraction germ on the index-raised structure: on level \(m\) of \(E'\), i.e. level \(m + 1\) of \(W\), \(B\) contracts by Definition 3.7 and \(S\) by the remainder estimate, and \(L^{-1}P_2\) is bounded Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.levelMap_pushB Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushB_isSc0ContractionGerm. So the push-forward is a basic germ with contraction map \(\hat B\) Chapter3/BasicClasstheorem_3_38. Its zeros correspond to those of \(f + \iota s\) under \(\psi\), since \(\Psi\) is a linear isomorphism Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap_eq_zero_iff. The index: \(\mathrm{ind}(1 + A) = \mathrm{ind}(1) = 0\) (Proposition 1.10 with its index), i.e. \(\dim C = \dim Z\), so \(n' - N' = (n + \dim C) - (N + \dim Z) = n - N\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.finrank_Cs_eq_finrank_Zs.

The same on level \(0\). For §§III.19–III.20 the coordinate changes are also needed before the index raise: \(\psi\), \(\psi^{-1}\), \(\Psi\), \(\Psi^{-1}\) on every level Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.split₀ Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.glue₀ Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiber₀, the germ \(\psi(U_m)\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushGerm₀, and \(g = \Phi_*(f + s) = \Psi \circ (f + \iota s) \circ \psi^{-1}\) on level \(0\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap₀, sc-smooth Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap₀_isScSmoothGerm, whose level-\(1\) map is the index-raised push-forward Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap_eq_levelMap_pushMap₀.

III.19 The linearization at nearby solutions: Corollary 3.41

Corollary 3.41. For the data of Theorem 3.38 with \(f := h\) basic and \(D(h + \iota s)(0)\) surjective, there is \(r > 0\) such that every zero \(x\) of \(h + \iota s\) in \(U_0\) with \(|x|_0 < r\) is \(\iota(x_1)\) with \(x_1 \in U_1\), and \(D(h + \iota s)(x_1) : E_0 \to F_0\) is a surjective Fredholm operator of index \(\dim P - \dim Q\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.corollary_3_41. The text’s sc⁺-map \(s\) has an \(\mathbb R^N\)-component; it can be absorbed into the basic germ (as in §III.23), so the data carry only the \(W\)-component.

The derivative on \(U_1\). For \(x \in U_1\), \(D(h + \iota s)(x) = Dh(x) + \iota Ds(x)\) — uniqueness of the derivative within \(U_1\), then density of \(E_1\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.Dfs'_eq — and \(\mathrm{pr}_W Dh(x) = \mathrm{pr}_W - DB(x)\), from \(\mathrm{pr}_W h = \mathrm{pr}_W - B\) on \(U_0\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.snd_Df_eq; \(D_2B(0) = 0\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.DB_zero_snd. The decomposition. \(D(h + \iota s)(x) = D(h + \iota s)(0) + S(x) + K(x)\) with \(S(x)(\alpha, \zeta) = (0, -D_2B(x)\zeta)\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.Sop Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.Dfs'_eq_add of norm \(\le \varepsilon\) for \(x \in U_1\) small on level \(1\), by Lemma 3.9 (c) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.exists_norm_Sop_le, and \(K(x)\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.Kop compact: the sum of finite-rank operators through \(Q\) and through \(P\) and of \(\iota(Ds(x) - Ds(0))\) through the compact inclusion \(W_1 \to W_0\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.Kop_isCompactOperator.

Fredholm with index \(n - N\) at every small \(x \in U_1\). \(D(h + \iota s)(0)\) is Fredholm of index \(n - N\): \(Dh(0)\) is (Proposition 3.10 for the basic germ, §III.5) and \(\iota Ds(0)\) is compact Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.isFredholm_Dfs. A small perturbation of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm: if \(v\) is a quasi-inverse of \(u\) and \(\|v\|\|s\| < 1\), then \((1 + vs)^{-1}v\) is a quasi-inverse of \(u + s\) (Neumann series) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationisFredholm_add_of_norm_lt, with the same index Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationisFredholm_fredholmIndex_add_of_norm_lt; a compact perturbation does not change the index Chapter1/FredholmIndexfredholmIndex_add_isCompactOperator. So \(D(h + \iota s)(x)\) is Fredholm of index \(n - N\) for every \(x \in U_1\) small on level \(1\), not only at solutions Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.exists_isFredholm_Dfs'.

Surjectivity: the compactness argument. Let \(N\) be a closed complement of \(\ker D(h + \iota s)(0)\). Then \(\ker D(h + \iota s)(x) \cap N = 0\) for \(x \in U_1\) small on level \(1\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.exists_ker_Dfs'_inf_eq_bot. Otherwise there are \(x_k \to 0\) in \(E_1\) and unit vectors \((\alpha_k, \zeta_k) \in N\) in the kernels; the \(W\)-component of the equation reads \(\zeta_k = D_1B(x_k)\alpha_k + D_2B(x_k)\zeta_k - \iota Ds(x_k)(\alpha_k, \zeta_k)\). \(\alpha_k\) has a convergent subsequence (\(P\) finite-dimensional); \(Ds(x_k)(\alpha_k, \zeta_k)\) is bounded in \(W_1\) (the derivatives near \(0\) are uniformly bounded Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationIsSc1GermWith.exists_norm_deriv_le), so its image in \(W_0\) has a convergent subsequence; \(D_1B(x_k)\alpha_k \to D_1B(0)\alpha\) by the joint continuity of the tangent map Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationIsSc1GermWith.tendsto_deriv; and \(\|D_2B(x_k)\| \to 0\). So \(\zeta_k\) converges, \((\alpha_k, \zeta_k) \to (\alpha, z_0) \in N\) of norm \(1\) in \(\ker D(h + \iota s)(0)\) — a contradiction. (The text uses the Neumann series \(\zeta_k = \sum(D_2B(x_k))^l z_k\); here \(|\zeta_k - z_k| \le \varepsilon_k \to 0\) suffices.) Then \(\dim\ker D(h + \iota s)(x) \le \dim\ker D(h + \iota s)(0) = n - N = \mathrm{ind}\), and an operator of finite index with \(\dim\ker \le \mathrm{ind}\) is onto Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationHasFiniteIndex.surjective_of_finrank_ker_le — instead of the text’s “\(Df(x)|_N\) has index \(0\) and is injective”. Zeros are on level \(1\) and small there: by the lifts of Theorem 3.40, continuous at \(0\) (§III.12); the text’s detour through “bounded on level \(2\), hence convergent on level \(1\)” is not needed.

III.20 Local solvability: Lemma 3.46, Theorem 3.43, Lemmas 3.42, 3.44, Corollary 3.47

Lemma 3.46 (Appendix 3.8.2). If \(K' = \{(\alpha, L\alpha) : \alpha \in \widetilde K\}\), the image of the graph map Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitygraphMap (with \((\alpha, L\alpha) \in \widetilde C \oplus W\) iff \(\alpha \in \widetilde C\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitygraphMap_mem_prod_iff), has a good complement \(Y'\) with respect to \(\widetilde C \oplus W\), then \(\widetilde K\) has a good complement \(Z\) with respect to \(\widetilde C\) such that \(Z \times W\) is a good complement of \(K'\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitylemma_3_46. Proof. \(Z' := \mathrm{pr}_P(Y')\) satisfies \(P = \widetilde K + Z'\); choose \(Z \subseteq Z'\) with \(P = \widetilde K \oplus Z\) and a linear right inverse \(\rho : Z' \to Y'\) of the projection (bounded, finite dimensions); for \(|z| \le \varepsilon'|\alpha|\), \(\varepsilon' = \varepsilon/(\|\rho\| + 1)\), \(y = \rho(z) = (z, w) \in Y'\) has \(|y| \le \varepsilon|(\alpha, L\alpha)|\), so \((\alpha, L\alpha) \in C'\) iff \((\alpha, L\alpha) + y \in C'\), i.e. \(\alpha \in \widetilde C\) iff \(\alpha + z \in \widetilde C\). The text’s intermediate complement \(Y_0\) is not needed. Good position of \(K'\) gives good position of \(\widetilde K\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitylemma_3_46_isInGoodPosition.

Projecting solutions into the quadrant. A gap in the text’s proof of Theorem 3.43 (3): a solution \(a = k + z\) (\(k \in \widetilde K\), \(z \in Z\)) of \(H(a) = 0\) is matched with the solution of Theorem 3.78 by its uniqueness clause, which needs \(k \in \widetilde C\) — not verified in the text. It holds because \(z\) is small compared with \(k\): from \(H(a) = 0 = H(0)\) and \(DH(0)k = 0\), \(|DH(0)z| = o(|a|)\); \(DH(0)\) is injective on \(Z\), hence bounded below there Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityexists_norm_le_of_injOn; so \(|z| \le \varepsilon|k|\) near \(0\), and the good-complement property gives \(k \in \widetilde C\) from \(k + z = a \in \widetilde C\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityexists_proj_mem_of_eq_zero.

The data of Theorem 3.43. The text states it for \(g = \Phi_*(f + s)\); the formal statement is for any sc-smooth germ \(g\) on \(G\) with \(g(0) = 0\) whose index-raised germ \(g^1\) on the shifted germ is a basic germ with contraction map \(B\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData. Its solution germ \(\delta\) (of the working form of \(B\)) takes values in \(W_1\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.δ, with \(\mathrm{pr}_W g(a, \delta(a)) = 0\) on level \(0\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.snd_g_sol and uniqueness in the contraction region Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.eq_δ. Put \(H(a) = \mathrm{pr}_Q\,g(a, \delta(a))\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.H. Regularity of \(H\) (the text: “\(H\) restricted to \(U'_i\) is of class \(C^{i-1}\)”): for every \(j \ge 1\) there is a relatively open \(V \ni 0\) in \(\widetilde C\) on which \(H\) is \(C^j\) — by Corollary 3.34 for \(g^1\), \(\delta\) lifts to a \(C^j\) map into \(W_{2j}\), and \(g : E_{2j} \to F_j\) is \(C^j\) by Proposition 1.18 for germs Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.H_contDiffOn. A single \(C^1\) neighbourhood \(V_1\) carries the derivative data Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.exists_deriv: \(D\delta(0) : P \to W_1\), \(L = \iota D\delta(0)\), and \(DH(0) = \mathrm{pr}_Q Dg(0)(\alpha, L\alpha)\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.DH₀ Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.hasFDerivWithinAt_H, by the chain rule for \(a \mapsto g(a, \delta(a))\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.hasFDerivWithinAt_comp.

Lemma 3.44. “Recalling from Lemma 3.9 that \(D_2B(0) = 0\)”: Lemma 3.9 gives this for \(g^1\), on level \(1\); the kernel of \(Dg(0)\) is computed on level \(0\). So first the \(W\)-component of \(Dg(0)(0, \zeta)\) is \(\zeta\) for \(\zeta \in W_1\), by Lemma 3.9 (b) for \(g^1\), and then for all \(\zeta \in W_0\) by density Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.snd_Dg_inr. Differentiating \(\mathrm{pr}_W g(a, \delta(a)) = 0\) at \(0\) gives \(\mathrm{pr}_W Dg(0)(\alpha, L\alpha) = 0\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.snd_Dg_graph. Hence \(Dg(0)(\alpha, \zeta) = 0\) iff \(\zeta = L\alpha\) and \(DH(0)\alpha = 0\): \(\ker Dg(0) = \{(\alpha, D\delta(0)\alpha) : \alpha \in \ker DH(0)\}\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.ker_Dg_eq, and \(DH(0)\) is onto when \(Dg(0)\) is Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Deriv.DH₀_surjective.

Theorem 3.43 Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitytheorem_3_43. Hypotheses: \(\widetilde C\) a partial quadrant, \(Dg(0)\) onto, \(K' = \ker Dg(0)\) in good position to \(\widetilde C \oplus W\), and the regularity of Lemma 3.42 as an explicit hypothesis: for every \(\varepsilon > 0\) there is \(r > 0\) such that every zero \(x\) of \(g\) in \(U_0\) with \(|x|_0 < r\) has \(W\)-component \(\iota(w_1)\), \(|w_1|_1 < \varepsilon\). The choices Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.exists_sol: \(\widetilde K = \ker DH(0)\) with \(K'\) its graph (Lemma 3.44); the good complement \(Z\) of \(\widetilde K\) with \(Z \oplus W\) good for \(K'\) (Lemma 3.46); and the solution \(\sigma : V' \to Z\) of \(H(k + \sigma(k)) = 0\) with its uniqueness constants, from Theorem 3.78 applied to \(H\) (§III.17). Then \(\tau(y) = (\sigma(v), \delta(v + \sigma(v)) - Lv)\) for \(y = (v, Lv)\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.τ on \(V = \pi^{-1}(V')\), relatively open in \(K' \cap C'\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.V Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.V_relOpen, with values in \(Z \oplus W\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.τ_mem_Y, so that \(y + \tau(y) = (a, \delta(a))\) with \(a = v + \sigma(v)\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.coe_add_τ. (3), first half: \(y + \tau(y)\) lies in \(U_0\) and is a zero, since \(\mathrm{pr}_W g(a, \delta(a)) = 0\) and \(\mathrm{pr}_Q g(a, \delta(a)) = H(a) = 0\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.sol_mem_and_eq_zero. Regularity: \(\tau\) is \(C^1\) on \(V\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.τ_contDiffOn with \(W\)-component on level \(1\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.snd_τ_mem_range, and \(D\tau(0)\eta = -D\delta(0)\pi(\eta) + D\delta(0)\pi(\eta) = 0\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.hasFDerivWithinAt_τ Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.fderivWithin_τ — (2). (3), second half Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.exists_eq_add_τ: a zero \(x = (a, w)\) near \(0\) has, by the regularity hypothesis, \(w\) on level \(1\) and small there, so \(w = \delta(a)\) by the uniqueness of the solution germ on level \(1\), so \(H(a) = 0\); write \(a = k + z\) with the projection along \(Z\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.projK; then \(k \in \widetilde K \cap \widetilde C\) (the gap above) and \(z = \sigma(k)\) by the uniqueness clause of Theorem 3.78; so \(x = y + \tau(y)\) for \(y = (k, Lk)\). Clause (1), “\(\tau\) is an sc-smooth germ”, is proved level-wise: for every \(k \ge 1\) there are a relatively open \(V_k \subseteq V\) containing \(0\) and a \(C^k\) map \(\tau_k : V_k \to E_k = P \oplus W_k\) with \(\iota_k\tau_k = \tau\) on \(V_k\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityShiftedBasicData.Sol.exists_contDiffOn_level — the reading of Corollary 3.34 and Definition 3.25 (ii). The proof applies Theorem 3.78 to \(H\) at regularity \(k\) on the neighbourhood of its regularity lemma, and identifies the \(C^k\) solution \(\sigma_k\) with \(\sigma\) near \(0\) through the uniqueness clause (3) of Theorem 3.78 — which needs \(\sigma\) continuous at \(0\) with \(\sigma(0) = 0\), so that \(|\sigma(y)|\) is below the uniqueness constant for \(y\) small; the text says nothing about why the solutions produced for the different \(k\) coincide. The \(W\)-component \(\iota\delta(a) - L\pi(y)\), \(a = \pi y + \sigma(\pi y)\), lifts to \(W_k\) through the \(C^k\) lift of \(\delta\) into \(W_{2k}\), with \(L\) the derivative of that lift at \(0\) composed with the inclusion (uniqueness of the derivative of \(\iota\delta\) at \(0\)). The full statement is Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitytheorem_3_43_sc_smooth; the statement without (1) is kept for Theorem 3.54.

Lemma 3.42. For the push-forward \(g = \Phi_*(f + s)\) of Theorem 3.38 — packaged as the data of Theorem 3.43, \(g\) on level \(0\) with index-raised basic germ \((\Phi_*(f + s))^1\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityStabilityData.toShiftedBasicData — the regularity hypothesis holds: a zero \(x'\) of \(g\) in \(\psi(U_0)\) with \(|x'|_0\) small has \(\psi^{-1}(x')\) a zero of \(f + \iota s\), which by the lifts of Theorem 3.40, continuous at \(0\), lies on level \(1\) and is small there; \(\psi\) is linear on level \(1\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityStabilityData.lemma_3_42.

Corollary 3.47 Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitytheorem_3_47_sc_smooth Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitytheorem_3_47. For a basic germ \(f\) and the data of Theorem 3.38 with \(D(f + \iota s)(0)\) surjective and kernel \(K\) in good position to \(C = \widetilde C \oplus W\): a good complement \(Y\), \(V\) relatively open in \(K \cap C\), \(\sigma : V \to Y\) of class \(C^1\) with values on level \(1\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), \(D\sigma(0) = 0\), the graph consisting of zeros of \(f + \iota s\), an open \(U'' \ni 0\) in which every zero lies on the graph, and for every \(k\) a \(C^k\) lift of \(\sigma\) into \(E_k\) near \(0\). Proof. Theorem 3.43 for \(g = \Phi_*(f + s)\), with Lemma 3.42 for its regularity hypothesis. Since the coordinate change is linear, \(Dg(0) = \Psi \circ D(f + \iota s)(0) \circ \psi^{-1}\) (chain rule for sc-operators) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityStabilityData.scDerivGerm_pushMap₀, so surjectivity and the kernels correspond, \(\ker Dg(0) = \psi(K)\); good position of \(\psi(K)\) follows by Lemma 3.45 (finite dimensionality of \(K\) from Lemma 3.44); and the conclusion is transported back by \(\psi^{-1}\): \(Y = \psi^{-1}(Y')\), \(V = \psi^{-1}(V')\), \(\sigma = \psi^{-1}\tau\psi\). The text transports the solution set back with the nonlinear \(\varphi\) and justifies the good position with the degeneracy index (Lemma 3.70, Theorem 3.72); with \(\psi\) linear neither is needed. The transport uses that \(\widetilde C \oplus C\) is a partial quadrant for finite-dimensional \(C\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilityIsPartialQuadrant.const_prod_univ.

III.21 The linearization at a zero (Proposition 3.52) and good position of a germ (Definition 3.53)

Proposition 3.52 (text): if \(f\) is an sc-Fredholm section of a tame strong bundle and \(f(x) = 0\), then \(Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x\) is an sc-Fredholm operator. Formalized in the chart of Definition 3.11 centred at a zero \(x_0\), with the level-\(0\) Fredholm property Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGproposition_3_52 Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGproposition_3_52_local: \(Dg(0) : E_0 \to F_0\) and \(Tf(x_0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O} : T_0O \to K_0\) are Fredholm with \(\mathrm{ind}\,Tf(x_0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0)\). Here \(Dg(0)\) is the value at \(0\) of a derivative family \(Dg\) of the filling germ on a germ \(G\) with \(G_0 \subseteq U\), the same for every family and every germ (§III.4); the statement exposes \(G\) and \(Dg\), where the whole-chart statement Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationproposition_3_52_wholeChart has the derivative on \(U\), a junk value for a germ. (The sc-Fredholm property of \(Tf(x)\) would need \(T_0O = Dr(0)E\) and \(K_0 = \rho(0)F\) as sc-Banach spaces, not set up. The statements quantify the index as “\(n - N\) for some natural numbers \(n\), \(N\)”, which every integer satisfies; the identification with \(\dim P - \dim Q\) of the conjugating basic germ is made inside the proof, by proposition_3_10_basic_level_zero, and not exported.)

Step (a): the derivative of the conjugation Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGIsConjugateToBasicGerm.scDeriv_isFredholm. Let \(k = g - \iota s\), an sc¹-germ on \(G_g \cap G_s\) (§III.48) with \(k(0) = 0\) (\(s(0) = g(0)\) in Definition 3.11, \(g(0) = \mathbf f(0) = 0\) by the filler) and \((\Psi(u, k(u)))_2 = h(\psi(u))\) near \(0\). Linearizing needs: the chain rule for the germ \(h \circ \psi\) on a germ small enough that \(\psi\) maps it into the germ of \(h\) (§III.1, ScNbhdGerm.preimage); the derivative of \(u \mapsto \Gamma(u)k(u)\) at \(0\), where \(\Gamma(u) = (\Psi(u, \cdot))_2\) is a bounded operator Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.fiberCLM and \(D(\mathrm{pr}_{F'} \circ \Psi)(0, 0)(h, k) = \Gamma(0)k\) (as in §III.4) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.scDeriv_fiber_zero, so the derivative is \(\Gamma(0)Dk(0)\) because \(k(0) = 0\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.scDeriv_fiber_comp — for the germ \(k\) by the chain rule with the whole-chart outer map \(\mathrm{pr}_{F'} \circ \Psi\), the two derivative families agreeing at \(0\) on \(G_k \cap \psi^{-1}(G)\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGIsStrongBundleIso.fiberCLM_comp_deriv_zero_eq_germ, so no shrinking of the basic germ is needed at \(0\); and the invertibility of \(D\psi(0)\) and \(\Gamma(0)\) (inverses \(D\psi'(0)\), \(\Gamma'(0)\), chain rule for \(\psi' \circ \psi = \mathrm{id}\)). Then \(\Gamma(0)Dk(0) = Dh(0)D\psi(0)\), so \(Dk(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1}Dh(0)D\psi(0)\) is Fredholm with the index of \(Dh(0)\): Fredholm operators and their index are stable under composition with isomorphisms on both sides Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationisFredholm_equiv_comp_equiv, and \(Dh(0)\) is Fredholm by Proposition 3.10 for the basic germ Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationproposition_3_10_basic_level_zero. Step (b): \(Dg(0) = Dk(0) + \iota Ds(0)\) — for germs this is algebra at \(0\): \(g - \iota s\) has the derivative family \(Dg - \iota Ds\) on \(G_g \cap G_s\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGIsSc1GermWith.sub_toBase_shift Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGIsSc1GermWith.deriv_zero_eq_add_scPlus (on \(U\) it was the uniqueness of the derivative within \(U_1\) and density) — a compact perturbation since \(\iota Ds(0)\) is the level-\(0\) map of an sc⁺-operator (\(s\) is an sc¹-germ into \(F^1\) and \(0\) is smooth); the index is unchanged (Part I, §I.9). Step (c): Proposition 3.5 (§III.4) transfers both to \(Tf(x_0)\); it needs \(g(0) = 0\).

Definition 3.53 (text): \((f, x)\) with \(f(x) = 0\) is in good position if (1) \(f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x\) is onto and (2) if \(d_X(x) \ge 1\), \(\ker f'(x)\) is in good position to the partial cone \(C_xX\) in \(T_xX\). In the chart: Definition 3.21 inside a subspace \(T \subseteq E_0\) — \(N \subseteq T\), interior of \(N \cap C\) in \(N\) nonempty, and a good complement \(P \subseteq T\) of \(N\) in \(T\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsInGoodPositionIn (for \(T = E_0\) it is Definition 3.21 Chapter3/GoodPositionGermisInGoodPositionIn_top_iff); and the germ is in good position if \(Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O}\) is onto and \(\ker Dg(0)\) is in good position to \(T_0O \cap C\) inside \(T_0O = Dr(0)E\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsGoodPositionAt Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsGoodPositionAt.surjective_fillerRestrict. Here \(\ker Dg(0) \subseteq T_0O\), because \((1 - \rho(0))Dg(0)\) is injective on \(\ker Dr(0)\) (filler (3)) and \((1 - \rho(0))Dg(0)Dr(0) = 0\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsFillerOf.ker_deriv_le_range, and it is the kernel of \(Tf(0)\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsFillerOf.map_ker_fillerRestrict — the text’s “\(\ker Tf(0) \oplus \{0\} = \ker Dg(0)\) by the properties of the filler”. The case distinction \(d_X(x) \ge 1\) is dropped: at an interior point the partial cone is the whole tangent space and (2) holds for every subspace. For a filling germ the condition is one on the operator \(Dg(0)\) (the text’s \(f'(x)\) is defined through the filler at the centre only), which the chart notion takes as a parameter Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGIsGoodPositionAtGerm — the notion above is the case of the derivative on \(U\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGisGoodPositionAt_iff_germ — and the two kernel facts hold with the same proofs Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGIsFillingGerm.ker_deriv_le_range Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGIsFillingGerm.map_ker_fillerRestrict. For a section, \((f, x_0)\) is in good position if it has the data of Definition 3.11 at \(x_0\) and a derivative family \(Dg\) of the filling germ on a germ inside \(U\), with the germ in good position at \(Dg(0)\) in that chart Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm; as \(Dg(0)\) does not depend on the family, “for some family” and “for every family” agree Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.forall_isGoodPositionAtGerm; it is then an sc-Fredholm germ Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.isScFredholmGerm. The definition is in a chart, not in \(T_xX\); the transport of \(C_xX\) to \(T_xX\) (Definition 2.38) is not formalized.

III.22 Good position along a graph: Lemma 3.55

Lemma 3.55 (text, Appendix 3.8.3): for \(N\) in good position to \(C\) with good complement \(Y\), \(V \subseteq N \cap C\) relatively open and \(\tau : V \to Y_1\) of class \(C^1\) with \(\tau(0) = 0\), \(D\tau(0) = 0\), for \(v\) near \(0\): (1) \(v + \tau(v) \in C_1\); (2) \(Y\) is a topological complement of \(N_v = \{n + D\tau(v)n\}\); (3) for some \(\gamma_v > 0\), \(n \in C_x \iff n + y \in C_x\) for \(n \in N_v\), \(y \in Y\), \(|y|_0 \le \gamma_v|n|_0\), \(x = v + \tau(v)\). Formalized Chapter3/GoodPositionOpenlemma_3_55 in the model \(\mathbb R^n \oplus W\), with the core in coordinates for any \(C\) cut out by functionals Chapter3/GoodPositionOpenlemma_3_55_core: for \(N\) in good position with good complement \(Y\), \(Y\) closed, and \(\tau : N \to E\) with values in \(Y\), \(C^1\) on \(N \cap C\), \(\tau(0) = 0\), \(D\tau(0) = 0\): there is \(\rho > 0\) such that for \(v \in N \cap C\), \(|v| < \rho\), \(v + \tau(v) \in C\) and \(Y\) is a good complement of \(N_v\) (the subspace \(\{n + Ln\}\) for \(L = D\tau(v)\) Chapter3/GoodPositionOpengraphSpace) with respect to the partial quadrant \(C_{v + \tau(v)}\).

The added hypothesis. The step “\(D\tau(v)n \in Y\) for all \(n \in N\)” needs \(Y\) closed: the derivative within \(N \cap C\) at a point of unique differentiability of a map with values in a closed subspace takes values there, because the tangent cone of a subset of a closed subspace lies in it Chapter3/GoodPositionOpentangentConeAt_subset_of_subset_closed Chapter3/GoodPositionOpenfderivWithin_mem_of_mapsTo; for a non-closed algebraic complement it fails. The text’s \(Y = Y_0\) is a topological complement, hence closed. With \(Y\) closed, (2) is linear algebra: \(E_0 = N_v \oplus Y\) whenever \(E_0 = N \oplus Y\) and \(L\) takes values in \(Y\) Chapter3/GoodPositionOpengraphSpace_isCompl, and \(N_v\) is closed (finite-dimensional) Chapter3/GoodPositionOpengraphSpace_isClosed.

The estimate. (1) is Lemma 3.70’s smallness: \(|\tau(v)| \le \varepsilon|v|\) near \(0\) and good position. For (3), take \(\varepsilon_0 = \min(\varepsilon, 1)\) and the neighbourhood where \(\|D\tau(v)\| \le \varepsilon_0/4\); then \(\gamma = \varepsilon_0/4\) works for every \(v\), since \(\gamma(1 + \varepsilon_0/4) + \varepsilon_0/4 \le \varepsilon_0\) (the text: \(\gamma_v(1 + \varepsilon) + \varepsilon < \gamma\), with \(\gamma_v\) chosen after \(v\)). If \(v \in N \cap W\), \(C_x = C\) and the estimate transfers the good-complement property from \(N\) to \(N_v\). If \(v \notin N \cap W\), no normal form is needed: if \(\ell_i(v) = 0\) then \(i \in \Sigma\), so \(\ell_i\) vanishes on \(Y\) (Lemma 3.65), and \(\ell_i(v + \tau(v)) = 0\) iff \(\ell_i(v) = 0\) (Lemma 3.70); so \(\ell_i(h + y) = \ell_i(h)\) for every coordinate \(i\) that defines \(C_x\), and (3) holds for every \(\gamma\). The text’s cases \(\dim N = 1\), \(\dim N > 1\) are not needed, and the sc-level of the values of \(\tau\) plays no role. The formal \(\tau\) is given on all of \(N \cap C\) rather than on a neighbourhood \(V\); the conclusion is local.

III.23 Theorem 3.54: the linear part and the graph description of the solution set

Theorem 3.54 (text): for an sc-Fredholm section \(f\) of a tame strong bundle with \(f(x) = 0\) and \((f, x)\) in good position there is an open \(V \ni x\) such that \(S = \{y \in V : f(y) = 0\}\) satisfies (1) \((f, y)\) is in good position at every \(y \in S\), and (2) \(S\) is a sub-M-polyfold with the structure of a manifold with boundary with corners. The proof: the linear part (surjectivity and good position transported from \(T_xX\) to the chart and the push-forward); (3), the graph description of \(S\) from Corollary 3.47 for \(\Psi_*(g) = h + t\); then Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55 for (1), and Theorem 3.27 for (2). Formalized: the linear part and (3).

The linear part Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGtheorem_3_54_linear. In the chart, with the germ in good position and \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\) (the minimal subspace at the corner \(0\); Proposition 2.35 for the tame retraction \(r\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGtheorem_3_54_linear_of_isTameWith Chapter2/TameRetractsproposition_2_35): \(Dg(0)\) is onto (Proposition 3.5 for the filling germ, §III.4, from the surjectivity of \(Tf(0)\)), and \(\ker Dg(0)\) is in good position to \(C\) in \(E\); only the filler at \(0\) enters, and \(r\) is whole-chart, so \(Dr(0)\) is a genuine derivative. The latter is the transport lemma: for a bounded idempotent \(\pi\) with \((1 - \pi)E_0\) inside the minimal subspace at \(0\), good position inside \(\pi E_0\) gives good position in \(E_0\), with the good complement \(P \oplus (1 - \pi)E_0\) and the constant \(\varepsilon/(\|\pi\| + 1)\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsInGoodPositionIn.isInGoodPosition. Two points the text passes over: for \(p = z + k\) with \(|p| \le \varepsilon'|n|\) the \(T_0O\)-component is \(z = Dr(0)p\), so \(|z| \le \|Dr(0)\|\varepsilon'|n|\) — the splitting must be topological; and \(\ker Dr(0) \subseteq E_0\) is used only as “the \(\mathbb R^n\)-coordinates of \(k\) vanish, so \(n + z + k \in C \iff n + z \in C\)”. This inclusion is the only place where tameness enters.

\(C' = T\psi(0)C\). Not part of the data of a conjugation (§III.6); it is a theorem: for an sc-diffeomorphism \(\psi\) between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants with \(\psi(0) = 0\), \(x \in C \iff D\psi(0)x \in C'\), by the one-sided sign argument for \(\psi\) and \(\psi^{-1}\) (Part II, §II.12) Chapter2/BoundaryIsSc1With.mapsTo_partialQuadrant, since \(C_0 = C\) at the corner Chapter3/GoodPositionGermpartialQuadrantAtWith_zero Chapter3/GoodPositionGermscDeriv_mem_iff_of_inverse.

The text instead obtains the Fredholm property of \(D(h + t)(0)\) from Propositions 3.10 and 1.10.

The graph description Chapter3/GlobalIFTGtheorem_3_54_graph. Let the charts of the bundle have tame base retractions (htame, the hypothesis of the first formalization; it cannot be met, and it is replaced by good position in a tame chart, §III.47), \(f(x_0) = 0\), \((f, x_0)\) in good position. The proof, in the order of the Lean.

  1. The chart and the identities. Take the chart of Definition 3.53 centred at \(x_0\), filling germ \(g\) on \(G_g\), sc⁺-germ \(t_0\) on \(G_s\) and conjugation \(\Psi\) covering \(\psi\), with inverse \(\Psi'\) covering \(\psi'\). Shrink the basic germ to the germ \(G''\) of the points of \(G\) that \(\psi'\) sends into \(G_g \cap G_s\) level by level: same \(\Psi\), \(h\), \(B\) and conjugation identity Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.shrink (§III.48); below, \(G\) denotes \(G''\). There is an open \(N_1 \ni 0\) on which \(\mathbf f = g\) on \(O\), zeros of \(g\) in \(U\) lie in \(O\), and \(\Psi(u, (g - \iota t_0)(u))_2 = h(\psi(u))\) (filler (1), (2) and the conjugation).
  2. The sc⁺-germ \(t\). \(t(u') = \Psi[1](\psi'(u'), t_0(\psi'(u')))_2\) is an sc-smooth germ into \((Q \oplus W)^1\) on \(G\): \(t_0 \circ \psi'\) is a germ on the preimage of \(G_s\), which contains \(G = G''\), and the whole-chart \(\Psi[1]\) is composed on the outside (§III.48). (With \(t_0\) sc-smooth on \(U\), \(t\) was sc-smooth on all of \(U'\).) On \(U \cap N_1\), \(\Psi_*(g)(\psi(u)) = h(\psi(u)) + \iota t(\psi(u))\), by the linearity of the fibre maps.
  3. Absorbing the \(\mathbb R^N\)-component. The data of Theorem 3.38 carry only the \(W\)-component of an sc⁺-germ. Let \(t_Q\), \(t_W\) be the two components of \(t\), through the sc-operators \((q, w) \mapsto (q, 0)\) and \((q, w) \mapsto w\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTScBanach.qPartOp Chapter3/GlobalIFTScBanach.wPartOp. Then \(h' = h + (t_Q, 0)\) is again a basic germ with the same contraction \(B\) (Definition 3.7 constrains only the \(W\)-component), and with the data \(\mathcal S\) of Theorem 3.38 for \(s = t_W\) (they exist, §III.18) one has \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h' = h' + \iota t_W = h + \iota t\).
  4. The hypotheses of Corollary 3.47. Tameness gives \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\) (Proposition 2.35), so the push-forward step applies: \(D(\Psi_*g)(0)\) is surjective with kernel in good position. Since \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h' = \Psi_*(g)\) only on a neighbourhood \(W'\) of \(0\), the two derivatives at \(0\) are identified by the uniqueness of the derivative within \(G''_1\) and density of \(E_1\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTscDeriv_eq_of_eqOn_nhds; \(\Psi_*(g)\) is a germ on the preimage of \(G_g\), which contains \(G''\).
  5. Corollary 3.47 for \(h + t\) gives \(Y\), \(V_0\), \(\sigma\) (good complement, \(C^1\), level \(1\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), \(D\sigma(0) = 0\)), the graph consisting of zeros, and \(U''\) in which every zero lies on the graph.
  6. The neighbourhoods (the text does not say which \(V\)). Let \(\Omega = U'' \cap W'\) and \(V' = V_0 \cap (1 + \sigma)^{-1}(\Omega)\), relatively open in \(K \cap C'\) because \(v \mapsto v + \sigma(v)\) is continuous. Let \(V_x = \{y \in \mathrm{dom}\,\varphi : \varphi(y) \in N_1,\ \psi\varphi(y) \in \Omega \cap G_0\}\), open and containing \(x_0\) by continuity of \(\psi \circ \varphi\). \(D\sigma(0) = 0\) persists on the smaller \(V'\) (unique differentiability at \(0\) of \(V'\)).
  7. The conclusions. \(\psi \circ \varphi\) is injective on \(V_x\) (\(\varphi\) is, and \(\psi' \circ \psi = \mathrm{id}\) on \(U\)). For \(y \in V_x\): \(f(y) = 0 \iff \mathbf f(\varphi y) = 0 \iff g(\varphi y) = 0 \iff (h + \iota t)(\psi\varphi y) = 0\) (items 1–2). If \(f(y) = 0\), then \(\psi\varphi(y)\) is a zero in \(U'' \cap G_0\), hence \(v + \sigma(v)\) with \(v \in V_0\), and \(v \in V'\) since \(v + \sigma(v) \in \Omega\). Conversely, for \(v \in V'\), \(u = \psi'(v + \sigma(v))\) lies in \(U \cap N_1\), \(g(u) = 0\), so \(u \in O\) and \(u = \varphi(y)\) for some \(y\), which lies in \(V_x\) and is a zero.

So \(\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x : f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) : v \in V'\}\). When this section was written, (1) and (2) were not formalized; they are now: the kernel and good position at the nearby zeros in §§III.32–III.33 (the surjectivity of \(f'(y)\) under an added hypothesis), the data of Definition 3.25 at every zero in §§III.34–III.36, and the theorem in §III.37. The graph description also records, since then, that \(Y\) is closed, that the kernel is a smooth subspace and the level-wise lifts of \(\sigma\) (Corollary 3.47 (1)), and it is a corollary of the version with a good complement whose projection maps \(C'\) into itself (§III.29).

Theorems 3.56 and 3.57, the step from the tangent germ property. With \(S = \{f = 0\}\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTsolutionSet: if \(S \ne \emptyset\) has at every point regular data of Definition 3.25 (§III.24), then \(S\) is a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and an \(n\)-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners (Theorem 3.27) Chapter3/GlobalIFTtheorem_3_57_of_tangentGerm; if \(X\) has no boundary, the induced structure is without boundary, since \(d_S \le d_X = 0\) (Lemma 2.26) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldlemma_2_26 Chapter3/GlobalIFTtheorem_3_56_of_tangentGerm. The first step of the text’s proof — good position at every zero gives the tangent germ property — was not formalized when this section was written; the theorems with the text’s hypotheses are in §III.37.

III.24 The tangent germ property: Definition 3.25 and Theorem 3.27

Definition 3.25. The data at \(x \in M\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart: a chart \(\varphi : (U, x) \to (O, 0)\) onto a tame retract \((O, C, E)\); an \(n\)-dimensional smooth \(N \subseteq E\) in good position to \(C\) with a good complement \(Y\), \(Y\) closed; a relatively open \(V \ni 0\) in \(N \cap C\); \(\delta : V \to E\) continuous with values in \(Y\); (i) \(\varphi(M \cap U) = \{v + \delta(v) : v \in V\}\); (ii) \(\delta(0) = 0\), \(D\delta(0) = 0\) and \(\delta\) an sc^∞-germ, read as: for every \(m\), \(k\) a relatively open \(V_{m,k} \ni 0\) in \(N \cap C\) with \(\delta(V_{m,k}) \subseteq E_m\) and \(\delta : V_{m,k} \to E_m\) of class \(C^k\) Chapter3/TangentGermIsScInftyGermAt. This \(k\)-dependent reading is what the germ implicit function theorem delivers (§III.11); the reading “sc-smooth on one fixed germ” implies it by Proposition 1.18 for germs Chapter3/TangentGermIsScSmoothGerm.isScInftyGermAt, as does sc-smoothness on \(V\) as a set Chapter3/TangentGermIsScSmooth.isScInftyGermAt, so the theorem covers all three. \(M\) has the property if \(M \subseteq X_\infty\) and every point has such data Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.HasTangentGermProperty. With these data: \(N \cap C\) is a partial quadrant in \(N\) (Proposition 3.22) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.isPartialQuadrant, and \(N\), \(Y\) are topological complements — this is where \(Y\) closed is used — so the projection \(\pi : E \to N\) along \(Y\) is continuous Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.isTopCompl Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.π; with \(\Gamma(v) = v + \delta(v)\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.Γ, \(\pi\Gamma = \mathrm{id}\) and \(\varphi(y) = \Gamma(\pi\varphi(y))\) for \(y \in M \cap U\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_eq_Γ.

Proposition 3.26 Chapter3/TangentGermproposition_3_26. For an sc-diffeomorphism \(\psi : X \to X'\) (sc-smooth on all of \(X\) with sc-smooth inverse \(\psi'\) on all of \(X'\)) and \(\psi(M) = M'\), \(M'\) has the \(n\)-dimensional tangent germ property iff \(M\) has it. One direction suffices, applied to \(\psi\) and \(\psi'\) Chapter3/TangentGermproposition_3_26_image: \(\psi(M) \subseteq X'_\infty\) because sc-smooth maps preserve the levels, and the data at \(\psi(x)\) are the transported chart \(\varphi \circ \psi^{-1}\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndextransportChart, whose model is that of \(\varphi\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.transportChart_model_O, with the same \(N\), \(Y\), \(V\), \(\delta\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.transport: condition (i) is transported because \(\varphi\psi^{-1}(\psi(M) \cap \psi(U)) = \varphi(M \cap U)\). As in the text; tameness of \(X\) plays no role.

Two gaps in the text’s proof of Theorem 3.27, and the conditions that close them Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.IsRegular. (a) The text asserts that \(\delta\) is an sc^∞-germ near every \(v_0 \in V\), by linearizing at \(v_0\) and claiming that a certain map \(N' \to N\) is an isomorphism. That needs \(\delta\) differentiable at \(v_0\), known only near \(0\), and fails: in \(X = \mathbb R^2\) take \(M\) the graph of \(g\) with \(g(s) = s^2\) near \(0\) and \(g(s) = 4 + (s - 2)^{1/3}\) near \(2\), a smooth embedded curve with a vertical tangent at \((2, 4)\); with \(\varphi = \mathrm{id}\), \(N\) the horizontal axis, \(Y\) the vertical one and \(\delta = g\), the data at \(0\) satisfy Definition 3.25, \(M\) has the tangent germ property (at \((2, 4)\) use a rotated chart), but \(\delta\) is not differentiable at \(2\) and the chart \(\pi\varphi\) on all of \(M \cap U\) is not smoothly compatible with the chart at \((2, 4)\). So condition (a): \(\delta\) is sc-smooth on \(V\) as a map on a set. (b) The text’s \(\Sigma = \{v + y \in C : v \in V, y \in Y\}\) is claimed relatively open in \(C\), so that \(t(v + w) = v + \delta(v)\) is defined near \(0\) in \(O\). False: \(E = \mathbb R^3\), \(C = [0, \infty)^3\), \(N = \mathbb R(1, 1, 1)\), \(Y = \{x + y - z = 0\}\) is a good complement, and \(\pi(x, y, z) = (x + y - z)(1, 1, 1)\), so \(\pi z \in C\) iff \(x + y \ge z\); \(\Sigma\) is not open at \((1, 0, 1)\) and points \((\varepsilon, 0, \varepsilon + \varepsilon^2) \notin \Sigma\) approach \(0\). So condition (b): \(\pi(O) \subseteq C\); then \(\Sigma \cap O = \{z \in O : \pi z \in V\}\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.Sig is relatively open in \(O\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.Sig_eq. (A good complement with \(\pi'(C) \subseteq N \cap C\) always exists, via the normal form, but then \(M \cap U\) must be rewritten as a graph along it with the quadrant inverse function theorem, and the regularity problem of (a) returns; this is not done.)

The charts \(\pi \circ \varphi\). On \(M \cap U_0\), \(y \mapsto \pi\varphi(y)\) is a chart with model \((V, N \cap C, N)\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.model, a tame retract (the identity retraction) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.model_isTameRetract, with inverse \(v \mapsto \varphi^{-1}(v + \delta(v))\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.chartInv Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.chart, a finite-dimensional corner chart of dimension \(n\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.chart_isCorner containing \(x\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.mem_chart_source.
