III.25 Lemmas 3.59–3.61: towards the basic germ criterion

Lemmas 3.59 and 3.60, abstract form. In the proof of Theorem 3.58 the family \(L(b) = P_Y \circ Df(b)|_X : X \to Y\) is shown to be injective for \(b\) near \(0\) (Lemma 3.59) and to satisfy uniform lower bounds \(|L(b)h|_m \ge c_m|h|_m\) (Lemma 3.60) — the hypotheses of Lemma 3.61. Both are sequence arguments, and all they use of the compactness condition (2) of Theorem 3.58 is a property of the family itself: if \(b_j \to b\), \((h_j)\) is bounded in \(X_m\) and \(L(b_j)h_j \to 0\) in \(Y_m\), then \((h_j)\) has a convergent subsequence in \(X_m\) Chapter3/BasicGermCriterionFamilyCompactness. (For \(L = P_Y \circ Df|_X\) it follows from (2), since \(Df(b_j)h_j - L(b_j)h_j = (1 - P_Y)Df(b_j)h_j\) lies in the finite-dimensional smooth complement \(A\) and is bounded on every level.) The two lemmas are formalized for an abstract family of sc-operators with jointly continuous level maps. Lemma 3.59: if \(L(0)\) is injective, so is \(L(b)\) for \(b\) near \(0\) — otherwise \(b_j \to 0\) and unit vectors \(h_j\) with \(L(b_j)h_j = 0\) give, by the compactness property, a limit \(h\) with \(|h| = 1\) and \(L(0)h = 0\) Chapter3/BasicGermCriterionlemma_3_59. Lemma 3.60: on a compact parameter set \(K\) on which every \(L(b)_m\) is injective there is \(c_m > 0\) with \(c_m|h|_m \le |L(b)h|_m\) — otherwise \(b_j \in K\) and unit \(h_j\) with \(|L(b_j)h_j|_m \to 0\) give, after subsequences, \(b_j \to b \in K\), \(h_j \to h\), \(|h|_m = 1\), \(L(b)h = 0\) Chapter3/BasicGermCriterionlemma_3_60. The text’s step “\(P_Y \circ Df(b)|_X\) is an injective sc-Fredholm operator of index \(0\), hence an sc-isomorphism” is needed only to feed Lemma 3.61. The setting of Theorem 3.58 (the splitting as coordinates, the complement \(A\), the index computation), the strong bundle map \(\Phi((b, x), (c, y)) = ((b, x), (c, L(b)^{-1}y))\) and the contraction estimate from condition (3) were not formalized when this section was written; they are now, in the coordinates of the text’s proof, and there the hypotheses of the two lemmas are derived from those of the theorem (§III.38).

Lemma 3.61 (quoted by the text from [25, Proposition 4.8] without proof). Let \(V\) be a germ of relatively open neighbourhoods of \(0\) in a partial quadrant \(\widetilde C\) of a finite-dimensional \(G\), \(V \oplus E\) the product germ with levels \(V_m \times E_m\) Chapter3/InverseFamilyScNbhdGerm.prodFull, and \(L(v) : E \to F\) sc-isomorphisms such that \(\Phi(v, h) = L(v)h\) Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamMap is an sc-smooth germ on \(V \oplus E\) and \(c_m|h|_m \le |L(v)h|_m\) for \(v \in V_0\). Then \(\Lambda(v, k) = L(v)^{-1}k\) Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv is an sc-smooth germ on \(V \oplus F\) Chapter3/InverseFamilylemma_3_61. Operator-norm continuity of \(v \mapsto L(v)\) is not assumed.

sc⁰. On level \(m\), with \(h_0 = L(v_0)^{-1}k_0\), \(|L(v)^{-1}k - L(v_0)^{-1}k_0|_m \le c_m^{-1}(|k - k_0|_m + |(L(v_0) - L(v))h_0|_m)\), and \(v \mapsto L(v)h_0\) is continuous Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv_isSc0Germ.

Differentiability Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv_hasFDerivWithinAt. The candidate is \(D\Lambda(v, k)(\delta v, \delta k) = L(v)^{-1}(\delta k - D_1\Phi(v, L(v)^{-1}k)\delta v)\) Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInvDeriv. With \(h = \Lambda(v, k)\) and \(w = D\Lambda(v, k)(\delta v, \delta k)\), \(\Lambda(v', k') - \Lambda(v, k) - w = L(v')^{-1}[(L(v) - L(v'))w] - L(v')^{-1}r\), where \(r = \Phi(v', h) - \Phi(v, h) - D_1\Phi(v, h)\delta v = o(|\delta v|)\) is the remainder of \(\Phi\) along \((\delta v, 0)\) with \(h\) fixed, so that only the finite-dimensional variable moves. The term \((L(v) - L(v'))w\) is \(o(|(\delta v, \delta k)|_1)\) because the increment is measured on level \(1\): \(w/|(\delta v, \delta k)|_1\) lies in the compact set \(D\Lambda(v, k)(\iota(B_1))\) (\(\iota : F_1 \to F_0\) compact), and \((L(v) - L(v'))u \to 0\) uniformly for \(u\) in a compact set — a tube lemma for jointly continuous maps vanishing on \(\{x_0\} \times K\) Chapter3/InverseFamilyexists_forall_norm_le_of_isCompact. Strong continuity plus the compactness of \(F_1 \to F_0\) replace the operator-norm continuity; the differentiability of \(\Lambda\) as a map \((V \oplus F)_0 \to E_0\) would need the latter and is not claimed.

The tangent map and the induction. \(T\Lambda((v, k), (\delta v, \delta k)) = (\Lambda(v, k), \Lambda(v, \delta k - (T\Phi((v, \Lambda(v, k)), (\delta v, 0)))_2))\), a composition of \(\Lambda\), \(T\Phi\) and sc-operators (the projections Chapter3/InverseFamilytangentBaseOp Chapter3/InverseFamilytangentInlOp Chapter3/InverseFamilytangentFiberOp and subtraction Chapter3/InverseFamilyScBanach.subOp); it is sc⁰ Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv_tangent_isSc0, so \(\Lambda\) is sc¹ Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv_isSc1GermWith; and if \(\Phi\) is sc^{k+1}, then \(\Lambda\) (sc^k by induction) and \(T\Phi\) (sc^k) make \(T\Lambda\) sc^k, so \(\Lambda\) is sc^{k+1} Chapter3/InverseFamilyfamInv_isSckGerm. The sc¹ step uses no quadrant hypothesis; the induction uses the composition rules for germs.

III.26 What the formalization taught us

  1. The germ implicit function theorem holds with the text’s hypotheses, but on shrinking germs: the solution germ is sc^k on the germ shifted by \(2^k - 1\) levels. In the text’s reading of germs (up to shrinking) this is the theorem; read with fixed germs, “if \(f\) is sc-smooth so is its solution germ” holds for every \(k\) on a germ depending on \(k\). Every later “sc-smooth germ” (Definition 3.25 (ii), Theorem 3.43 (1), Corollary 3.47 (1)) must be read the same way. Whether the shrinking is intrinsic is open.
  2. Theorem 3.30 has a short proof, which the text cites from [21]: an approximate fixed point and the \(\tfrac12\)-contraction on level \(0\), at parameters where the level-\(1\) operators exist.
  3. The contraction regions must be explicit for “from the uniqueness we conclude \(\delta^{(1)} = T\delta\)” (Lemma 3.31) to be true.
  4. Several “immediate consequences” are proofs of their own: the compactness of Theorem 3.12 (not in Theorem 3.40), the induction of Theorem 3.40 (lifts, bounds and continuity together), the sc-smoothness and regularizing property in Theorem 3.15, the sc⁺ property in Proposition 3.10, the projection of solutions into the quadrant in Theorem 3.43.
  5. Three added hypotheses: \(Y\) closed in Lemma 3.55 and Definition 3.25; and the two regularity conditions of Theorem 3.27, each with a counterexample to the step of the text’s proof it replaces.
  6. Tameness is nearly unused: not in §3.1 at all, and in §3.6 only through \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\) and, for the tangent germ property of the solution set, the tameness of the model of the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) (§III.27).
  7. Linear coordinate changes in Theorem 3.38 make the text’s degeneracy-index argument for Corollary 3.47 unnecessary.
  8. The extreme-ray lemmas and the iterated tangent maps are not needed: Proposition 3.22 by a segment argument, the regularity in Theorems 3.72 and 3.78 by bootstrapping, without shrinking.
  9. What remained of Theorem 3.54 when this list was written — the re-centring of good position at the nearby zeros, and the level-wise regularity of the solution map in the data of Definition 3.25 at every zero — is done in §§III.31–III.37, with one added hypothesis for Theorem 3.54 (1); see §III.39.

III.27 Tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms, and by open subsets

The text never states that tameness is invariant under sc-diffeomorphisms, or that an open piece of a tame retract is a tame retract, but it uses both. In the proof of Theorem 3.54 the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) onto \(\psi(O)\) must be a chart of the tame M-polyfold \(X\) for Definition 3.25 to apply; in the proof of Proposition 3.26 it writes “\(X' = \psi(X)\) is tame”; and wherever a chart is restricted to a smaller domain (the shrinking of the data of Definition 3.25 in §§III.36–III.37) the model of the restricted chart must again be a tame retract. Both facts are proved here, with Definition 2.34 as the formalization states it (Part II).

The objects. An sc-diffeomorphism between relatively open subsets \(U \subseteq C\), \(U' \subseteq C'\) of partial quadrants is a pair \(\psi : U \to U'\), \(\psi' : U' \to U\) of sc-smooth maps, each mapping its domain into the other’s, inverse to each other on \(U\) and on \(U'\) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant (its inverse is again one Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.symm). A retraction \(r : U \to U\) is tame for a presentation \(T\) of \(C\) if (1) \(d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)\) for \(x \in U\) and (2) at every smooth point \(x\) of \(O = r(U)\) on level \(1\) the tangent space \(T_xO = Dr(x)E\) has an sc-complement \(A\) contained in the minimal subspace \(E_x\) Chapter2/TameScRetraction.IsTameWith; it is tame if it is tame for every presentation Chapter2/TameScRetraction.IsTame, and \((O, C, E)\) is a tame retract if \(O\) is the image of a tame retraction Chapter2/TameIsTameRetract.

The transported retraction. For an sc-smooth retraction \(r\) with domain \(U\), put \(r' = \psi \circ r \circ \psi' : U' \to U'\) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.transport. It maps \(U'\) into \(U'\) because \(\psi'(U') \subseteq U\), \(r(U) \subseteq U\) and \(\psi(U) \subseteq U'\); it is sc-smooth by the chain rule applied twice; and it is idempotent, \(r'(r'(u')) = \psi(r(\psi'\psi(r(\psi'u')))) = \psi(r(r(\psi' u'))) = r'(u')\), since \(\psi'\psi = \mathrm{id}\) on \(U\) and \(r\) is idempotent. Its image is \(\psi(O)\) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.transport_retract: \(r'(u') = \psi(r(\psi'u'))\) with \(r(\psi'u') \in O\); conversely, for \(z \in O\), \(r'(\psi z) = \psi(r(z)) = \psi(z)\).

Condition (1). The degeneracy index is preserved by \(\psi\), \(d_{C'}(\psi(u)) = d_C(u)\) for \(u \in U\): this is Theorem 1.25 Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.degIndex_eq Chapter2/DegeneracyIndextheorem_1_25. Then for \(u' \in U'\): \(d_{C'}(r'(u')) = d_C(r(\psi'u')) = d_C(\psi'u') = d_{C'}(\psi\psi'u') = d_{C'}(u')\), the middle step being condition (1) for \(r\).

The derivative of \(r'\). On level \(0\), \(D\psi'(\psi(x)) \circ D\psi(x) = 1\) for \(x \in U_1\) and \(D\psi(\psi'(y)) \circ D\psi'(y) = 1\) for \(y \in U'_1\), by the chain rule for \(\psi' \circ \psi = \mathrm{id}\) and \(\psi \circ \psi' = \mathrm{id}\) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.deriv_inv_deriv Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.deriv_deriv_inv Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexscDeriv_comp_eq_self. If \(y \in U'_1\) and \(\psi'(y) \in O\), then with \(x = \psi'_1(y)\), \[Dr'(y) = D\psi(x) \circ Dr(x) \circ D\psi'(y)\] Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.scDeriv_transport. The chain rule is applied to \(\psi \circ (r \circ \psi')\) and then to \(r \circ \psi'\) Chapter2/TameFacesscDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain; the outer derivative of \(\psi\) is taken at the level-\(1\) point of \(r \circ \psi'\) over \(y\), and this point is \(x\) because \(r\) fixes \(\psi'(y) \in O\). Without \(\psi'(y) \in O\) the formula would involve \(Dr\) at \(\psi'(y)\) and \(D\psi\) at the different point \(r(\psi'(y))\).

Sc-isomorphisms carry sc-splittings. Let \(D : E \to E'\) be an sc-operator with an sc-operator inverse \(D'\). Its level maps are topological linear isomorphisms \(E_m \cong E'_m\) Chapter2/TameInvariancescIsoLevel (inverse to each other by the injectivity of the inclusions into level \(0\)); they carry \(A_m = A \cap E_m\) onto \((DA)_m\) Chapter2/TameInvariancelevelSub_map_eq and smooth points to smooth points Chapter2/TameInvariancemem_smoothLvl_of_isScOperator. Hence an sc-subspace \(A\) (closed, with the smooth points of \(A_m\) dense in \(A_m\) for every \(m\)) is carried to the sc-subspace \(DA\): \(DA = (D')^{-1}(A)\) is closed, and the image of the closure of the smooth points of \(A_m\) lies in the closure of the image Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScSubspace.map. An sc-splitting \(E = F \oplus A\) (sc-subspaces, complementary on every level) is carried to the sc-splitting \(E' = DF \oplus DA\), since an isomorphism of each level carries complements to complements Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScSplitting.map.

Condition (2) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.isTameWith_transport. Let \(T\), \(T'\) be presentations of \(C\), \(C'\), \(r\) tame for \(T\), and \(y\) a smooth point of \(\psi(O)\) on level \(1\). Then \(x = \psi'_1(y)\) lies on level \(1\) of \(O\) (if \(y = \psi(z)\) with \(z \in O\), then \(\psi'(y) = z\)) and is smooth, because sc-smooth maps carry smooth points to smooth points. Tameness of \(r\) at \(x\) gives an sc-splitting \(E = T_xO \oplus A\) with \(A \subseteq E_x\). Because \(x\) and \(y\) are smooth points, \(D\psi(x)\) and \(D\psi'(y)\) are sc-operators (the remark after Proposition 1.16) Chapter1/PropertiesIsSc1With.scOperator_deriv — at a point that is only on level \(1\) they need not be — and they are inverse to each other. From the formula for \(Dr'(y)\) and \(D\psi'(y)D\psi(x) = 1\): \(T_y\psi(O) = \mathrm{range}\,Dr'(y) = D\psi(x)(\mathrm{range}\,Dr(x)) = D\psi(x)(T_xO)\). So \(E' = T_y\psi(O) \oplus D\psi(x)A\) is an sc-splitting. Finally \(D\psi(x)A \subseteq E'_y\): the derivative of an sc¹-map between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants maps the minimal subspace \(E_x\) into \(E'_{\psi(x)}\) (the one-sided sign argument, and density) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexIsSc1With.mapsTo_minimalSubspace, which needs \(\psi(U) \subseteq C'\), and \(\psi(x) = y\). Since \(T'\) was arbitrary and the presentation \(T\) of \(C\) is available, the transported retraction of a tame retraction is tame Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.isTame_transport, and the image \((\psi(O), C', E')\) of a tame retract under an sc-diffeomorphism is a tame retract, with retraction \(\psi \circ r \circ \psi^{-1}\) Chapter2/TameInvarianceIsScDiffeoQuadrant.isTameRetract_image.

Open subsets. For an open \(W \subseteq E_0\), the restriction of \(r\) to \(U \cap r^{-1}(W)\) is an sc-smooth retraction onto \(O \cap W\) (Proposition 2.10 (1)) Chapter2/RetractsScRetraction.restrict. It is tame if \(r\) is Chapter3/SolutionGermRecentreScRetraction.restrict_isTame: condition (1) is inherited pointwise; for (2), at a smooth point \(x\) of \(O \cap W\) on level \(1\) the derivative of the restricted retraction is \(Dr(x)\), because the two maps agree on the smaller relatively open domain, which contains \(x\) since \(r(x) = x \in W\), and the derivative at a level-\(1\) point depends only on the map near the point Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_eq_of_eqOn_relOpen; so the complement \(A\) of \(r\) at \(x\) serves. Hence \(O \cap W\) is a tame retract whenever \(O\) is Chapter3/SolutionGermRecentreIsTameRetract.inter_isOpen. For a chart \(\varphi\) and an open \(s\) inside its source, \(\varphi(s) = O \cap W\) for an open \(W\) Chapter2/MPolyfoldMChart.exists_isOpen_image_eq, so the model of the restricted chart is a tame retract when that of \(\varphi\) is Chapter3/SolutionGermRecentreMChart.isTameRetract_image.

These are used in §III.34 (the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) of Theorem 3.54 has the tame model \(\psi(O)\)) and in §§III.36–III.37 (the shrunk data of Definition 3.25 keep tame models). The text’s sentence “\(X' = \psi(X)\) is tame” in Proposition 3.26 is not needed there (§III.24): the tameness Definition 3.25 asks for is that of the chart models, which the transport of charts leaves unchanged.

III.28 Corollary 3.39: composition with a given conjugation

Corollary 3.39 (text): if the sc-germ \(g\) is equivalent, by a strong bundle isomorphism \(\Phi\), to a basic germ and \(s\) is an sc⁺-germ, there is a strong bundle map \(\Psi\) such that \(((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(g + s))^1\) is a basic germ. The text’s proof: \(\Phi_*(g) = h\) is basic, \(t = \Phi_*(s)\) is an sc⁺-germ with \(t(0) = 0\), \(\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t\), and Theorem 3.38 gives \(\Psi\) with \((\Psi_*(h + t))^1\) basic; take \(\Psi \circ \Phi\). Four things are silent: that Theorem 3.38’s coordinate change is a strong bundle isomorphism; that the index raise of a strong bundle isomorphism is one between the shifted structures; that strong bundle isomorphisms and push-forwards compose; and that \(\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t\) holds only where the conjugation identity holds. The formalization proves all four and states the corollary with the composite explicit.

Linear strong bundle isomorphisms. Two sc-operators \(S : E \to E'\), \(T : F \to F'\) give the sc-operator \(S \oplus T\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionScOperator.prodMap, and if \(S(U) \subseteq U'\) the map \((u, k) \mapsto (Su, Tk)\) is a strong bundle map \(U \triangleleft F \to U' \triangleleft F'\) (Definition 2.47 as formalized Chapter2/TameIsStrongBundleMap): its base component does not depend on \(k\), it is linear in \(k\), it preserves the double filtration because sc-operators preserve the levels, it is the sc-operator \(S \oplus T\) on \((U \triangleleft F)[0]\), and on \((U \triangleleft F)[1]\) it is \(S \oplus T^1\) with \(T^1\) the shifted operator Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionScOperator.isStrongBundleMap_prodMap. With inverse sc-operators \(S'\) (inverse to \(S\) on \(U\), \(U'\)) and \(T'\) it is a strong bundle isomorphism Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionScOperator.isStrongBundleIso_prodMap.

Theorem 3.38’s coordinate change as an isomorphism. In §III.18 the change of coordinates of Theorem 3.38 is the pair of linear sc-isomorphisms $= $ split, $= $ fiber (inverses glue, fiberInv) on the index-raised spaces Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.split Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fiber. Put \(\Lambda((a, w), (q, w')) = (\psi(a, w), \Psi(q, w'))\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.linIso. For every \(U\) relatively open in the shifted quadrant \((\widetilde C \oplus W)^1\), \(\psi(U) = \mathrm{glue}^{-1}(U)\) is relatively open in \((\widetilde C \oplus C) \oplus X^1\) (glue is continuous and preserves the quadrant coordinates) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.isRelOpen_glue_preimage, and \(\Lambda : U \triangleleft (\mathbb R^N \oplus W)^1 \to \psi(U) \triangleleft ((\mathbb R^N \oplus Z) \oplus X^1)\) is a strong bundle isomorphism by the preceding paragraph Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.linIso_isStrongBundleIso. Before the index raise, the same construction with the level-\(0\) operators split₀, fiber₀ gives \(\Lambda_0\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.linIso₀, a strong bundle isomorphism \(U \triangleleft (\mathbb R^N \oplus W) \to \psi(U) \triangleleft ((\mathbb R^N \oplus Z) \oplus X)\) — the text’s “strong bundle map covering \(\psi\)” Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.linIso₀_isStrongBundleIso — and its index raise is \(\Lambda\), because split and fiber are split₀ and fiber₀ on the levels \(m + 1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionStabilityData.strongShift_linIso₀.

The index raise. For \(\Psi : E_0 \times F_0 \to E'_0 \times F'_0\) let \(\Psi^1\) be its level-\(1\) map on \(E_1 \times F_1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionstrongShift. For a strong bundle map it exists on \(U_1 \oplus F_1\) and satisfies \(\iota\Psi^1(p) = \Psi(\iota p)\), because \(\Psi\) maps \(U_1 \oplus F_1\) into \(U'_1 \oplus F'_1\) (the filtration with \(k = 1 \le m + 1\)) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.toBase_strongShift; its base map is the level-\(1\) map of the base map of \(\Psi\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.toBase_base_strongShift. \(\Psi^1\) is a strong bundle map \(U^1 \triangleleft F^1 \to U'^1 \triangleleft F'^1\) of the shifted structures Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.shift: independence of the base component and fibre linearity are read through the injective inclusions; the double filtration \((U^1 \triangleleft F^1)_{m,k} = U_{m+1} \oplus F_{k+1}\) is preserved because \(k + 1 \le (m + 1) + 1\) whenever \(k \le m + 1\), so the filtration property of \(\Psi\) applies; \((U^1 \triangleleft F^1)[0]\) is the shift of \((U \triangleleft F)[0]\), so \(\Psi^1\) is sc-smooth there by Proposition 1.17 Chapter1/LevelsIsScSmooth.shift; and \((U^1 \triangleleft F^1)[1]\), with levels \(E_{m+1} \oplus F_{m+2}\), is the shift of \((U \triangleleft F)[1]\), on which \((\Psi^1)[1]\) agrees with \((\Psi[1])^1\) (the lift of the fibre component to \(F'_2\) is the same element, by the injectivity of \(F'_2 \to F'_1 \to F'_0\)), so Proposition 1.17 applies again. For a strong bundle isomorphism with inverse \(\Psi'\), \(\Psi'^1\) is the inverse of \(\Psi^1\), again checked after the inclusion into level \(0\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleIso.shift. The text uses this whenever it writes \(((\Psi \circ \Phi)_*(\cdot))^1\).

Composition. The base map of \(\Lambda \circ \Phi\) is the composite of the base maps on \(U\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.base_comp, and \((\Lambda \circ \Phi)[1] = \Lambda[1] \circ \Phi[1]\) on \(U \oplus F_1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.shiftFiber_comp; so the composite is a strong bundle map — fibre linearity because over \(u\) it is the fibre map of \(\Lambda\) over \(\varphi(u)\) after that of \(\Phi\) over \(u\), sc-smoothness on \([0]\) and \([1]\) by the chain rule Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.comp — and the composite of strong bundle isomorphisms is one, with the inverses composed in the opposite order Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleIso.comp. Push-forwards compose: \((\Lambda \circ \Phi)_*g = \Lambda_*(\Phi_*g)\) on the target of \(\Lambda\), since the base of \((\Lambda \circ \Phi)^{-1}\) is \(\varphi^{-1} \circ \lambda^{-1}\) and \(\Phi(\varphi^{-1}(w), \cdot)\) lies over \(w\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleIso.pushforward_comp Chapter3/GermPushforwardpushforward. The index raise commutes with composition, \((\Lambda \circ \Phi)^1 = \Lambda^1 \circ \Phi^1\) on \(U_1 \oplus F_1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.strongShift_comp.

Corollary 3.39 as formalized Chapter3/BasicClassCompositioncorollary_3_39. Let \(U\) be relatively open in a partial quadrant \(C\) of \(E\) with \(0 \in U\), \(g : U \to F\) sc-smooth (the text’s “sc-germ”; sc-smoothness is what makes \((g + s)^1\) take values on level \(1\)), \(d\) conjugation data of \(g\) (§III.30: a strong bundle isomorphism \(\Phi : U \triangleleft F \to U' \triangleleft (\mathbb R^N \oplus W)\) covering \(\varphi\) with \(\varphi(0) = 0\) and a basic germ \(h\) on a germ \(G\) inside \(U'\), with \((\Phi(u, g(u)))_2 = h(\varphi(u))\) for \(u \in U\) near \(0\); the text’s “equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism to the basic germ \(\Phi_*g\)”), and \(s : U \to F^1\) sc-smooth into \(F^1\) with \(s(0) = 0\) (the text’s sc⁺-germ \(s : O(C, 0) \to (F, 0)\)). The proof, in the order of the Lean:

  1. The sc⁺-germ \(t = \Phi[1]_*s\). Put \(t(u') = (\Phi[1](\varphi^{-1}u', s(\varphi^{-1}u')))_2\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.pushPlus. It is sc-smooth from \(U'\) into \((\mathbb R^N \oplus W)^1\): the pairing of \(\varphi^{-1}\) with \(s \circ \varphi^{-1}\) maps \(U'\) into \(U \oplus F^1\), and \(\Phi[1]\) is sc-smooth there by Definition 2.47; restricted to the germ \(G \subseteq U'\) it is an sc-smooth germ. And \(t(0) = 0\), from \(\varphi^{-1}(0) = 0\), \(s(0) = 0\) and \(\Phi(0, 0)_2 = 0\) (fibre linearity).
  2. Absorbing the \(\mathbb R^N\)-component. As in Theorem 3.54 (§III.23, step 3), \(h' = h + (t_{\mathbb R^N}, 0)\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.absorb Chapter3/GlobalIFTScBanach.qPartOp is a basic germ with the same contraction map: it is an sc-smooth germ (pairing and the sum operator), \(h'(0) = h(0) + 0 = 0\), and its \(W\)-component is that of \(h\). The \(W\)-component \(t_W\) is an sc-smooth germ into \(W^1\) vanishing at \(0\), so the data \(\mathcal S\) of Theorem 3.38 exist for \(s = t_W\) on the germ \(G\) of \(h\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.exists_of_scPlus, and \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h' = h + \iota t\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.fsum.
  3. \(\Phi_*(g + s) = h + t\) near \(0\). For \(u \in U\) at which the conjugation identity holds, \(\Phi_*(g + \iota s)(\varphi(u)) = (\Phi(u, g(u) + \iota s(u)))_2\) because \(\varphi^{-1}\varphi(u) = u\); by fibre linearity this is \((\Phi(u, g(u)))_2 + (\Phi(u, \iota s(u)))_2 = h(\varphi(u)) + \iota t(\varphi(u))\), where \(\iota(\Phi[1](u, s(u)))_2 = (\Phi(u, \iota s(u)))_2\) Chapter3/SectionCompactnessIsStrongBundleMap.toBase_shiftFiber_snd. So \(\Phi_*(g + s) = \mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h'\) at the points \(\varphi(u)\), \(u \in U\) near \(0\) — not everywhere, as the text’s “clearly” suggests.
  4. The composite. \(\Gamma = \Lambda \circ \Phi^1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.compIso, with inverse \(\Phi'^1 \circ \Lambda^{-1}\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.compIsoInv, is a strong bundle isomorphism \(U^1 \triangleleft F^1 \to \psi(U'^1) \triangleleft ((\mathbb R^N \oplus Z) \oplus X^1)\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.compDomain: the index raise of \(\Phi\) (relatively open \(U'_1\) in the shifted quadrant) followed by \(\Lambda\), composed by the composition lemma. Its base map is \(u \mapsto \psi(\varphi_1(u))\), which vanishes at \(0\); \(\Gamma_* = \Lambda_* \circ \Phi^1_*\) (composition of push-forwards); and the germ of \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{pushMap}\,h'\) lies in the target, because glue maps the level-\(1\) part of \(G\) into \(U'_1\).
  5. The basic germ. \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{pushMap}\,h' = \mathrm{fiber} \circ (\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h')^1 \circ \mathrm{glue}\) Chapter3/BasicClassStabilityData.pushMap is a basic germ by Theorem 3.38 (§III.18) Chapter3/BasicClasstheorem_3_38.
  6. The conjugation identity on level \(1\). For \(u \in U^1\) near \(0\): \((\Gamma(u, (g + s)^1(u)))_2 = \mathcal S.\mathrm{pushMap}\,h'(\gamma(u))\). Since \(\gamma(u) = \mathrm{split}(\varphi_1(u))\) and \(\mathrm{glue} \circ \mathrm{split} = \mathrm{id}\), both sides are fiber applied to elements of \((\mathbb R^N \oplus W)_1\), which are compared after the injective inclusion into level \(0\): \(\iota(\Phi^1(u, (g + s)^1(u)))_2 = (\Phi(\iota u, (g + s)(\iota u)))_2\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionIsStrongBundleMap.toBase_strongShift_snd, which is \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h'(\varphi(\iota u))\) by step 3, and this is \(\iota\) of \((\mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h')^1(\varphi_1(u))\). “Near \(0\)” means: \(\iota u\) lies in the neighbourhood where the conjugation identity holds (continuity of \(\iota : E_1 \to E_0\)), and \(\varphi_1(u)\) lies in the level-\(1\) part of the germ \(G\), a relatively open condition at \(0\) by the continuity of \(\varphi\) on level \(1\).

The conclusion of corollary_3_39 collects these: \(\mathcal S\) with \(\mathcal S.G = G\) and \(\mathcal S.s = t_W\), \(t(0) = 0\), \(h'\) basic, \(\Phi_*(g + s) = \mathcal S.\mathrm{fsum}\,h'\) near \(0\), \(\Gamma\) a strong bundle isomorphism onto a relatively open subset of \((\widetilde C \oplus C) \oplus X^1\) with \(\gamma(0) = 0\) and \(\Gamma_* = \Lambda_* \circ \Phi^1_*\), the basic germ \(\mathcal S.\mathrm{pushMap}\,h'\) inside the target, and the identity of step 6. In the form of Definition 3.11: \((g + s)^1 : U^1 \to F^1\) is conjugated to a basic germ on the shifted structures \(E^1\), \(F^1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositioncorollary_3_39_isConjugate, with parameter space \(\mathbb R^n \oplus C\), target \(\mathbb R^N \oplus Z\) and fibre \(X^1\) (the text’s \(\tau : Z \to C\) is not applied, as in §III.18). The text’s form “\(\Gamma = \Psi \circ \Phi\), then raise the index” is the same map: \(\Lambda_0 \circ \Phi\) is a strong bundle isomorphism on level \(0\) and \((\Lambda_0 \circ \Phi)^1 = \Lambda_0^1 \circ \Phi^1 = \Lambda \circ \Phi^1\) on \(U_1 \oplus F_1\) Chapter3/BasicClassCompositionConjugationData.compIso_eq_strongShift. No hypothesis is added beyond the two readings (“sc-germ” as sc-smooth on \(U\); “equivalent by a strong bundle isomorphism” as conjugation data). The first reading is the whole-chart one of §III.6, narrower than the text’s germs; no theorem of the germ reading uses Corollary 3.39 (the facts at the nearby zeros come from the chart at \(x_0\) through the linear coordinate change of Theorem 3.38, §III.43).

III.29 Good complements with a projection into the quadrant; Theorems 3.43, 3.47 and 3.54 (3) with a closed projecting complement

Two steps of the text depend on the choice of a good complement without saying so. In the proof of Theorem 3.27 the retraction \(t(v + w) = v + \delta(v)\) is defined on \(\Sigma = \{v + y \in C : v \in V,\ y \in Y\}\), which the text calls relatively open in \(C\); §III.24 shows that this fails for the good complement \(Y = \{x + y - z = 0\}\) of \(N = \mathbb R(1, 1, 1)\) in \(C = [0, \infty)^3\), and makes the remedy a hypothesis: condition (b) of the regularity conditions, \(\pi(O) \subseteq C\) for the projection \(\pi\) onto \(N\) along \(Y\) Chapter3/TangentGermMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.IsRegular. In the proof of Theorem 3.43 (Lemma 3.46) a good complement \(Z\) of \(\widetilde K = \ker DH(0)\) is produced by projecting a good complement of \(K'\). This section shows that for solution sets the complement can be chosen once and for all, at the bottom of the chain Theorem 3.78 → Theorem 3.43 → Corollary 3.47 → Theorem 3.54 (3), so that its projection maps the partial quadrant into itself; condition (b) then holds for the chart of §III.34 without any hypothesis (Findings, Chapter 3, items 130–133). Along the way the closedness of the complement, which Lemma 3.55 and Definition 3.25 need (items 49, 81), is recorded in the statements (item 93).

The projection property. For subspaces \(N\), \(Y\) of a vector space and a set \(C\), \(N\) projects \(C\) into itself along \(Y\) if \(z \in C\), \(k \in N\) and \(z - k \in Y\) imply \(k \in C\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionProjectsInto. The definition avoids naming the projection; when \(E = N \oplus Y\) it says exactly that the projection \(\pi\) onto \(N\) along \(Y\) maps \(C\) into \(C\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionProjectsInto.projectionOnto_mem Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionprojectsInto_of_projectionOnto_mem (\(z - \pi z \in Y\), and conversely \(z - k \in Y\), \(k \in N\) force \(\pi z = k\)). It is carried by a linear isomorphism \(S\) with \(x \in C \iff Sx \in C'\): given \(z' \in C'\), \(k \in N\) and \(z' - Sk = Sy\) with \(y \in Y\), the point \(S^{-1}z'\) lies in \(C\) and \(S^{-1}z' - k = y\), so \(k \in C\) and \(Sk \in C'\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionProjectsInto.map, in particular for continuous linear isomorphisms Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionProjectsInto.mapL — the analogue of Lemma 3.45 (§III.14).

The finite-dimensional lemma. If the finite-dimensional subspace \(N\) is in good position to the partial quadrant \(C\) of the sc-Banach space \(E\), then \(N\) has a closed good complement \(Y\) such that the projection onto \(N\) along \(Y\) maps \(C\) into \(N \cap C\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_goodComplement_projectsInto. The text has no such statement; Definition 3.21 and Proposition 3.22 do not need it. The proof works in the coordinates of §III.14: after a presentation, \(C = \{\ell_i \ge 0\}\) for continuous functionals \(\ell_1, \dots, \ell_n\) jointly onto \(\mathbb R^n\), the cone \(Q = N \cap C\) is \(\{x \in N : \ell_i(x) \ge 0\}\), \(\Sigma\) is the set of indices vanishing at some nonzero point of \(Q\), and for a set \(S\) of indices \(Q_S = (\ell_i)_{i \in S} : N \to \mathbb R^S\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectioncoordOn (for \(S = \Sigma\) it is the map \(Q_\Sigma\) of Proposition 3.22 Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionsigmaCoord_eq_coordOn).

Step 1: the choice of coordinates Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_coordSet. Wanted is a set \(S\) of indices with (1) \(Q_S\) onto, (2) \(Q = \{x \in N : \ell_i(x) \ge 0 \text{ for } i \in S\}\), (3) every \(\ell_i\), \(i \notin S\), positive on \(Q \setminus 0\). Property (3) holds for \(S = \Sigma\) by the definition of \(\Sigma\) Chapter3/GoodPositionpos_of_not_mem_vanIdx, and (1) for \(S = \Sigma\) is the consequence of Lemma 3.65 proved in §III.14 Chapter3/GoodPositionsigmaCoord_surjective. Three cases, those of the normal form. If \(Q = N\), take \(S = \Sigma\); (2) is trivial. If \(\Sigma \ne \emptyset\), take \(S = \Sigma\); (2) is the segment argument of Proposition 3.22 Chapter3/GoodPositionmem_quadCone_of_vanIdx. In the remaining case, \(\Sigma = \emptyset\) and \(Q \ne N\), the choice \(S = \Sigma\) fails, and here the sketch of Finding 83, which takes \(S = \Sigma\) throughout, misses a case (item 131). With \(S = \emptyset\), (2) would say \(Q = N\); and the formula of Step 4 below would reduce to an arbitrary projection onto \(N\), which need not map \(C\) into \(C\): for \(C = [0, \infty)^2\) and \(N = \mathbb R(1, 1)\) every nonzero point of \(Q\) has both coordinates positive, so \(\Sigma = \emptyset\); the line \(\mathbb R(1, 2)\) is a good complement of \(N\) (for \(|s| \le \varepsilon|t|\) the coordinates of \(t(1, 1) + s(1, 2)\) have the sign of \(t\)), and the projection along it maps \((0, 1) = -(1, 1) + (1, 2)\) to \(-(1, 1) \notin C\). The formal proof keeps one coordinate. Some \(x_1 \in N\) lies outside \(C\), so there is at least one coordinate, \(j_0\) say, and \(S = \{j_0\}\). An interior point \(y\) of \(Q\) is nonzero — if \(0\) were interior, \(Q\) would contain a ball of \(N\) around \(0\) and, being closed under positive scaling, all of \(N\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionmem_quadCone_of_zero_mem_interior Chapter3/GoodPositionsmul_mem_quadCone — so \(\ell_{j_0}(y) > 0\) by (3), and \(Q_{\{j_0\}}\) is onto: \(k \mapsto (k/\ell_{j_0}(y))\,y\) is a preimage. Property (2) for \(S = \{j_0\}\) is the next step.

Step 2: the segment argument for any \(S\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionmem_quadCone_of_coordSet. Suppose (3) holds for \(S\), some \(i_0 \in S\) is positive at a point \(y \in Q\), and \(x \in N\) has \(\ell_i(x) \ge 0\) for \(i \in S\). The set \(T = \{s \ge 0 : x + sy \in Q\}\) is nonempty (for \(i \in S\), \(\ell_i(x) + s\ell_i(y) \ge 0\) for all \(s \ge 0\); for \(i \notin S\), \(\ell_i(y) > 0\), so large \(s\) work), closed and bounded below; let \(s^* = \min T\). If \(s^* > 0\), the point \(z = x + s^*y\) is nonzero, since \(\ell_{i_0}(z) \ge s^*\ell_{i_0}(y) > 0\); so by (3) all \(\ell_i\), \(i \notin S\), are positive at \(z\) and, by continuity, at \(x + sy\) for \(s\) near \(s^*\); the coordinates in \(S\) stay \(\ge 0\) for all \(s \ge 0\); so a point \(s_1 = \max(0, s^* - \delta/2) < s^*\) lies in \(T\), contradicting minimality. Hence \(s^* = 0\) and \(x \in Q\). This is the argument of Proposition 3.22, Case C (§III.14), with the positivity outside \(S\) as the only input; with \(S = \{j_0\}\) and \(y\) interior it gives (2) in the third case of Step 1.

Step 3: a lower bound Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_coord_ge. A coordinate positive on \(Q \setminus 0\) is bounded below by \(c|x|\) on \(Q\), \(c > 0\): its minimum on the compact set \(Q \cap \{|x| = 1\}\) is positive, and \(Q\) is a cone.

Step 4: the projection and the estimate Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_proj_quadCone. Take \(S\) from Step 1, a continuous projection \(p_N : E_0 \to N\) (Hahn–Banach, \(N\) finite-dimensional), a linear right inverse \(g\) of \(Q_S\), and \[\pi(z) = p_N(z) + g\big((\ell_i(z - p_N z))_{i \in S}\big).\] Then \(\pi\) is continuous, \(\pi = \mathrm{id}\) on \(N\) (the bracket vanishes), and \(\ell_i(\pi z) = \ell_i(p_Nz) + \ell_i(z - p_Nz) = \ell_i(z)\) for \(i \in S\), so for \(z \in C\) the coordinates of \(\pi z\) in \(S\) are \(\ge 0\) and \(\pi z \in Q\) by (2): \(\pi(C) \subseteq N \cap C\). The kernel of \(\pi\) is a complement of \(N\), and it is a good complement. For \(p \in \ker\pi\) the coordinates in \(S\) vanish (\(\ell_i(p) = \ell_i(\pi p) = 0\)). Let \(c_i\) be the constants of Step 3 for \(i \notin S\) and \(\varepsilon' = \min_i c_i/(\|\ell_i\| + 1)\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_pos_le_of_finite. Let \(x \in N\), \(p \in \ker\pi\), \(|p| \le \varepsilon'|x|\). If \(x \in C\): for \(i \in S\), \(\ell_i(x + p) = \ell_i(x) \ge 0\); for \(i \notin S\), \(\ell_i(x + p) \ge c_i|x| - \|\ell_i\|\,|p| \ge c_i|x| - \|\ell_i\|\varepsilon'|x| \ge 0\). If \(x + p \in C\): the coordinates of \(x\) in \(S\) are those of \(x + p\), hence \(\ge 0\), and \(x \in Q\) by (2). The reverse implication needs no estimate.

Step 5: partial quadrants. For a partial quadrant presented by an sc-isomorphism \(T\) the functionals are the coordinate functions of \(T\), continuous Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectioncontinuous_coordFun and jointly onto Chapter3/GoodPositioncoordFun_surj; good position supplies a good complement \(P\) with its constant and the interior point. Step 4 then gives a continuous projection \(\pi : E_0 \to N\) with \(\pi(C) \subseteq C\) whose kernel is a good complement Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_proj_goodComplement (\(\ker\pi\) is a topological complement of \(N\), as the kernel of a continuous projection). With \(Y = \ker\pi\), closed as the kernel of a continuous map, the projection property is immediate: \(z \in C\), \(k \in N\), \(z - k \in Y\) give \(k = \pi k = \pi z \in C\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_goodComplement_projectsInto.

Theorem 3.43 with a prescribed good complement. In the text’s proof the complement \(Z\) of \(\widetilde K = \ker DH(0)\) in \(\mathbb R^{n'}\) comes from a good complement of \(K' = \{(\alpha, L\alpha) : \alpha \in \widetilde K\}\) through Lemma 3.46 (§III.20). Nothing later uses that origin. For every good complement \(Z\) of \(\widetilde K\) (constant \(\varepsilon\)), \(Z \oplus W\) is a good complement of \(K'\) with respect to \(\widetilde C \oplus W\), with constant \(\varepsilon/(\|L\| + 1)\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionIsGoodComplement.prod_top_graph. The splitting: \(K' \cap (Z \oplus W) = 0\) because \(\widetilde K \cap Z = 0\), and \((a, w) = (\alpha, L\alpha) + (z, w - L\alpha)\) for \(a = \alpha + z\). The estimate: with the maximum norm, \(|(\alpha, L\alpha)| \le (\|L\| + 1)|\alpha|\), so \(|(z, w)| \le \varepsilon/(\|L\| + 1)\cdot|(\alpha, L\alpha)|\) gives \(|z| \le \varepsilon|\alpha|\), and \((\alpha, L\alpha) + (z, w) \in \widetilde C \oplus W\) iff \(\alpha + z \in \widetilde C\) iff \(\alpha \in \widetilde C\) iff \((\alpha, L\alpha) \in \widetilde C \oplus W\) Chapter3/LocalSolvabilitygraphMap_mem_prod_iff. This is the second half of the proof of Lemma 3.46 for an arbitrary \(Z\); Lemma 3.46 itself is needed only for the good position of \(\widetilde K\). The projection property passes the same way: if \(z \in \widetilde C \oplus W\) and \(z - (\alpha, L\alpha) \in Z \oplus W\), then \(z_1 - \alpha \in Z\), so \(\alpha \in \widetilde C\) when \((\widetilde K, Z)\) has the property, and \((\alpha, L\alpha) \in \widetilde C \oplus W\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionProjectsInto.prod_top_graph; the projection along \(Z \oplus W\) is \((a, w) \mapsto (\pi_Z a, L\pi_Z a)\), and \(\widetilde C \oplus W\) constrains only the first component.

Where the formal route departs from the text. The text never chooses the good complement; Definition 3.25 lets it be any good complement, and for an arbitrary subset with the tangent germ property the repair of the claim “\(\Sigma\) is relatively open” would need a re-graphing over a better complement, which is not done (\(\pi(O) \subseteq C\) remains a hypothesis of Theorem 3.27, §III.24). For solution sets the complement is not given but produced, at Theorem 3.78, and every link of the chain accepts a prescribed complement; so the repair is a choice made at the bottom of the chain, not a change in the proof of Theorem 3.27 (item 130). The closedness of \(Y\) is part of the text’s sc-complement and is recorded because Lemma 3.55 and Definition 3.25 use it at the nearby zeros (items 49, 81, 93).

III.30 Proposition 3.52 with its index

Proposition 3.52 (text): the linearization \(Tf(x) : T_xX \to Y_x\) of an sc-Fredholm section at a zero is an sc-Fredholm operator; in the proof (and in Theorem 3.54) its index is the index \(n - N\) of the basic germ \(h : O(([0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k}) \oplus W, 0) \to (\mathbb R^N \oplus W, 0)\) to which \(g - s\) is conjugated. The statements of §III.21 state the index as “\(n - N\) for some natural numbers \(n\), \(N\)”, which every integer is. The reason is that the conjugation of Definition 3.11 is an existential proposition Chapter3/StrongBundleSectionsIsConjugateToBasicGerm, so the dimensions of the basic germ cannot be named outside it. Here the witnesses become data.

Conjugation data Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexConjugationData: finite-dimensional normed spaces \(P_n\) (the text’s \(\mathbb R^n\)) and \(Q\) (the text’s \(\mathbb R^N\)), an sc-Banach space \(W\), a partial quadrant \(\widetilde C \subseteq P_n\), a relatively open \(U' \subseteq \widetilde C \oplus W\), a strong bundle isomorphism \(\Psi : U \triangleleft F \to U' \triangleleft (Q \oplus W)\) with inverse \(\Psi'\) and \(\psi(0) = 0\) for its base map, a germ \(G\) with \(G_0 \subseteq U'\), a basic germ \(h\) on \(G\) with contraction map \(B\), and \((\Psi(u, k(u)))_2 = h(\psi(u))\) for \(u \in U\) near \(0\). A map is conjugated to a basic germ iff such data exist Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexisConjugateToBasicGerm_iff_nonempty.

The derivative of a conjugated map Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexGConjugationData.scDeriv_isFredholm_index. Let \(U\) be relatively open in the partial quadrant \(C\), \(0 \in U\), \(k\) an sc¹-germ with derivative family \(Dk\) on a germ \(G_k\) with \((G_k)_0 \subseteq U\), \(k(0) = 0\), and \(d\) conjugation data of \(k\). Then \(Dk(0) : E_0 \to F_0\) is Fredholm of index \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\); for \(k\) sc-smooth on \(U\) this is the whole-chart form Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexConjugationData.scDeriv_isFredholm_index_wholeChart. The proof is that of §III.21, step (a), with the dimensions kept:

(a) \(Dh(0)\) is Fredholm of index \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\) (Proposition 3.10 for the basic germ on level \(0\)) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationproposition_3_10_basic_level_zero.

(b) \(\Gamma(0)Dk(0) = Dh(0)D\psi(0)\), with \(\Gamma(0) = (\Psi(0, \cdot))_2\) the fibre operator of \(\Psi\) at \(0\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.fiberCLM. The left side is the derivative at \(0\) of \(u \mapsto (\Psi(u, k(u)))_2\), because \(k(0) = 0\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.scDeriv_fiber_comp. For the right side, let \(N_1\) be an open neighbourhood of \(0\) on which the conjugation identity holds; the germ \(\{U \cap N_1\}\) has a subgerm \(G_1\) mapped by \(\psi\) into \(G\) level by level Chapter3/GermFillingScNbhdGerm.preimage; on \(G_1\) the chain rule for germs gives the derivative family \(Dh(\psi_1(x))D\psi(x)\) of \(h \circ \psi\) Chapter3/GermIsSc1GermWith.comp; and \(u \mapsto (\Psi(u, k(u)))_2\), an sc¹-germ on \(G_k\) by the chain rule with the whole-chart outer map (§III.48), agrees with \(h \circ \psi\) on \(G_1 \cap G_k\), so the two derivative families agree at \(0\) (uniqueness of the derivative of a germ at points of \(U_1\)) Chapter3/GermIsSc1Germ.scDerivGerm_eqOn, with \(\psi_1(0) = 0\).

(c) \(D\psi(0)\) and \(D\psi'(0)\) are inverse to each other (chain rule for \(\psi' \circ \psi = \mathrm{id}\) on \(U\) and \(\psi \circ \psi' = \mathrm{id}\) on \(U'\)) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexscDeriv_comp_eq_self, and so are \(\Gamma(0)\) and the fibre operator \(\Gamma'(0)\) of \(\Psi'\) at \(0\): \(\Psi'(\Psi(0, y)) = (0, y)\) with \(\Psi(0, y) = (0, \Gamma(0)y)\) because \(\psi(0) = 0\), and symmetrically.

(d) Hence \(Dk(0) = \Gamma(0)^{-1} \circ Dh(0) \circ D\psi(0)\), a Fredholm operator composed with isomorphisms on both sides, of the same index Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationisFredholm_equiv_comp_equiv.

Consequently the index \(n - N\) does not depend on the conjugation: two conjugation data \(d\), \(d'\) of the same \(k\) give \(\dim d.P_n - \dim d.Q = \mathrm{ind}\,Dk(0) = \dim d'.P_n - \dim d'.Q\) Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexGConjugationData.index_eq. This is the text’s remark after Theorem 3.38 that “the Fredholm index is invariant under strong bundle isomorphisms”, for the conjugations of one germ.

Proposition 3.52 in the chart, with the index Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexGproposition_3_52_local_index. Hypotheses: \(U\) relatively open in \(C\), \(R\) a strong bundle retraction on \(U \triangleleft F\) with base retraction \(r\), \(0 \in U\) and \(0 \in O = r(U)\); \(g\) a filling germ of the principal part \(\hat f\) (§III.3) and \(Dg\) a derivative family of \(g\) on a germ \(G\) with \(G_0 \subseteq U\); \(\hat f(0) = 0\) and \((x, \hat f(x)) \in K\) for \(x \in O\); \(s\) an sc⁺-germ with derivative family \(Ds\) and \(\iota s(0) = g(0)\); and conjugation data \(d\) of \(k = g - \iota s\). Since \(0\) is a smooth point, \(Ds(0) : E \to F^1\) is an sc-operator (the remark after Proposition 1.16, for germs) Chapter3/BasicGermLinearizationIsSc1GermWith.isScOperator_deriv_zero, so \(\iota Ds(0)\) is the level-\(0\) map of an sc⁺-operator and compact. \(Dg(0) = Dk(0) + \iota Ds(0)\) is then the value at \(0\) of the identity \(Dg = (Dg - \iota Ds) + \iota Ds\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGIsSc1GermWith.deriv_zero_eq_add_scPlus; on \(U\) it was the uniqueness of derivatives within \(U_1\) and the density of \(E_1\) Chapter3/BasicGermLinearizationContinuousLinearMap.ext_of_comp_toBase_one. A compact perturbation of a Fredholm operator is Fredholm of the same index Chapter1/FredholmPerturbationisFredholm_add_isCompactOperator Chapter1/FredholmIndexfredholmIndex_add_isCompactOperator. Proposition 3.5 (§III.4) transfers the Fredholm property and the index to \(Tf(0)\) Chapter3/GermFillerLinearizationIsFillingGerm.proposition_3_5.

Proposition 3.52, with the index Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexGproposition_3_52_index. Let \(f\) be a section of the strong bundle \(P : Y \to X\) with \((f, x_0)\) an sc-Fredholm germ and \(f(x_0) = 0\). In the strong bundle chart of Definition 3.11 centred at \(x_0\), with the filling germ \(g\) of \(\hat f\), its germ \(G\) and a derivative family \(Dg\), and the local sc⁺-germ \(s\), conjugation data of \(g - s\) exist, \(Dg(0)\) and \(Tf(x_0)\) are Fredholm, and for every conjugation data \(d\) of \(g - s\) their index is \(\dim d.P_n - \dim d.Q\). Proof: unpack Definition 3.11; \(0 \in O\) because the chart is centred at \(x_0\); \(\hat f(0) = 0\) from \(f(x_0) = 0\); \((x, \hat f(x)) \in K\) because the principal part of a section lies in the retract \(K\) of the chart; data \(d_0\) exist by the equivalence above and give the Fredholm property; and the local theorem applied to an arbitrary \(d\) gives the index. No hypothesis is added. As in §III.21, only the level-\(0\) Fredholm property is proved (\(T_0O\) and \(K_0\) are not set up as sc-Banach spaces). The statements of §III.21 stand next to these, with the same proofs and without the dimensions; the whole-chart forms are kept as well Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexproposition_3_52_index_wholeChart.

III.31 The linearization at a zero in charts, its chart independence, and Definition 3.53 from a non-centred chart

Definition 3.53 is stated in \(T_xX\), with the linearization \(f'(x) : T_xX \to Y_x\) and the partial cone \(C_xX\) of Definition 2.38. The text defines \(f'(x)\) only at the centre of a chart, before Definition 3.4, as the restriction of \(D(\mathbf f \circ r)(0)\) to \(T_0O\), identifies it with \(Dg(0)|_{T_0O}\) for a filler \(g\), and appeals to Proposition 2.30 for the independence of \(T^R_xX\) and \(C_xX\) of the chart. That \(f'(x)\) itself, and the two conditions of Definition 3.53, do not depend on the chart is used — the proof of Theorem 3.54 repeats “as above” the argument at \(x_0\) in a chart centred at a nearby zero \(y\) — but not proved (Finding 110). The formalization (§III.21) states Definition 3.53 in the chart of Definition 3.11 centred at the zero; this section proves the local form of the missing independence at a zero, in charts, and the assembly step that Theorem 3.54 (1) needs: Definition 3.53 at a zero \(y\) from data in a chart which is not centred at \(y\) (the chart at \(x_0\)). Throughout, \(z\) is a point on level \(1\) (the text has smooth points), and tameness is not used.

Linear algebra of conjugate operators. Let \(L : T \to K\) and \(L' : T' \to K'\) be bounded operators between normed spaces and \(A : T \cong T'\), \(\Gamma : K \cong K'\) topological linear isomorphisms with \(L'A = \Gamma L\). Then \(L' = \Gamma L A^{-1}\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartseq_comp_of_conj, so \(L\) is onto iff \(L'\) is Chapter3/LinearizationChartssurjective_iff_of_conj; \(\ker L' = A(\ker L)\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsker_eq_map_of_conj; for complete spaces \(L\) is Fredholm iff \(L'\) is, with the same index, because Fredholm operators and their index are stable under composition with isomorphisms on both sides Chapter3/LinearizationChartsisFredholm_iff_of_conj Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationisFredholm_equiv_comp_equiv; and if \(D \subseteq K\) is dense and contained in the range of \(L\), then \(\Gamma(D)\) is dense in \(K'\) and contained in the range of \(L'\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsdense_image_of_conj. The isomorphisms that occur are restrictions of bounded operators \(a : E_0 \to E'_0\), \(a' : E'_0 \to E_0\) which map a subspace \(T\) into \(T'\) and \(T'\) into \(T\) and are inverse to each other there Chapter3/LinearizationChartsrestrictEquiv. A subspace \(N \subseteq E_0\) is transported by \(A : T \cong T'\) to \(A(N) = \{Ax : x \in T \cap N\} \subseteq T'\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartstransportSub, with \(y \in A(N) \iff A^{-1}y \in N\) for \(y \in T'\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsmem_transportSub_iff and \(A^{-1}(A(N)) = N\) for \(N \subseteq T\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartstransportSub_symm.

Good position inside a subspace is transported Chapter3/LinearizationChartsIsInGoodPositionIn.transport. Good position inside \(T\) (§III.21, Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsInGoodPositionIn) asks: \(N \subseteq T\), the interior of \(N \cap C\) in \(N\) nonempty, and a complement \(P \subseteq T\) of \(N\) in \(T\) with the \(\varepsilon\)-condition of Definition 3.21. If \(A : T \cong T'\) respects the cones (\(x \in C \iff Ax \in C'\) for \(x \in T\)) and \(N\) is in good position to \(C\) inside \(T\), then \(A(N)\) is in good position to \(C'\) inside \(T'\). The interior: \(A\) restricts to a homeomorphism \(N \cong A(N)\) which carries \(N \cap C\) onto \(A(N) \cap C'\), so it carries interior points to interior points. The complement: \(A(P)\); \(A(N) \cap A(P) = 0\) and \(A(N) + A(P) = T'\) by pulling back with \(A^{-1}\). The constant: with \(a = \|A\|\), \(b = \|A^{-1}\|\), take \(\varepsilon' = \varepsilon/(ab + 1)\); for \(y = Ax\), \(q = Ap\) with \(|q| \le \varepsilon'|y|\), \(|p| \le b|q| \le b\varepsilon' a|x| \le \varepsilon|x|\), so \(x \in C \iff x + p \in C\), i.e. \(y \in C' \iff y + q \in C'\) — the constant of Lemma 3.45, no finite dimensionality needed (Finding 115). Applied to \(A\) and \(A^{-1}\) this gives an equivalence Chapter3/LinearizationChartsisInGoodPositionIn_transport_iff.

Two derivative tools at a level-\(1\) point. (i) Uniqueness: if \(f_1 = f_2\) on a relatively open \(V \subseteq U_1 \cap U_2\) containing \(z\), then \(Df_1(z) = Df_2(z)\): both are derivatives within \(V_1\) (level \(1\)), \(V\) is an sc-domain with unique differentiability, and two operators \(E_0 \to F_0\) that agree after composition with the dense inclusion \(E_1 \to E_0\) are equal Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_eq_of_eqOn_relOpen. (ii) The fibre derivative at a point of the zero section Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_fiber_of_vanishing: let \(\Phi\) be sc¹ on a set \(D \subseteq E \oplus F\) containing \(\{(u, 0) : u \in S\}\) (\(S\) relatively open, \(z \in S_1\)) and the whole fibre \(\{z\} \times F\), with \(\Phi(u, 0) = 0\) on \(S\) and \(\Phi(z, k) = \Gamma k\) for a bounded \(\Gamma\). Then \(D\Phi(z, 0)(h, k) = \Gamma k\). Proof: along \(k_1 \mapsto (z, k_1)\), \(k_1 \in F_1\), the composite is \(\Gamma \circ \iota\), so \(D\Phi(z, 0)\) restricted to the fibre direction is \(\Gamma\) after composition with the inclusion, hence equal to \(\Gamma\) by density; along \(u_1 \mapsto (u_1, 0)\), \(u_1 \in S_1\), the composite vanishes, and unique differentiability of \(S_1\) at \(z\) gives zero in the base direction. This is the generalization from \(0\) to \(z\) of the identities of §III.4 and §III.21; it is the reason why only the fibre part survives at a zero (Finding 112).

The linearization at a point of the retract, without a filler. For the principal part \(\mathbf f\) of a section in a strong bundle chart with retraction \(R(u, h) = (r(u), \rho(u)h)\) and a level-\(1\) point \(z\) of \(O = r(U)\), put \[\mathrm{Lin}(z) = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}, \qquad T_zO = Dr(z)E_0\] Chapter3/LinearizationChartslinAt; \(Dr(z)\) is idempotent Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_r_idem_at. Three facts make it the right object.

Its values lie in \(K_z = \rho(z)F\) at a zero Chapter3/LinearizationChartsrho_scDeriv_comp_r (the text’s “\(\rho(0)Tf(0) = Tf(0)\)”, now at any zero). Since \((r(u), \mathbf f(r(u))) \in K\), \(\rho(r(u))\mathbf f(r(u)) = \mathbf f(r(u))\) on \(U\) Chapter3/Fillerρ_eq_self_of_mem_K; so \(\mathbf f \circ r\) equals \(\Psi_2(u) = (R(r(u), \mathbf f(r(u))))_2\), and their derivatives at \(z\) agree by (i). The chain rule for \(\Psi_2 = (\text{fibre part of } R) \circ (r, \mathbf f \circ r)\) at \(z\), where \((r, \mathbf f \circ r)\) passes through \((z, 0)\) (because \(r(z) = z\) and \(\mathbf f(z) = 0\)), and (ii) for the fibre map \((u, k) \mapsto \rho(u)k\), which vanishes on the zero section and is \(\rho(z)\) on the fibre over \(z\), give \(D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)v = \rho(z)D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)v\). The fibre \(K_z\) is the fibre of \(K\) over \(z\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsmem_rangeS_ρCLM_iff.

The bridge to fillers Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_comp_r_eq_of_eventuallyEq (the text’s “\(Tg(0) = Tf(0)\) on \(T_0O\)”, now at any point): if \(g\) is sc¹ and agrees with \(\mathbf f\) on \(O\) near \(z\), say on \(O \cap W\) with \(W\) open, then \(\mathbf f \circ r = g \circ r\) on the relatively open \(U \cap r^{-1}(W)\), so by (i) and the chain rule (\(r\) maps \(z\) to itself on level \(1\)) \(D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z) = Dg(z)Dr(z)\). Hence \(\mathrm{Lin}(z) = Dg(z)\) on \(T_zO\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartslinAt_eq_scDeriv, by idempotence of \(Dr(z)\). At a centre, for a filled version, \(\mathrm{Lin}(0)\) is the \(Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O}\) of Proposition 3.5 Chapter3/LinearizationChartsIsFilledVersion.fillerRestrict_eq_linAt Chapter3/FillerLinearAlgebrafillerRestrict. At \(z \ne 0\) the full \(Dg(z) : E \to F\) is not related to \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) (condition (3) of the filler holds at \(0\) only), so the relevant kernel is \(\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO = \ker \mathrm{Lin}(z)\) (Finding 111). For a filling germ \(g\) on \(G\) the bridge needs two things the whole-chart one did not: \(Dg(z)\) exists only for \(z\) on level \(1\) of \(G\), and the chain rule for \(g \circ r\) is the inner one on the germ \(r^{-1}(G)\), which is defined when \(r(0) = 0\), i.e. \(0 \in O\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGscDeriv_comp_r_eq_germ. Under these two conditions \(\mathrm{Lin}(z) = Dg(z)\) on \(T_zO\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGlinAt_eq_germDeriv Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.linAt_eq_germDeriv_chart, and at the centre, which lies in every germ, \(\mathrm{Lin}(0) = Tf(0)\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGIsFillingGerm.fillerRestrict_eq_linAt. Both hold wherever the bridge is used: the chart is centred at a zero, and the points \(z \ne 0\) are the level-\(1\) lifts of nearby zeros, which lie in the germ of \(g\) by the shrinking of the basic germ (§§III.32, III.48).

Fibres of strong bundle charts and of transitions. For a strong bundle chart \(\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K\) covering \(\varphi\): points of \(K\) lie over \(O\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.fst_mem_O; \(\Phi^{-1}(x, \cdot)\) is additive and homogeneous on the fibre of \(K\) over \(x\), since \(\Phi\) is a fibrewise linear bijection of \(P^{-1}(\varphi^{-1}(x))\) onto that fibre Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.symm_add Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.symm_smul; the fibre of \(K\) is closed under scalars and contains \((u, \rho(u)k)\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.mem_K_ρ. For a second chart \(\Phi'\) the transition \(\Theta = \Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}\) covers the base transition \(\tau = \varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_fst, is linear on the fibres Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_snd_add Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_snd_smul, maps the zero section to the zero section Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_snd_zero and \(K\) into \(K'\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_mem_K, and is inverted by the reverse transition Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transition_transition. Over a point \(x\) of the base overlap, \(\Gamma(x)k = (\Theta(x, \rho(x)k))_2\) is a bounded operator \(F \to F'\) — linear by the fibre linearity, continuous as a composition of \(\rho(x)\), \(\Phi^{-1}\) and \(\Phi'\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transitionFiberCLM — which on \(K_x\) is the transition itself Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.transitionFiberCLM_apply_of_mem. The text’s “bounded linear on the fibres” (Definition 2.50) is about \(\Phi\) only; the linearity of \(\Phi^{-1}\) on the fibres of \(K\) is this lemma (Finding 113). Finally, if \(\varphi(V \cap V') = O \cap W\) with \(W\) open, the overlap of \(K\) is \(K \cap (W \times F)\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundleChart.overlap_eq_inter_prod.

The chart change at a zero Chapter3/LinearizationChartslinAt_chart_change. Statement. Let \(c\), \(c'\) be strong bundle charts whose transition \(\Theta\) is sc-smooth on \([0]\) (as a map between the overlap retracts of \(K\) and \(K'\)), \(f\) a section whose representatives \(z \mapsto (z, \mathbf f(z))\) are sc-smooth \(O \to K\) and \(O' \to K'\), \(y\) a zero of \(f\) in both chart domains, and \(z\), \(z'\) level-\(1\) points over \(\varphi(y)\), \(\varphi'(y)\). Then there are topological isomorphisms \(A : T_zO \cong T_{z'}O'\) and \(\Gamma : K_z \cong K'_{z'}\) with \(\Gamma \circ \mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z') \circ A\), and \(x \in C_z \iff Ax \in C'_{z'}\) for \(x \in T_zO\), where \(C_z\) is the partial quadrant at \(\varphi(y)\) of a presentation of \(C\) Chapter2/TamepartialQuadrantAtWith. The proof, in the order of the Lean:

  1. The base transition as a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms. The base charts are compatible (both are charts of \(X\), Chapter2/MPolyfoldIsChart.compatible). Choose open \(W\), \(W'\) with \(\varphi(V \cap V') = O \cap W\) and \(\varphi'(V \cap V') = O' \cap W'\) Chapter2/MPolyfoldexists_isOpen_image_eq and restrict the base retractions to \(U \cap r^{-1}(W)\), \(U' \cap r'^{-1}(W')\) (Proposition 2.10 (1)); their retracts are the overlaps. Then \(\tau\), \(\tau' = \varphi \circ \varphi'^{-1}\) form a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between them Chapter2/BoundaryScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm, and \(\tau \circ r_W\) maps \(z\) to \(z'\) on level \(1\). The derivatives of the restricted retraction and of \(\mathbf f \circ r\) at \(z\) are those on the full domains, by (i) (Finding 114).
  2. The transition near the zero section. Restrict the strong bundle retraction to \(W \times F\); its retract is the overlap of \(K\), so \(\Theta \circ R_W\) is sc-smooth and its fibre part \(\Phi\) is sc¹. \(\Phi(z, k) = \Gamma(z)k\) because \(R(z, k) = (z, \rho(z)k)\); \(\Phi(u, 0) = 0\) because \(R(u, 0) = (r(u), 0)\) and \(\Theta\) preserves the zero section.
  3. The section in the two charts. For \(u\) in the restricted domain, \(r(u) = \varphi(y_1)\) for some \(y_1 \in V \cap V'\), and both \(\mathbf f' \circ r' \circ \tau \circ r_W\) and \(\Phi \circ (r, \mathbf f \circ r)\) take at \(u\) the value \((\Phi'(f(y_1)))_2\) (the principal parts are the fibre parts of \(\Phi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}\) and \(\Phi' \circ f \circ \varphi'^{-1}\), Chapter3/StrongBundleSectionsStrongBundleChart.apply_section'). By (i) their derivatives at \(z\) agree.
  4. The key identity. The chain rule on both sides, with \((r, \mathbf f \circ r)\) passing through \((z, 0)\) since \(\mathbf f(z) = 0\), and (ii) for \(\Phi\) give \[D(\mathbf f' \circ r')(z')\,D(\tau \circ r_W)(z)v = \Gamma(z)\,D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)v .\] The derivative of \(x \mapsto \Gamma(x)\mathbf f(z)\) in the base direction has dropped out because \(\mathbf f(z) = 0\); away from zeros the linearization is not chart independent (Finding 112).
  5. The isomorphism \(A\). \(A_0 = D(\tau \circ r_W)(z)\) maps \(T_zO\) into \(T_{z'}O'\) and \(A_0' = D(\tau' \circ r'_{W'})(z')\) maps back Chapter2/BoundaryScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mem_range; on these subspaces they are inverse Chapter2/BoundaryScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_inv_deriv (with the idempotence of \(Dr(z)\)); \(A\) is the induced isomorphism (restrictEquiv).
  6. The isomorphism \(\Gamma\). \(\Gamma(z)\) maps \(K_z\) into \(K'_{z'}\) (the transition maps \(K\) into \(K'\) and covers \(\tau\)), the fibre operator \(\Gamma'(z')\) of the reverse transition maps back, and they are inverse on these fibres (the reverse transition inverts the transition).
  7. Conclusions. For \(x \in T_zO\), \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)x = D(\mathbf f \circ r)(z)x\) and \(\mathrm{Lin}'(z')(Ax) = D(\mathbf f' \circ r')(z')A_0x\), so step 4 is \(\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(z')A\). The cones: Proposition 2.30 for the partial cone, applied to the germ of step 1 Chapter2/Boundaryproposition_2_30_cone, gives \(A_0(T_zO \cap C_z) = T_{z'}O' \cap C'_{z'}\) for the formalized partial cone Chapter2/TamepartialConeWith, which is the cone condition on \(T_zO\).

Hypotheses. Of the compatibility of Definition 2.50 only the sc-smoothness of \(\Theta\) on \([0]\) is used — not on \([1]\), not the reverse transition (Finding 116). For two strong bundle charts of \(P\) it holds because both are charts of the M-polyfold \(Y[0]\), hence compatible Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.IsChart.transition_isScSmoothRetractMap; and for an sc-smooth section the representatives are sc-smooth in every strong bundle chart of \(P\), so no hypothesis is added.

Chart independence Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.linAt_chart_independence. For two strong bundle charts of \(P\) around a zero \(y\) of an sc-smooth section, with level-\(1\) points \(z\), \(z'\) over \(\varphi(y)\), \(\varphi'(y)\): the linearizations \(L = \mathrm{Lin}(z) : T_zO \to K_z\) and \(L' = \mathrm{Lin}'(z') : T_{z'}O' \to K'_{z'}\) (corestricted to the fibres by the first fact above) are simultaneously surjective, simultaneously Fredholm with the same index, and \(\ker L\) is in good position to \(C_z\) inside \(T_zO\) iff \(\ker L'\) is in good position to \(C'_{z'}\) inside \(T_{z'}O'\). The four spaces are complete, being ranges of the idempotents \(Dr(z)\), \(\rho(z)\) and their primed versions Chapter3/FillerLinearAlgebraisClosed_range_of_idem; the rest is the conjugation algebra, with \(\ker L' = A(\ker L)\) and the transport of good position.

Definition 3.53 at a zero, from a non-centred chart Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart_dense. Statement. Let \(f\) be an sc-smooth section, \(y\) a zero with \((f, y)\) an sc-Fredholm germ (Definition 3.11), \(c\) a strong bundle chart of \(P\) around \(y\) (not necessarily centred at \(y\)), \(z\) on level \(1\) over \(\varphi(y)\), and \(g\) sc¹ on \(U\) agreeing with \(\mathbf f\) on \(O\) near \(\varphi(y)\) — the case in view was the chart at \(x_0\) with a whole-chart filled version. Assume (a) the range of \(Dg(z)|_{T_zO}\) contains \(\rho(z)\hat k\) for every smooth \(\hat k \in F_\infty\), and (b) \(\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO\) is in good position to \(C_{\varphi(y)}\) inside \(T_zO\). Then \((f, y)\) is in good position in the whole-chart sense Chapter3/GoodPositionGermStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart, in the chart \(c'\) centred at \(y\) given by Definition 3.11, with its filled version \(g'\). Proof. The chart change between \(c\) at \(z\) and \(c'\) at \(0\) gives \(A\), \(\Gamma\) with \(\Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \mathrm{Lin}'(0)A\); the bridges give \(\mathrm{Lin}(z) = Dg(z)\) on \(T_zO\) and \(\mathrm{Lin}'(0) = Dg'(0)\) on \(T_0O'\) (filler condition (1)). Surjectivity of \(Tf(y) = Dg'(0)|_{T_0O'}\) onto \(K'_0\). By Proposition 3.52 in the centred chart \(c'\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationGproposition_3_52_local it is Fredholm, so its range \(S\) is closed in the closed subspace \(K'_0\), hence closed in \(F'\). The map \(k \mapsto \Gamma(\rho(z)k)\) is continuous \(F \to F'\); by (a) and the conjugation it maps \(F_\infty\) into \(S\); it maps \(F\) onto \(K'_0\) (preimages by \(\Gamma^{-1}\), which lands in \(K_z\) where \(\rho(z)\) is the identity); since \(F_\infty\) is dense in \(F\), every point of \(K'_0\) is a limit of points of \(S\), hence in \(S\). So only a dense subset of \(K_z\) in the range is needed (Finding 117 (b)). The kernel. (b) is transported by \(A\) to good position inside \(T_0O'\) with respect to \(C'_0 = C'\) (the partial quadrant at the corner is \(C'\) itself Chapter3/GoodPositionGermpartialQuadrantAtWith_zero); and the transported subspace is \(\ker Dg'(0)\): \(\ker Dg'(0) \subseteq T_0O'\) by condition (3) of the filler \(g'\) at its centre Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsFillerOf.ker_deriv_le_range, and for \(w \in T_0O'\), \(Dg'(0)w = 0 \iff \Gamma(Dg(z)A^{-1}w) = 0 \iff A^{-1}w \in \ker Dg(z)\). This is where the hypothesis is on \(\ker Dg(z) \cap T_zO\) and not on \(\ker Dg(z)\): at \(z \ne 0\) condition (3) is not available and \(\ker Dg(z)\) need not lie in \(T_zO\) (Finding 117 (a)). Variants: with all of \(K_z\) in the range Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart, and with the hypotheses on \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) itself, taking \(g = \mathbf f \circ r\), which agrees with \(\mathbf f\) on \(O\) because \(r\) is the identity there Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj.

In the germ reading the assembly is the same, with \(g\) a germ with derivative family \(Dg\), \(z\) on level \(1\) of its germ, and the bridge for germs at \(z\) and at \(0\); the conclusion is good position at \(Dg'(0)\) for the filling germ \(g'\) at \(y\). The dense form needs the closed range of \(Dg'(0)|_{T_0O'}\), which is now a hypothesis at chart level Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionAtGerm_of_chart_dense, supplied at section level by Proposition 3.52 for germs in a chart centred at \(y\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGermTame_of_chart_dense. The forms with all of \(K_z\) in the range need no Proposition 3.52 at all: \(\mathrm{Lin}'(0) = \Gamma\,\mathrm{Lin}(z)A^{-1}\) is then onto \(K'_0\) directly Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionAtGerm_of_chart (the whole-chart variant had gone through the dense one).

What remains is to supply (a) and (b) in the chart at \(x_0\), at the zeros \(z_0 = \varphi(y)\) near \(0\): (b) with the text’s hypotheses (§III.32), (a) first under an added hypothesis (§III.33) and then with the text’s hypotheses (§III.43).

III.32 Theorem 3.54 (1) at the nearby zeros: Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55 on the graph, and the kernel

The text proves property (4) of Theorem 3.54 — at every zero \(y \in V\), with \(\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)\), “\(\ker f'(y)\) is in good position to \(C_yX\) and \(f'(y)\) is surjective” — in one sentence: it follows from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55. Unpacked, three steps are needed beyond the graph description of §III.23. First, Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55 have to be applied at the graph points, Lemma 3.55 on the relatively open \(V'\) of Corollary 3.47 and for a general presentation of \(C'\) (Finding 92). Second, Lemma 3.55 is about the tangent space \(N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n\}\) of the graph, not about a kernel; the identification \(N_v = \ker D(h + t)(v + \sigma(v))\) is not commented on (Finding 91 (a), 101). Third, the statements live in the push-forward chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\), about \(D(h + t)\) on \(E'\), while Definition 3.53 at \(y\) (via §III.31) asks for statements about \(Dg(z_0)\) on \(T_{z_0}O\) in the chart at \(x_0\) (Findings 102–104). This section proves all of it for the kernel; the surjectivity of \(f'(y)\) is §III.33. No hypothesis beyond those of the graph description is used.

Lemma 3.55 for a relatively open domain and a general presentation Chapter3/GlobalIFTFulllemma_3_55_relOpen. Statement. Let \(C = \{x : \ell_i(x) \ge 0\}\) be a partial quadrant presented by an sc-isomorphism \(T\), with the coordinate functionals \(\ell_i(x) = (Tx)_i\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTFullcoordCLMWith, \(N\) finite-dimensional in good position to \(C\) with a good complement \(Y\), \(Y\) closed, \(V\) relatively open in \(N \cap C\) with \(0 \in V\), and \(\sigma : N \to E_0\) with values in \(Y\), \(C^1\) on \(V\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), \(D\sigma(0) = 0\) (within \(V\)). Then there is \(\rho > 0\) such that for \(v \in V\) with \(|v| < \rho\) and \(z = v + \sigma(v)\): \(z \in C\); \(Y\) is a good complement of \(N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n\}\) Chapter3/GoodPositionOpengraphSpace with respect to the partial quadrant \(C_z\); and \(N_v\) is in good position to \(C_z\). Proof. \(D = N \cap C\) is convex with nonempty interior in \(N\) (good position), so \(D\) and \(V = D \cap O\) have unique differentiability. The extension. The text’s Lemma 3.55 (§III.22, Chapter3/GoodPositionOpenlemma_3_55_core) wants a map on the whole cone. Take a ball \(B(0, r) \subseteq O\) and a smooth bump \(b\) equal to \(1\) on \(\bar B(0, r/2)\) and \(0\) outside \(B(0, r)\), and \(\Phi(v) = b(v)v\). \(\Phi\) maps \(D\) into \(V\): \(D\) is closed under nonnegative scaling, and \(|b(v)v| < r\). So \(\tau = \sigma \circ \Phi\) is \(C^1\) on the cone, agrees with \(\sigma\) on \(B(0, r/2)\), and there its derivatives within the cone are those of \(\sigma\) within \(V\) (a neighbourhood of the point inside \(O\) does not change derivatives within a set); in particular \(\tau(0) = 0\), \(D\tau(0) = 0\). Lemma 3.55 in coordinates for \(\tau\), with the good-complement estimate of \((N, Y)\) rewritten in the \(\ell_i\) and the joint surjectivity of the coordinates (\(T^{-1}(k, 0)\) has coordinates \(k\)), gives \(\rho_1\), the membership \(z \in C\), and the good complement \(Y\) of \(N_v\) with respect to \(C_z\). The interior, which Lemma 3.55 does not state but good position requires: by the continuity of \(D\sigma\) at \(0\) (a \(C^1\) map on a set of unique differentiability) there is \(\rho_2\) with \(\|D\sigma(v)\| < \varepsilon\), the good-complement constant of \((N, Y)\). \(L = D\sigma(v)\) takes values in \(Y\) — this is where \(Y\) closed is used Chapter3/GoodPositionOpenfderivWithin_mem_of_mapsTo — so \(n \mapsto n + Ln\) is injective (\(N \cap Y = 0\)), a linear homeomorphism \(N \cong N_v\) in finite dimensions. It carries the interior of \(D\) to an open subset of \(N_v\) contained in \(C_z\): for \(w\) in the interior of \(D\), \(w \in C\) and \(|Lw| \le \varepsilon|w|\), so \(w + Lw \in C\) by the good-complement property, and \(C \subseteq C_z\). Take \(\rho = \min(\rho_1, r/2, \rho_2)\).

Corollary 3.41 at the graph points Chapter3/GlobalIFTFullStabilityData.exists_surjective_Dfs'_graph. For the data of Theorem 3.38 with \(D(h + s)(0)\) surjective and a continuous \(\sigma\) on \(V \ni 0\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), whose graph points \(v + \sigma(v)\) are zeros in the germ: there is \(\rho > 0\) such that for \(v \in V\), \(|v| < \rho\), the zero \(v + \sigma(v)\) lies on level \(1\), at a point \(x_1\) of the level-\(1\) germ, and \(D(h + s)(x_1) : E_0 \to F_0\) is a surjective Fredholm operator of index \(\dim P - \dim Q\). Corollary 3.41 Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.corollary_3_41 gives a radius \(r\) for the zeros, and continuity of \(v \mapsto v + \sigma(v)\) at \(0\) gives \(\rho\).

Property (4) in the push-forward chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTFullGtheorem_3_54_nearby. Statement. For a section \(f\) of a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions, \(f(x_0) = 0\) and \((f, x_0)\) in good position: the data of the graph description (§III.23, Chapter3/GlobalIFTGtheorem_3_54_graph: chart, \(\psi\), \(h + t\), \(K\), closed \(Y\), \(V'\), \(\sigma\), \(V_x\)), a presentation \(T\) of \(C' = \widetilde C \oplus W\), and an open \(V_{x,1} \subseteq V_x\) containing \(x_0\) such that for every zero \(y \in V_{x,1}\), with \(\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)\), \(v \in V'\): the point lies on level \(1\) and \(D(h + t)\) there is surjective Fredholm of index \(n - N\); \(v + \sigma(v) \in C'\); \(Y\) is a good complement of \(N_v\) with respect to \(C'_{v + \sigma(v)}\), and \(N_v\) is in good position to it. Only \(f\) a section is assumed, not an sc-Fredholm section. Proof. Take the radii \(\rho_1\) (Corollary 3.41 at the graph points) and \(\rho_2\) (Lemma 3.55, relatively open form), \(\rho = \min(\rho_1, \rho_2)\), and the projection \(\pi\) onto \(K\) along \(Y\), continuous because \(Y\) is closed and \(K\) finite-dimensional. Put \(V_{x,1} = V_x \cap (\psi\varphi)^{-1}B(0, \rho/(\|\pi\| + 1))\), open since \(\psi \circ \varphi\) is continuous on \(V_x\). For a zero \(y \in V_{x,1}\), \(\psi\varphi(y) = v + \sigma(v)\) by the graph description, \(v = \pi(\psi\varphi(y))\) because \(\sigma(v) \in Y\), so \(|v| \le \|\pi\|\,|\psi\varphi(y)| < \rho\), and both lemmas apply at \(v\).

Derivative identities at a nearby zero. Four lemmas move these statements from \(E'\) and \(N_v\) to \(E\) and \(\ker Dg(z_0)\).

Uniqueness at a point of \(C_1\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphscDeriv_eq_of_eqOn_nhds_at: two maps with sc¹-derivatives \(D_1\), \(D_2\) at \(x \in C_1\) that agree on \(W_1 \cap C_1\) for an open \(W_1 \ni x\) of \(E_1\) have \(D_1 = D_2\) — uniqueness of the derivative within the quadrant on level \(1\), then density of \(E_1\). The text writes \(\Psi_*(g) = h + t\) as an identity; formally they agree only on \(U' \cap W'\), and this lemma identifies their derivatives at every nearby point (Finding 104).

The fibre derivative of a strong bundle map at \((u_0, 0)\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleMap.scDeriv_fiber_at: for a strong bundle map \(\Psi\) with fibre operators \(\Gamma(u) = (\Psi(u, \cdot))_2\) Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationIsStrongBundleMap.fiberCLM and \(u_0 \in U_1\), \(D(\mathrm{pr}_{F'} \circ \Psi)(u_0, 0)(h, k) = \Gamma(u_0)k\); hence the derivative of \(u \mapsto \Gamma(u)k(u)\) at a zero \(u_0\) of \(k\) is \(\Gamma(u_0)Dk(u_0)\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleMap.scDeriv_fiber_comp_at — §III.21’s identity at \(0\), moved to \(u_0\).

The chain rule for the push-forward at a zero Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleIso.scDeriv_pushforward_at: for a strong bundle isomorphism \(\Psi\) covering \(\psi\) with inverse \(\Psi'\) covering \(\psi'\), and a zero \(u_0 \in U_1\) of the sc-smooth \(g\), \(\Psi_*(g) = \kappa \circ \psi'\) with \(\kappa(u) = (\Psi(u, g(u)))_2\), so \[D(\Psi_*g)(\psi(u_0)) = \Gamma(u_0) \circ Dg(u_0) \circ D\psi'(\psi(u_0)).\] \(D\psi'(\psi(u_0))\) and \(D\psi(u_0)\) are inverse on level \(0\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleIso.scDeriv_base_inv_base, and \(\Gamma(u_0)\) is injective because \(\Psi'\) inverts \(\Psi\) on the fibres Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleIso.fiberCLM_injective; hence \(\ker Dg(u_0) = D\psi'(\psi(u_0))(\ker D(\Psi_*g)(\psi(u_0)))\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsStrongBundleIso.ker_scDeriv_eq_map. For a germ \(g\) with derivative family \(Dg\) the formula is an identity of the explicit derivative family of \(\Psi_*(g)\) (§III.23), valid at every level-\(1\) zero \(u_0\) and for every family Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphGIsStrongBundleIso.pushforwardDeriv_at, and the kernel formula follows as before Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphGIsStrongBundleIso.ker_deriv_eq_map_germ; that \(g\) is sc¹ at \(u_0\) then means that \(u_0\) lies on level \(1\) of the germ of \(g\).

Corresponding partial quadrants Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphscDeriv_mem_partialQuadrantAtWith_iff: for an sc-diffeomorphism \(\psi : U \to U'\) between relatively open subsets of partial quadrants with inverse \(\psi'\) and \(z \in U'_1\), \(x \in C'_z \iff D\psi'(z)x \in C_{\psi'(z)}\): the one-sided sign argument Chapter2/BoundaryIsSc1With.mapsTo_partialQuadrant for \(\psi'\) at \(z\) gives one direction, for \(\psi\) at \(\psi'(z)\) the other, and \(D\psi(\psi'(z))D\psi'(z) = 1\). At the centre this was “\(C' = T\psi(0)C\)” (§III.23).

Tangent vectors of a family of points of a retract Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphscDeriv_apply_toBase_deriv_eq_of_fixed: let \(\rho\) be sc¹ on \(U\) and \(\Theta_1 : N \to E_1\) differentiable at \(v\) within \(V\) (unique differentiability at \(v\)), with values in \(U_1\) and \(\rho(\iota\Theta_1(w)) = \iota\Theta_1(w)\) for \(w \in V\). Then \(D\rho(\Theta_1(v))\) fixes \(\iota(D\Theta_1(v)n)\) for every \(n\): differentiate \(\rho \circ \iota \circ \Theta_1 = \iota \circ \Theta_1\) at \(v\). For \(\rho\) a retraction onto \(O\): the tangent vectors of a \(C^1\) family of points of \(O\) lie in \(T_{z_0}O\).

\(N_v = \ker D(h + s)(v + \sigma(v))\) (Finding 101). The inclusion Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphStabilityData.graphSpace_le_ker_Dfs'. For the solution graph \(\sigma\) of Theorem 3.47 on \(V\), a \(C^1\)-lift \(\sigma_1 : V_1 \to E_1\) of \(\sigma\) on a relatively open \(V_1 \subseteq V\) (Theorem 3.47 (1), §III.20), \(v \in V_1\) and the level-\(1\) point \(x_1\) over \(v + \sigma(v)\) in the germ: \(N_v \subseteq \ker D(h + s)(x_1)\). Proof. \(h + s\) is differentiable on level \(1\) only, so the graph is lifted: the kernel \(K\) is a smooth subspace Chapter3/SolutionGermRegularityStabilityData.ker_Dfs_le_smooth, hence lifts linearly to \(E_1\) Chapter3/BasicClassfinLift, and \(\Gamma_1 = \mathrm{lift} + \sigma_1\) is a \(C^1\) map \(V_1 \to E_1\) with \(\iota\Gamma_1(w) = w + \sigma(w)\) and \(\Gamma_1(v) = x_1\). \(V_1 = V \cap O_1\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphrelOpen_cone_inter has unique differentiability at its points Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphuniqueDiffWithinAt_relOpen_cone, and \(D\sigma(v) = \iota \circ D\sigma_1(v)\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphfderivWithin_eq_toBase_comp. The composite \((h + s) \circ \iota \circ \Gamma_1\) vanishes on \(V_1\), and near \(v\) (on \(V_1 \cap \Gamma_1^{-1}\) of the open set defining the level-\(1\) germ) \(\Gamma_1\) maps into the level-\(1\) germ, where \(h + s\) has the derivative \(D(h + s)(x_1)\) composed with \(\iota\) Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.isSc1GermWith_Dfs'. The chain rule and uniqueness give \(D(h + s)(x_1)(n + D\sigma(v)n) = 0\) for \(n \in K\).
