There the push-forward identity of \(g\), the description of \(\hat e_k\) as the \(\Psi\)-fibre image of \(\rho(r(u_\mu))k\) transported by the linear \(\mathrm{fiber}\), and the injectivity of the fibre maps of \(\Psi\) turn \((g + \mu\iota\hat e_k)(u'(\mu)) = 0\) into \(g(u_\mu) + \mu\rho(r(u_\mu))k = 0\).
  10. Tangency. By the first lemma of §III.41 and condition (2) on \(N_2\), \(u_\mu \in O\).
  11. Differentiation. \(r\) is sc¹ on \(U\), and \(g\) is an sc¹-germ on \(G_g\); the curve \(u(\mu)\) stays on level \(1\) of \(G_g\), because \(\mathrm{glue}\,\iota u'(\mu)\) lies on level \(1\) of the germ of the stability data and \(\psi'_1\) maps that into \((G_g)_1\) Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.levelMap_inclK_mem_of_subset_shrinkGerm. So both are differentiable from level \(1\) to level \(0\) at \(z_{0,1}\) along the curve, \(g\) by the chain rule within \((G_g)_1\) with derivative \(Dg(z_{0,1})\) (with \(g\) sc-smooth on \(U\) no such condition was needed). Along the curve, \(r(u_\mu) = u_\mu\), so the right derivatives at \(0\) agree, \(Dr(z_{0,1})\xi_0 = \xi_0\) (\(\xi_0 = \iota\xi_1\); uniqueness of right derivatives, §III.41): \(\xi_0 \in T_{z_0}O\). The map \(\mu \mapsto \rho(r(u_\mu))k\) is continuous at \(0\) (\(R\) is continuous on level \(0\)), so \(\mu \mapsto \mu\rho(r(u_\mu))k\) has the right derivative \(\rho(r(z_0))k = \rho(z_0)k\); differentiating \(g(u_\mu) = -\mu\rho(r(u_\mu))k\) gives \(Dg(z_{0,1})\xi_0 = -\rho(z_0)k\). Take \(x = -\xi_0\). \(\square\)

Where the hypotheses enter. Tameness and good position at \(x_0\) through the graph description, Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55 (steps 1, 3) and the inward direction at boundary zeros (step 6); condition (2) of the filler through the tangency (step 10); \(K \ne 0\) for the inward direction. The sc-Fredholm property at \(y\) is not used here; it enters only through the closed range in the assembly step. Condition (3) of the filler at the nearby zeros is not used. Why there is no uniformity problem. The only \(k\)-dependent quantities are the constants \(c_m\) and the \(\mu\)-intervals; \(N_4\) is fixed in step 2 before \(k\) is chosen. The perturbation argument of §III.33 applied the implicit function theorem at \(x_0\) to the \(\Lambda_0\)-extended problem, whose neighbourhood depends on \(\Lambda_0\); here it is applied at the nearby zero (Finding 181).

Theorem 3.54 (1) with the text’s hypotheses Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54_one'. Statement. Let \(f\) be an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions, \(f(x_0) = 0\), and \((f, x_0)\) in good position. Then there is an open \(V_x \ni x_0\) such that \((f, y)\) is in good position at every zero \(y \in V_x\). Proof. Destructure the good position at \(x_0\): the centred chart \(c\), the filling germ \(g\) with its derivative family, the sc⁺-germ, the conjugation, shrunk to \(G''\) (§III.48), and the good position in the chart. Tameness gives \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\) by Proposition 2.35 Chapter2/TameRetractsproposition_2_35; the graph description in the chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphGtheorem_3_54_chart_graph and the kernel at the nearby zeros Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyKernelGtheorem_3_54_chart_kernel give \(N_1 \supseteq N_2 \supseteq N_3\). A zero \(y\) of \(f\) in the chart domain with \(\varphi(y) \in N_2\) is a zero of \(g\) (\(\mathbf f = g\) on \(O \cap N_1\)). Case \(K = 0\). Put \(V_x = \varphi^{-1}(N_2)\) in the chart domain. A zero \(y \in V_x\) maps by \(\psi\varphi\) onto a graph point \(v + \sigma(v)\) with \(v \in K = 0\), so \(\psi(\varphi(y)) = \sigma(0) = 0 = \psi(0)\), \(\varphi(y) = 0\) (as \(\psi^{-1}\psi = 1\) on \(U\)), and \(y = x_0\) by the injectivity of the chart: the only zero is \(x_0\), in good position by hypothesis. Case \(K \ne 0\). Theorem A gives \(N_4\) (condition (2) on \(U \cap N_2\) is the filler’s, §III.29); put \(V_x = \varphi^{-1}(N_3 \cap N_4)\) in the chart domain. For a zero \(y \in V_x\): \(z_0 = \varphi(y) \in O\) is a zero of \(g\); the kernel theorem gives the level-\(1\) point \(z_{0,1}\), \(\ker Dg(z_{0,1}) \subseteq T_{z_0}O\) and its good position inside \(T_{z_0}O\); \(y\) is smooth Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection.mem_smoothSet_of_isZeroAt, so \((f, y)\) is an sc-Fredholm germ; \(\mathbf f = g\) on \(O\) near \(z_0\). The assembly step in its germ form Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGermTame_of_chart_dense (§III.31; whole-chart Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart_dense) applies at \(z_{0,1} \in (G_g)_1\) with (a) from Theorem A — \(\rho(z_0)\hat k\) in the range of \(Dg(z_{0,1})|_{T_{z_0}O}\) for every smooth \(\hat k\) — and (b) from the kernel theorem, \(\ker Dg(z_{0,1}) \cap T_{z_0}O = \ker Dg(z_{0,1})\). \(\square\) No hypothesis is added: the statement has exactly the hypotheses of the kernel theorem of §III.32 plus the sc-Fredholm property (Finding 189).

Theorems 3.54, 3.23 and 3.19 with the text’s hypotheses. Theorem 3.54 (1) and (2) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54': (1) as above on \(V_x\), and (2), the regular data of Definition 3.25 at \(x_0\) of a dimension \(d\) that every nearby datum shares, by §III.37 Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGtheorem_3_54_two fed with (1). Theorem 3.23 Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_23': (1) supplies the open set of nearby good position that the boundary case from the nearby good position needs Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGtheorem_3_23_of_nearby, and every zero of the resulting \(U\) is in good position. Theorem 3.19 Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_19': Theorem 3.23 and Lemma 2.26, \(d_S \le d_X = 0\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldlemma_2_26. The first forms under the filler condition at the nearby zeros (§§III.33, III.37) are kept; that condition is now a theorem (§III.45).

III.44 The dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index, and the index is locally constant

Theorem 3.19 says that the solution set is a manifold “whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index”, and the proof of Theorem 3.54 takes \(d = \dim\ker f'(x)\). In the statements of §§III.34–III.37 the dimension was existential. This section identifies it, at every zero and in every chart, and deduces the local constancy of the index along the solution set (Findings 170–171).

“\(f'(y)\) is onto, Fredholm, of index \(d\)”, chart-intrinsically Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexStrongBundle.IsSurjLinOfIndex: in every strong bundle chart around \(y\) compatible with the atlas, at the level-\(1\) point \(z\) over \(\varphi(y)\), every corestriction \(L : T_zO \to K_z\) of the linearization \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) (§III.31) is onto and Fredholm with \(\mathrm{ind}\,L = \dim\ker L = d\). “\(f'(y)\) is onto” alone Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexStrongBundle.IsLinSurjAt: in some chart, \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) maps onto the fibre \(\{k \mid (\varphi(y), k) \in K\}\); by the chart independence it is then onto in every chart.

Proposition 3.52 in every chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.linAt_index_of_conjugationData. Statement. Let \(f\) be an sc-smooth section, \(x_0\) a zero, \(c\) a strong bundle chart centred at \(x_0\) with a filling germ \(g\) of \(\mathbf f\) and a derivative family \(Dg\) on a germ inside \(U\), an sc⁺-germ \(s\) with \(s(0) = g(0)\), and conjugation data \(d_c\) of \(g - s\) to a basic germ Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexConjugationData with finite-dimensional spaces \(P_n\), \(Q\). Then in every strong bundle chart \(c'\) around \(x_0\), at the level-\(1\) point \(z'\) over \(\varphi'(x_0)\), every corestriction \(L'\) of \(\mathrm{Lin}'(z')\) is Fredholm of index \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\), and onto if the germ is in good position at \(Dg(0)\) in \(c\). Proof. Proposition 3.52 in \(c\) (§III.30, Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexGproposition_3_52_local_index): \(Tf(0)\) is Fredholm of index \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\). \(Tf(0) = Dg(0)|_{T_0O}\) is \(\mathrm{Lin}(0)\) by the bridge for germs at the centre, which lies in every germ Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGIsFillingGerm.fillerRestrict_eq_linAt (whole-chart: Chapter3/LinearizationChartsIsFilledVersion.fillerRestrict_eq_linAt), up to the identification of the fibres \(\rho(0)F\) and \(\rho(\iota0)F\), which are equal subspaces but different types in Lean Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexexists_rangeS_ρCLM_equiv. The chart independence (§III.31, Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.linAt_chart_independence) carries the Fredholm property, the index and the surjectivity from \(c\) at \(0\) to \(c'\) at \(z'\); the four spaces are complete as ranges of idempotents Chapter3/FillerLinearAlgebraisClosed_range_of_idem. \(\square\) At a zero in good position this gives \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, x_0, \dim P_n - \dim Q)\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isSurjLinOfIndex_of_conjugationData, because for a surjective Fredholm operator the kernel dimension is the index Chapter3/GlobalIFTfinrank_ker_eq_fredholmIndex_of_surjective; and the \(d\) with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, x_0, d)\) equals \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\) for every conjugation in the chart of Definition 3.53 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.exists_isSurjLinOfIndex (a conjugation exists, Chapter3/FredholmGermIndexisConjugateToBasicGerm_iff_nonempty). The first clause of Theorem 3.19 with the index Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_19_linearization_index: for an sc-Fredholm section and a zero in good position, in the chart of Definition 3.53, \(Dg(0)\) and \(Tf(x_0)\) are Fredholm, \(Tf(x_0)\) is onto, and \(\mathrm{ind}\,Dg(0) = \mathrm{ind}\,Tf(x_0) = \dim\ker Tf(x_0) = \dim d.P_n - \dim d.Q\) for every conjugation \(d\) — the old formulation’s “\(n - N\) for some natural numbers” made precise.

The conjugation exposed. The graph description and the tangent germ data at the centre are built from the chart of Definition 3.53 by destructuring the existential good position, so their statements did not record which conjugation they used. Their proofs now prove versions that expose it Chapter3/GlobalIFTGtheorem_3_54_graph_proj_conj Chapter3/GlobalIFTCenterGtheorem_3_54_tangentGermChart_proj_conj: the filling germ with its germ and derivative family \(Dg\), the sc⁺-germ, the good position at \(Dg(0)\) in the chart and conjugation data \(d_c\), with \(\dim K = \dim d_c.P_n - \dim d_c.Q\) for \(K = \ker D(h + t)(0)\), because \(D(h + t)(0)\) is onto and Fredholm of index \(n - N\) (§III.18, Chapter3/SolutionLinearizationStabilityData.isFredholm_Dfs). The earlier statements are corollaries.

Dimension = index. At the centre Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_tangentGermChart_index: for an sc-smooth section of a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions and a zero \(x_0\) in good position, the data of Definition 3.25 at \(x_0\) for \(\{y \in V_x : f(y) = 0\}\) (with \(\pi(O) \subseteq C\)) have a dimension \(d\) with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, x_0, d)\): the exposed \(d = \dim K = \dim d_c.P_n - \dim d_c.Q\) and the previous paragraph. The same for the global solution set Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_tangentGermChart_solutionSet_index (restriction of the chart, §III.37) and for the regular data of Theorem 3.54 (2) Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_two_index (the re-centring keeps the dimension, Chapter3/SolutionGermRecentreMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_isRegular_of_locally). At a nearby zero Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGisSurjLinOfIndex_of_forall_dim: if \(y\) is a zero in good position at which every datum of Definition 3.25 for the solution set has dimension \(d\), then \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, y, d)\) — the data at \(y\) from the centre theorem at \(y\) have dimension \(\mathrm{ind}\,f'(y)\), and that dimension is \(d\).

The index is locally constant along the solution set Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_index_locally_constant. Statement. For an sc-Fredholm section of a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions, a zero \(x_0\) in good position: there are an open \(V_x \ni x_0\) and \(d\) with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, y, d)\) at every zero \(y \in V_x\); in particular \(\mathrm{ind}\,f'(y) = \mathrm{ind}\,f'(x_0)\). Proof. Theorem 3.54 (1) (§III.43) gives an open \(V_{x,1}\) of nearby good position; Theorem 3.54 (2) with the index on it gives regular data \(D\) of dimension \(d\) with source in \(V_{x,1}\) along which every datum has dimension \(d\); on the source of \(D\), every zero is in good position with all its data of dimension \(d\), and the previous paragraph applies. \(\square\) The proof does not repeat the kernel computation of the matrix argument (Finding 188): “the dimension is locally constant” (from the re-centring and Sard’s lemma in fixed dimension, §III.35) and “the dimension is the index” give “the index is locally constant”. Along the solution set this is the index stability of the text’s Proposition 6.2, whose proof needs exactly the surjectivity of §III.43. Theorem 3.54 with the index Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_index: on an open \(V_x \ni x_0\) every zero is in good position with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, y, d)\), and the solution set has at \(x_0\) regular data of dimension \(d\) whose chart domain is \(V_x\), every datum at a point of the solution set in \(V_x\) having dimension \(d\).

Theorems 3.23, 3.19 and 3.57 with the index. Theorem 3.23 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_23_index: for an sc-Fredholm section with tame base retractions and a zero \(x\) in good position, an open \(U \ni x\) and \(d\) such that every zero \(y \in U\) is in good position with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, y, d)\), the zeros in \(U\) are smooth, and \(S(f, U)\) is a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure equivalent to a \(d\)-dimensional manifold with boundary with corners — the proof of the boundary case from the nearby good position (§III.37) with Theorem 3.54 (2) with the index. Theorem 3.19 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_19_index: for \(d_X \equiv 0\) the same, with degeneracy index \(0\) everywhere (Lemma 2.26): “a smooth manifold whose dimension agrees with the Fredholm index”, now with the tameness of the induced structure. Theorem 3.57 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_57_index: under the hypotheses of §III.37 (good position at every zero, \(S \ne \emptyset\)), at every \(x \in S\) there are regular data of a dimension \(d\), shared by every datum at the points of \(S\) in their chart domain, with \(\mathrm{IsSurjLinOfIndex}(f, y, d)\) at every zero \(y\) of that domain.

III.45 The kernel as tangent space, good position at interior zeros, and the filler condition as a theorem

“\(\ker f'(y) = T_yS(f, U)\)”, in a chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_ker_eq_tangent. Statement. For an sc-smooth section of a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions and a zero \(x_0\) in good position, there are the strong bundle chart \(c\) centred at \(x_0\) of Definition 3.53, the conjugating sc-diffeomorphism \(\psi : U \to U' \subseteq C'\) with inverse \(\psi'\) and \(\psi(0) = 0\), the finite-dimensional \(K = \ker D(h + t)(0)\), the solution graph \(\sigma : V' \to E'\) (\(C^1\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), \(D\sigma(0) = 0\), \(V'\) relatively open in \(K \cap C'\)), an open \(V_x \ni x_0\) with \(\psi\varphi(\{y \in V_x : f(y) = 0\}) = \{v + \sigma(v) : v \in V'\}\), and an open \(V_{x,2} \subseteq V_x\) containing \(x_0\), such that at every zero \(y \in V_{x,2}\), with \(\psi(\varphi(y)) = v + \sigma(v)\), and every level-\(1\) point \(z\) over \(\varphi(y)\): \[D\psi(z)\big(\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\big) = N_v = \{n + D\sigma(v)n \mid n \in K\},\] the tangent space at \(v\) of the graph, which is the solution set in the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) of its tangent germ data. Proof. From the kernel statement at the nearby zeros (§III.32, Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGtheorem_3_54_nearby_kernel): \(z\) lies on level \(1\) of the germ of \(g\), \(\ker Dg(z) = D\psi'(\psi z)N_v\), \(\ker Dg(z) \subseteq T_zO\), and \(\mathrm{Lin}(z) = Dg(z)\) on \(T_zO\) (the bridge for germs, which needs exactly \(z\) in the germ and \(0 \in O\), Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGlinAt_eq_germDeriv; whole-chart Chapter3/LinearizationChartslinAt_eq_scDeriv), so \(\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) = \ker Dg(z)\); and \(D\psi(z)D\psi'(\psi z) = 1\) on level \(0\) by the chain rule for \(\psi \circ \psi' = 1\) on \(U'\). \(\square\) The intrinsic statement, with \(T_yS\) as a subspace of \(T_yX\) (Definition 2.38), is not formalized: \(T_yX\) has no linear structure in the formalization (Chapter 2 gap G.13); the chart form is the statement (Finding 172).

Good position at a zero with \(d_X = 0\) is surjectivity. Linear algebra Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexisInGoodPositionIn_of_subset: a subspace \(N\) of \(T \subseteq E_0\) is in good position inside \(T\) to every cone \(C\) containing \(T\) — \(N \cap C = N\) has interior in \(N\), and any algebraic complement of \(N\) in \(T\) is a good complement with any constant, both sides of the condition being true. The statement Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj_of_degIndex_eq_zero: let \(f\) be an sc-smooth section, \(y\) a zero with \((f, y)\) an sc-Fredholm germ and \(d_X(y) = 0\), \(c\) a strong bundle chart around \(y\) with tame base retraction, and \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) onto \(K_z\) at the level-\(1\) point \(z\) over \(\varphi(y)\); then \((f, y)\) is in good position. Proof. The model of \(c\) is a tame retract, so \(d_C(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y) = 0\) by the strong form of Proposition 2.36 Chapter2/TameRetractsdegIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameRetract; no coordinate of the presentation vanishes at \(\varphi(y)\), so the partial quadrant at \(\varphi(y)\) is the whole space, and the kernel condition of the assembly step holds by the linear algebra. The assembly step with all of \(K_z\) in the range Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj concludes. \(\square\) For an sc-Fredholm section with tame base retractions, “\(f'(y)\) onto in some chart” therefore gives good position at a zero with \(d_X(y) = 0\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt (\(y\) is smooth, so the germ is sc-Fredholm); conversely good position gives “\(f'(y)\) onto” in the chart of Definition 3.53 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.isLinSurjAt; so at such a zero the two are equivalent Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_iff_isLinSurjAt — the text’s remark after Theorem 3.54. In a non-tame chart \(d_C(\varphi(y))\) can exceed \(d_X(y)\), and the cone would have to be transported from a chart realizing \(d_X(y)\); the standing tameness hypothesis makes that unnecessary (Finding 173).

Theorems 3.19 and 3.56 with “\(f'(x)\) surjective”. Theorem 3.19 Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_19_of_surjective: for \(d_X \equiv 0\), an sc-Fredholm section with tame base retractions, \(f(x_0) = 0\) and \(f'(x_0)\) onto in some chart: the equivalence gives good position at \(x_0\), and Theorem 3.19 with the index (§III.44) applies. Theorem 3.56 with the tameness and the regular data Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_56_tame: for \(d_X \equiv 0\) and good position at every zero, \(S \ne \emptyset\): Theorem 3.57 with the index (§III.44) and Lemma 2.26 — the solution set is a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure, a manifold of locally constant dimension without boundary, with regular data at every zero of a dimension equal to the index at the zeros of their chart domain. With “\(f'(x)\) surjective at every zero” Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_56_of_surjective: the equivalence at every zero, then the previous statement.

The converse of the matrix argument, and the filler condition as a theorem. The converse Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexnormal_injective_of_exists_range_scDeriv_eq_ρ. Let \(z\) be a level-\(1\) point over a point \(z_0\) of the retract with \(\ker Dg(z) \subseteq T_{z_0}O\), and suppose \(\rho(z_0)k \in Dg(z)(T_{z_0}O)\) for every \(k \in F\). Then \(Dr(z)b = 0\) and \(\rho(z_0)Dg(z)b = Dg(z)b\) imply \(b = 0\): choose \(a \in T_{z_0}O\) with \(Dg(z)a = \rho(z_0)Dg(z)b = Dg(z)b\); then \(a - b \in \ker Dg(z) \subseteq T_{z_0}O\), so \(b \in T_{z_0}O\); writing \(b = Dr(z)w\), idempotence gives \(b = Dr(z)b = 0\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsscDeriv_r_idem_at. The surjectivity of \(Dg(z)\) is not needed for this direction. With the direction of §III.33 Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjexists_range_scDeriv_eq_ρ_of_normal_injective, under \(Dg(z)\) onto and \(\ker Dg(z) \subseteq T_{z_0}O\) (and \(g\) agreeing with \(\mathbf f\) on \(O\) near a zero \(z_0\) of \(\mathbf f\)): \(\rho(z_0)F \subseteq Dg(z)(T_{z_0}O)\) iff condition (3) of Definition 3.4 holds at \(z_0\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexexists_range_scDeriv_eq_ρ_iff_normal_injective — the “iff” of Finding 100, both directions formalized. Both are linear algebra in the operator \(Dg(z)\) and hold for a germ at the points of its germ Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGnormal_injective_of_exists_range_deriv_eq_ρ_germ Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGexists_range_deriv_eq_ρ_iff_normal_injective_germ. The filler condition Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGisGoodPositionGermFilled_of_isGoodPositionGerm: for an sc-Fredholm section with tame base retractions and a zero \(x_0\) in good position, \((f, x_0)\) is in good position with the filler condition at the nearby zeros Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermFilled. Proof. Take the chart and filler of the kernel statement (§III.32) and the open \(V_{x,1}\) of nearby good position (§III.43); let \(N\) be an open neighbourhood of \(0\) on which \(\mathbf f = g\) on \(O\) and \(O \cap N = \varphi(V_{x,2} \cap V_{x,1})\) (Chapter2/MPolyfoldexists_isOpen_image_eq). At a level-\(1\) zero \(z_1\) of \(g\) over a point of \(O \cap N\), on level \(1\) of the germ of \(g\) (the condition asks no more, §III.33): \(z_0 = \varphi(y)\) for a zero \(y\) of \(f\) in \(V_{x,2} \cap V_{x,1}\); \(y\) is in good position, so \(\mathrm{Lin}(z_1)\) is onto \(K_{z_0}\) in the chart \(c\) (§III.44); the kernel statement gives \(\ker Dg(z_1) \subseteq T_{z_0}O\); and the converse gives condition (3) at \(z_0\). \(\square\) So the added hypothesis of the first forms of Theorems 3.54, 3.23, 3.19 (§§III.33, III.37) holds whenever their other hypotheses do: it was never a restriction, but proving that needed the surjectivity of §III.43 (Finding 174).

III.46 What the second addendum taught us

  1. The text’s Theorem 3.54 (1) is true, and the gap of its proof can be closed. The surjectivity of \(f'(y)\) at the zeros near a zero in good position does not follow from Corollary 3.41 and Lemma 3.55, as the text (and the book’s arXiv version) says; it follows from an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero for the perturbed filler \(g + \mu\rho(r(\cdot))k\), one smooth direction \(k\) at a time, whose curve of zeros is tangent to the retract by condition (2) of the filler Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54_chart_onto Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54_one' (§§III.41–III.43). With it, Theorems 3.54, 3.23 and 3.19 hold with the text’s hypotheses.
  2. The uniformity problem disappears when the contraction regions are written down. Theorem 3.30 is applied at the centre to the \(k\)-extended contraction germ, whose regions in \(a\) are those of the unperturbed germ Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGermShiftedBasicData.perturbContraction; only the \(\mu\)-interval depends on \(k\), and the bounds of the perturbation scale linearly in \(k\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoXiexists_xi_radii_bounds. The black-box use of Corollary 3.47 for an extended problem gives neighbourhoods depending on the extension.
  3. The index raise of Theorem 3.38 is what makes the perturbation \(C^1\) on the shifted levels (§III.42), and the surjectivity of the reduced finite-dimensional problem comes from a dimension count on level \(0\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoCurveShiftedBasicData.surjective_DH_and_ker_eq, not from inverting \(1 - D_2B\).
  4. The index is locally constant along the solution set Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_index_locally_constant, the special case of the text’s Proposition 6.2, and the dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index at every zero, in every chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_19_index (§III.44); \(\ker f'(y)\) is the tangent space of the solution set in the chart of the proof Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_ker_eq_tangent (§III.45).
  5. The filler condition at the nearby zeros was never a restriction Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGisGoodPositionGermFilled_of_isGoodPositionGerm, and good position at a zero with \(d_X = 0\) is surjectivity for a tame strong bundle Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_iff_isLinSurjAt (§III.45), so Theorems 3.19 and 3.56 hold with “\(f'(x)\) surjective”.
  6. Theorem 3.18’s “readily verified” is a construction: translation charts of \(\mathbb R^n\), the pull-back bundle as a structure, the product rule for a scalar factor, and the extension of a basic germ by inert parameters Chapter3/ParamPerturbationIsBasicGerm.paramExtend Chapter3/ParamPerturbationGtheorem_3_18 (§III.40).
  7. What is left of Chapter 3: Proposition 3.52 as an sc-Fredholm operator on \(T_xX\); \(\ker f'(y) = T_yS\) with \(T_yS \subseteq T_yX\); Theorem 3.58 for a general sc-splitting; Lemma 3.70 for a general presentation of the partial quadrant; Theorem 3.27 for sets whose data violate the second regularity condition; and Proposition 6.2 beyond solution sets (since proved, with the text’s hypotheses for paths on \(\mathbb R\), §III.49). The only added hypotheses are the closedness of good complements and the regularity conditions of Theorem 3.27 for general subsets.

III.47 The tameness hypothesis repaired

The implicit function theorems of §§III.23 and III.32–III.45 were first formalized with the hypothesis, htame in the Lean, that the base retraction of every strong bundle chart compatible with the atlas is tame; the phrase “a strong bundle whose charts have tame base retractions” in those sections describes it. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies it, so the statements that assumed it were vacuously true (Finding 190). This section records why, and what replaced it. The proofs told above are unchanged; the hypotheses and the charts of the conclusions changed, and the names of the theorems did not.

Why the hypothesis fails. Compatibility of strong bundle charts (Definition 2.50) constrains the transition maps between the retracts \(K\), not the retraction whose image \(K\) is. From a compatible chart with base retraction \(r\) on \(U \subseteq C\), the chart \((1, \varphi)\) onto \(\{1\} \times O\), with model \(\mathbb R \oplus E\), quadrant \([0, \infty) \times C\) and base retraction \(r'(a, u) = (1, r(u))\) on \([0, \infty) \times U\), has the transition maps of the first chart composed with affine maps, so it is compatible with every chart the first one is; but \(r'\) lowers the degeneracy index at \((0, u)\). The last point is machine-checked. The constant retraction \((a, w) \mapsto (1, 0)\) of \([0, \infty) \oplus W\) Chapter3/TameVacuityScRetraction.halfLineConst has retract \(\{(1, 0)\}\) Chapter3/TameVacuityScRetraction.halfLineConst_retract, and its product with any sc-smooth retraction \(r\) of a nonempty \(U\) is not tame Chapter3/TameVacuityScRetraction.halfLineConst_prod_not_isTame: the degeneracy index of a product is the sum of the indices Chapter2/FibredProductdegIndex_prod, so it is \(1 + d_C(u)\) at \(((0, 0), u)\), \(u \in r(U)\), and \(d_C(u)\) at the image \(((1, 0), u)\), against condition (1) of Definition 2.34. That the chart \((1, \varphi)\) is compatible is not formalized.

The new hypotheses. The text asks for the tameness of particular charts: the chart of an sc-Fredholm germ has “a tame strong local bundle” \(K \to O\) (Definitions 3.6 and 3.50), and the proof of Proposition 3.52 starts from “a tame strong bundle chart”. A tame chart is a compatible strong bundle chart whose base retraction is tame Chapter3/TameGermsStrongBundle.IsTameChart. Tame germ data at \(x\) are the data of Definition 3.11 (§III.6) in a tame chart Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame; good position in a tame chart adds Definition 3.53 in that chart (§III.21) Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame; and an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data has them at every smooth point Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame. Each implies the notion without tameness Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.isScFredholmGerm Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.isGoodPositionGerm. They can be met: tameness depends only on the domain of a retraction and its values there Chapter3/TameGermsScRetraction.IsTame.congr, and the identity retraction is tame Chapter2/TameScRetraction.id_isTame, so a compatible chart whose base retraction is the identity of \(U\) is tame Chapter3/TameGermsStrongBundle.isTameChart_of_eqOn_id.

The restated theorems. The proofs used the tameness for three charts only (Finding 191): the chart of the germ data at \(x_0\), for \((1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0\) in the linear part (§III.23) Chapter3/GlobalIFTGtheorem_3_54_graph_proj_conj; the chart \(\psi \circ \varphi\) built from it, whose model is tame because \(r\) is (§§III.27, III.34) Chapter3/GlobalIFTCenterGtheorem_3_54_tangentGermChart_proj_conj; and the chart in which \(f'(y)\) is onto at a zero with \(d_X(y) = 0\) (§III.45). So each theorem now takes \((f, x_0)\) in good position in a tame chart in place of good position and htame; where it concludes something at the other zeros it takes an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data; its conclusions are good position in tame charts, and the charts it produces are tame. This applies to Theorem 3.54 (1) with the text’s hypotheses Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54_one', to its first form, whose filler condition is now stated in a tame chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermFilled Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbySurjGtheorem_3_54_one, to Theorems 3.23 and 3.19 Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_23' Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_19', to the global theorems, with good position in a tame chart at every zero Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGtheorem_3_57 Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGtheorem_3_56 Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGcorollary_3_24, to the forms with the index Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_index, and to the filler condition as a theorem Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGisGoodPositionGermFilled_of_isGoodPositionGerm.

Reading the conclusion in the tame chart. At a nearby zero \(y\) the good position is proved in the chart at \(x_0\) and carried to a chart centred at \(y\) (§III.31). That chart was the one Definition 3.11 supplies at \(y\), of which nothing says that it is tame. The chart change now gives the good position in every chart carrying germ data at \(y\) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.isGoodPositionAt_of_chart_dense, the statement of §III.31 being its corollary Chapter3/LinearizationChartsStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_chart_dense. A good position given in any chart therefore holds in the tame chart of the germ data Chapter3/TameGermsAddGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.toTame: in the chart of the given good position \(Tf(0)\) maps onto \(K_0 \supseteq \rho(0)F_\infty\), \(\ker Dg(0) \subseteq T_0O\) and \(C_0 = C\), which are the hypotheses of the chart change at \(z = 0\); in the germ reading the point \(z = 0\) lies in every germ, \(Tf(0)\) is onto all of \(K_0\), and the form of the chart change with all of \(K_0\) in the range needs no Proposition 3.52 (§III.31) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionAtGerm_of_chart. The same step gives good position from “\(f'(y)\) surjective” at a zero with \(d_X(y) = 0\): the surjectivity, given in one chart, holds in every chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexStrongBundle.IsLinSurjAt.linAt_surjective, in particular in the tame chart of the germ data at \(y\), where \(d_C = d_X = 0\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt.

Theorems 3.15 and 3.18 keep tame germ data. The proof of Theorem 3.15 (§III.6) does not change the chart, so \(f + s\) has germ data in the tame charts of \(f\) Chapter3/TameGermsAddGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.sectionAdd Chapter3/TameGermsAddGtheorem_3_15_tame. For Theorem 3.18 (§III.40) the germ of \(\tilde f\) at \((r_0, x)\) is taken in the product chart \((r \mapsto r - r_0) \times \varphi\), whose base retraction \(1 \times r\) on \(\mathbb R^n \times U\) is tame when \(r\) is: the identity retraction of \(\mathbb R^n\) is tame, so \(d(a, u) = d_C(u)\), and the minimal subspaces and tangent spaces of the product are products Chapter2/FibredProductScRetraction.IsTameWith.prod Chapter3/ParamPerturbationPullbackChartData.ofProd_isTame. Hence \(\tilde f\) has tame germ data Chapter3/ParamPerturbationGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmGermTame.param Chapter3/ParamPerturbationGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame.param, and so has \(F(r, x) = f(x) + \sum_i r_is_i(x)\) Chapter3/ParamPerturbationGtheorem_3_18_tame, which is what the implicit function theorems need when applied to \(F\).

Not done (Finding 199): the compatibility of the chart \((1, \varphi)\), that is, the vacuity of htame at the level of charts; and the passage from an atlas of tame charts to tame germ data (Definition 3.11 ⟹ Definition 3.50). The text builds the tame chart into Definition 3.50, and so do the theorems.

Germ data and the charts of a tame atlas (Findings 350–353, fourth addendum). The passage was to be made by re-centring a tame chart of the atlas at the point and transporting the filler and the conjugation to it. That strategy fails, because a filling is bound to its chart. Condition (3) of Definition 3.4 is a condition on the chart: a filling germ in a chart with strong bundle retraction \(R = (r, \rho)\) gives a topological isomorphism \(\ker Dr(0) \cong \ker\rho(0)\), the linearization of the fill defect \(y \mapsto [1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)\) on \(\ker Dr(0)\) Chapter3/TameGermDataIsFillingGerm.nonempty_kerEquiv; so in a chart with \(\ker Dr(0) \ne 0\) and \(\rho(0)\) injective no map fills anything Chapter3/TameGermDatanot_isFillingGerm_of_ker. A tame chart with no filling. For the trivial bundle \(\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n\) take the model \(\mathbb R \oplus \mathbb R^n\) without boundary, the base retraction \(r(a, u) = (0, u)\), the product of the constant retraction of \(\mathbb R\) onto \(0\) with the identity Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.Reven, the chart \(x \mapsto (0, x)\), and \(R((a, u), h) = ((0, u), h)\) Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.evenBundleChart. It is compatible with the translation charts Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.isChart_evenBundleChart and tame — the degeneracy index of \(\mathbb R \oplus \mathbb R^n\) is \(0\) everywhere and \(\mathbb R \oplus 0\) is an sc-complement of \(T_xO = 0 \oplus \mathbb R^n\) Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.Reven_isTame Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.isTameChart_evenBundleChart — but \(\ker Dr(0) = \mathbb R \oplus 0\) while \(\rho(0) = 1\), so no map fills the principal part of any section in it Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.not_isFillingGerm_evenBundleChart. A tame atlas without germ data in its chart. With the one-chart atlas \(\{\)this chart\(\}\) Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.bundleEven every chart of the atlas is tame Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.bundleEven_atlas_isTameChart, the graph section of a \(C^\infty\) map has tame germ data — in the compatible translation charts Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.isScFredholmSectionTame_graphSection_even — and in the chart of the atlas no section has a filling Chapter3/TameGermDataTrivialBundle.tame_atlas_no_germData_in_atlas_chart. So Definition 3.50 must be the existential over all compatible tame charts, as formalized; read as “in a chart of the tame atlas” it would make every section of this bundle non-Fredholm. Whether germ data in some compatible chart give germ data in some compatible tame chart, for a tame atlas, stays open: the transition between two charts is defined on the retracts only, while the filling lives off them, so it cannot simply be pushed forward.

III.48 Definition 3.11 on germs

The text states Definitions 3.4, 3.6 and 3.11 for germs: the filled version is “a germ \((g, 0)\)”, the sc⁺-section a local one, and a germ of neighbourhoods (Definition 3.1) is a sequence \(U_m\) that may shrink with \(m\). The first formalization asked \(g\) and \(s\) to be sc-smooth on the whole chart domain \(U\), on the ground that a chart can be restricted. This section records why that was narrower, and the two devices on which the proofs in the text’s germ reading rest: the calculus of germs with whole-chart maps, and the shrinking of the basic germ (Findings 260–334).

Germs are not restrictions. On \(\mathbb R\) with the constant structure, \(f(x) = \sum_n c_n(x - a_n)^{n+1}|x - a_n|\), \(a_n = 1/(n+2)\), \(c_n = (4(n+2))^{-(n+2)}\), is \(C^k\) on \(U_k = (-1/(k+2), 1/(k+2))\) — the terms \(n \le k\) have their singular points outside, the tail is \(C^{k+2}\) — and \(C^{n+2}\) on no open set containing \(a_n\). So \(f\) is an sc-smooth germ on \((U_m)\) and sc-smooth on no open \(U \ni 0\) Chapter3/GermVsChartexists_isScSmoothGerm_not_isScSmooth. Restricting a chart on level \(0\) never makes the levels shrink, so the whole-chart reading is a restriction of the class of sections; for a section sc-smooth on \(X\) the two readings of Definition 3.11 differ exactly in the regularity of \(g\) and \(s\) away from their germs (§III.6). Whether every germ datum can be traded for a whole-chart one is open: replacing the sc⁺-germ by a whole-chart sc⁺-section costs one level (the index raise of Theorem 3.38), and on level \(0\) no argument was found in either direction (Finding 264). No theorem depends on the answer, since the theorems are proved in the germ reading.

The calculus with whole-chart maps. The text forms \(g + s\), \(g - s\), \([1 - \rho(r(y))]g(y)\) and \(\Psi_*(g)\) for germs without comment. Sums, differences, scalar multiples and compositions with sc-operators of sc¹-germs are sc¹-germs with the explicit derivative families, on \(G_1 \cap G_2\) for germs on two germs Chapter3/GermCalculusIsSc1GermWith.add Chapter3/GermCalculusIsScSmoothGerm.add_inter. The chain rule of §III.1 composes two germs at \(0\), but \(R\) and \(\Psi\) are applied at \((r(y), g(y))\), which is \((0, 0)\) only when \(g(0) = 0\) and \(0 \in O\); so the chain rule is proved again with the outer map sc¹ on a set \(V\) and the inner one a germ mapping \(G_0\) into \(V\), with no condition at a base point Chapter3/GermCalculusIsSc1With.comp_germ Chapter3/GermCalculusIsScSmooth.comp_germ, and with a whole-chart inner map \(\psi\), \(\psi(0) = 0\), on the preimage germ Chapter3/GermCalculusIsScSmoothGerm.comp_preimage. Hence the fill defect of a germ is a germ on the same germ (§III.4); the push-forward \(\Psi_*(g)\) is a germ on the germ of the points that \(\psi^{-1}\) maps into the germ of \(g\), with \(D(\Psi_*g)(0) = \Gamma(0)Dg(0)D\psi(0)^{-1}\) (§III.23); a germ plus a whole-chart map is a germ on the same germ (Theorem 3.15, §III.6); and \((a, u) \mapsto g(u)\) is a germ on \(\mathbb R^n \times G\) (Theorem 3.18, §III.40). The strong bundle isomorphism \(\Psi\) and the basic germ \(h\) remain what they were.

A basic germ restricts. Definitions 3.7 and 3.28 pass to every smaller germ with the same \(h\) and \(B\): the contraction field after shrinking its radius, since every level of a germ is a relatively open neighbourhood of \(0\), and the sc-smoothness by the uniqueness of derivatives in the quadrant Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkIsBasicGerm.mono.

The shrunk basic germ \(G''\). The text does not relate the germ \(G\) of the basic germ to the germs \(G_g\), \(G_s\) of \(g\) and \(s\), and nothing forces \(\psi^{-1}(G_m) \subseteq (G_g)_m\). For conjugation data with base map \(\psi\), inverse \(\psi'\) and basic germ on \(G\), let \(G''_m = \{x \in G_m \mid \psi'_m(x) \in (G_g)_m \cap (G_s)_m\}\), the preimage germ along the sc⁰-germ \(\psi'|_G\) (\(\psi'\) is sc-smooth on all of \(U'\) and \(\psi'(0) = 0\)) Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.shrinkGerm. The conjugation data shrunk to \(G''\) have the same \(\Psi\), \(h\), \(B\) and conjugation identity Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.shrink Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.basic_shrinkGerm; a point of \(G''_m\) is sent by \(\psi'_m\) into \((G_g)_m \cap (G_s)_m\) Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.levelMap_mem_inter_of_mem_shrinkGerm, and read on the \(E\)-side, \(u \in U_m\) with \(\psi_m(u) \in G''_m\) lies in both germs Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkConjugationData.mem_of_levelMap_base_mem. Corollary 3.41 on \(G''\): every zero \(x\) of the normal form with \(|x|_0\) small is \(\iota x_1\) with \(x_1\) on level \(1\) of \(G''\) — it is small on level \(1\) (Theorem 3.40), and the contraction field puts a level-\(1\) ball around \(0\) inside \(G''_1\) — so \(\psi'_1(x_1)\) lies on level \(1\) of \(G_g\) and \(G_s\) Chapter3/BasicGermShrinkIFTConjugationData.corollary_3_41_shrink. This is the device of every argument at the nearby zeros: the level-\(1\) lift \(z_{0,1}\) of a zero near \(x_0\) lies in the germ of \(g\), where \(Dg(z_{0,1})\) is defined (§§III.32, III.33, III.43, III.45). It relies on the lifts being small on level \(1\); a point small on level \(0\) only need not lie in \(G''_1\). At the centre no shrinking is needed: \(0\) lies in every germ, and \(Dg(0)\) is the same for all germs and families (§III.4).

What the proofs use of \(g\) and \(s\). At \(0\): \(Dg(0)\) and \(Ds(0)\) (Propositions 3.5 and 3.52, Definition 3.53, the linear part of Theorem 3.54; §§III.4, III.21, III.23, III.30). On level \(0\) near \(0\): continuity of \(g\) and of the sc⁺-part (Theorem 3.12, §III.13; the local step of Theorem 5.5, §V.6). At the level-\(1\) lifts of the nearby zeros: \(Dg\), through \(G''\) (Theorem 3.54 (1), §§III.32–III.33, III.43, III.45). Nowhere \(g\) or \(s\) on \(U \cap E_m\) away from their germs. So every theorem of Chapter 3 holds in the germ reading with the text’s hypotheses and its former conclusions, and no hypothesis is added; the statements that named the derivative of \(g\) on \(U\) at \(0\) (Proposition 3.52, the linearization statements of Theorems 3.19 and 3.54) now name the germ, a derivative family \(Dg\) and \(Dg(0)\), and Corollary 5.8 in a chart has an sc⁺-germ on the shifted germ for its sc⁺-part (§V.7).

The switch. The canonical names now denote the germ reading: Definitions 3.11, 3.14, 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53 with the tame, filled and sc variants of good position Chapter3/GermFillingChartStrongBundle.IsScFredholmGerm Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSection Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm, and the theorems built on them. The whole-chart notions and theorems keep their statements under the names …WholeChart and …_wholeChart, and each whole-chart notion implies its germ twin Chapter3/TameGermsGStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionWholeChart.isScFredholmSection Chapter3/GoodPositionGermGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermWholeChart.isGoodPositionGerm. The non-vacuity witnesses are whole-chart data, hence germ data. Chapter 5 is stated with the germ notions: the local step of Theorem 5.5 and the spanning sections changed locally, and Corollary 5.8 in a chart changed its statement (§§V.6, V.12, V.7).

III.49 Definition 6.1 and Proposition 6.2: the index along paths

The text’s Chapter 6 opens with the index of an sc-Fredholm germ at a smooth point which need not be a zero (Definition 6.1, pp. 200–201) and proves that it is constant along sc-smooth paths of smooth points (Proposition 6.2, p. 201). Its proof is the device that §III.44 used along the zero set: stabilize by finitely many sc⁺-sections and apply the implicit function theorem. This section retells both: first with sc⁺-sections on all of \(X\), which needs bump functions (Findings 340–348), then as the text does it, with locally defined sections on the restriction of the bundle to a chart domain and without bump functions (Findings 349, 360–367).

Definition 6.1 Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.IsIndexAt. \(f\) has index \(i\) at \(x\) if there is an sc⁺-section \(s\) of \(P\) with \((f + s)(x) = 0\) and \((f + s)'(x)\) Fredholm of index \(i\) in every strong bundle chart around \(x\) (the chart-intrinsic statement of §III.44). The text’s \(f - s\) with \(s(x) = f(x)\) is \(f + (-s)\); the text’s section is local, this one global; the reading with local sections, and the agreement of the two readings under bump functions, close this section. Well defined. At a zero of an sc-Fredholm section the index in IsLinOfIndex is unique, because in a chart \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) is a bounded operator into \(K_z\) (§III.44), so the quantification over corestrictions is not vacuous Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.IsLinOfIndex.unique. Adding an sc⁺-section \(s\) with \(s(x) = 0\) at a zero \(x\) of \(f\) does not change the index: the germ datum of \(f\) at \(x\), with conjugation data \(dc\), gives the index \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\) of \(f'(x)\) (Proposition 3.52), and Theorem 3.15 gives germ data of \(f + s\) in the same chart whose conjugation data are \(dc\) up to their values on \(U\), since \((g + \hat s \circ r) - (\hat s_1 \circ r + t_0) = g - t_0\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.isLinOfIndex_sectionAdd_of_isZeroAt. For two sections \(s, s'\) of the definition, \(s' - s\) is an sc⁺-section vanishing at \(x\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisZeroAt_sectionDiff_of_isZeroAt_sectionAdd and \((f + s) + (s' - s) = f + s'\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathssectionAdd_sectionAdd_sectionDiff, so the indices agree Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.IsIndexAt.unique. The text argues instead that \((t - s)'(x)\) is an sc⁺-operator, hence compact on every level, and invokes Proposition 1.10; the project has no lemma that the linearization of an sc⁺-section is compact, and the germ data make it unnecessary. At a zero the index of the germ is that of \(f'(x)\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.isIndexAt_of_isZeroAt Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.IsIndexAt.isLinOfIndex_of_isZeroAt. Existence. If \(X\) admits bump functions, every smooth point has an index: \(f(x)\) is a smooth point of \(Y\), Lemma 5.11 gives an sc⁺-section \(s_0\) with \(s_0(x) = f(x)\), and for \(s = -s_0\) the germ data of the sc-Fredholm section \(f + s\) at its zero \(x\) (Theorem 3.15) give the index Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsStrongBundle.exists_isIndexAt.

Along the zero set, without good position (Findings 240–242). Let \(X\) admit bump functions, \(f\) be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and \(f(x_0) = 0\); neither good position nor surjectivity at \(x_0\) is assumed. In a chart centred at \(x_0\), finitely many smooth vectors span a complement of the range of \(\mathrm{Lin}(0)\), closed of finite codimension by Proposition 3.52, and Lemma 5.11 realizes them as allowable sc⁺-sections \(s_1, \dots, s_k\) Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGexists_spanning_sections_germ; with further sections that tilt the kernel into good position at a corner (the conditions (i)–(ii) of §V.19), the parametrized section \(F(\lambda, x) = f(x) + \sum_i\lambda_is_i(x)\) of Theorem 3.18 is in good position at \((0, x_0)\) in a tame chart Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGexists_sections_isParamGP_germ Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGisGoodPositionGermTame_paramSection_of_isParamGP. So the index of \(F'\) is one integer \(d\) at the zeros of \(F\) near \((0, x_0)\) (§III.44), among them \((0, y)\) for every zero \(y\) of \(f\) near \(x_0\). At \((0, y)\), in the product chart, \(\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)(\delta\lambda, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_f(0)\delta u + \sum_i\delta\lambda_i\hat s_i(0)\), a finite-rank extension, so \(d = k + \operatorname{ind} f'(y)\) Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantfredholmIndex_eq_of_param Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGStrongBundle.isLinOfIndex_of_paramSection_isLinOfIndex. Hence \(f'(y)\) has index \(d - k\) in every chart at every zero \(y\) near \(x_0\) Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGindex_locally_constant_of_admitsBumpFunctions, also as an sc-Fredholm operator on every level Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantGtheorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general. This is the text’s device for Proposition 6.2 in the case of a zero.

The local form. For \(X\) with bump functions, \(f\) with tame germ data and an sc⁺-section \(s\) with \((f + s)(x_0) = 0\), the index of the germ is one integer at the zeros of \(f + s\) near \(x_0\): \(f + s\) has tame germ data (§III.47) and the previous paragraph applies to it Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisIndexAt_locally_constant_of_isZeroAt_sectionAdd. Hence along a path continuous at \(t_0\) on which \(f + s\) vanishes near \(t_0\) the index is constant near \(t_0\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisIndexAt_eventually_const_of_path, and on a preconnected parameter space a locally constant index is constant: by uniqueness the index is a locally constant function of \(t\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisIndexAt_const_of_forall_eventually. What remains is a section \(s\), depending on \(t_0\), that vanishes along the path — the text’s \(s(t, x)\) on \([0, 1] \times X\) — and the passage from the product back to \(X\).

Bump functions on \(\mathbb R^n \times X\). The device works on the product of Theorem 3.18 (§III.40), which must admit bump functions when \(X\) does. A \(C^\infty\) function on \(\mathbb R^n\) is sc-smooth on the M-polyfold \(\mathbb R^n\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisScSmoothMap_rn_real_of_contDiff, products of sc-smooth functions are sc-smooth by the product rule in every chart Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.mul, and \((r, x) \mapsto \beta_1(r)\beta_2(x)\) has support in \(\operatorname{supp}\beta_1 \times \operatorname{supp}\beta_2\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathstsupport_prod_mul_subset; so \(\mathbb R^n \times X\) admits bump functions Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsMPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_prod_rn. Then for the pull-back \(\tilde f = f \circ \pi\) and an sc⁺-section \(S\) of \(\pi^*P\) with \(\tilde f + S\) vanishing along the graph \(t \mapsto (t, \varphi(t))\) near \(t_0\), the index of \((\tilde f + S)'(t, \varphi(t))\) in every chart is one integer for \(t\) near \(t_0\): \(\tilde f + S\) has tame germ data (§§III.40, III.47), and the local constancy along its zero set applies Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsisLinOfIndex_paramLift_sectionAdd_eventually_const. The proposition thereby reduces to two steps, the section along the path (E) and the index count on a slice (S) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsproposition_6_2_of_sections_of_slice.

(E): the text’s section along the path Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceexists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path. For an sc-smooth section \(f\) (sc-Fredholm is not needed), an sc-smooth path \(\varphi : \mathbb R^n \to X\) and \(t_0\), there is an sc⁺-section \(S\) of \(\pi^*P\) with \(\tilde f + S = 0\) along the graph near \(t_0\). Take a strong bundle chart \(c\) around \(\varphi(t_0)\). First the path is reparametrized by a \(C^\infty\) map \(\sigma\) of \(\mathbb R^n\) equal to the identity near \(t_0\) with values in \(\varphi^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi_c)\), \(\sigma(t) = t_0 + b(t - t_0)(t - t_0)\) for a smooth bump \(b\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceexists_contDiff_eq_id_near_mapsTo; \(C^\infty\) self-maps of \(\mathbb R^n\) are sc-smooth Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceisScSmoothMap_rn_of_contDiff, so \(\psi = \varphi \circ \sigma\) is an sc-smooth path that stays in the chart. The representative \(t \mapsto \Phi(f(\psi(t)))\) is sc-smooth from the constant structure \(\mathbb R^n\) into \(E \oplus F\); Proposition 1.17 makes it sc-smooth from \((\mathbb R^n)^1 = \mathbb R^n\) into \((E \oplus F)^1 = E^1 \oplus F^1\), and its \(F^1\)-component \(\hat e_1\) is the curve of smooth points that the text’s \(s(t, x) = R(x, f(\varphi(t)))\) needs in \(F^1\) — no new analysis is required. In the product chart \((r \mapsto r - t_0) \times \varphi_c\) of \(\pi^*P\) the local section is \(\tau(a, u) = -R[1](u, \hat e_1(a + t_0))_2\), sc-smooth into \(K[1]\) because the bundle retraction is sc-smooth on \([1]\); it is cut off by a bump of \(X\) equal to \(1\) near \(\varphi(t_0)\) with support in the chart domain (Proposition 5.30) and extended by \(0\) (§V.9). Along the graph \(\Phi(S(t, \varphi(t)))_2 = -R(\varphi_c(\varphi(t)), \Phi(f(\varphi(t)))_2)_2 = -\Phi(f(\varphi(t)))_2\), since \(\Phi(f(\varphi(t))) \in K\) is fixed by \(R\), so \(\tilde f + S\) vanishes there for \(t\) near \(t_0\), where \(\sigma(t) = t\) and the bump is \(1\). The bump function and the reparametrization make the text’s local section global; the text needs neither.

(S): the slice. The slice \(S(t, \cdot)\) of a section of \(\pi^*P\), read in \(Y\) through the fibres \((\pi^*Y)_{(t, x)} = P^{-1}(x)\), is a section of \(P\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDevicepullbackSlice Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceIsSection.pullbackSlice; \(G(t, x) = 0\) iff the slice vanishes at \(x\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceisZeroAt_pullback_iff_pullbackSlice, and the slice of \(\tilde f + S\) is \(f + S(t, \cdot)\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDevicepullbackSlice_sectionAdd_paramLift. The slice of an sc⁺-section is sc⁺ Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceStrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.pullbackSlice: for a chart \(c\) of the atlas of \(P\), the product chart \((r \mapsto r - t) \times \varphi_c\) is a chart of the atlas of \(\pi^*P\), and the local representative of \(S(t, \cdot)\) is that of \(S\) composed with the sc-operator \(u \mapsto (0, u)\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceScBanach.prodSndLeftOp and projected. The linearization on the slice direction: in the product chart at \((t, x)\), whose base retraction is \((a, u) \mapsto (a, r(u))\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDevicePullbackChartData.r_ofProd, \(\mathrm{Lin}_G(0)(0, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_{G(t, \cdot)}(0)\delta u\), by the chain rule for \(u \mapsto \hat G(0, r(u))\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceStrongBundle.linAt_ofProd_slice. The index count: if \(G\) is an sc-Fredholm section of \(\pi^*P\) whose slice \(g = G(t, \cdot)\) is an sc-Fredholm section with \(g(x) = 0\), and \(G'(t, x)\) is Fredholm of index \(i\) in every chart, then \(g'(x)\) is Fredholm of index \(i - n\) in every chart: \(\mathrm{Lin}_G(0)(\delta a, \delta u) = \mathrm{Lin}_g(0)\delta u + \mathrm{Lin}_G(0)(\delta a, 0)\) by linearity and the slice identity, the last term has rank at most \(n\), and the parameter count of the zero-set case applies, the chart independence coming from the germ datum of \(g\) at \(x\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceStrongBundle.isLinOfIndex_pullbackSlice_of_isLinOfIndex. For \(G = \tilde f + S\) (\(n = 1\)) this is \(\mathrm{ind}(f, x) = i - 1\), with \(S(t, \cdot)\) as the section of Definition 6.1 Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceStrongBundle.isIndexAt_of_pullback_isLinOfIndex.

Proposition 6.2 Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceproposition_6_2. Let \(X\) admit sc-smooth bump functions, \(f\) be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and \(\varphi : \mathbb R \to X\) an sc-smooth path. Then \(\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t))\) is one integer for all \(t\); in particular \(\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(0)) = \mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(1))\). For each \(t_0\), (E) gives \(S\); the index of \(\tilde f + S\) is constant near \(t_0\) along the graph; (S) turns it into \(\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t)) + 1\); and \(\mathbb R\) is connected. The paracompactness of \(\mathbb R \times X\) and of \(\pi^*Y\) is supplied by Theorem 2.16 Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsDeviceproposition_6_2'. Against the text. (i) The path is defined on \(\mathbb R\), not on \([0, 1]\): \(\mathbb R \times X\) is the product of Theorem 3.18 and has no boundary, and the text’s “tame M-polyfold \([0, 1] \times X\)” is not used; a path on \([0, 1]\) that extends sc-smoothly to \(\mathbb R\) is covered, and by the reparametrization in (E) only a neighbourhood of each \(t_0\) matters. (ii) The hypotheses are tame germ data, the reading of “tame strong bundle” of §III.47, and bump functions, which the text does not assume (“we do not need a sc-smooth partition of unity”): they are used for the stabilizing sections (Lemma 5.11) and for the cut-off of the section along the path, both globalizations of the text’s locally defined sections. Without them the device runs on the restriction of \(P\) to a chart domain, as the text intends; that is the rest of this section. (iii) Definition 6.1 is proved well defined without Proposition 1.10. (iv) The two points the text’s proof does not address — the tilting sections for the kernel condition at a corner and the uniformity in the zero — are those of the zero-set case above.

Without bump functions: the restriction to an open set (Findings 349, 360). The text restricts the bundle to a chart domain without comment (“in a chart, \(s(y) = R(y, f(x))\)”; “we do not need a sc-smooth partition of unity”, p. 202). For an open \(V \subseteq X\), a chart of \(X\) whose domain lies in \(V\) is transported to a chart of the subtype \(V\) with the same model Chapter3/RestrictOpenMChart.restrictTo, compatibility is transported Chapter3/RestrictOpenMChart.Compatible.restrictTo, and the charts of \(X\) inside \(V\) form the atlas of the M-polyfold \(V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenMPolyfold.restrictOpen, whose levels are the traces of those of \(X\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenMPolyfold.mem_levelSet_restrictOpen_iff; an sc-smooth map with values in \(V\) is sc-smooth into \(V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.codRestrict_restrictOpen. The restriction \(P|V\) lives on the pull-back \(\iota^*Y = \{(v, y) \mid P(y) = v\}\) of Definition 2.53, as the restricted sections of Definition 5.20 do (§V.23), and its fibres are those of \(P\). A strong bundle chart of \(P\) with base domain inside \(V\) is transported with the same \(F\), \(U\), \(R\), \(K\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundleChart.restrictTo Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundleChart.Compatible.restrictTo, and these charts form the atlas of \(P|V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundle.restrictOpen Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundle.restrictTo_mem_restrictOpen_atlas; every chart of \(P\) restricts to \(\operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundleChart.restrictInter. The restriction \(f|_V\) of an sc-smooth, sc⁺ or regularizing section is again one Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.restrictOpen Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.restrictOpen Chapter3/RestrictOpenStrongBundle.regularizing_restrictOpen. Two choices of the formalization: the paracompactness of \(V\) and of \(\iota^*Y\) is supplied by Theorem 2.16, and \(V\) is nonempty, for the junk values of the transported inverse charts.

Germ data and the index on \(P|V\) (Findings 361, 362). The data of Definition 3.11 on a relatively open \(U\) restrict to every relatively open \(U_0 \subseteq U\) containing \(0\): the germs of the filling and of the sc⁺-part are intersected with \(U_0\), and \(Dr(0)\) and \(\rho(0)\) do not change, so the kernel isomorphism of condition (3) is the same Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsIsFillingGerm.of_subset Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsIsScPlusGerm.of_subset; the strong bundle isomorphism \(\Psi\) of the conjugation is restricted to \(U_0 \triangleleft F \to \psi(U_0) \triangleleft F'\), where \(\psi(U_0) = U' \cap \psi'^{-1}(U_0)\) is relatively open by the continuity of \(\psi'\), and the basic germ is shrunk to \(G \cap \psi'^{-1}(U_0)\) as for \(G''\) (§III.48), with the same \(P_n\), \(Q\), \(h\), \(B\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsConjugationData.ofSubset Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsIsConjugateToBasicGerm.of_subset. So a germ datum at \(x \in V\) survives in its chart restricted to \(\operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundleChart.germData_restrictInter, which is tame when the chart is Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.IsTameChart.restrictInter, and an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data restricts to one on \(P|V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.IsScFredholmSectionTame.restrictOpen. The index. At a zero \(x \in V\), \(f'(x)\) has index \(i\) in every chart of \(P\) iff \((f|_V)'(x)\) has index \(i\) in every chart of \(P|V\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.IsLinOfIndex.restrictOpen Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.IsLinOfIndex.of_restrictOpen. The charts are not compared — a chart of \(P|V\) need not come from one of \(P\) —: in either bundle the index is \(\dim P_n - \dim Q\) for the germ datum (§III.44), whose restriction keeps \(P_n\) and \(Q\) Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.isLinOfIndex_restrictOpen_of_conjugationData, and uniqueness identifies it with \(i\). The same argument passes from \(P|V\) to \(P|W\) for an open \(W \subseteq V\), where the chart restricted to \(\operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap W\) is common to both and the two linearizations agree in it Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalsectionRestrict Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.restrictOpen_of_subset Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsLinOfIndex.restrictOpen_of_subset; Definition 6.1 restricts accordingly Chapter3/RestrictOpenGermsStrongBundle.IsIndexAt.restrictOpen Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsIndexAt.restrictOpen_of_subset.

The stabilizing sections of a chart, without cut-off (Finding 363). In the zero-set argument above, bump functions enter only through Lemma 5.11, as sc⁺-sections through given smooth points of the fibres. That property — through every smooth point \(e\) of the fibre over a smooth point \(x\) there is an sc⁺-section \(s\) with \(s(x) = e\) — is isolated Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalStrongBundle.HasScPlusSectionsThrough. Bump functions give it by Lemma 5.11 Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalMPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough, and so does a chart of the atlas over the whole base, with no cut-off Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalStrongBundle.hasScPlusSectionsThrough_of_chart: \(\hat e = \Phi(e)_2\) is a smooth point of \(F\), with a lift \(\hat e_1 \in F^1\), and the section \(y \mapsto \Phi^{-1}(\varphi(y), R(\varphi(y), \hat e))\) — the text’s \(R(\cdot, e)\) — has the local representative \(z \mapsto R[1](z, \hat e_1)_2\), sc-smooth into \(K[1]\) because the bundle retraction is sc-smooth on \([1]\); it is the cut-off section of Lemma 5.11 with \(\beta = 1\) (§V.9), and its value at \(x\) is \(e\) since \(\Phi(e) \in K\) is fixed by \(R\). The restriction \(P|V\) to a chart domain \(V\) has such a chart: the chart itself, transported to \(V\). The three steps of the zero-set argument — the spanning sections, the tilting sections that put the parametrized section in good position, the local constancy — are repeated with this property in place of bump functions Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalexists_spanning_sections_of_sections Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalexists_sections_isParamGP_of_sections Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalindex_locally_constant_of_sections; the support and norm bounds of Lemma 5.11, which the index argument does not use, are dropped. The index along the zero set with the text’s hypotheses Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocalindex_locally_constant_tame: let \(f\) be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data of any strong bundle and \(x_0\) a zero; then there are an open \(V \ni x_0\) and \(i \in \mathbb Z\) with \(f'(y)\) Fredholm of index \(i\) in every chart at every zero \(y \in V\). Take a chart around \(x_0\) with domain \(V\): \(f|_V\) has tame germ data on \(P|V\), which has sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point, so the index of \(f|_V\) is one integer at its zeros near \(x_0\), and at each of them it is the index on \(P\). In sc form, with the sc-Fredholm property of \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) at every zero in every chart Chapter3/LinearizationChartsScGStrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm, \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) is sc-Fredholm of index \(i\) on every level Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocaltheorem_3_54_index_locally_constant_general_tame. This is the localization that Finding 343 described; the gap \(\operatorname{ind} C(z) = 0\) of Finding 243 remains only without tame germ data.

Definition 6.1 with local sections (Finding 364) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsIndexAtLocal. \(f\) has index \(i\) at \(x\) if there are an open \(V \ni x\) and an sc⁺-section \(s\) of \(P|V\) with \((f|_V + s)(x) = 0\) and \((f|_V + s)'(x)\) Fredholm of index \(i\) in every chart of \(P|V\): the global definition at the beginning of this section, on \(P|V\). Well defined. Two local sections, on \(V\) and on \(V'\), both restrict to \(V \cap V'\) (the restriction of Definition 6.1 to a smaller open set, above), where the uniqueness on \(P|V \cap V'\) applies Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsIndexAtLocal.unique. A global section gives a local one, with \(V = X\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.IsIndexAt.isIndexAtLocal, and at a zero the index is that of \(f'(x)\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.isIndexAtLocal_of_isZeroAt. Existence, without bump functions. On the domain \(V\) of a chart around \(x\), the section through \(f(x)\) of the previous paragraph, negated, is an sc⁺-section \(s\) of \(P|V\) with \((f|_V + s)(x) = 0\), and Theorem 3.15 gives the germ datum of \(f|_V + s\) at \(x\), hence an index Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalStrongBundle.exists_isIndexAtLocal. As for the global reading, a locally constant local index along a map from a preconnected space is constant Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalisIndexAtLocal_const_of_forall_eventually.

Proposition 6.2 with the text’s hypotheses (Finding 365) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalproposition_6_2_local. Let \(f\) be an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data of a strong bundle \(P : Y \to X\) — no bump functions — and \(\varphi : \mathbb R \to X\) an sc-smooth path. Then \(\mathrm{ind}(f, \varphi(t))\), read with local sections, is one integer for all \(t\); any two values of the index at \(\varphi(0)\) and at \(\varphi(1)\) agree Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalproposition_6_2_local'. The proof is that of (E), (S) and Proposition 6.2 above, run near each \(t_0\) on \(P|V\), \(V\) the domain of a chart \(c\) around \(\varphi(t_0)\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalisIndexAtLocal_eventually_const_of_path. The path is reparametrized into \(V\) as in (E), and is then an sc-smooth path of the M-polyfold \(V\). The section along the path is the one of (E) with the cut-off as a datum Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalexists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path_of_bump, taken equal to \(1\), which is possible because the chart \(c|_V\) of \(P|V\) covers its base Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalexists_isScPlusSection_pullback_of_path_of_chart. The product chart of \(c|_V\) covers \(\mathbb R \times V\), so the pull-back has sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point without cut-off Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalhasScPlusSectionsThrough_pullback_rn_of_chart, and the index of \(\tilde f + S\) is constant along the graph near \(t_0\) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalisLinOfIndex_paramLift_sectionAdd_eventually_const_of_sections. The slice relation (S), applied to \(P|V\) unchanged, turns it into \(\mathrm{ind}(f|_V, \varphi(t)) = i - 1\) near \(t_0\), a local index of \(f\), and the connectedness of \(\mathbb R\) ends the proof. Against the text, what remains is the domain of the path: it is \(\mathbb R\), and a path sc-smooth on \([0, 1]\) only is not covered, the project having no M-polyfold \([0, 1]\). The hypotheses on \(f\) are the text’s, tame germ data being the reading of “tame strong bundle” of §III.47.

The two readings agree under bump functions (Finding 367) Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalBumpStrongBundle.isIndexAtLocal_iff_isIndexAt. If \(X\) admits bump functions, a local section of Definition 6.1 gives a global one with the same index Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalBumpStrongBundle.IsIndexAtLocal.isIndexAt: the local section \(s\) on \(V\) is restricted to \(W = \operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap V\) for a chart \(\varphi\) around \(x\), read in that chart as \(\tau : O \to F^1\), and cut off by a bump \(\beta\) supported in \(W\) and equal to \(1\) near \(x\); the cut-off of Lemma 5.11 is made here in a chart of \(P\) that need not belong to the atlas Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalBumpStrongBundle.cutoffSection_mem_oneSet_of_isChart Chapter3/IndexAlongPathsLocalBumpStrongBundle.isScPlusSection_cutoffSection_of_isChart. Then \(f + \beta\tau\) vanishes at \(x\), and its linearization there has the index of \((f|_W + s)'(x)\): the two sections agree where \(\beta = 1\), so the two linearizations coincide in the chart restricted to that set, and the germ datum of \(f + \beta\tau\) at \(x\) carries the index to every chart. So the global definition of the beginning of this section and the text’s local one are the same notion whenever the hypotheses of Chapter 5 hold, and only the text’s is available without them.

Part IV. Manifolds with boundary with corners (HWZ Chapter 4, §§4.1–4.4)

Chapter 4 asks when an M-polyfold — a space glued from images of sc-smooth retractions — is secretly an ordinary manifold with boundary with corners, and why the fibres of a family of such manifolds are good for almost every parameter. The pivot is the sc⁺ condition: a retraction that gains a level. At a smooth point its derivative is compact, so its retract has finite-dimensional tangent spaces (Lemma 4.7), and near a point where the tangent space is in good position to the partial quadrant the retract is the graph of a map over that tangent space (Proposition 4.9). Theorem 4.2 characterizes the manifolds with corners among M-polyfolds by these two properties; Theorem 4.18 applies the characterization to submanifolds in good position; Theorem 4.22 describes a submanifold near a point of general position; Theorem 4.23 combines that description with Sard’s theorem on the strata of the corners. This Part retells: finite-dimensional sc-spaces and corner charts (§IV.1); sc⁺-maps (§IV.2); sc⁺-retractions, Lemmas 4.5 and 4.7 (§IV.3); Proposition 4.8 with its chart form and Remark 4.3 (§IV.4); charts centred at a smooth point, which the text uses and never constructs (§IV.5); Proposition 4.9 with Lemmas 4.11 and 4.12, by a direct proof (§§IV.6–IV.9); Theorem 4.2 (§IV.10); smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds and Remark 4.14 (§IV.11); Proposition 4.15 (§IV.12); good and general position in charts and their chart independence (§IV.13); Lemma 4.19 and Theorem 4.18 (§IV.14); Remark 4.20 (§IV.15); the linear algebra at the corner of a centred chart (§IV.16); Theorem 4.22 (§§IV.17–IV.18) and Remark 4.24 (§IV.19); Sard’s theorem (§IV.20); the finite-dimensional core of Theorem 4.23 (§§IV.21–IV.22); the fibre over a regular value (§IV.23); Theorem 4.23 (§IV.24); what is not formalized (§IV.25); and what the formalization taught us (§IV.26).

What is proved, and what is not. Theorems 4.2, 4.18, 4.22 and 4.23 are proved with the text’s hypotheses; Theorem 4.2 needs no tameness at all. Proposition 4.9 is proved with two hypotheses the text leaves implicit — the good complement \(Y\) is closed, and \(p\) is the projection onto \(T_0O\) along \(Y\) rather than \(Dt(0)\) — and by a direct argument (§§IV.6–IV.9), because the text’s route through Lemma 4.10 and Corollary 3.47 yields the graph map only as a germ over a complement of its own choosing; where Proposition 4.9 is applied (Theorems 4.2, 4.18, 4.22, Remark 4.20), the closed complement is chosen, so nothing is added there. One step of Lemma 4.19 is false and is repaired (§IV.14). Theorem 4.22 (4), which the text leaves to “the previous arguments”, is proved (§IV.18). In Theorem 4.23 “regular value” has to be read as the stratified notion of its proof, and the finite cover of its proof is replaced by a countable one (§IV.24). Proved although the text does not construct it: charts and strong bundle charts centred at a smooth point (§IV.5), an sc⁺-retraction onto the fibre \(A_\lambda\) (§IV.23), Theorem 3.78 in \(C^\infty\) form (§IV.21), and Sard’s theorem in all dimensions (§IV.20). Remark 4.3’s “\(X^1 \ne X\) is possible”, for which the text gives no example, is proved by one, an M-polyfold whose retraction loses a level in its first derivative, with a new criterion for sc-smoothness (§IV.27). Not formalized: Lemma 4.10 (no longer needed), the whole of §4.4 on sc-differential forms, the open question after Proposition 4.15, and the chart independence of stratified regularity (§IV.25).

Five structural choices. (1) sc⁺ is a property of maps. The text defines it for retractions and operators and uses it for maps; here a map is sc⁺ when its lift into \(F^1\) is sc-smooth, and the calculus of such maps is proved first (§IV.2). (2) Tangent spaces of \(X\) are read in charts. \(T_xX\) carries no linear structure in the formalization (gap G.7 of Chapter 2), so \(T_aA\), good position, general position and stratified regularity are stated in a chart, and — except for stratified regularity — proved independent of the chart (§IV.13). (3) Centred charts are re-centred charts. A chart with \(\psi(x) = 0\) is the chart \(\varphi - \varphi(x)\) on the set where the partial quadrant \(C\) agrees with \(C_{\varphi(x)}\), which exists only at smooth points (§IV.5). (4) Proposition 4.9 on fixed sets. The sc-diffeomorphism \(p : O \cap W \to V\) is proved with \(\Gamma = p^{-1}\) sc-smooth on a fixed relatively open \(V\), by contraction arguments on level \(1\), a frame formula for \(D\Gamma\) and a \(C^k\)-bootstrap along the finite-dimensional tangent space. (5) Stratified Sard. Sard’s theorem is applied stratum by stratum in the chart of Theorem 4.22, and the null sets of critical values of countably many charts are collected.
