Throughout, \(C = T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)\) is a partial quadrant presented by an sc-isomorphism \(T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W\), with coordinates \(\lambda_1, \dots, \lambda_n\); \(I(e) = \{i : \lambda_i(e) = 0\}\), \(d_C(e) = \#I(e)\), \(C_e = \{\lambda_i \ge 0, i \in I(e)\}\) and \(E_e = \{\lambda_i = 0, i \in I(e)\}\) (Definition 2.33, §II.12). For a retract \(O = r(U)\) and a level-\(1\) point \(z\), \(T_zO = Dr(z)E_0\) is the tangent space of Definition 2.17 and \(T^R_zO = T_zO \cap E_z\) the reduced tangent space.

IV.1 Finite-dimensional sc-spaces and corner charts (Definition 4.1)

Finite-dimensional sc-spaces. Definition 4.1 models its charts on finite-dimensional spaces “with the constant sc-structure”; the text remarks after Definition 1.1 that a finite-dimensional space has only that one. This is proved. If \(E_0\) is finite-dimensional, every level \(E_m\) is, since it injects into \(E_0\) Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.finiteDimensional_lvl. The range of \(E_m \to E_0\) is then a finite-dimensional, hence closed, subspace; it contains the smooth points, which are dense (Definition 1.1 (2)); so it is all of \(E_0\) Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.toBase_surjective. The inclusions are therefore bijective, and they form an sc-isomorphism of \(E\) onto \(E_0\) with the constant structure Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.scIsoConst; in particular every point of \(E_0\) is smooth Chapter4/CharacterizationScBanach.mem_smooth_of_finiteDimensional. The density axiom is what makes this work: \(E_0 = \mathbb R\), \(E_m = 0\) for \(m \ge 1\) has compact injective inclusions and levels that differ (Findings, Chapter 4, item 6).

Definition 4.1. A chart of \(X\) is a corner chart if its local model is \((U, C, V)\) with \(V\) a finite-dimensional real normed space carrying the constant sc-structure, \(C\) a partial quadrant in \(V\), \(U\) relatively open in \(C\), and the identity retraction Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart. Its model is then relatively open in a partial quadrant Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.isRelOpenInQuadrant, finite-dimensional Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.finiteDimensional, a tame retract — the identity retraction is tame Chapter2/TameScRetraction.id_isTame Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.isTameRetract — and an sc⁺-retract by Remark 4.3 (§IV.4) Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.isScPlusRetract; every point of its model space is smooth Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.mem_smooth. \(X\) has a corner structure if it has an atlas of corner charts equivalent to its own atlas Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.HasCornerStructure. The dimension of \(V\) may vary from chart to chart, as in the text. The text’s “sc-smoothly compatible charts”, “\(\varphi\) an sc-diffeomorphism”, is read as compatibility with the atlas of \(X\), as for tameness (Definition 2.37).

The definition is local Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_iff: \(X\) has a corner structure iff every point lies in a corner chart that is a chart of the M-polyfold structure. One direction takes a chart of the equivalent atlas through the point. For the other, the corner charts that are charts of \(X\) form an atlas: they cover \(X\) by hypothesis, any two charts of \(X\) are compatible Chapter2/MPolyfoldMPolyfold.IsChart.compatible, and the atlas is equivalent to that of \(X\) because each of its members is a chart of \(X\). A corner structure makes \(X\) tame Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.HasCornerStructure.isTame: the same atlas is an atlas of tame charts.

The transition maps are \(C^\infty\). For a chart whose model is relatively open in a partial quadrant, every overlap \(\chi(V \cap V')\) is relatively open Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.isRelOpenInQuadrant_overlap. For compatible corner charts, the transition map is sc-smooth between the overlap retracts; composed with the identity retraction of the overlap it is sc-smooth on a relatively open subset of a partial quadrant in a finite-dimensional space with the constant structure, and such maps are exactly the \(C^\infty\) maps with derivatives within the set Chapter1/ExpositionLemmasisScSmooth_iff_contDiffOn_const Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.contDiffOn_transition. That is the text’s “classically smooth”; “the atlas defines the structure of a smooth manifold with boundary with corners” is not formalized beyond it, because Mathlib’s manifolds with corners have a single model space and here the partial quadrants vary from chart to chart.

Arbitrary finite-dimensional models. The constant structure is no restriction. A partial quadrant of a finite-dimensional \(E\) is one of \(E_0\) with the constant structure Chapter4/CharacterizationIsPartialQuadrant.toConst Chapter4/CharacterizationIsRelOpenInQuadrant.toConst, and the identity of \(E_0\) is an sc-diffeomorphism between the two models Chapter4/CharacterizationIsRelOpenInQuadrant.isScDiffeoQuadrant_toConst. Composing a chart with it (the construction \(\mathtt{compDiffeo}\) of Chapter 3) Chapter3/GlobalIFTCenterMChart.compDiffeo gives, with the same map and domain, a corner chart of the same dimension Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.exists_isCornerChart_of_finiteDimensional. Hence \(X\) has a corner structure iff it has an equivalent atlas of charts onto relatively open subsets of partial quadrants in sc-Banach spaces with finite-dimensional \(E_0\) Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_iff_finiteDimensional — verbatim the definition of the manifolds with corners of locally constant dimension of Theorem 3.27 (§III.36) — and the manifolds with corners of dimension \(n\) of Theorem 3.27 are the corner structures all of whose charts have dimension \(n\) Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.isManifoldWithCorners_iff Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.IsManifoldWithCorners.hasCornerStructure.

IV.2 Sc⁺-maps

The text uses “sc⁺-map” in the proof of Lemma 4.7 and composes sc⁺-retractions with sc-smooth maps in Lemma 4.5, but defines sc⁺ only for retractions (Definition 4.4) and operators (Definition 1.4). The formalization defines it for maps on any set, as the neighbouring notions of the project are (sc⁺-operators are sc-operators into \(F^1\), sc⁺-sections sc-smooth maps into \(K[1]\)).

The lift. For \(x \in E_1 \subseteq E_0\), \(1_0^1 x\) is the point of \(E_1\) over \(x\), with a junk value off \(E_1\) Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.liftOne Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.toBase_liftOne Chapter4/ScPlusScBanach.liftOne_toBase.

Definition. \(f\) is sc⁺ on \(U\) if \(f(U) \subseteq F_1\) and the lift \(x \mapsto 1_0^1 f(x)\), a map \(U \to F^1\), is sc-smooth Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus. Then \(f(U_m) \subseteq F_{m+1}\): the lift is sc⁰, so it maps \(U_m\) into \((F^1)_m = F_{m+1}\) Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.mem_range_succ. On an sc-domain the canonical lift can be replaced by any sc-smooth \(g : U \to F^1\) with \(\iota \circ g = f\), which is how the text phrases it Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.iff_exists. The calculus: an sc⁺-map is sc-smooth, being \(\iota \circ\) (lift) with the sc-operator \(\iota : F^1 \to F\) Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.isScSmooth; the property depends only on the values on \(U\) Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.congr and passes to smaller sc-domains Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.mono; sc⁺ ∘ sc-smooth is sc⁺, the lift of \(g \circ f\) being (lift of \(g\)) \(\circ f\), sc-smooth by the chain rule Chapter1/ChainRuleIsScSmooth.comp Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.comp_isScSmooth; sc-smooth ∘ sc⁺ is sc⁺, the lift of \(g \circ f\) being \(g^1 \circ\) (lift of \(f\)) with \(g^1 : V^1 \to G^1\) the map \(g\) induces on level \(1\), sc-smooth by Proposition 1.17 Chapter1/LevelsIsScSmooth.shift Chapter4/ScPlusIsScSmooth.comp_isScPlus; and an sc⁺-operator is an sc⁺-map Chapter4/ScPlusScPlus.isScPlus.

The derivative at a smooth point Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.exists_scPlus_deriv. Let \(f\) be sc⁺ on an sc-domain \(U\) and \(x \in U_1\) smooth. The lift \(g\) is sc-smooth into \(F^1\), so its derivative at the smooth point \(x\) is an sc-operator \(E \to F^1\) (the remark after Proposition 1.16), that is an sc⁺-operator \(S : E \to F\). Since \(f = \iota \circ g\) on \(U\), the chain rule and the uniqueness of the derivative on an sc-domain give \(Df(x) = \iota \circ Dg(x)\), the level-\(0\) operator of \(S\). This is the text’s step “\(Dr(o)\) is a sc⁺-operator, since \(r\) is a sc⁺-map”. Consequently \(Df(x)\) is compact, and so is every level operator of \(S\) Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlus.isCompactOperator_deriv.

A compact projection has finite-dimensional range Chapter4/ScPlusfiniteDimensional_range_of_isCompactOperator_of_idem: if \(P = P \circ P\) is compact, its range is the closed set \(\{v : Pv = v\}\), \(P\) restricts to a compact operator of the range which is the identity, and a normed space with compact identity is finite-dimensional (Riesz). The text takes this for granted.

IV.3 Sc⁺-retractions and sc⁺-retracts (Definitions 4.4, 4.6, Lemmas 4.5, 4.7)

Definition 4.4. An sc-smooth retraction \(r : U \to U\) is an sc⁺-retraction if it is an sc⁺-map on \(U\) Chapter4/ScPlusScRetraction.IsScPlus. The text’s condition \(r(U_m) \subseteq U_{m+1}\) is then a consequence, not a hypothesis Chapter4/ScPlusScRetraction.IsScPlus.mem_lvlSet_succ. On an open subset \(V\) of an M-polyfold, an sc⁺-retraction is a map \(s\), sc-smooth on \(V\), with \(s(V) \subseteq V\), \(s \circ s = s\) on \(V\), \(s(V) \subseteq X_1\), and \(1_0^1 \circ s : V \to X^1\) sc-smooth Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.IsScPlusRetractionOn; the junk value of \(1_0^1\) off \(X_1\) is quantified over and plays no role.

Lemma 4.5 Chapter4/ScPluslemma_4_5. If \(t\) is an sc⁺-retraction onto \(O\) and \(s\) an sc-smooth retraction (of a possibly different relatively open set) onto \(O\), then \(s\) is sc⁺. The text’s proof: \(s\) maps its domain into \(O\), which lies in the domain of \(t\), and \(t\) fixes \(O\), so \(s = t \circ s\), which is sc⁺ ∘ sc-smooth. (The text writes “\(s(V) = 0\)” for \(s(V) = O\).)

Definition 4.6. \((O, C, E)\) is an sc⁺-retract if it is the retract of an sc⁺-retraction Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlusRetract; it is then a retract Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlusRetract.isScRetract, every sc-smooth retraction onto it is sc⁺ by Lemma 4.5 Chapter4/ScPlusIsScPlusRetract.isScPlus, and so the property is intrinsic Chapter4/ScPlusisScPlusRetract_iff_forall.

Lemma 4.7 (i) Chapter4/ScPluslemma_4_7_i. The retract of an sc⁺-retraction consists of smooth points. By induction on \(m\): a point \(y \in O\) lies in \(E_m\); then \(y \in U_m\), and \(y = r(y) \in E_{m+1}\) by the level gain. (ii) Chapter4/ScPluslemma_4_7_ii. At a level-\(1\) point \(o\) over a point of \(O\), \(Dr(o)E_0\) is finite-dimensional. \(o\) is smooth by (i), so \(Dr(o)\) is compact (§IV.2); it is a projection because \(r \circ r = r\) gives \(Dr(o) \circ Dr(o) = Dr(o)\) at points of \(O\) Chapter2/RetractsScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self; and a compact projection has finite-dimensional range. In the form with the tangent space of Definition 2.17 Chapter4/ScPluslemma_4_7_ii_tangentSpace: every \(o \in O\) has a smooth lift \(o_1 \in E_1\) Chapter2/TameRetractsexists_smoothLvl_one_of_mem_smooth, and \(T_{o_1}O\) is the range of \(Dr(o_1)\) Chapter2/RetractstangentSpace_eq_coe_submodule, finite-dimensional. Tangent spaces are indexed by level-\(1\) points, which is why the statement mentions the lift.

IV.4 Proposition 4.8, its chart form, and Remark 4.3

Proposition 4.8 Chapter4/ScPlusproposition_4_8. A retract \((O, C, E)\) is an sc⁺-retract iff \(O \subseteq E_\infty\) and the lift \(1_0^1\) is sc-smooth from \((O, C, E)\) to \((O_1, C_1, E^1)\) in the sense of Definition 2.7. (⇒) \(O \subseteq E_\infty\) is Lemma 4.7 (i); and by the criterion of Definition 2.7 through one retraction Chapter2/RetractsisScSmoothRetractMap_iff_exists, the lift is sc-smooth between the retracts because \(1_0^1 \circ r\) is the lift of the sc⁺-map \(r\). (⇐) For a retraction \(r\) onto \(O\), the composite \(U \to O \to O_1 \to E^1\) is sc-smooth (Definition 2.7, the field \(\mathtt{comp\_isScSmooth}\) of Chapter2/RetractsIsScSmoothRetractMap) and is the lift of \(r\), whose values lie in \(E_1\) because \(O \subseteq E_\infty\). The text’s proof is complete; it ends “the lemma is proved”.

The chart form. Theorem 4.2 needs the statement for the charts of an M-polyfold, which the text does not state. The map \(1_0^1 : X \to X^1\) is defined on \(X_1\), with a junk value \(x_0\) off it Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.toLevelOne Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.levelVal_toLevelOne Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.toLevelOne_levelVal. In the chart \(\varphi\) of \(X\) and the level chart \((V_1, \varphi, (O_1, C_1, E^1))\) of \(X^1\) Chapter2/LevelPolyfoldMPolyfold.levelChart it is the lift \(O \to O_1\) Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.levelChart_toLevelOne. A point of a chart domain is smooth iff its image is Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.mem_smoothSet_iff. So the model of a chart \(\varphi : V \to O\) is an sc⁺-retract iff \(V \subseteq X_\infty\) and \(1_0^1\) is sc-smooth on \(V\) Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.proposition_4_8_chart: (⇒) continuity on \(V\) comes from the lift read in the charts, and sc-smoothness is checked in the pair of charts \(\varphi\), \(\mathtt{levelChart}\,\varphi\) Chapter2/LevelPolyfoldIsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts, where it is Proposition 4.8; (⇐) the same pair of charts turns the sc-smoothness of \(1_0^1\) on \(V\) into that of the lift on \(O\). Hence “\(X_0 = X_\infty\) and \(1_0^1\) sc-smooth” holds iff every chart of \(X\) is modelled on an sc⁺-retract Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_toLevelOne_iff, and already if some cover of \(X\) by such charts exists Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_toLevelOne_of_cover — sc-smoothness being local.

Remark 4.3. The inclusion \(\iota : (O_1, C_1, E^1) \to (O, C, E)\) is sc-smooth between retracts Chapter4/ScPlusisScSmoothRetractMap_toBase_one, so \(1_1^0 : X^1 \to X\) is always sc-smooth, being \(\iota\) in the charts \(\mathtt{levelChart}\,\varphi\) and \(\varphi\) Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.remark_4_3_levelVal. If every point lies in \(X_1\) and \(1_0^1\) is sc-smooth, it is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse \(1_1^0\) Chapter4/ScPlusMPolyfold.remark_4_3_isScDiffeo. For a finite-dimensional \(V\) with the constant structure, \(V^1 = V\) definitionally, the lift is the identity, and every retract in \(V\) is an sc⁺-retract, its retraction being its own lift Chapter4/ScPlusremark_4_3_const. The remark’s “it is possible that \(X^1 \ne X\) as M-polyfolds although the sets agree” is given without an example; one is constructed in §IV.27.

IV.5 Charts centred at a smooth point

Theorem 4.2 (ii) asks for charts with \(\psi(x) = 0\), the proofs of Theorems 4.18 and 4.22 and of Lemma 5.11 use them, and the text never says where they come from. Translating a chart \(\varphi : V \to O \subseteq C\) by \(e = \varphi(x)\) fails twice: translation by \(e\) preserves every level only if \(e\) is smooth, and \(C - e\) is not a partial quadrant unless \(e \in C \cap (-C)\). The construction (Findings, items 1, 2) uses the partial quadrant \(C_e\) and the neighbourhood on which it agrees with \(C\).

The partial quadrant \(C_e\) and the neighbourhood \(G(e)\). Let \(G(e) = \{v : \lambda_i(v) > 0\) whenever \(\lambda_i(e) \ne 0\}\) Chapter4/RecentrerecentreNbhd, open Chapter4/RecentreisOpen_recentreNbhd and containing \(e\) when \(e \in C\) Chapter4/Recentremem_recentreNbhd. On it \(C\) and \(C_e\) agree: \(G(e) \cap C = G(e) \cap C_e\), because on \(G(e)\) the coordinates not vanishing at \(e\) are positive anyway Chapter4/RecentrerecentreNbhd_inter_eq. \(C_e\) is invariant under translation by \(e\) Chapter4/Recentreadd_mem_partialQuadrantAtWith_iff, so \(C_e - e = C_e\) Chapter4/Recentreimage_sub_partialQuadrantAtWith. \(C_e\) is a partial quadrant — Definition 2.33 asserts it without proof: the vanishing indices \(I(e)\) Chapter4/RecentrezeroIdx, \(d = \#I(e)\) of them Chapter4/RecentrerecentreDim, are put first, \(\mathbb R^n \cong \mathbb R^{I(e)} \times \mathbb R^{\text{rest}}\) Chapter4/RecentresplitCoordsL, which gives an sc-isomorphism \(\mathbb R^n \oplus W \cong \mathbb R^{I(e)} \oplus (\mathbb R^{\text{rest}} \oplus W)\) Chapter4/RecentresplitCoordsIso and the presentation \(T_e\) of \(C_e\) Chapter4/RecentrerecentreIso Chapter4/RecentrepartialQuadrantAtWith_eq_preimage Chapter4/RecentreisPartialQuadrant_partialQuadrantAtWith: the coordinates not vanishing at \(e\) join the linear factor. Re-centring keeps the tame data near \(e\). For \(v \in G(e)\) the vanishing coordinates of \(v - e\) for \(T_e\) are those of \(v\) for \(T\) Chapter4/RecentrerecentreIso_fst_sub Chapter4/Recentrezero_of_mem_recentreNbhd, so \(d_{C_e}(v - e) = d_C(v)\) Chapter4/RecentredegIndexWith_recentreIso Chapter4/RecentredegIndex_sub_recentre, and the minimal subspaces and partial quadrants agree: \(E^{T_e}_{v - e} = E^T_v\) Chapter4/RecentreminimalSubspaceWith_recentreIso, \((C_e)_{v - e} = C_v\) Chapter4/RecentrepartialQuadrantAtWith_recentreIso.

Translations. Translation by a smooth vector \(a\) is sc-smooth on every sc-domain: its level maps are \(x \mapsto x + a_m\), \(a_m\) the lift of \(a\) to \(E_m\), and the criterion of Proposition 1.19 applies Chapter1/LevelsIsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_levels Chapter4/RecentreisScSmooth_add_const Chapter4/RecentreisScSmooth_sub_const. Re-centred retracts. IV.6 Proposition 4.9: the data, and the mean value estimate

The text. Let \(t : U \to U\) be an sc⁺-retraction onto \(O \ni 0\) with \(T_0O\) in good position to \(C\), \(Y\) a good complement and \(p = Dt(0)\) “the sc-projection”. Then \(p\) maps a neighbourhood of \(0\) in \(O\) sc-diffeomorphically onto one in \(T_0O \cap C\). The proof: the section \(\mathbf f(u) = (1 - p)(u - t(u))\) of \(U \triangleleft Y\) is sc-Fredholm (Lemma 4.10), Corollary 3.47 describes its zeros near \(0\) as a graph \(\{a + \delta(a)\}\), Lemma 4.11 says that every small zero is on the graph, Lemma 4.12 that the graph lies in \(O\).

What changes, and why. (a) \(Dt(0)\) is a projection onto \(T_0O\) along \(\ker Dt(0)\), which nothing relates to \(Y\); Lemma 4.12 writes \(t(a + \delta(a)) = p\,t(a + \delta(a)) + \delta(a)\) with \(\delta(a) \in Y\), which needs the projection along \(Y\). (b) \(Y\) must be closed, or that projection is not continuous. (c) Corollary 3.47 gives \(\delta\) over a complement of its own choosing and sc-smooth only as a germ — \(C^k\) into \(E_m\) on neighbourhoods shrinking with \(m\) and \(k\) (§III.20) — while the claim is an sc-diffeomorphism between fixed open sets. The formalization therefore takes \(p\) to be the projection along a closed \(Y\) and proves the proposition directly, with the sc⁺ property doing the work of the Fredholm theory (Findings, items 20–28).

The data Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData: the sc⁺-retraction \(t\) with \(0 \in O\); \(N\) with \(N = T_0O\), which equals \(Dt(0)E_0\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.N_eq_range and is finite-dimensional by Lemma 4.7 Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.finiteDimensional; \(N\) in good position; a good complement \(Y\), closed; and \(p : E_0 \to N\) continuous linear with \(p = 1\) on \(N\), \(p = 0\) on \(Y\). The tangent space consists of smooth points: \(Dt(0)\) is an sc⁺-operator and \(N\) its fixed vectors Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.smooth. \(Y = \ker p\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.mem_Y_iff. Because \(N \subseteq E_\infty\) is finite-dimensional, it lifts continuously to every level Chapter3/TangentGermfinSmoothLift Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.liftN, and \(p\), \(q = 1 - p\) act on every level \(E_m\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.pL Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.qL. The identities the text uses hold for this \(p\) on every level: \((1 - p)Dt(0) = 0\), because the range of \(Dt(0)\) is \(N\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.qL_lvlDeriv_zero, and \(Dt(0) = 1\) on \(N\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.lvlDeriv_zero_of_mem_N. The good complement has a constant \(\varepsilon\): for \(n \in N\), \(y \in Y\), \(|y|_0 \le \varepsilon|n|_0\), \(n \in C \iff n + y \in C\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.eps Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.eps_spec. Its level-\(1\) version is \(\varepsilon' = \varepsilon/(\|\iota_1\|\|\mathrm{lift}_N\| + 1)\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.eps': \(|y|_1 \le \varepsilon'|a|_1\) implies \(|y|_0 \le \varepsilon|a|_0\) for \(a \in N\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.norm_toBase_le_eps_mul.

The level data of an sc⁺-retraction. The lift \(t^1 : U \to E^1\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.liftOne is sc-smooth Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.IsScPlus.isScSmooth_liftOne, sc¹ with derivative family \(Dt^1\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.liftDeriv Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.IsScPlus.isSc1With_liftOne. The mean value estimate (the text’s (76)–(77)). The abstract form Chapter4/ScPlusGraphexists_norm_sub_sub_le_of_hasFDerivWithinAt: if \(s\) is differentiable within a convex set \(S\) with derivative \(D\) continuous at \(u_0 \in S\), then for every \(\theta > 0\) there is \(r > 0\) with \(|s(z') - s(z) - D(u_0)(z' - z)| \le \theta|z' - z|\) for \(z, z' \in S \cap B(u_0, r)\) — the mean value inequality for \(s - D(u_0)\). For an sc⁺-retraction Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_mvt: at \(u_0 \in U_{k+1}\) a ball meets \(C_{k+1}\) inside \(U_{k+1}\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.exists_ball_inter_subset Chapter4/ScPlusGraphScRetraction.lvlSet_U_subset_lvlSet_C, the set \(C_{k+1} \cap B(u_0, r_0)\) is convex, and the abstract form and the continuity of \(Dt\) give \(r\) with \(C_{k+1} \cap B(u_0, r) \subseteq U_{k+1}\), \(\|Dt(z) - Dt(u_0)\| \le \theta\) and the estimate with constant \(\theta\) there. The text integrates along segments in \(U_{k+1}\), which need not be convex; the convex set \(C_{k+1} \cap B\) is the repair.

A shortcut does not work: inverting \(p \circ t\) on the finite-dimensional quadrant \(N \cap C\) by Proposition 3.73. In \(\mathbb R^3\) with \(C = [0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R\), \(\Gamma(a) = (a_1, a_2, a_2^2)\) and \(t(x) = \Gamma(x_1 + (x_3 - x_2^2)^2, x_2)\), \(t\) is a retraction with \(N = \mathbb R^2 \times 0\), but \(p\,t(x_1, x_2, 0) = (x_1 + x_2^4, x_2)\) misses \((0, y_2)\) for \(y_2 > 0\).

IV.7 Lemmas 4.11 and 4.12: uniqueness and existence on level 1

Lemma 4.11, the contraction estimate Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.exists_contraction_radius. For \(\theta > 0\) the mean value estimate at \(u_0 = 0\) gives \(r > 0\) with the estimates of §IV.6 on \(C_{k+1} \cap B(0, r)\) and, for \(u, u' \in O_{k+1}\) with norms below \(r\), \(|(1 - p)(u' - u)|_{k+1} \le \|1 - p\|\theta|u' - u|_{k+1}\): since \(u = t(u)\), \(u' = t(u')\) and \((1 - p)Dt(0) = 0\), \((1 - p)(u' - u) = (1 - p)[t(u') - t(u) - Dt(0)(u' - u)]\). Uniqueness Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.eq_of_p_eq: if \(p(u) = p(u')\) and \(|(1 - p)(u' - u)| \le c|u' - u|\) with \(c < 1\), then \(u' - u \in Y\), so \((1 - p)(u' - u) = u' - u\) and \(u' = u\). This is what the text’s Lemma 4.11 is used for; its statement, “\(y = \delta(a)\)”, presupposes the \(\delta\) of Corollary 3.47.

Lemma 4.12, existence by a contraction Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.exists_graph_point. Suppose the estimates hold on \(C_1 \cap B(0, r)\) with \(\theta < 1\), \(\|1 - p\|\theta < 1\) and \(\|1 - p\|\theta(1 + \varepsilon') \le \varepsilon'\). As \(t(0) = 0\) and \(t : U_1 \to E_1\) is continuous at \(0\), there is \(\delta\) with \(|t(u)|_1 < r\) for \(|u|_1 < \delta\); put \(r' = \min(r, \delta)\) and \(\rho = r'/(1 + \varepsilon')\). For \(a \in N \cap C\) with \(|a|_1 < \rho\):

  1. The set \(B_a = \{y \in Y_1 : |y|_1 \le \varepsilon'|a|_1\}\) is closed, hence complete, because \(Y\) is closed — the first use of that hypothesis.
  2. For \(y \in B_a\), \(a + y \in C_1\) by the good complement property, \(|y|_0 \le \varepsilon|a|_0\) coming from \(|y|_1 \le \varepsilon'|a|_1\); and \(|a + y|_1 \le (1 + \varepsilon')|a|_1 < r'\). So \(a + y\) lies in \(U_1\), where \(t\) is defined — a point the text does not check.
  3. \(\Phi_a(y) = (1 - p)t(a + y)\) maps \(B_a\) into itself: \(\Phi_a(y) = (1 - p)[t(a + y) - t(0) - Dt(0)(a + y)]\), of norm at most \(\|1 - p\|\theta(1 + \varepsilon')|a|_1 \le \varepsilon'|a|_1\), and it lies in \(Y\).
  4. \(\Phi_a\) is a contraction with constant \(\|1 - p\|\theta < 1\), by the estimate between \(a + y\) and \(a + y'\).
  5. Its fixed point \(y\) (Banach’s theorem on the complete \(B_a\)) gives \(u = a + y\) with \((1 - p)(t(u) - u) = 0\), i.e. \(w - u \in N\) for \(w = t(u)\). Now \(w \in O\), \(|w|_1 < r\) by the choice of \(\delta\), \(t(w) = w\), and \(Dt(0)(w - u) = w - u\). The estimate between \(u\) and \(w\) reads \(|t(w) - t(u) - Dt(0)(w - u)|_1 = |w - u|_1 \le \theta|w - u|_1\), so \(w = u\): \(u = t(u) \in O\) — the text’s argument “\(a_1 = a\)”.

So \(u \in O_1\), \(p(u) = a\), \(u - a \in Y\), \(|u - a|_1 \le \varepsilon'|a|_1\) and \(|u|_1 < r\). The text’s “\(|a(\tau)|_1 \le \varepsilon_1\) if \(|a|_0 < \varepsilon\)” is the level-\(1\) continuity of \(t\) at \(0\) used in step 5.

IV.8 The step \(p(O \cap W) \subseteq C\), and the neighbourhoods

\(p\) maps points of \(O\) near \(0\) into \(C\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.p_mem_C, which the conclusion “\(p : U_0 \to V \subseteq T_0O \cap C\)” needs and the text never checks. If \(u \in O_1\) has \(|(1 - p)u|_1 \le \kappa|u|_1\) with \(\kappa \le \frac12\), then \(|u|_1 \le |pu|_1 + \frac12|u|_1\), so \(|u|_1 \le 2|pu|_1 \le 2\|\mathrm{lift}_N\||pu|_0\), and \(|(1 - p)u|_0 \le \|\iota_1\|\kappa|u|_1 \le 2\|\iota_1\|\kappa\|\mathrm{lift}_N\||pu|_0\); if that constant is at most \(\varepsilon\), the good complement property gives \(p(u) \in C \iff p(u) + (1 - p)u = u \in C\), and \(u \in O \subseteq C\). The hypothesis on \(u\) is the contraction estimate between \(0\) and \(u\).

The neighbourhoods Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.exists_nbhd. For every \(\theta_0 > 0\) the proof chooses, in this order:

  1. \(\theta = \min(\theta_0, \theta_1, \theta_2)\) with \(\theta_1 = \varepsilon'/(2(\|1 - p\| + 1)(1 + \varepsilon'))\) (so that \(\|1 - p\|\theta \le \frac12\) and \(\|1 - p\|\theta(1 + \varepsilon') \le \varepsilon'\), for Lemmas 4.11 and 4.12) and \(\theta_2 = \varepsilon/(2\|\iota_1\|\|\mathrm{lift}_N\|(\|1 - p\| + 1) + 1)\) (for \(p(O \cap W) \subseteq C\));
  2. \(r\) from the contraction estimate on level \(1\), and \(\rho\) and the graph points \(u(a)\) from Lemma 4.12;
  3. \(\delta_0\) from the continuity of the lift \(t^1 : U \to E_1\) at \(0\) on level \(0\): \(|t(u)|_1 < r\) for \(u \in U\), \(|u|_0 < \delta_0\);
  4. \(\rho' = \min(\rho, r/(1 + \varepsilon'), \delta_0/(\|\iota_1\|(1 + \varepsilon') + 1))\), the open \(V' = \{a \in N : |a|_1 < \rho'\}\) of \(N\), \(V = V' \cap C\), and \(W = B_0(0, \delta_0) \cap p^{-1}(V')\), open in \(E_0\);
  5. \(\Gamma(a) = u(a)\) for \(a \in V\).

Then \(\Gamma(a) \in O \cap W\) (on level \(0\), \(|\Gamma(a)|_0 \le \|\iota_1\|(1 + \varepsilon')|a|_1 < \delta_0\)), \(p\Gamma(a) = a\), \(\Gamma(a) - a \in Y\), \(|\Gamma(a)|_1 < r\). A point \(u_0 \in O \cap W\) satisfies \(u_0 = t(u_0)\), hence \(|u_0|_1 < r\) by step 3 — this is how a neighbourhood open on level \(0\) is controlled on level \(1\), the sc⁺ property a second time; the contraction estimate between \(0\) and \(u_0\) and the first constraint on \(\theta\) then give \(p(u_0) \in C\), so \(p(u_0) \in V\), and uniqueness gives \(\Gamma(p(u_0)) = u_0\). Also \(\|Dt(z) - Dt(0)\|_{\mathcal L(E_1)} \le \theta_0\) on \(C_1 \cap B(0, r)\), and \(|(1 - p)(u' - u)|_1 \le \frac12|u' - u|_1\) on \(O_1 \cap B_1(0, r)\). Consequently \(\Gamma(V) = O \cap W\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.image_V, \(\Gamma(0) = 0\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.Γ_zero, and \(p\) is injective on \(O \cap W\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.injOn_p.

If \(\Gamma_{j+k+1}\) and \(w : V \to N\) are \(C^k\), then so is \(a \mapsto Dt_j(\Gamma_{j+1}(a))\,\mathrm{lift}(w(a))\) Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_lvlDeriv_Γ; in particular \(a \mapsto A(\Gamma(a))\) is \(C^k\) when \(\Gamma_{k+1}\) is Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_A_Γ, and so is its inverse, inversion being smooth on the invertible operators Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_M_Γ. Now induct on \(k\), for all levels at once Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_Γ_lvl: \(\Gamma_{j+1}\) is \(C^0\) (continuity); if every \(\Gamma_{j'+1}\) is \(C^k\), the derivative \(a \mapsto \mathrm{frame}_j(\Gamma_{j+1}(a))\) applied to \(n\) is \(Dt_j(\Gamma_{j+1}(a))\mathrm{lift}(M(\Gamma_1(a))n)\), which is \(C^k\) because \(\Gamma_{j+k+1}\) is (the hypothesis at \(j' = j + k\)) and \(M(\Gamma_1(\cdot))n\) is (the hypothesis at \(j' = k\), through \(A\)); so \(\Gamma_{j+1}\) is \(C^{k+1}\). Derivatives of \(t\) are only ever applied to the smooth vectors of the finite-dimensional \(N\), so the loss of levels in \(Tt\) is absorbed by \(\Gamma\) being \(C^k\) into every level and does not accumulate. Hence \(\Gamma\) is \(C^\infty\) into every level Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_Γ_lvl_succ_infty Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.contDiffOn_Γ_lvl_infty and sc-smooth on \(V\) by the criterion of Proposition 1.19 for a finite-dimensional source Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.isScSmooth_Γ.

The sc-diffeomorphism. \((O \cap W, C, E)\) is a retract (Proposition 2.10 (1)) Chapter2/Retractsproposition_2_10_1 Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.isScRetract_inter_W; \((V, N \cap C, N)\) is a local model, \(N \cap C\) being a partial quadrant of \(N\) (Proposition 3.22) and \(V\) relatively open in it Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.V_isRelOpenInQuadrant Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.isScRetract_V. \(p\) is sc-smooth \(E \to N\) as a continuous linear map into a finite-dimensional space (Corollary 1.20) Chapter1/LevelsIsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.p_isScSmooth, so \(p\) and \(\Gamma\) are sc-smooth between the retracts Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.p_isScSmoothRetractMap Chapter4/ScPlusGraphGraphData.Nbhd.Γ_isScSmoothRetractMap.

Proposition 4.9 Chapter4/ScPlusGraphproposition_4_9. Statement. Let \(t\) be an sc⁺-retraction onto \(O \ni 0\), \(N = T_0O\) in good position to \(C\), \(Y\) a closed good complement of \(N\) and \(p : E_0 \to N\) the projection along \(Y\). There are an open \(W \ni 0\) in \(E_0\), a relatively open \(V \ni 0\) of \(N \cap C\) and \(\Gamma : N \to E_0\), sc-smooth on \(V\), with \(p \circ \Gamma = 1\) on \(V\), \(\Gamma(a) - a \in Y\), \(\Gamma(V) = O \cap W\), \(\Gamma \circ p = 1\) on \(O \cap W\), \(\Gamma(0) = 0\), and \(p\), \(\Gamma\) sc-smooth between \((O \cap W, C, E)\) and \((V, N \cap C, N)\). Proof. \(\theta_0\) from the frame condition, the neighbourhoods of §IV.8 for it, and the regularity above. The finite dimension of \(N\), an instance argument needed to form \(N\) as an sc-Banach space, is Lemma 4.7 Chapter4/ScPlusGraphfiniteDimensional_tangentSpace_zero.

IV.10 Theorem 4.2: the characterization

Statement Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.theorem_4_2_general. For every M-polyfold \(X\) and every junk value \(x_0 \in X_1\) of \(1_0^1\), the following are equivalent. (i) \(X\) has a corner structure. (ii) Every point of \(X\) is smooth, \(1_0^1 : X \to X^1\) is sc-smooth, and every \(x\) lies in a chart \(\psi\) of \(X\) with \(\psi(x) = 0\) whose model is a tame retract and whose tangent space \(N = T_0O\) is finite-dimensional and in good position to \(C\). The text’s form, for tame \(X\), is the same statement with an unused hypothesis Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.theorem_4_2. Tameness is used neither in the text’s proof nor here, and (i) implies it (§IV.1).

Charts composed with an sc-diffeomorphism between retracts. The proof of (ii) ⇒ (i) composes a chart with \(p\), which is an sc-diffeomorphism between retracts, not between relatively open sets, so the construction of Chapter 3 does not apply. For a chart \(\varphi\) onto \((O, C, E)\) and mutually inverse \(f\), \(g\) sc-smooth between \((O, C, E)\) and \((O', C', E')\), \(f \circ \varphi\) is a chart onto \((O', C', E')\) Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.compRetract, and a chart of the M-polyfold when \(\varphi\) is Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.compRetract_isChart: for a chart \(\varphi'\) of \(X\) the transition maps are \((\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ g\) and \(f \circ (\varphi \circ \varphi'^{-1})\), compositions of maps sc-smooth between retracts (Theorem 2.8) Chapter2/RetractsIsScSmoothRetractMap.comp. This is the compatibility the text’s “we obtain a smoothly compatible atlas” skips (Findings, item 55).

(i) ⇒ (ii). Corner charts are modelled on sc⁺-retracts, so every point is smooth and \(1_0^1\) is sc-smooth by Proposition 4.8 on a cover (§IV.4). The text stops here; (ii) also asks for a centred tame chart with \(T_0O\) finite-dimensional and in good position (Findings, item 53). Let \(x\) lie in a corner chart \(\chi\). Its image is smooth (§IV.1), so the re-centred chart \(\psi = \chi - \chi(x)\) exists; its model is a relatively open subset of \(C_{\chi(x)}\) in the same finite-dimensional space Chapter4/Characterizationimage_sub_const_eq_preimage_add' Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.exists_centred. With the identity retraction it is a tame retract; the tangent space of a relatively open subset of a partial quadrant is the whole space, because the derivative of the identity retraction is the identity Chapter4/CharacterizationtangentSpace_relOpen; and the whole space is in good position to every partial quadrant, with the complement \(0\), the interior of a partial quadrant being nonempty Chapter4/CharacterizationisInGoodPosition_top Chapter4/CharacterizationMChart.IsCornerChart.exists_centred_tame.

(ii) ⇒ (i). The data of the corner chart Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData for a chart \(\psi\) and a finite-dimensional \(N\): a closed good complement \(Y\), the projection \(p\) along it, \(W\), \(V\), \(\Gamma\) with \(p\), \(\Gamma\) mutually inverse and sc-smooth between \((O \cap W, C, E)\) and \((V, N \cap C, N)\). They exist when the model of \(\psi\) is an sc⁺-retract containing \(0\) and \(N = T_0O\) is in good position Chapter4/Characterizationexists_cornerChartData: here no complement is prescribed, so one can be chosen — the normal form of Proposition 3.22 gives a continuous projection onto \(N\) whose kernel is a good complement, closed, even mapping \(C\) into \(C\) Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_proj_goodComplement — and Proposition 4.9 is applied to an sc⁺-retraction onto \(O\) (Definition 4.6). The issue “\(p = Dt(0)\)” of §IV.6 does not arise, and nothing is added to Theorem 4.2 (Findings, item 54). The chart \(p \circ \psi\) on \(\psi^{-1}(W)\) Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.chart is \(\psi\) restricted to \(\psi^{-1}(W)\) composed with \(p\) by \(\mathtt{compRetract}\), modelled on \((V, N \cap C, N)\) Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.model; it is a corner chart Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.chart_isCornerChart, a chart of \(X\) Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.chart_isChart, contains \(x\) when \(\psi(x) = 0\) Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.mem_chart_source and sends it to \(0\) Chapter4/CharacterizationCornerChartData.chart_apply_eq_zero. At every point Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.theorem_4_2_chart: if all points are smooth and \(1_0^1\) is sc-smooth, the model of every chart is an sc⁺-retract (§IV.4), so for a chart \(\psi\) with \(\psi(x) = 0\) and \(N = T_0O\) finite-dimensional and in good position the corner chart \(p \circ \psi\) exists. With such a chart at every point, \(X\) has a corner structure by the local form of Definition 4.1 Chapter4/CharacterizationMPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_of_centred — whether or not the charts \(\psi\) are tame.

IV.11 Smooth finite-dimensional submanifolds; the chart retraction; Remark 4.14

Definition 4.13. \(A \subseteq X\) is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold if every \(a \in A\) has an open \(V \ni a\) and an sc⁺-retraction \(s\) on \(V\) with \(s(V) = A \cap V\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold; the data at a point are a structure Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_iff. An sc⁺-retraction is an sc-smooth retraction, so the data are those of Definition 2.20 Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.toSubData, \(A\) is a sub-M-polyfold Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSubMPolyfold and carries the induced structure of Proposition 2.21 Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold. Its points lie on level \(1\), as \(a = s(a) \in X_1\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.mem_levelSet_one.

The sc⁺ condition read in a chart (Lemma 6.A of the exposition). The text never reads the sc⁺ condition in charts, and all of §§4.2–4.3 rests on it (Findings, item 60). Let \(\varphi\) be a chart of \(X\) and \(W = V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap s^{-1}(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi)\), the open set of the proof of Proposition 2.21 Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.shrink. (a) The lift of \(\varphi \circ s \circ \varphi^{-1}\) into \(E^1\) is sc-smooth from \((\varphi(W), C, E)\) to \((O_1, C_1, E^1)\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.isScSmoothRetractMap_lift: it is the sc-smoothness of \(1_0^1 \circ s\) read in the charts \(\varphi\) of \(X\) and \(\mathtt{levelChart}\,\varphi\) of \(X^1\), where \(1_0^1\) is the lift. (b) For every retraction \(r\) onto \(O\): \(\varphi(W) = O \cap G\) for an open \(G\); \(\rho = \varphi \circ s \circ \varphi^{-1}\) is sc-smooth on the retract \(\varphi(W)\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_isScSmooth and idempotent there Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_idem, with image \(\varphi(W \cap A)\) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.SubData.rho_image; so \(t = \rho \circ r\) on \(U \cap r^{-1}(G)\) — the restriction of \(r\) Chapter2/RetractsScRetraction.restrict composed with \(\rho\) Chapter2/MetrizableScRetraction.compRetraction — is a retraction onto \(\varphi(W \cap A)\), and it is sc⁺: its values \(\varphi(s(x))\) lie in \(E_1\) because \(s(x) \in X_1\), and its lift is the map of (a) composed with \(r\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.exists_chartRetraction. This is the text’s \(t = \varphi \circ s \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r\) of the proof of Theorem 4.18, with \(W\) in place of “\(V = \varphi^{-1}(O)\)”. Hence the model \(\varphi(W \cap A)\) of the chart of \(A\) induced by \(\varphi\) is an sc⁺-retract Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.isScPlusRetract_image, and \(\varphi(a)\) is smooth for \(a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) (Lemma 4.7 (i)) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.apply_mem_smooth.

Tangent spaces of sub-retracts. The tangent space of a retract is a germ: for an open \(K\), \(T_z(Q \cap K) = T_zQ\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldstangentSpace_inter_isOpen. For retracts \(Q \subseteq O = r(U)\), \(T_zQ \subseteq T_zO\): a retraction \(s\) onto \(Q\) satisfies \(s = r \circ s\), so \(Ds(z) = Dr(z)Ds(z)\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldstangentSpace_subset_of_subset. And if \(F \circ r\) is sc-smooth and \(F\) maps the sub-retract \(Q\) into a retract \(Q'\), then \(D(F \circ r)(z)\) maps \(T_zQ\) into \(T_{F(z)}Q'\) (Proposition 2.6 (3) for \(F|_Q\)) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsscDeriv_mem_tangentSpace_of_subset.

Remark 4.14 in a chart Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.remark_4_14. The text: \(T_aA = Ts(a)(T_aX)\) is the image of the sc⁺-operator \(Ts(a)\), hence finite-dimensional. In a chart, at \(a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) and the level-\(1\) point \(z\) over \(\varphi(a)\): \(z\) is smooth (Lemma 4.7 (i) for the chart retraction \(t\)); the tangent map of \(\rho\) at \(z\) maps \(T_zO = T_z(\varphi(W))\) onto \(T_z(\varphi(W \cap A))\) (Proposition 2.21 (4) for \(\rho\)) Chapter2/Metrizableproposition_2_21_4; \(T_z(\varphi(W \cap A)) \subseteq T_zO\); and it is the range of \(Dt(z)\), finite-dimensional by Lemma 4.7 (ii). The sc⁺-operator is \(Dt(z)\), not \(Ts(a)\).

Points with \(d_X = 0\). The remark adds that near points with \(d_X(a) = 0\), \(A\) is a classical manifold. Every subspace is in good position to the whole space, any algebraic complement being good Chapter4/SubmanifoldsisInGoodPosition_univ, and at a point with \(d_C(e) = 0\) the partial quadrant \(C_e\) is the whole space Chapter4/SubmanifoldspartialQuadrantAtWith_eq_univ_of_degIndex_eq_zero. So at \(a \in A\) with \(d_X(a) = 0\), in a chart realizing \(d_X(a) = 0\) Chapter2/DegeneracyIndexMPolyfold.exists_isChart_degIndex_eq, \(A\) is in good position (Definition 4.16, §IV.13) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isGoodPositionAt_of_degIndex_eq_zero; and if \(d_X = 0\) on all of \(A\), re-centring at each point gives charts modelled in \(C_{\varphi(a)} = E\), in which \(T_0(\psi(W \cap A))\) is in good position, so the induced structure has a corner structure by the core of Theorem 4.18 (§IV.14) — without tameness of \(X\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero. The local statement for the open piece \(A \cap \{d_X = 0\}\) of an arbitrary \(A\) is not formalized.

The open question after Proposition 4.15 — is a sub-M-polyfold with \(A = A_\infty\) and finite, locally constant \(\dim T_aA\) a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold; is the “T” \(\{(x, 0) : |x| < 1\} \cup \{(0, y) : 0 \le y < 1\}\) homeomorphic to a retract \(O = O_\infty\) — is a question and is not formalized. Its last sentence, that this is impossible for sc⁺-retracts, is for a retract \((O, E, E)\) without boundary the statement just proved with \(A = O\): an sc⁺-retract in \(E\) is a manifold; that the “T” is not a topological manifold is not formalized.

IV.12 Proposition 4.15

(1) \(A \subseteq X_\infty\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.subset_smoothSet: in a chart at \(a\), \(\varphi(a)\) lies in the retract of the sc⁺ chart retraction (Lemma 4.7 (i)). The text does not distinguish this from “\(A = A_\infty\) for the induced structure”, which holds because the levels of the induced structure are the traces of those of \(X\), computed in the induced charts Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subPolyfold_isChart Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.mem_levelSet_subPolyfold_iff Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.proposition_4_15_1.

(2) \(A\) is locally closed Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.proposition_4_15_2. The text’s definition is garbled — “a point \(b \in V(a)\) belongs to \(A\) if \(U \cap A \ne \emptyset\) for all open neighbourhoods \(U\) of \(b\)”, with \(U\) also the letter of the domain — and is read as \(V(a) \cap \overline A \subseteq A\), one of the equivalent forms of Mathlib’s \(\mathtt{IsLocallyClosed}\) (the intersection of an open and a closed set). Proof: for \(b \in V \cap \overline A\), \(b\) is in the closure of \(A \cap V\) (\(V\) open), so the filter of neighbourhoods of \(b\) within \(A \cap V\) is nontrivial; \(s\) is continuous at \(b\) and equal to the identity on \(A \cap V\), so \(s(b)\) and \(b\) are both limits of the identity along that filter, and \(s(b) = b\) (\(X\) Hausdorff); hence \(b \in s(V) \subseteq A\). A filter replaces the text’s sequence \(a_k \to b\), so no metrizability is needed.

(3) \(\partial A = \{d_A \ge 1\} \subseteq \partial X\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.proposition_4_15_3, by \(d_A \le d_X\) (Lemma 2.26) Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldlemma_2_26. The text’s argument for \(d_X(a) = 0\) is the proof of that lemma; it needs the chart re-centred at \(a\), since only \(C_{\varphi(a)}\), not \(C\), is the whole space.

(4) \(1_0^1 : A \to A^1\) is sc-smooth Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.proposition_4_15_4. The text says only that “the postulated sc⁺-retraction is the identity on the retract \(A\)”. The proof: every point of \(A\) lies in an induced chart Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldMPolyfold.subChart whose model \(\varphi(W \cap A)\) is an sc⁺-retract (§IV.11), and Proposition 4.8 on a cover applies (§IV.4).

IV.13 Good and general position in charts, and their chart independence (Definitions 4.16, 4.17, 4.21)

Definition 4.16 in a chart. For retracts \(Q \subseteq O\), a presentation \(T\) and a level-\(1\) point \(z\): \(T_zQ\) is in good position to \(C_z\) inside \(T_zO\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGoodPositionRetractAt — in the sense of Definition 3.21 inside a subspace Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsInGoodPositionIn: \(T_zQ \subseteq T_zO\), \(T_zQ \cap C_z\) has interior points in \(T_zQ\), and \(T_zQ\) has a complement inside \(T_zO\) with a constant \(\varepsilon\). The condition depends only on the two tangent spaces Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGoodPositionRetractAt.congr. For the data \(d\) of Definition 4.13, a chart \(\varphi\) and \(Q = \varphi(W \cap A)\) it is the chart condition Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.IsGoodPositionChart, and \(A\) is in good position at \(a\) if it holds for some data at \(a\), some chart at \(a\), some presentation and the level-\(1\) point over \(\varphi(a)\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGoodPositionAt. Explicitly, for retractions \(r\) onto \(O\) and \(t\) onto \(\varphi(W \cap A)\), the condition says that \(Dt(z)E\) is in good position to \(C_z\) inside \(Dr(z)E\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.isGoodPositionChart_iff. The text states Definition 4.16 for tame \(X\) so that \(C_aX\) is a partial quadrant (Proposition 2.36); the chart form does not need it.

Definition 4.21 in a chart. \(T_zQ\) has in \(T_zO\) an sc-complement contained in \(T^R_zO\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGeneralPositionRetractAt: an sc-subspace \(B \subseteq T_zO \cap E_z\) of \(E\) with \((T_zO)_m = (T_zQ)_m \oplus B_m\) on every level, the sc-structure of \(T_zO\) being the one induced from \(E\); again it depends only on the tangent spaces Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGeneralPositionRetractAt.congr. The chart condition Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.SubmanifoldData.IsGeneralPositionChart and general position at \(a\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt are defined as for good position. Definition 4.17: \(A\) is tame if its induced structure is Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsTameSubmanifold.

Transport by a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms. Let \(F\) be a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between retracts \(O = r(U)\) and \(O' = r'(U')\) with inverse \(G\) Chapter2/BoundaryIsDiffeoGerm, mapping sub-retracts \(Q\), \(Q'\) into each other. At \(z \in Q_1\), \(\mathcal A = D(F \circ r)(z)\) restricts to an isomorphism \(T_zO \cong T_{F(z)}O'\) with inverse \(D(G \circ r')(F(z))\), carrying the partial cones onto each other (Proposition 2.30) Chapter2/Boundaryproposition_2_30_cone and \(T_zQ\) onto \(T_{F(z)}Q'\) (§IV.11 in both directions). Good position inside a subspace is transported by such an isomorphism (Lemma 3.45) Chapter3/LinearizationChartsIsInGoodPositionIn.transport, so good position of \(Q\) at \(z\) gives good position of \(Q'\) at \(F(z)\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGoodPositionRetractAt.transport. For general position \(z\) must be smooth: then \(\mathcal A\) is an sc-operator, it carries \(T^R_zO\) onto \(T^R_{F(z)}O'\) (Proposition 2.30) Chapter2/Boundaryproposition_2_30_reduced, and the image of the sc-complement \(B\) is an sc-complement inside \(T^R_{F(z)}O'\), level by level Chapter4/SubmanifoldsIsGeneralPositionRetractAt.transport.

The chart change Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.chart_change_of_transport. Let \(\Phi\) be a property of \((Q \subseteq O, T, z)\) that depends only on the tangent spaces and is carried by germs of sc-diffeomorphisms at smooth points. If \(\Phi\) holds for \(\varphi(G \cap A) \subseteq O\) at \(z\) (smooth), it holds for \(\varphi'(G' \cap A) \subseteq O'\) at \(z'\), for any presentations: on \(H = G \cap G'\) the transition \(\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}\) is a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between the overlap retracts Chapter2/BoundaryIsScSmoothRetractMap.isDiffeoGerm carrying \(\varphi(H \cap A)\) onto \(\varphi'(H \cap A)\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMChart.image_inter_eq_inter, and the tangent spaces at \(z\) are those of the open pieces (the germ property). Applied to the two properties Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isGoodPositionRetractAt_chart_change Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isGeneralPositionRetractAt_chart_change, with \(G\), \(G'\) the open sets of two submanifold charts: if \(A\) is in good position at \(a\), the chart condition holds for every data, chart, presentation and lift Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGoodPositionAt.isGoodPositionChart, and good position is equivalent to the condition for all of them Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isGoodPositionAt_iff_forall; likewise for general position Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGeneralPositionChart Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.isGeneralPositionAt_iff_forall, the smoothness of the point holding on \(A\). The text takes this independence for granted (Findings, item 66).

IV.14 Lemma 4.19 and Theorem 4.18

Lemma 4.19, the complement kept explicit Chapter4/SubmanifoldsisGoodComplement_sup_range. Let \(\pi\) be a bounded idempotent with \((1 - \pi)E_0\) inside the minimal subspace at \(0\), \(E^{\min}_0 = \{\lambda = 0\}\), and \(Y \subseteq \pi E_0\) a complement of \(N\) inside \(\pi E_0\) with constant \(\varepsilon\). Then \(Y \oplus (1 - \pi)E_0\) is a good complement of \(N\) in \(E_0\) with constant \(\varepsilon/(\|\pi\| + 1)\): for \(y \in Y\), \(k \in (1 - \pi)E_0\) with \(|y + k| \le \frac{\varepsilon}{\|\pi\| + 1}|n|\), \(y = \pi(y + k)\), so \(|y| \le \varepsilon|n|\) and \(n \in C \iff n + y \in C\); and adding \(k \in E^{\min}_0\) changes no coordinate, so \(n + y \in C \iff n + y + k \in C\). The splitting: \(N \oplus Y = \pi E_0\) and \(\pi E_0 \oplus (1 - \pi)E_0 = E_0\). Lemma 4.19 Chapter4/Submanifoldslemma_4_19: in the situation of the lemma, if \(N\) is in good position to \(C\) inside \(\pi E_0\), then \(N\) is in good position to \(C\) in \(E_0\), with good complements \(Y \oplus (1 - \pi)E_0\). The good-position half is the transport lemma of the proof of Theorem 3.54 Chapter3/GoodPositionGermIsInGoodPositionIn.isInGoodPosition (§III.23).

The text’s proof makes a false step. It concludes \(n + y \in C\) from \(n + y + z \in C\) “since \(z \in Z \subset C\)”. This needs \(-z \in C\): in \(C = [0, \infty)\), \(z = 1\) and \(n + y = -\frac12\) give \(n + y + z \in C\), \(n + y \notin C\). What holds, and what is used, is \(Z \subseteq E^{\min}_0 \subseteq C \cap (-C)\) — Proposition 2.35 at the corner of the centred chart. The text’s norm \(|y|_0 + |z|_0\) on \(Y \oplus Z\) is not the norm of \(E\); the constant \(\varepsilon/(\|\pi\| + 1)\) compares them (Findings, item 69).

Good position read in a tame centred chart Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGoodPositionAt.isInGoodPosition_of_tame. If \(A\) is in good position at \(a\) and \(\psi\) is a chart of \(X\) with \(\psi(a) = 0\) modelled on a tame retract \(O = r(U)\), then \(N = T_0(\psi(W \cap A))\) is in good position to \(C\) in \(E\): by chart independence the chart condition holds in \(\psi\), i.e. \(N\) is in good position to \(C_0\) inside \(T_0O = \mathrm{range}\,Dr(0)\); at the corner of the centred chart \(C_0 = C\) Chapter3/GoodPositionGermpartialQuadrantAtWith_zero; Proposition 2.35 for the tame \(r\) at the smooth point \(0\) gives \((1 - Dr(0))E_0 \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) Chapter2/TameRetractsproposition_2_35; and \(Dr(0)\) is idempotent. Lemma 4.19 with \(\pi = Dr(0)\) concludes. Tameness of \(X\) enters Theorem 4.18 here and nowhere else.

The corner charts of \(A\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.hasCornerStructure_of_centred_isInGoodPosition. If every \(a \in A\) lies in a chart \(\psi\) of \(X\) with \(\psi(a) = 0\) in which \(T_0(\psi(W \cap A))\) is in good position to \(C\) in \(E\), the induced structure has a corner structure. Proof (for nonempty \(A\)): every point of \(A\) is smooth and \(1_0^1 : A \to A^1\) is sc-smooth (Proposition 4.15 (4)); the chart of \(A\) induced by \(\psi\) is a chart of the induced structure, centred at \(a\), modelled on \(\psi(W \cap A)\); its tangent space at \(0\) is the range of \(Dt(0)\) for the sc⁺ chart retraction, finite-dimensional (Lemma 4.7), and in good position by hypothesis; Theorem 4.2 (ii) ⇒ (i) for the M-polyfold \(A\) (§IV.10) concludes.

Theorem 4.18 Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.theorem_4_18. Statement. Let \(X\) be tame and \(A\) a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold in good position at every point. Then the induced structure on \(A\) has a corner structure, and \(A\) is tame. Proof (the text’s route through Theorem 4.2): at \(a \in A\) take a tame chart centred at \(a\) (§IV.5) — the “sc-smooth tame chart \(\varphi : (V, a) \to (O, 0)\)” the text takes for granted; good position read in it (above) gives the hypothesis of the previous paragraph; and a corner structure makes \(A\) tame (§IV.1). What the text skips, besides the false step of Lemma 4.19: the centred chart; the set \(W\) in place of “\(V = \varphi^{-1}(O)\)” (§IV.11); the sc⁺ condition in charts; the closed complement and the projection along it in place of “\(p = Dt(0)\)” (§IV.10); and the compatibility of the charts \(p \circ \varphi\) (§IV.10). The text’s “\(V(a) = \varphi^{-1}(V_0) \cap A\)” should be \((p \circ \varphi)^{-1}(V_0) \cap A\); its “Proposition 4.2” is Theorem 4.2 (Findings, item 68). No hypothesis is added.

IV.15 Remark 4.20: good position is an open condition

Statement Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.remark_4_20. For tame \(X\), if \(A\) is in good position at \(a\), there is an open \(U \ni a\) with \(A\) in good position at every point of \(U \cap A\). The text omits “tame” (Definition 4.16 is for tame \(X\), and Lemma 4.19 is used) and argues “since the tangent spaces of \(A\) move only slowly, Lemma 3.55 implies…”. The formal proof makes this precise.

The tangent spaces along a graph Chapter4/SubmanifoldstangentSpace_eq_range_graph. If the retract \(Q\) is the image of \(\Gamma : (V, N \cap C, N) \to (Q, C, E)\), sc-smooth between retracts with inverse \(p\), then at \(v \in V\) and the level-\(1\) point \(y\) over \(\Gamma(v)\): \(\Gamma\) is differentiable within \(V\) with derivative its sc-derivative Chapter4/SubmanifoldshasFDerivWithinAt_scDeriv_const, \(T_yQ = D\Gamma(v)N\), and \(p \circ D\Gamma(v) = 1\) — the tangent maps of the germ of sc-diffeomorphisms \(\Gamma\), \(p\).

Proof of Remark 4.20. Take a tame chart \(\psi\) centred at \(a\) with tame retraction \(r\), the sc⁺ chart retraction \(t\) onto \(\psi(W \cap A)\), and \(N = T_0\), in good position to \(C\) in \(E\) (§IV.14). The normal form of Proposition 3.22 gives a continuous projection \(\pi\) onto \(N\) with closed kernel a good complement Chapter3/GoodComplementProjectionexists_proj_goodComplement, and Proposition 4.9 gives \(W_1\), \(V\), \(\Gamma\) over \(N \cap C\). Write \(\Gamma(v) = v + \sigma(v)\) with \(\sigma(v) \in \ker\pi\). Then \(\sigma\) is \(C^1\) on \(V\), \(\sigma(0) = 0\), and \(D\sigma(0) = 0\): \(D\Gamma(0)m\) lies in \(T_0 = N\), so \(D\Gamma(0)m = \pi D\Gamma(0)m = m\). The tangent space at \(\Gamma(v)\) is the graph \(\{n + D\sigma(v)n\}\) Chapter3/GoodPositionOpengraphSpace. Lemma 3.55, with the closed complement \(\ker\pi\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTFulllemma_3_55_relOpen, gives \(\rho > 0\) such that for \(|v| < \rho\) this graph is in good position to \(C_{\Gamma(v)}\) in \(E\). It lies in \(T_{\Gamma(v)}O\) (Remark 4.14 in the chart), and good position in \(E\) of a subspace of \(T_{\Gamma(v)}O\) gives good position inside \(T_{\Gamma(v)}O\), with the complement cut down by the modular law Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyGraphIsInGoodPosition.isInGoodPositionIn_of_le. That is Definition 4.16 at \(b = \psi^{-1}(\Gamma(v))\), read in \(\psi\). The neighbourhood is \(U = W \cap \psi^{-1}(W_1 \cap \{|\pi u| < \rho\})\).

IV.16 Linear algebra at the corner of a centred chart; Lemmas 7.A and 7.B of the exposition

In a chart centred at \(0\), every coordinate vanishes at \(0\), so the minimal subspace there is \(E^{\min}_0 = \{\lambda = 0\}\), the text’s “\(\{0\} \oplus W\)” Chapter4/LocalStructuremem_minimalSubspaceWith_zero, and it lies in every \(E_x\) Chapter4/LocalStructureminimalSubspaceWith_zero_le. Adding a vector of \(E^{\min}_0\) changes no coordinate Chapter4/LocalStructurecoord_add_of_mem_zero, hence neither the degeneracy index Chapter4/LocalStructuredegIndexWith_add_of_mem_zero nor membership in \(C\) Chapter4/LocalStructureadd_mem_iff_of_mem_zero.

Closed complements. If \(N\) is finite-dimensional, \(K\) closed and \(N + K\) the whole space, \(N\) has a closed complement \(Y \subseteq K\): take a continuous projection \(q\) onto the finite-dimensional \(N \cap K\) and \(Y = K \cap \ker q\) Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_isClosed_isCompl_le. The projection along a closed complement of a finite-dimensional subspace is continuous, with kernel exactly the complement Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_proj_of_isCompl.

Good position from \(N + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\). Let \(N\) be finite-dimensional with \(N + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\). The coordinates restricted to \(N\) Chapter4/LocalStructurecoordsOn map \(N\) onto \(\mathbb R^n\) Chapter4/LocalStructurecoordsOn_surjective, so \(N \cap C\) has interior points, those with all coordinates positive Chapter4/LocalStructureinterior_nonempty_of_sup_eq_top. A complement inside \(E^{\min}_0\) is good with every \(\varepsilon\) Chapter4/LocalStructureisGoodComplement_of_le_zero. Hence \(N\) is in good position, with a closed good complement \(Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_goodComplement_le_zero. The degeneracy index on the slice Chapter4/LocalStructuredegIndex_slice: \(N \cap C\) is the partial quadrant of \(N\) presented by \(v \mapsto (\lambda(v), v - s(\lambda(v)))\), \(s\) a linear section of \(\lambda|_N\), and \(d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(v)\) — both count the vanishing coordinates. This replaces the text’s splitting \(T_0A = N \oplus (T_0A \cap W)\), \(E = N \oplus W\) (Findings, item 83).

Lemma 7.A: an sc-complement inside an sc-subspace Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_scComplement_le. Let \(N \subseteq E_\infty\) be finite-dimensional, \(R\) an sc-subspace and \(M = N + R\). Then \(N\) has in \(M\) an sc-complement \(B \subseteq R\): \(K = N \cap R\) is finite-dimensional and smooth, so it has an sc-complement \(G\) in \(E\) (Proposition 1.6) Chapter1/ScBanachScBanach.proposition_1_6; put \(B = R \cap G\). Then \(R = K \oplus B\), \(N + R = N + B\), \(N \cap B \subseteq K \cap G = 0\), and \(M_m = N \oplus B_m\) on every level because \(N \subseteq E_\infty\). \(B\) is closed with \(B_m = (1 - P)R_m\), \(P\) the sc-projection onto \(K\), so the smooth points of \(B\) are dense in every level: for \(x \in B_m\) and smooth \(u \in R_m\) near \(x\), \(u - Pu \in B\) is smooth and near \(x - Px = x\).

General position from \(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) Chapter4/LocalStructureisGeneralPositionRetractAt_of_sup_eq_top. Let \(r\) be tame, \(Q \subseteq O\) a retract, \(y \in Q_1\) smooth, and \(T_yQ\) finite-dimensional, smooth, with \(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\). As \(E^{\min}_0 \subseteq E_y\), intersecting with \(T_yO \supseteq T_yQ\) gives \(T_yO = T_yQ + (T_yO \cap E^{\min}_0) \subseteq T_yQ + T^R_yO\) (modular law). \(T^R_yO\) is an sc-subspace by Proposition 2.36 for the tame \(r\) Chapter2/PartialConeproposition_2_36_partialCone, and Lemma 7.A gives the sc-complement inside it. This is the step of Theorem 4.22 (3) “implying that \(T_aA\) has in \(T_aO\) a sc-complement contained in \(T^R_aO\)” (Findings, item 85).

Lemma 7.B: general position implies good position Chapter4/LocalStructureIsGeneralPositionRetractAt.isGoodPositionRetractAt. For \(r\) tame and a smooth \(z \in O_1\): if \(T_zQ\) has in \(T_zO\) an sc-complement \(B \subseteq T^R_zO\), then \(T_zQ\) is in good position to \(C_z\) inside \(T_zO\). \(B \subseteq E_z\) changes none of the coordinates \(\lambda_i\), \(i \in I(z)\), so it is a good complement with every \(\varepsilon\). The coordinates \(\lambda_{I(z)}\) restricted to \(T_zO\) have kernel \(T^R_zO\), whose codimension is \(d_C(z) = \#I(z)\) (Proposition 2.36) Chapter2/TameRetractsquotDim_reducedTangentSpaceWith_eq, so they map \(T_zO\) onto \(\mathbb R^{I(z)}\); they kill \(B\), so they map \(T_zQ\) onto \(\mathbb R^{I(z)}\), and the preimage of the open positive orthant gives interior points of \(T_zQ \cap C_z\). The text never states this step, which Theorem 4.22 (4) and Theorem 4.23 need for tameness and corner structures.

IV.17 Theorem 4.22 (1)–(3): local structure in general position

\(T_0Q + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) from general position at the centre Chapter4/LocalStructuresup_minimalSubspaceWith_eq_top. If \(T_0Q\) has in \(T_0O\) an sc-complement \(B \subseteq T^R_0O \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) and \(r\) is tame, then \(E_0 = T_0O + (1 - Dr(0))E_0\) with \((1 - Dr(0))E_0 \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) (Proposition 2.35), so \(E_0 = T_0Q + B + (1 - Dr(0))E_0 \subseteq T_0Q + E^{\min}_0\). (The text: “\(E = T_0O \oplus Z = T_0A \oplus \widetilde A \oplus Z\), so \(T_0A\) has in \(E\) an sc-complement \(Y\) contained in \(W\)”; only \(T_0A + W = E\) is used afterwards.)

\(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) along the graph Chapter4/LocalStructuresup_minimalSubspaceWith_eq_top_graph. If \(\Gamma : V \to Q \cap W\) is the graph map of Proposition 4.9 for a projection \(p\) onto \(N\) whose kernel lies in \(Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\), and \(N + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\), then at \(y\) over \(\Gamma(v)\), \(T_yQ = D\Gamma(v)N\) (§IV.15) and \(D\Gamma(v)n - n \in \ker p \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) because \(p \circ D\Gamma(v) = 1\); so \(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = N + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\). This is the text’s “by means of the particular form of the map \(\alpha : h \mapsto h + D\delta(v)h\), also \(T_aA + W = E\)”, which needs \(D\delta(v)h \in W\).

Theorem 4.22 in a tame centred chart Chapter4/LocalStructuretheorem_4_22_chart. Let \(r\) be tame onto \(O \ni 0\), \(t\) an sc⁺-retraction onto \(Q \subseteq O\) with \(0 \in Q\), \(N = T_0Q\), and suppose \(Q\) is in general position at \(0\). Then: \(N + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) (above); \(N\) is in good position with a closed good complement \(Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) (§IV.16) and the projection \(p\) along it, with kernel exactly \(Y\); Proposition 4.9 for this \(Y\) gives \(W\), \(V\), \(\Gamma\); (2) \(d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(\Gamma(v))\) for \(v \in V\), because \(d_{N \cap C}(v) = d_C(v)\) on the slice and \(\Gamma(v) - v \in Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) changes no coordinate; (3) at every level-\(1\) point \(y\) over \(Q \cap W\), \(Q\) is in general position: \(y\) is smooth (Lemma 4.7 (i)), \(T_yQ\) is the range of \(Dt(y)\), finite-dimensional (Lemma 4.7 (ii)) and smooth — the range of \(Dt(y)\) is an sc-subspace at a smooth point Chapter2/TameRetractsScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv, finite-dimensional sc-subspaces are smooth Chapter1/ScBanachScBanach.proposition_1_6_iff — and \(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) along the graph gives general position (§IV.16).

Theorem 4.22 Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.theorem_4_22. Statement. Let \(X\) be tame, \(A\) a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold, in general position at \(x \in A\). There are a chart \(\psi\) of \(X\) with \(\psi(x) = 0\), a tame retraction \(r\) onto its model for a presentation with \(n\) half-line coordinates, and an open \(U \ni x\) inside the domain of \(\psi\), such that: (1) \(d_X(x) = n\), and \(\psi(x)\) lies in exactly \(d_X(x)\) faces of the M-polyfold \(O\); (2) \(d_X(a) = d_A(a)\) for \(a \in A \cap U\); (3) \(A\) is in general position at every point of \(A \cap U\); (4) for every \(\sigma \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}\) the intersection of local faces \(F_\sigma\) is a tame sub-M-polyfold inside \(U\) with \(d_{F_\sigma} + \#\sigma = d_X\), and \(A \cap F_\sigma\) is a tame smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of \(F_\sigma\), in general position in \(F_\sigma\) at each of its points. Proof. \(x\) is smooth (Proposition 4.15 (1)), so there is a tame chart \(\psi\) centred at \(x\) (§IV.5), with a tame retraction \(r\) and a presentation \(T\); the chart retraction \(t\) of \(A\) in \(\psi\) is sc⁺ (§IV.11), and general position at \(x\) read in \(\psi\) (chart independence, §IV.13) is general position of \(t(U)\) at \(0\). Theorem 4.22 in the chart gives \(Y\), \(p\), \(W_1\), \(V\), \(\Gamma\); put \(U = W \cap \psi^{-1}(W_1)\), \(W\) the open set of the submanifold chart.

  1. (1) is a statement about the chart. At the centre all \(n\) coordinates vanish, so \(d_C(0) = n\); the tame chart realizes \(d_X\) Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith, so \(d_X(x) = n\). The face count is Corollary 2.41 for the M-polyfold \(O\) Chapter2/TameRetractsisFaceStructured_toMPolyfold Chapter2/TameRetractsLocalModel.degIndex_toMPolyfold_of_isTameWith. “Precisely \(d\) local faces contained in \(U\)” is read for the faces \(O \cap \{\lambda_i = 0\}\) of the chart model; their identification with global faces of \(X\) is not formalized (Findings, item 86).
  2. (2). The text: “\(p : A \to (T_0A \cap C) \cap V\) is a sc-diffeomorphism … by Proposition 2.24, \(d_A(a) = d_{T_0A \cap C}(p(a))\)”. The sc-diffeomorphism is the corner chart \(p \circ \psi\) of \(A\): the data of §IV.10 for the chart of \(A\) induced by \(\psi\), with the complement \(Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\), give a chart of the induced structure modelled on \((V, N \cap C, N)\) with the identity retraction. That model is tame, so the chart realizes \(d_A\) Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameRetract; \(\psi\) realizes \(d_X\); and \(d_{N \cap C}(p\psi(a)) = d_C(\Gamma(p\psi(a))) = d_C(\psi(a))\) by (2) of the chart form (Findings, item 84).
  3. (3) is (3) of the chart form, read back through the chart: at \(b \in U \cap A\) the level-\(1\) point over \(\psi(b)\) is smooth, and the chart condition in \(\psi\) is general position at \(b\).
  4. (4) is §IV.18.

The text’s further claims “\(\delta(0) = 0\) and \(D\delta(0) = 0\)” hold (§IV.15) but are not used.

IV.18 Theorem 4.22 (4): the faces, and \(A \cap F_\sigma\)

The text: “in view of the arguments in the proof of Proposition 2.43, the sets \(F_\sigma\) are tame M-polyfolds. Moreover, \(A \cap F_\sigma\) are smooth submanifolds of \(F_\sigma\). The previous arguments, but now applied to \(A \cap F_\sigma\) conclude the proof.” Four things are missing (Findings, item 89): Proposition 2.43 is about one face, and intersections need Proposition 2.44 (second sentence); “smooth submanifold of \(F_\sigma\)” needs an sc⁺-retraction in the M-polyfold \(F_\sigma\); general position in \(F_\sigma\) needs an argument; and tameness of \(A \cap F_\sigma\) needs Theorem 4.18 in \(F_\sigma\) and good position.

Killing coordinates. For \(\sigma \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}\), \(a \mapsto a \cdot 1_\sigma\) keeps the coordinates in \(\sigma\) Chapter4/LocalStructuremaskL, and for a linear section \(s\) of \(\lambda|_N\), \(\kappa_\sigma(v) = v - s(\lambda(v)1_\sigma)\) Chapter4/LocalStructurekillOn has \(\lambda_i(\kappa_\sigma v) = 0\) for \(i \in \sigma\) and \(\lambda_j(\kappa_\sigma v) = \lambda_j(v)\) otherwise Chapter4/LocalStructurecoordsOn_killOn, fixes the vectors of the stratum \(f_\sigma = \{\lambda_i = 0, i \in \sigma\}\) Chapter4/LocalStructurekillOn_eq_self, is idempotent Chapter4/LocalStructurekillOn_idem and maps \(N \cap C\) into itself Chapter4/LocalStructurekillOn_mem. A continuous linear map into a finite-dimensional space is an sc-operator for the constant structure Chapter4/LocalStructureopToConst.

The sc⁺-retraction onto \(A \cap F_\sigma\) in the chart Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_scPlus_retraction_corner. In the situation of the chart form of Theorem 4.22, for every open \(B \ni 0\) there are an open \(G \ni 0\), \(G \subseteq W \cap B\), and an sc⁺-retraction \(t_\sigma = \Gamma \circ \kappa_\sigma \circ p \circ t\) on \(U \cap t^{-1}(G)\) onto \(Q_\sigma = Q \cap G \cap f_\sigma\): (a) it is sc⁺, as sc-smooth ∘ sc⁺ (§IV.2), \(p\), \(\kappa_\sigma\) and \(\Gamma\) being sc-smooth; (b) it is a retraction, because \(t\Gamma = \Gamma\), \(p\Gamma = 1\) and \(\kappa_\sigma^2 = \kappa_\sigma\); (c) its image is \(Q \cap G \cap f_\sigma\), because \(\Gamma(v) - v \in Y \subseteq E^{\min}_0\) changes no coordinate, so \(\lambda(\Gamma(v)) = \lambda(v)\); (d) at a point \(y\) of \(Q_\sigma\) the tangent vectors of \(Q\) lying in \(f_\sigma\) are tangent to \(Q_\sigma\): for such \(h\), \(k = ph\) has \(\lambda(k) = \lambda(h)\), so \(\kappa_\sigma k = k\) and \(Dt_\sigma(y)h = D\Gamma(w)\kappa_\sigma pDt(y)h = D\Gamma(w)k = h\), \(w = p(y)\), by the chain rule and \(T_yQ = D\Gamma(w)N\).

The corner model Chapter4/LocalStructureexists_cornerModel_retraction. For a retraction \(S\) with retract in \(f_\sigma\), \(\pi_\sigma \circ S \circ \iota_\sigma\) on \(\iota_\sigma^{-1}(S.U)\), with the corner inclusion and projection of Chapter 2 Chapter2/CornerGermscornerIncl Chapter2/CornerGermscornerProj, is a retraction of \([0, \infty)^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W\) onto \(\pi_\sigma(S(U))\), sc⁺ if \(S\) is.

Theorem 4.22 (4) in the chart Chapter4/LocalStructuretheorem_4_22_four_chart. For every \(\sigma\) and every open \(B_0 \ni 0\) there are faces \(F_i \ni 0\) of \(O\) (\(i \in \sigma\)) and an open \(G \ni 0\), \(G \subseteq W \cap B_0\), such that: \(F_\sigma\) near \(0\) is a tame retract — \(O \cap G \cap f_\sigma\) is the retract of the face retraction of Proposition 2.44 Chapter2/CornerGermscorner_retraction restricted to \(G\), whose corner model is the retract of a tame retraction \(r'\) with \(d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma = d_C(y)\) Chapter2/CornerGermscorner_tameModel; \(A \cap F_\sigma\) near \(0\) is an sc⁺-retract — \(Q \cap G \cap f_\sigma\) is the retract of \(t_\sigma\), and its corner model that of the sc⁺-retraction \(t'\), inside the retract of \(r'\); general position in \(F_\sigma\) — at a level-\(1\) point \(y'\) of \(\pi_\sigma(Q \cap G \cap f_\sigma)\), with \(y = \iota_\sigma(y')\): \(T_yQ + E^{\min}_0 = E_0\) (§IV.17) gives for every \(b \in \mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma}\) a \(v \in T_yQ\) with \(\lambda(v) = \iota(b)\), zero on \(\sigma\); \(v \in f_\sigma\), so \(v\) is tangent to \(Q_\sigma\), and \(\pi_\sigma v\) is tangent to \(\pi_\sigma(Q_\sigma)\) at \(y'\) (§IV.11), with coordinates \(b\); so the tangent space of the corner model plus its minimal subspace at \(0\) is everything, and general position follows (§IV.16), in the corner model with the identity presentation.

sc⁺-retractions in a chart are sc⁺-retractions on open subsets Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart — the converse of §IV.11, which the text does not state. For a chart \(\chi\) and an sc⁺-retraction \(\tau\) of its model with \(\tau(U) \subseteq O\), \(s = \chi^{-1} \circ \tau \circ \chi\) is an sc⁺-retraction on the open set \(\chi^{-1}(\tau.U)\), with image \(\chi^{-1}(\tau(U))\): sc-smoothness of \(s\) and of \(1_0^1 \circ s\) are read in the charts \(\chi\) of \(X\) and \(\mathtt{levelChart}\,\chi\) of \(X^1\), where they are \(\tau\) and its lift; the values lie in \(X_1\) since \(\tau(U) \subseteq E_\infty\) (Lemma 4.7 (i)).

(4) on the M-polyfold, for one \(\sigma\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.theorem_4_22_four_of_chart. In the tame chart \(\psi\) centred at \(x\) with the chart data of §IV.17: the faces \(F_i\) and \(G\) of the chart form, with \(G\) inside the domain of the submanifold chart, give \(F_\sigma = \psi^{-1}(G \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma}F_i)\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMChart.cornerPreimage, which contains \(x\) and lies in \(W\). It is a sub-M-polyfold, a local property Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local; its face chart \(\pi_\sigma \circ \psi\), compatible with the induced charts Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart, is a chart of the induced structure Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible modelled on the tame corner model, so \(F_\sigma\) is tame Chapter2/TameFacesMPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart with \(d_{F_\sigma} + \#\sigma = d_X\). \(A \cap F_\sigma\) is, in the face chart, the retract of the sc⁺-retraction \(t'\), which the previous paragraph turns into an sc⁺-retraction on an open subset of \(F_\sigma\): it is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of \(F_\sigma\). It is in general position at each of its points by the chart form read in the face chart. Its tameness is Theorem 4.18 in the tame M-polyfold \(F_\sigma\), good position following from general position (Lemma 7.B). \(F_\sigma\) is a germ, chosen inside \(U\) — the text’s “contained in \(U\)” — and \(G\) depends on \(\sigma\). Paracompactness of \(F_\sigma\) and \(A \cap F_\sigma\), instance arguments of the induced structures, holds for every subset Chapter2/MetrizableMPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype.

The proof of Theorem 4.23 uses \(\dim(A \cap F_\sigma) = \dim A - \#\sigma\), which Theorem 4.22 does not state; it is proved in the model in §IV.21.

IV.19 Remark 4.24

If \(T_zO = T_zQ + B\) with \(B \subseteq K\), the image of \(T_zQ\) spans \(T_zO/K\), so \(\dim(T_zO/K) \le \dim T_zQ\) Chapter4/LocalStructurequotDim_le_finrank_of_eq_sup. In a chart Chapter4/LocalStructureremark_4_24_chart: at a smooth point \(z\) of a tame retract, \(\dim(T_zO/T^R_zO) = d_C(z)\) (Proposition 2.36), and if \(T_zQ\) has in \(T_zO\) an sc-complement inside \(T^R_zO\), then \(d_C(z) \le \dim T_zQ\). On the M-polyfold: for tame \(X\) and smooth \(x\), in a tame chart at \(x\) the reduced tangent space has codimension \(d_X(x)\) Chapter2/TameRetractsMPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.remark_4_24_codim — the remark’s first sentence, which needs \(X\) tame and \(x\) smooth; if \(A\) is in general position at \(a\), then \(d_X(a) \le \dim T_aA\) in any tame chart at \(a\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.remark_4_24; and a submanifold in general position with \(T_aA = 0\) does not meet \(\partial X\) at \(a\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.remark_4_24_not_mem_boundary. The remark’s “\(x \in A_\lambda\) can only belong to a corner if \(d_X(x) \le \dim A_\lambda\)” holds for every submanifold in general position, so it applies to the \(A_\lambda\) of Theorem 4.23 once their general position is proved (§IV.24).

IV.20 Sard’s theorem, vendored

The proof of Theorem 4.23 applies “Sard’s theorem” to maps \(A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m\) between spaces of arbitrary dimensions. Mathlib has the cases \(\dim E \le \dim F\) only. The Milnor project of this repository proves the general theorem by Milnor’s induction; its import closure is copied into Polyfold/Vendor/MilnorSard/ with the namespace renamed and no statement or proof changed (Findings, item 100). The proof, in Milnor’s steps:

  • The objects. \(\mathrm{Crit} = \{x \in U : Df(x)\) not onto\(\}\) Vendor/MilnorSard/BasicMilnorSard.Sard.critSet, and \(C_k\), the points where all derivatives of orders \(1, \dots, k\) vanish Vendor/MilnorSard/BasicMilnorSard.Sard.vanishSet, with \(\mathrm{Crit} \subseteq (\mathrm{Crit} \setminus C_1) \cup \bigcup_{1 \le i < k}(C_i \setminus C_{i+1}) \cup C_k\) Vendor/MilnorSard/BasicMilnorSard.Sard.critSet_subset_union. IV.21 The strata, Sard on the strata, and Theorem 3.78 in \(C^\infty\) form

The finite-dimensional model of the proof of Theorem 4.23: a finite-dimensional \(V\) (in the application \(T_0A\) of the chart of Theorem 4.22) with linear coordinates \(\ell : V \to \mathbb R^n\) (those of the tame chart, onto), the partial quadrant \(C = \{\ell \ge 0\}\) Chapter4/FamiliesLocalquadC, a relatively open \(U = O \cap C\) and a map \(f\) of class \(C^\infty\) on \(U\) (in the application the projection to \(\mathbb R^m\) composed with the graph map \(\Gamma\)).

The strata. The stratum subspace of \(\sigma\) is \(\{\ell_i = 0, i \in \sigma\}\) Chapter4/FamiliesLocalstratSub Chapter4/FamiliesLocalmem_stratSub, the tangent space of \(A \cap F_\sigma\); \(\sigma(v) = \{i : \ell_i(v) = 0\}\) is the set of faces through \(v\) Chapter4/FamiliesLocalzeroSetOf, and \(v\) lies in the stratum subspace of \(\sigma(v)\) Chapter4/FamiliesLocalmem_stratSub_zeroSetOf. The dimension count Chapter4/FamiliesLocalfinrank_stratSub: if \(\ell\) is onto, the stratum subspace of \(\sigma\) has dimension \(\dim V - \#\sigma\) — it is the kernel of \(v \mapsto (\ell_i(v))_{i \in \sigma}\), which is onto \(\mathbb R^\sigma\). This is the count “\(A \cap F_\sigma^\circ\) is a smooth manifold … having dimension \(\dim(A) - \#\sigma\)”, which the text attributes to “Theorem 4.23” (it means Theorem 4.22, which does not state it).

Stratified critical points Chapter4/FamiliesLocalstratCritSet: the \(v \in U\) at which \(Df(v)\) restricted to the stratum subspace of \(\sigma(v)\) is not onto — the critical points of the text’s \(p_\sigma : A \cap F_\sigma^\circ \to \mathbb R^m\) for \(\sigma = \sigma(v)\). Sard on the strata Chapter4/FamiliesLocalmeasure_image_stratCritSet: the stratified critical values form a null set for every Haar measure. The open stratum of \(\sigma\), \(\{k \in O : \ell_i(k) = 0\ (i \in \sigma),\ \ell_j(k) > 0\ (j \notin \sigma)\}\), is an open subset of the stratum subspace and lies in \(U\); \(f\) restricted to it is \(C^\infty\), with derivative \(Df(v)\) restricted to the stratum subspace; so a stratified critical point \(v\) with \(\sigma = \sigma(v)\) is a critical point of \(f\) on the open stratum of \(\sigma\), and Sard’s theorem applies to each of the finitely many strata. The union of the open strata is \(U\), and a point is stratified-regular iff it is a regular point of the \(p_\sigma\) for its own \(\sigma\); so the stratified critical values are the union of the critical values of all the \(p_\sigma\).

Theorem 3.78 in \(C^\infty\) form. Theorem 3.78 (§III.17) is stated for one \(j\), with \(j\)-dependent constants in its proof; the fibre retraction below needs one solution that is \(C^\infty\). In the normalized form Chapter4/FamiliesLocalContractionData.exists_solution_smooth: if the contraction data of the proof hold for every \(j \ge 1\), the radii of Lemmas 3.79–3.80 Chapter3/QuadrantIFTContractionData.exists_radii and the fixed point \(\tau(k)\) are those for \(j = 1\), independent of \(j\), and only the regularity statement depends on \(j\) Chapter3/QuadrantIFTRadii.contDiffOn_τ; so one \(\tau\) is \(C^j\) for every \(j\).
