Then \(N\) is in good position to the cone \(C_z\) inside \(T_zO\) (Definition 3.21): \(B\) is a good complement, because adding a vector of \(E_z\) does not change membership in \(C_z\) (the coordinates \(\lambda_i\), \(i \in I(z)\), vanish on \(E_z\)); and \(N \cap C_z\) has non-empty interior in \(N\), because the coordinates \(\lambda_i\), \(i \in I(z)\), map \(T_zO\) onto \(\mathbb R^{I(z)}\) — \(\dim T_zO/T^R_zO = d_C(z)\) in a tame retract (Proposition 2.36) — and vanish on \(B\), so they map \(N\) onto \(\mathbb R^{I(z)}\), and a vector of \(N\) with all these coordinates equal to \(1\) is interior. The text omits the interior condition; this is the argument of Part IV for tangent spaces Chapter4/LocalStructureIsGeneralPositionRetractAt.isGoodPositionRetractAt, for a subspace not given as one.

Lemma 5.26 Chapter5/TransversalityStrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm.isGoodPositionGerm. For \(f\) sc-Fredholm and \((f, y)\) in general position: in the chart of Definition 5.17 \(\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) is onto and its kernel is in good position by the linear algebra; Definition 3.53 then follows Chapter3/LinearizationChartsGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj. For \(f\) with tame germ data, good position holds in the tame chart of the germ data Chapter3/TameGermsAddGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.toTame Chapter5/TransversalityStrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm.isGoodPositionGermTame — the form the §3.6 theorems take. \(X\) itself need not be tame. (The text places the lemma after Theorem 5.25 and calls it “clear” after Theorem 5.18; it is used in Theorems 5.18 and 5.25 here.)

V.17 The bridge lemma, and \(T_yS = \ker f'(y)\)

Theorem 5.18 applies Theorem 4.23 to the parametrized solution set \(\tilde S\), which needs \(\tilde S\) to be a smooth submanifold in the sense of Definition 4.13 — locally the image of an sc⁺-retraction. The implicit function theorem gives tangent germ data (Definition 3.25), and the text never connects the two.

sc⁺ on a finite-dimensional domain Chapter5/GeneralPositionisScPlus_of_isScSmooth_const. On a finite-dimensional space with the constant structure all levels of the domain coincide, so an sc-smooth \(f\) is \(C^\infty\) into every \(F_m\), and its lift into \(F^1\) is sc-smooth: \(f\) is sc⁺.

The bridge lemma. Let \(D\) be regular tangent germ data for \(M\) at \(x\) (Definition 3.25 (2)), with graph map \(\Gamma : V \to E\) over the finite-dimensional \(N\), projection \(\pi\) onto \(N\), and \(r\) a retraction onto the chart model. Then \(\Gamma\) is sc⁺ on \(V\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.Γ_isScPlus, so \(\tau = \Gamma \circ \pi \circ r\), on the set of points whose image under \(\pi \circ r\) lies in \(V\), is an sc-smooth retraction (as in the proof of Theorem 3.27) Chapter3/TangentGermtheorem_3_27 which is sc⁺ (sc⁺ ∘ sc-smooth), with \(\tau \circ \Gamma = \Gamma\) on \(V\) and retract the chart image of \(M\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_scPlusRetraction. Transported to \(X\) it is an sc⁺-retraction on an open set with image \(M \cap V\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_isScPlusRetractionOn. Hence a set with regular tangent germ data at each point is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_of_isRegular. For solution sets: if all zeros of \(f\) in an open \(W\) are in good position in a tame chart, Theorem 3.54 (2) gives regular data at each, on charts inside \(W\), and \(S_f \cap W\) is a smooth submanifold Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundle.isSmoothSubmanifold_solutionSet_inter.

\(T_yS \subseteq \ker f'(y)\) Chapter5/GeneralPositiontangentSpace_subset_linKer. In a chart, let \(Q \subseteq O\) be a retract on which the principal part \(\hat f\) vanishes, \(S\) a retraction onto \(Q\), \(z\) a level-\(1\) point of \(Q\). Then \(T_zQ = \operatorname{range}DS(z) \subseteq T_zO\), and \(\hat f \circ r \circ S = 0\) gives \(D(\hat f \circ r)(z) \circ DS(z) = 0\) by the chain rule, i.e. \(T_zQ \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundleChart.mem_linKer_iff.

Equality, by counting Chapter5/GeneralPositionexists_tangentSpace_eq_linKer. Let \(f\) have tame germ data and \((f, x_0)\) be a zero in good position in a tame chart. The index form of Theorem 3.54 gives an open \(V \ni x_0\) whose zeros are in good position, and regular data \(D\) of a fixed dimension \(d\) at each zero, with \(\dim\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) = d\) in every chart Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGtheorem_3_54_index Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexStrongBundle.IsSurjLinOfIndex. On the other side, the tangent space of the bridge retraction \(\tau\) at the point over \(\Gamma(v)\) contains the \(d\) vectors \(D\Gamma(v)b_i\), \(b_i\) a basis of \(N\): \(D\tau \circ D\Gamma(v) = D(\tau \circ \Gamma)(v) = D\Gamma(v)\), and \(\pi \circ D\Gamma(v) = 1\) makes them independent Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_linearIndependent_tangentSpace. “Having \(d\) independent tangent vectors” Chapter5/GeneralPositionHasIndepTangent is carried by germs of sc-diffeomorphisms, since \(D(F \circ r)(z)\) maps \(T_zQ\) into \(T_{F(z)}Q'\) and is injective on \(T_zO\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionHasIndepTangent.transport, so it passes from the chart of \(D\) to any chart \(\Phi\) through the transition maps Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.chart_change_of_transport. A \(d\)-dimensional subspace of the \(d\)-dimensional \(\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) — tangent spaces of retracts are germs, so the retract \(\varphi(G \cap S_f \cap V)\) of any small open \(G\) has the same tangent space — is all of it.

V.18 General position: chart independence and openness

Definition 5.17 is Definition 4.21 Chapter5/GeneralPositionexists_isGeneralPositionGerm_iff. Near a zero \(x_0\) in good position (with \(f\) of tame germ data) there is an open \(V\) such that every zero in \(V\) is in good position, \(S = S_f \cap V\) is a smooth submanifold (§V.17), and at every zero \(y \in V\): \((f, y)\) is in general position iff \(S\) is in general position at \(y\) (Definition 4.21, Part IV). Since \(T_zS = \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) in every chart, an sc-complement of \(\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) inside \(T^R_zO\) is an sc-complement of \(T_zS\) inside \(T^R_zO\). Definition 4.21 is chart independent (Part IV) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGeneralPositionChart, so Definition 5.17 is too, at these zeros.

From submanifold general position to good position Chapter5/GeneralPositionisGoodPositionGermTame_of_isGeneralPositionAt. If \(f'(y)\) is onto and a smooth submanifold \(A \subseteq S_f\) is in general position at \(y\), then in the tame chart of the germ data \(T_zA \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)\) (§V.17) Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundleChart.linKer_le and \(T_zA + T^R_zO = T_zO\); so \(\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) + T^R_zO = T_zO\), the kernel has an algebraic complement inside \(T^R_zO\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionexists_compl_le_of_sup_eq, and §V.16 gives good position.

Openness Chapter5/GeneralPositionexists_isOpen_isGeneralPositionGerm. Let \(X\) be tame, \(f\) with tame germ data, \((f, x_0)\) in general position. By Lemma 5.26 it is in good position; the previous paragraph turns its general position into general position of the submanifold \(S_f \cap V\) at \(x_0\); Theorem 4.22 (3) for tame \(X\) (Part IV) makes that open along the submanifold Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.theorem_4_22; Definition 4.21 depends only on the germ of the submanifold, since tangent spaces of chart models agree on open sets Chapter5/GeneralPositionMPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.congr_nhds; and the equivalence turns it back into general position of \((f, y)\) at the nearby zeros. The text uses this without proof (“they will also hold at \((0, y)\) for \(y \in S_f\) close to \(x\)”; “the properties (i)–(ii) hold for all \((\lambda, y) \in \tilde S\)”).

V.19 Properties (i)–(ii)

In a chart centred at \(y\), with a presentation \(T\), the properties of the proof of Theorem 5.18 are Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundleChart.IsParamGP: (i) \(\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)(T_0O) + \operatorname{span}\{\hat t_i(0)\} = K_0\) — \(F'(0, y)\) onto; (ii) every \(w \in T_0O\) is \(u + e\) with \(e \in E_0\) and \(\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)u + \sum a_i\hat t_i(0) = 0\) for some \(a\) — \(\ker F'(0, y)\) transversal to \(\mathbb R^m \oplus T^R\). Adding sections keeps both, by linear algebra Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundleChart.IsParamGP.comp.

(i)–(ii) give general position Chapter5/GeneralPositionisGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP. In the tame product chart \((r \mapsto r) \times \Phi\) of a tame chart centred at \(y\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionpc0, whose tangent space at the centre is \(\mathbb R^m \times T_0O\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionofProd_mem_rangeS and whose reduced tangent space is \(\mathbb R^m \times T^R_0O\), the minimal subspace of \(\mathbb R^m\) being everything Chapter5/GeneralPositionminimalSubspaceWith_rnPres: (i) is the surjectivity of \(F'(0, y)\); (ii) says \(\ker F'(0, y) + T^R = T(\mathbb R^m \times O)\) on level \(0\), so the kernel has an algebraic complement inside \(T^R\), and §V.16 gives good position of \((F, (0, y))\). Achieving (i)–(ii) Chapter5/GeneralPositionexists_sections_isParamGP. Spanning sections give (i) (§V.12) Chapter5/GeneralPositionspanning_of_isLinSurjAt. For (ii), “take a linear subspace \(L\) complementing \(T^R_xX\) in \(T_xX\) and add sections which at \(x\) span \(f'(x)L\)”: the sections must come from Lemma 5.11, which needs smooth points of the fibre, so \(L\) must consist of smooth vectors. V.20 Theorem 5.18

From a family Chapter5/GeneralPositiontheorem_5_18_of_family. Let \(X\) be tame, \(f\) with tame germ data and compact solution set, \(N\) auxiliary, \(U\) from Theorem 5.5. Fix \(s_0\) with \(\operatorname{supp}s_0 \subseteq U\), \(N(s_0) \le 1 - \varepsilon\), and allowable \(t_1, \dots, t_m\) with \(F\) in general position at every \((0, x)\), \(x \in S_g\), \(g = f + s_0\).

  1. General position near the zero slice. \(\mathbb R^m \times X\) is tame Chapter3/ParamPerturbationprod_rn_isTame and \(F\) has tame germ data Chapter3/ParamPerturbationGtheorem_3_18_tame, so openness (§V.18) gives, around each \((0, x)\), an open set on which the zeros of \(F\) are in good and general position; their union \(W \supseteq \{0\} \times S_g\).
  2. Compactness and the omitted step as in §V.13: the zeros \(Z\) of \(F\) over \(|\lambda| \le \delta_1\) are compact, and \(Z \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta_0\} \subseteq W\).
  3. The submanifold. \(A = \tilde S \cap W \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta\}\) is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of \(\mathbb R^m \times X\) (the bridge lemma, §V.17), in general position at each of its points (Definition 4.21, by §V.18 and locality), with compact closure (inside \(Z\)).
  4. Theorem 4.23. In its countable-cover form (Part IV) Chapter4/Familiestheorem_4_23_of_subset, it gives a set \(\Sigma\) of parameters with null complement over which the fibre \(A_\lambda\) is a smooth submanifold of \(X\) in general position.
  5. Transversality. The Sard step of §V.14 on the compact zeros over \(|\lambda| \le \delta/2\) gives a further null set off which the slices are transversal at their zeros.
  6. The conclusions for \(\lambda\). For \(|\lambda| < \delta/2\) off both null sets, with \(h = f + s_\lambda\): the fibre of \(A\) over \(\lambda\) is \(S_h\); \(h\) is transversal; \(S_h\) is a submanifold in general position, so \((h, y)\) is in good position (§V.18), and then in general position by the equivalence of §V.18 applied at \(y\) together with the locality of Definition 4.21; Theorem 4.18 gives the corner structure and tameness of \(S_h\) Chapter4/SubmanifoldsMPolyfold.theorem_4_18, and Theorem 4.22 (2) gives \(d_{S_h} = d_X\) on \(S_h\) Chapter4/LocalStructureMPolyfold.theorem_4_22. These are the conclusions collected in Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundle.SolutionSetInGeneralPosition.

The generic form Chapter5/GeneralPositiontheorem_5_18. At every zero \(x\) of \(g\) choose a tame chart centred at \(x\) with a presentation; sections with (i)–(ii) there (§V.19) make \(F_x\) general at \((0, x)\), hence (openness, §V.18) at \((0, y)\) for the zeros \(y\) in an open \(U(x)\). Finitely many \(U(x_j)\) cover \(S_g\); the united family \(t\) keeps (i)–(ii) at every \((0, y)\) — read (i)–(ii) off general position in the chart of \(x_j\), add sections, go back — so \(F\) is in general position at every \((0, y)\), and the previous theorem applies. “Replacing \(f + s_0\) by \(f\) and \(N\) by \(cN\)” is not needed; the proof keeps \(s_0\).

The dense form Chapter5/GeneralPositiontheorem_5_18_dense is derived exactly as for Theorem 5.13 (§V.15).

The text’s \(\tilde S\) omits the equation \(F = 0\), and its “\(p^{-1}(\{|\lambda| \le \varepsilon\})\) is compact” is the omitted step of §V.13.

V.21 Theorem 5.25

Chapter5/GeneralPositiontheorem_5_25. Let \(X\) be tame with bump functions, \(f\) proper with tame germ data. Properness gives a compact solution set; Theorem 5.18 with \(s_0 = 0\) gives \(U\), \(t\), \(\delta\) and a null \(CV\) Chapter5/GeneralPositionStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.fiberZero_eq Chapter5/GeneralPositionsectionAdd_fiberZero; the ball \(\{|\lambda| < \delta\}\) has positive measure, so some \(\lambda\) avoids \(CV\), and \(s = \sum\lambda_it_i\) is allowable with \(f + s\) in general position at every zero and all the conclusions of Theorem 5.18; Lemma 5.26 turns general into good position in the tame chart of the germ data (§V.16). The text’s proof says “in view of Theorem 3.54 … in general position”, which is the openness of §V.18 (Theorem 3.54 is about good position), and writes \(x \in S_f\) for \(x \in S_{f+s_0}\). V.22 Theorem 5.19

Chapter5/GeneralPositiontheorem_5_19. Let \(X\) admit bump functions, \(f\) have tame germ data and compact solution set, and \((f, x)\) be in good position at the zeros \(x \in \partial X\). The text’s “as before” applies the implicit function theorem to \(F\) at the boundary zeros \((0, x)\), where all \(t_i\) vanish and \(\ker F'(0, x) = \mathbb R^m \times \ker f'(x)\); this is in good position to \(\mathbb R^m \times C_x\) only if \(\ker f'(x) + E_x \supseteq T_xX\), a general position condition that good position does not imply (\(\mathbb R(1, 1)\) in \([0, \infty)^2\); checked on paper only). The formal proof avoids those points:

  1. Near the boundary zeros. Theorem 3.54 (1) at each zero of \(f\) on \(\partial X\) gives an open set of zeros in good position Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoGtheorem_3_54_one'; their union \(V_{bd}\), and an open \(V_1\) with \(S_f \cap \partial X \subseteq V_1\) and \(\operatorname{cl}V_1 \subseteq V_{bd}\).
  2. Away from them. The zeros of \(f\) outside \(V_1\) are not on \(\partial X\), so interior (\(d = 0\)). Spanning sections at these zeros are taken with supports in \(U \setminus (\partial X \cup \operatorname{cl}V_1)\), an open set containing them; finitely many families cover the compact \(S_f \setminus V_1\), and \(F\) is onto at every \((0, y)\), \(y \in S_f\) outside \(V_1\).
  3. Good position of \(F\) off the boundary. At the interior points good position is surjectivity Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexGStrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt; Theorem 3.54 (1) for \(F\) gives an open \(W \supseteq \{0\} \times (S_f \setminus V_1)\) of zeros in good position, off \(\mathbb R^m \times \partial X\).
  4. Compactness and Sard as in §V.15 for the zeros of \(F\) over small \(\lambda\) outside \(\mathbb R^m \times V_1\).
  5. The conclusions. For small \(\lambda\) off the null set, \(h = f + s_\lambda\). On \(V_1\) all \(t_i\) vanish, so \(h = f\) there, and the good position of \((f, y)\) at the zeros in \(V_1\) passes to \((h, y)\) because good position depends only on the germ of the section Chapter3/Chapter5BridgeGStrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.congr_nhds. Off \(V_1\) the zeros of \(h\) are interior, \(h\) is transversal there by the Sard step, hence in good position. Theorem 3.57 makes \(S_h\), if non-empty, a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and a manifold with boundary with corners Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsGtheorem_3_57.

\(s_\lambda = \sum\lambda_it_i\) has support disjoint from \(\partial X\), so it vanishes on the open neighbourhood \(X \setminus \operatorname{supp}s_\lambda\) of \(\partial X\), and it is “arbitrarily small” as \(\lambda \to 0\). The text’s tameness of \(X\) is not used, and its “\((f, x)\) in good position for every \(x \in S_{f+s}\)” is \((f + s, x)\). No dense form is stated.

V.23 Definition 5.20, and Lemmas 5.23 and 5.24

Definition 5.20 Chapter5/HomotopyStrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy. \(X\) tame, \(f\) with tame germ data and compact solution set, \(t : X \to \mathbb R\) sc-smooth with \(t(X) = [0, 1]\), and for every \(\tau \in [0, 1]\): \(X_\tau = t^{-1}(\tau)\) a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.19) with tame induced structure, on which the restriction \(f|X_\tau\) — the section \(a \mapsto (a, f(a))\) of the pull-back of \(P\) along the inclusion Chapter5/HomotopyrestrictSection Chapter3/ParamPerturbationStrongBundle.pullback, the inclusion being sc-smooth (Proposition 2.21) — has tame germ data. The text never says what \(Y|X_t\) is; the pull-back of Proposition 2.54 is the strong bundle structure available. The end problems are the restrictions to \(t^{-1}(0)\) and \(t^{-1}(1)\); their solution sets are \(S_f \cap X_\tau\) Chapter5/HomotopyisZeroAt_restrictSection_iff, closed in the compact \(S_f\), hence compact Chapter5/HomotopyStrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict.

Lemma 5.23 and the hidden hypothesis. The proof of Theorem 5.22 fixes a critical point \(x\) of \(t|S\) and says “since \(x\) is a smooth point, we find a one-dimensional smooth linear sc-subspace \(Z \subset T_xX\) such that \(T_xX = Z \oplus \ker(dt(x))\)”. For \(dt(x) = 0\), \(\ker dt(x) = T_xX\) and the only complement is \(0\): a non-zero complement exists only if \(\ell \ne 0\) Chapter5/Homotopyne_zero_of_isCompl_ker. Theorem 5.22 does not assume that \(t\) is a submersion at the critical points of \(t|S\), so this is a hidden hypothesis. When \(\ell \ne 0\), some vector \(e\) of any spanning set (e.g. the dense smooth vectors) has \(\ell(e) \ne 0\), and \(\mathbb Re\) complements \(\ker\ell\) Chapter5/Homotopyexists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero. Lemma 5.23 is then linear algebra: \(\ell|_Z\) is an isomorphism onto \(\mathbb R\), so \(b = (\ell|_Z)^{-1} \circ \tau\) is the unique \(b : S \to Z\) with \(\ell \circ b = \tau\), and adding \(a\) with values in \(\ker\ell\) does not change \(\ell \circ b\) Chapter5/Homotopylemma_5_23.

The calculus. At a level-\(1\) point \(z\), \(D(a \cdot w)(z)v = Da(z)v \cdot w(z) + a(z)Dw(z)v\) for sc-smooth \(a : U \to \mathbb R\), \(w : U \to F\) Chapter5/HomotopyscDeriv_smul_apply, and \(D(\ell(\rho(\cdot) - p))(z) = \ell \circ D\rho(z)\) Chapter5/HomotopyscDeriv_clm_sub_apply. The function \(g = \beta \cdot \ell(\varphi(\cdot) - \varphi(x))\) on \(\operatorname{dom}\varphi\), \(0\) outside Chapter5/HomotopychartLinCutoff, is sc-smooth when \(\beta\) is with \(\operatorname{supp}\beta \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) Chapter5/HomotopyisScSmoothMap_chartLinCutoff.

Lemma 5.24. The construction Chapter5/Homotopyexists_scPlusSection_linAt: for a chart \(\Phi\) around the smooth point \(x\), a smooth point \(e\) over \(x\), a continuous linear \(\ell\) on the model space and \(U \ni x\), let \(s_e\) be the sc⁺-section through \(e\) of Lemma 5.11, supported in \(U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi\), \(\beta\) a bump with \(\beta \equiv 1\) near \(x\) and support in the chart domain, and \(s = g \cdot s_e\) with \(g\) as above. Then \(s\) is sc⁺ (§V.9), \(s(x) = g(x)e = 0\) Chapter5/Homotopyprincipal_sectionSmul, \(\operatorname{supp}s \subseteq U\) Chapter5/HomotopysectionSupport_sectionSmul_subset, and in the chart, by the product rule, \(\mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = D(g \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(z)v \cdot \hat s_e(\varphi(x)) + g(x)\mathrm{Lin}_{s_e}(z)v = \ell(Dr(z)v)\Phi(e)_2 = \ell(v)\Phi(e)_2\) for \(v \in T_zO\), since \(g \circ \varphi^{-1} = \ell(\cdot - \varphi(x))\) near \(\varphi(x)\) Chapter5/HomotopychartLinCutoff_of_mem and \(Dr(z) = 1\) on \(T_zO\). The lemma Chapter5/Homotopylemma_5_24: for a finite-dimensional \(K \subseteq T_zO\) (the text’s \(T_xS = \ker f'(x)\)) and a linear \(b : K \to T_zO\) with \(\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2\), extend \(-\lambda\) (linear on the finite-dimensional \(K\)) to a continuous linear functional \(\ell\) on the model space (Hahn–Banach) and apply the construction: \(\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) + \mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 - \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 = 0\). The text’s graph of \(S\) over \(T_xS\), its complement \(L\) with \(j : L \to \mathbb R\), and its case “if this operator is the zero operator we can take \(s = 0\)” are not needed. That \(f'(x) \circ b_\tau\) has its image in the line of a smooth point is a hypothesis; the text’s justification (“the image of any vector in \(T_xS\) belongs to \(Y_\infty\)”) is not formalized.

V.24 Bump functions in local models: Theorem 5.34 and Proposition 5.35

Definition 5.33 Chapter5/BumpFunctionsLocalModel.HasBumpProperty. For \(x \in O\) and \(W\) open in \(E_0\) with \(\operatorname{cl}(O \cap W) \subseteq O\), an sc-smooth \(f\) on \(O\) with \(f(x) \ne 0\) (as in Definition 5.9) and support in \(O\) inside \(W\).

A retract is closed near its points Chapter5/BumpFunctionsclosure_inter_ball_subset. If \(B(z, r) \subseteq W'\) and \(U = C \cap W'\) is the domain of a retraction \(\rho\) onto \(O\), then \(O \cap \operatorname{cl}B(z, r/2) \subseteq O\): a limit of points of \(O\) in the closed half ball lies in \(C\) (\(C\) closed) and in \(B(z, r)\), hence in \(U\), where \(\rho\) is continuous, and it is a fixed point of \(\rho\).

Theorem 5.34 Chapter5/BumpFunctionstheorem_5_34. “⇒”: every chart’s model has the property — given \(x\), \(W\), a bump of \(X\) at \(\varphi^{-1}(x)\) supported in \(\varphi^{-1}(O \cap W)\), read in the chart. “⇐”, “clearly” in the text, hides a support condition: a local bump \(f_0\) with support in \(U(x)\), \(\operatorname{cl}_E(U(x)) \subseteq O\), gives \(f = f_0 \circ \varphi\) on the chart domain, but \(\operatorname{cl}_X\{f \ne 0\}\) may leave the domain. For \(X = E\) a Hilbert space, the chart \(\varphi(u) = u/(1 - |u|_0^2)\) from the open unit ball onto \(O = E\), \(U(x) = O\) and \(f_0 \equiv 1\), the extension by \(0\) is the indicator of the ball. The proof chooses \(U_1 \ni x\) with \(\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) (regularity of \(X\)) and \(r\) with \(B(\varphi(x), r) \cap O \subseteq \varphi(U_1)\), takes the local bump in \(W = B(\varphi(x), r/2)\) — admissible by the previous paragraph — and extends \(f_0 \circ \varphi\) by \(0\): its support lies in \(\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U\), and it is sc-smooth because it vanishes on the open complement of its support and is sc-smooth in the chart (§V.8).

Proposition 5.35. If \(\kappa\|v\|^2 \le b(v, v)\) for a continuous bilinear \(b\) on \(E_0\), then \(f(v) = \tau(1 - b(v - x, v - x)/\rho)\) is \(C^\infty\) on \(E_0\), equal to \(1\) at \(x\) and supported in a small ball; it is sc-smooth on \(E\) by Corollary 1.20 from the base level Chapter1/LevelsIsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional, and so is its composition with any retraction onto \(O\) Chapter5/BumpFunctionsLocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic. “\(E_0\) is a Hilbert space” is stated as \(\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)\) Chapter5/BumpFunctionsproposition_5_35: an inner product structure on \(E_0\) would be a second normed structure next to that of the sc-scale. Translating by a non-smooth \(x\) is legitimate here because \(f\) is \(C^\infty\) on \(E_0\) itself; for a merely sc-smooth function it would not be. With Theorem 5.34: an M-polyfold covered by charts on sc-Hilbert spaces admits sc-smooth bump functions, the remark before Definition 5.9 Chapter5/BumpFunctionsMPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert.

V.25 Partitions of unity: Theorem 5.37 and Proposition 5.38

The algebra of sc-smooth functions. Sums, differences and products of sc-smooth functions are sc-smooth, on retracts Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityIsScSmoothRetractMap.real_add Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityIsScSmoothRetractMap.real_mul and on \(X\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_add Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_sub Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_mul, and so are finite sums and products Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisScSmoothMap_real_finsetSum Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisScSmoothMap_real_finsetProd. Sc-smoothness is local Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisScSmoothMap_real_of_eventuallyEq, so a locally finite sum, which near each point is a finite sum, is sc-smooth Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisScSmoothMap_real_finsum; and a function supported in a chart domain with sc-smooth representative is sc-smooth on \(X\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisScSmoothMap_real_of_chart.

Definitions 5.28 and 5.36. A partition of unity is Mathlib’s (continuous \(\rho_i \ge 0\), locally finite supports, \(\sum\rho_i = 1\)), sc-smooth if every \(\rho_i\) is Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity; \(X\) admits sc-smooth partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate one Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity. The approximation property: for \(V = O \cap W\) with \(\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O\), continuous \(f : O \to [0, 1]\) supported in \(V\) and \(\varepsilon > 0\), an sc-smooth \(g : O \to [0, 1]\) supported in \(V\) with \(|f - g| \le \varepsilon\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityLocalModel.HasApproxProperty. Partitions of unity give bump functions: the function attached to \(U\) of a partition subordinate to \(\{U, X \setminus \{x\}\}\) is \(1\) at \(x\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity.admitsBumpFunctions — the easy half of the open problem the text states after Definition 5.29.

“(i) ⇒ (ii)” Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityhasApproxProperty_restrict. The text calls \(f \circ \varphi\) “sc-smooth” (\(f\) is only continuous) and asserts \(\operatorname{cl}_X(\varphi^{-1}(V)) \subseteq U\); with the chart of the unit ball above, \(V = O\) and \(f \equiv 1\), the extension by \(0\) is not continuous. Since (ii) asks only for some atlas, the proof restricts each chart to an open \(s\) with \(\operatorname{cl}_X(s) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi\). Then for closed \(A \subseteq \varphi(s)\) the set \(\varphi^{-1}(A)\) is closed in \(X\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMChart.isClosed_inter_preimage, so \(F = f \circ \varphi\) extended by \(0\) is continuous. Cover \(X\) by \(\{F < \varepsilon/2\}\) and the sets \(U_x = \{|F - F(x)| < \varepsilon/2\} \cap \varphi^{-1}(V)\), take a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity \((\beta_0, \beta_x)\), and let \(\hat g = \sum_x\beta_xF(x)\): a locally finite sum of sc-smooth functions with values in \([0, 1]\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityPartitionOfUnity.finsum_mul_mem_Icc, supported in \(\varphi^{-1}(V)\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityPartitionOfUnity.tsupport_finsum_mul_subset, and within \(\varepsilon/2\) of \(F\), since every \(F(x)\) with \(\beta_x(y) \ne 0\) is Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityPartitionOfUnity.abs_sub_finsum_mul_le. Whether every chart has the property is not settled.

“(ii) ⇒ (i)”. Every point of a chart domain has small open neighbourhoods \(N\) with \(\operatorname{cl}_XN \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi\) and \(\operatorname{cl}\varphi(N) \subseteq O\) — half a ball inside the domain of a retraction, closed by §V.24 Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMChart.exists_small_nhds — and the approximation property transports to continuous functions on \(X\) supported in such \(N\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityLocalModel.HasApproxProperty.exists_approx. Sc-smooth Urysohn functions Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityexists_isScSmoothMap_urysohn: for disjoint closed \(s, t\), cover \(t\) by small neighbourhoods \(W_x\) inside \(X \setminus s\), take continuous \(f_x = 1\) near \(x\) supported in \(W_x\), a locally finite refinement, approximations \(\hat g_x\) within \(1/2\) — so \(\hat g_x \ge 1/2\) where \(f_x = 1\) — and \(F = \tau(4\sum\hat g_x - 1)\), sc-smooth, \(0\) on \(s\) and \(1\) on \(t\). Then Mathlib’s bump coverings produce a covering indexed by the given cover with sc-smooth functions Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnityBumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_prop, and \(\rho_i = f_i\prod_{j < i}(1 - f_j)\), locally a finite product, is the partition of unity Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnityBumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityadmitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx. This replaces the text’s refinement “with the same index set”, which does not exist in general (the cover \(\{X\}\)); metrizability is not needed.

Theorem 5.37 Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnitytheorem_5_37 combines the two directions, “atlas” read as a family of charts covering \(X\).

Proposition 5.38 Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityproposition_5_38 is not “an immediate consequence of Theorem 5.37”: that theorem produces some atlas, not the given model, and applied to \(O\) would need partitions of unity on an open subset of \(C\). The proof repeats “(i) ⇒ (ii)” in \(E_0\): \(A = \{x \in O \mid f(x) \ge \varepsilon/2\}\) is closed in \(E_0\) because \(\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O\); \(E_0 \setminus A\) and balls \(B(x, r_x) \subseteq W\), \(x \in V\), on which \(f\) varies by less than \(\varepsilon/2\), cover \(E_0\); a \(C^\infty\) partition of unity of \(E_0\) gives \(g = \sum\beta_xf(x)\), \(C^\infty\) on \(E_0\), hence sc-smooth (Corollary 1.20), composed with a retraction onto \(O\).

V.26 Banach space geometry: Definitions 5.31, 5.39, 5.41, Proposition 5.42, Corollary 5.44

A Banach space admits a \(C^k\)-bump function if some \(C^k\) function, not identically zero, has bounded support Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityHasContDiffBump, and \(C^k\) partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate \(C^k\) one Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityAdmitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity. \(c_0(\Gamma)\) is the subspace of \(\ell^\infty(\Gamma)\) of functions tending to \(0\) along the cofinite filter Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnitycZero, equivalently with \(\{|f(\gamma)| > \varepsilon\}\) finite for every \(\varepsilon\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnitymem_cZero_iff, normed by the supremum Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnitynorm_cZero; coordinate-wise \(C^k\) embeddings are as in the text Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityIsCoordinatewiseContDiffEmbedding, and Toruńczyk’s Theorem 5.40 is recorded as a statement, not proved and not used Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityTorunczykStatement. WCG means a weakly compact set with dense span Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityIsWCG; reflexive, used in Proposition 5.42 and not defined in the text, means \(V \to V''\) onto Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityIsReflexive.

Proposition 5.42. (i) For reflexive \(V\) the weak closure of the closed unit ball is weakly compact — Kakutani’s theorem, in Mathlib as Banach–Alaoglu in \(V''\) through the embedding of \((V, \text{weak})\) into \((V'', \text{weak-*})\) Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/DoubleDualNormedSpace.isCompact_closure_of_isBounded — and its span contains the ball, hence is \(V\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityspan_closedBall_eq_top Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityproposition_5_42_reflexive. (ii) For separable \(V\), a dense sequence \((y_n)\) scaled by \(1/((n + 1)(|y_n| + 1))\) is a null sequence; with \(0\) it is norm compact, hence weakly compact, and its span contains every \(y_n\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityproposition_5_42_separable. The text’s “\(\{0\} \cup \{x_n/n\}\)” has its index range missing.

Corollary 5.44 Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnitycorollary_5_44. Let \(\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)\) on \(E_0\), and assume Theorem 5.43 for \(E_0\) and \(k = \infty\), recorded as a statement Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityGodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement. A Hilbert space is reflexive: the parallelogram law holds, so the norm comes from an inner product Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/OfNormInnerProductSpace.ofNorm, and every \(\phi \in V''\) is evaluation at the Riesz representative of \(x \mapsto \phi(\langle x, \cdot\rangle)\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityisReflexive_of_hilbert; hence WCG by Proposition 5.42 (i). It has the \(C^\infty\)-bump \(\tau(1 - b(v, v))\) Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityhasContDiffBump_of_hilbert. Theorem 5.43 gives \(C^\infty\) partitions of unity of \(E_0\), and Proposition 5.38 — not Theorem 5.37, as the text says — the approximation property. With Theorem 5.37, an M-polyfold on such charts admits sc-smooth partitions of unity Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnityMPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert.

V.27 What is not formalized

  • Corollary 5.8 as one statement for all \(i\). It is proved for each fixed \(i\) (§V.29; gap G.41 closed in the fourth addendum). Not formalized: a family \(P^i\) indexed by \(i\), the identification of the iterated base \((X^1)^1\) with \(X_2\) as a topological space (the sets agree; gap G.6), and the tame form of the conclusion, which needs the tameness of the index raises of tame charts. Condition (3) of a filling on level \(1\) does not follow from level \(0\) alone — on \(E_m = \{x \mid \sum e^{2mk}x_k^2 < \infty\}\) the right shift \(T\) makes \(1 - T/2\) invertible on \(E_0\) while \((1 - T/2)^{-1}e_0 = \sum2^{-n}e_n \notin E_1\) — so the corollary’s proof needs the regularity argument of §V.29, through Lemma 3.17 Chapter3/Fillerlemma_3_17.
  • The non-completeness of \((\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)\) in the text’s setting (§V.30), and the identification of the completion of Remark 5.12; Remarks 5.14, 5.16, 5.21 (gaps G.43, G.44, G.47), and a dense form of Theorem 5.19 (gap G.45).
  • Weak against pointwise bump functions at a non-smooth point (§V.31).
  • Finding 88 (gap G.46): the failure of good position of \(F\) at the boundary zeros (§V.22) is checked on paper only.
  • Theorem 5.22 (gap G.48): it needs finite-dimensional Morse theory on manifolds with boundary, the cotangent bundle of the solution set, a parametric Sard theorem and a trivialization of the family \(S_\lambda\), none in Mathlib or the project, and the hidden hypothesis \(dt(x) \ne 0\) (§V.23). Theorem 5.27 (gap G.49): “the proof is left to the reader”.
  • Theorems 5.32, 5.40, 5.43 and the Sobolev remark (gaps G.50–G.53): deep Banach space geometry cited from [9], [12], and Sobolev spaces with their sc-structures (gap G.1). Nothing on the main line uses partitions of unity.

V.28 What the formalization taught us

The tameness hypothesis. The first formal versions of Theorem 5.13 and Lemma 5.26 assumed, as the §3.6 theorems then did, that the base retraction of every compatible strong bundle chart — and of every chart of the pull-backs to \(\mathbb R^k \times X\) — is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies this (a compatible chart \((1, \varphi)\) with base retraction \((a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))\) on \([0, \infty) \times U\) is never tame), so those statements were vacuous. The repair is the text’s own Definitions 3.50, 3.51, 3.53 in a tame chart: the perturbation theorems take \(f\) with tame germ data, the parametrized sections inherit them through the tame product chart, and Definition 5.17 lives in a tame chart, where Lemma 5.26’s count \(\dim T_zO/T^R_zO = d_C(z)\) holds.

What “it is easily verified” costs. The perturbation theorems of §5.3 are sketches. Their formal proofs needed the density of smooth vectors (§V.12), the compactness of the zeros over a small parameter ball (§V.13), a local, stratified Sard step (§V.14), the bridge from tangent germ data to Definition 4.13 (§V.17), \(T_yS = \ker f'(y)\) by a dimension count, which gives the chart independence of Definition 5.17 and the openness of general position (§§V.17–V.18), and, in Theorem 5.19, a route around the implicit function theorem at boundary points where its hypothesis fails (§V.22).

V.29 Corollary 5.8 on the shifted strong bundle

Corollary 5.8 says that, for an sc-Fredholm section \(f\) with compact solution set, \(f^i\) is an sc-Fredholm section of \(P^i : Y^i \to X^i\) with compact solution set, and that “it is a priori clear that \(f^i\) is sc-Fredholm”. The text defines \(Y[i]\) for \(i = 0, 1\) only, never \(Y^i\), and “a priori clear” hides the filler condition on level \(1\) (§V.7). Both are supplied here (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140–146).

The reading of \(Y^1\). \(Y^1 = Y_{1,1}\) with \((Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}\) — the convention of \(E^1\) and of \((U \triangleleft F)^1 = U^1 \triangleleft F^1\) — not \(Y[1] = Y_{0,1}\) and not \(Y_{1,2}\). It is forced by “\(f^i\) is obtained by raising the index”: an sc-smooth section maps \(X_1\) into \(Y_{1,1}\), and in general not into \(Y_{1,2}\).

Fibres of a strong bundle. Through a chart, \(P^{-1}(x)\) is linearly homeomorphic to \(K_{\varphi(x)} = \{h \mid \Gamma(\varphi(x), h) = h\}\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.fiberK Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.fiberCLE, the fixed points of a continuous projection, a closed subspace of the fibre model Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.isClosed_fiberK; so every fibre is a Banach space Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.isBanachable_fiber, which Definition 2.51 asks of a strong bundle.

The levels of \(X^1\), and raising the index of maps. \((X^1)_m = X_{m+1}\) and \((X^1)_\infty = X_\infty\) as sets Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftMPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftMPolyfold.mem_shift_smoothSet_iff (their topologies are not compared; gap G.6). An sc-smooth map \(f : X \to Z\) between M-polyfolds induces an sc-smooth \(f_1 : X^1 \to Z^1\): continuity, and in the level charts the local representatives are the level-\(1\) maps of those of \(f\), sc-smooth by Proposition 1.17 for retracts Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftMPolyfold.levelChart_apply_levelOne Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftMPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne.

The shifted strong bundle Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.shift. Its total space is \(Y_{1,1}\), the level \(1\) of the M-polyfold \(Y[0]\) with its level topology, Hausdorff and paracompact by Theorem 2.16 Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.ShiftSpace; the projection is \(P^1 = P|_{Y_{1,1}}\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.shiftProj, continuous and onto Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.continuous_shiftProj Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.surjective_shiftProj; the fibre \(P^{-1}(x) \cap Y_{1,1}\) is a linear subspace — in a chart it is the preimage of \(F_1\) under the linear fibre map Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.shiftFiberSubmodule — carries the topology of \(F_1\), not that of \(P^{-1}(x)\), and is a Banach space, a closed subspace of \(F_1\) through a chart Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.banachable_shift. The atlas consists of the index raises of the strong bundle charts Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.shift Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.shiftAtlas: base chart the level chart \(\varphi^1 : V_1 \to O_1\), fibre model \(F^1\), retraction \(R\) on \(U^1 \triangleleft F^1\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftIsStrongBundleRetraction.shift, bundle chart the level chart of \(\Phi\) in \(Y[0]\). Compatible charts have compatible index raises Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.Compatible.shift: on \([0]\) the transitions are level charts of compatible charts, on \([1]\) the transition \((\Phi'^1 \circ (\Phi^1)^{-1})[1]\) is the level-\(1\) map of \((\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]\) (Proposition 1.17 for retracts) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.shift_transition_one, and the \(F_1\)-condition of Definition 2.50 holds because the \([1]\)-transition is sc⁰ Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundleChart.shift_compatible_range. Checks: \((Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.mem_shift_doubleLevel_iff, the M-polyfold \(Y^1[0]\) is \(Y[0]^1\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.isChart_shift_toMPolyfold0_iff, and the index raise of every chart of \(P\) is a chart of \(P^1\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.isChart_shift.

The section \(f^1\). \(f^1 = f|_{X_1}\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.sectionShift is a section of \(P^1\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.isSection_sectionShift, sc-smooth by the raising of the index of maps Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.shift, with the zeros of \(f\) in \(X_1\) as its zeros Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.solutionSet_sectionShift, and regularizing, from \((X^1)_m = X_{m+1}\) and \((Y^1)_{m,m+1} = Y_{m+1,m+2}\) Chapter5/StrongBundleShiftStrongBundle.regularizing_sectionShift. In the index raise of a chart the principal part of \(f^1\) is the level-\(1\) map of that of \(f\) Chapter5/Corollary58StrongBundleChart.principal_sectionShift, and the raised chart is centred where the chart is Chapter5/Corollary58StrongBundleChart.shift_φ_eq_zero.

Condition (3) on every level, at every centre Chapter5/Corollary58IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_fillDefect. Let \((g, s)\) be a datum of Definition 3.11 in a chart — \(g\) a filling germ of \(\hat f\) with fill defect \(k = [1 - \rho(r)]g\) and derivative family \(Dk\), \(s\) an sc⁺-germ with \(s(0) = g(0)\), \(g - s\) conjugated to a basic germ. If \(v \in \ker Dr(0)\) and \(Dk(0)v \in F_m\), then \(v \in E_m\) — at the centre of the datum, which need not be a zero. At a zero this is the regularity of §III.45 Chapter3/LinearizationChartsScGIsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_scDeriv_r_eq_zero. The reduction to a zero needs neither a global sc⁺-section nor a bump function: \(g(0) = \iota s(0)\) is a smooth point of \(F\) Chapter5/Corollary58IsScSmoothGerm.toBase_zero_mem_smooth; \(\hat s(z) = \Gamma(z, -g(0))\) is sc-smooth on \(U\) Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoXiisScSmooth_const_of_smooth and a section of \(K \to O\), so by Lemma 3.17 \(g' = g + \hat s \circ r\) fills \(\hat f + \hat s\) with the same fill defect Chapter3/GermCalculusIsFillingGerm.add_section, and \(g'(0) = g(0) - \Gamma(0, g(0)) = 0\). With the sc⁺-germ \(s' = s + \Gamma^1(r(\cdot), -s(0))\), \(g' - s' = g - s\) on \(U\), so Proposition 3.52 in sc form makes \(Dg'(0)\) sc-Fredholm Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationScGproposition_3_52_local_sc; and \(Dk(0) = (1 - \rho(0))Dg'(0)\) Chapter3/GermFillerLinearizationfillDefect_deriv_zero_eq_rho, so the case of a zero applies to \(g'\).

The filling on level \(1\) Chapter5/Corollary58IsFillingGerm.germ_shift. The fill defect of \(g^1\) is the level-\(1\) map of \(k\), an sc¹-germ with derivative family \((Dk)_1\) by Proposition 1.17 for germs Chapter3/GermLevelsIsSc1GermWith.shift; \(\iota\,Dr^1(0) = Dr(0)\,\iota\), by the uniqueness of the derivative of \(r^1 = r_1\) on the shifted germ Chapter5/Corollary58toBase_scDeriv_r_shift, and \(\iota\,\rho^1(0) = \rho(0)\,\iota\) Chapter5/Corollary58toBase_ρCLM_shift. So \(Dk^1(0) = Dk(0)|_{E_1}\) maps \(\ker Dr^1(0)\) to \(\ker\rho^1(0)\); it is injective by condition (3) on level \(0\), onto by the regularity just proved with \(m = 1\), and a topological isomorphism by the open mapping theorem. Conditions (1) and (2) of the filling shift directly Chapter5/Corollary58StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_eq_on Chapter5/Corollary58StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_mem_of_fixed, and \(g^1\) is a filling germ of the principal part of \(f^1\) in \(\Phi^1\) Chapter5/Corollary58StrongBundleChart.shift_isFillingGerm.

Corollary 5.8. At every smooth point of \(X^1\), the datum \((g, s)\) of \(f\) in a chart \(\Phi\) gives the datum \((g^1, s^1)\) of \(f^1\) in \(\Phi^1\): \(g^1\) fills, \(s^1\) is an sc⁺-germ on the shifted germ, \(s^1(0) = g^1(0)\), and \(g^1 - s^1 = (g - s)_1\) near \(0\) is conjugated to a basic germ by the index raise of the conjugation (§V.7) Chapter5/Corollary58isScFredholmGerm_sectionShift. For an sc-Fredholm section \(f\), \(f^1\) is an sc-Fredholm section of \(P^1\) Chapter5/Corollary58corollary_5_8_isScFredholmSection; if \(f\) has compact solution set, so has \(f^1\), by the compactness on level \(1\) (§V.7) Chapter5/Corollary58corollary_5_8. Since this holds for every strong bundle, it applies to \(P^1\) and \(f^1\): \(f^2 = (f^1)^1\) is an sc-Fredholm section of \(P^2 = (P^1)^1\) with compact solution set Chapter5/Corollary58corollary_5_8_two, and so on for every fixed \(i\). The unpacked data in the shifted chart are kept for reference Chapter5/Corollary58corollary_5_8_data. No hypothesis beyond the text’s is added, and tameness is not used. Not done: a family \(P^i\) indexed by \(i\) (a dependent type of strong bundles), the identification of \((X^1)^1\) with \(X_2\) as topological spaces, and the tame form of the conclusion — germ data of \(f^1\) in tame charts of \(P^1\) — which needs the presentation independence of the degeneracy index for \(C^1\) and that \(A \cap E_1\) is an sc-complement of \(T_xO^1\) when \(A\) is one of \(T_xO\); there is no counterexample either.

V.30 The metric \(\rho\) on \(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)\)

The text: \(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)\) “becomes a metric space” for \(\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))\), and “is not complete” (p. 174). The first is proved here; the second turns out to need a hypothesis (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153).

The metric. \(\rho(s, s')\) is the supremum of the pointwise distances of §V.10 Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist. For an auxiliary norm the fibre norm is symmetric and subadditive (Definition 5.1 (1)) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.neg Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_le Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_triangle, so for allowable sections \(N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le N(s(x)) + N(s'(x)) \le 2\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.sectionDistAt_le_two: the supremum is finite and \(\rho \le 2\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist_le_two. \(\rho(s, s) = 0\), symmetry and the triangle inequality come from the fibre norms Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist_self Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist_comm Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist_triangle, and \(\rho(s, s') = 0\) forces \(s = s'\) because \(N\) vanishes only at \(0_x\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.eq_of_allowableDist_eq_zero. So \(\rho\) is a metric Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableMetric, carried by a type synonym of \(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)\), since the sections \(X \to Y\) carry the product topology Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.AllowableSpace. Only Definition 5.1 (1) is used. The density statements of Theorems 5.13 and 5.18 (§§V.15, V.20) are \(\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.allowableDist_le_iff.

Not complete, by an example Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections. Take the trivial bundle \(\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R\) of the non-vacuity witnesses of Chapter 3, the fibre norm \(N(x, v) = |v|\) — an auxiliary norm, including the condition on the topology of \(Y[1]\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.fibNorm Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.isAuxNorm_fibNorm — and \(U = \mathbb R\). Graphs of \(C^\infty\) maps are sc⁺-sections Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_graphSection, so \(s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))\) is allowable, with \(N \le 1/2\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.approx Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.graphSection_approx_mem, and \(\rho(s_i, s_j) \le (\varepsilon_i + \varepsilon_j)/2\) with \(\varepsilon_j = 1/(j+1)\), by \(|\sqrt{x^2 + a^2} - |x|| \le a\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.abs_sqrt_sub_abs_le Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.abs_approx_sub_limitFn. A \(\rho\)-limit \(s\) would have, by pointwise convergence, the fibre part \(|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.limitFn, which is not differentiable at \(0\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.not_differentiableAt_limit; but the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is \(C^1\), by Proposition 1.18 in the chart \(\Phi = \mathrm{id}\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.differentiable_snd_of_isScPlusSection.

Complete, in two cases. For \(U = \emptyset\) every allowable section is the zero section, so the space is a point, for every bundle and auxiliary norm Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.subsingleton_allowableSections_empty Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricStrongBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_empty. Over the point \(\mathbb R^0\) with fibre \(\mathbb R^k\) every section is the graph of a constant, hence sc⁺ Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_of_isSection_point, and the space is the closed unit ball of \(\mathbb R^k\) (or \(\{0\}\)), complete for every \(U\) Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetricTrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point. So the text’s “not complete” is false without a hypothesis and is read as “not complete in general”. In the text’s setting — \(U\) a neighbourhood of the solution set of an sc-Fredholm section on an M-polyfold with bump functions — one expects non-completeness as soon as \(U\) contains a non-isolated point over which \(Y_{0,1}\) is nonzero, by the same mechanism (bump functions times a non-smooth uniform limit); this is not formalized, and neither is the identification of the metric completion with the sections of Remark 5.12 (§V.10).

V.31 Weak and pointwise bump functions

§V.8 reads Definition 5.9 pointwise, \(f(x) \ne 0\), because Proposition 5.30 needs it, and keeps Definition 5.29’s “not identically zero” as the weak reading. How far apart are they? (Findings, Chapter 5, items 160–163.)

Bump points. \(x\) is a bump point if every open \(U \ni x\) carries an sc-smooth \(f\) with \(f(x) \ne 0\) and \(\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U\) Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwiseMPolyfold.HasBumpAt. The pointwise reading says that every point is a bump point Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwiseMPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_iff_forall_hasBumpAt, and the weak reading holds as soon as the bump points are dense: a bump at a bump point inside \(U\) is not identically zero and is supported in \(U\) Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwiseMPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense. (The converse, weak ⟹ dense bump points, is a nested-neighbourhoods argument with Cantor’s theorem in a chart; not formalized.)

On an sc-Banach space. An sc-Banach space \(E\) is an M-polyfold with the identity chart and model \((E, E, E)\) Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwisescChart Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwisescPolyfold, whose sc-smooth functions are the sc-smooth maps \(E \to \mathbb R\) Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwiseisScSmoothMap_scPolyfold_iff. There the weak reading gives a bump point at every smooth point Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwiseMPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth: given \(x \in E_\infty\) and \(B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U\), a weak bump supported in \(B(x, \varepsilon/2)\) is non-zero on a non-empty open set, which contains a smooth point \(y\) because \(E_\infty\) is dense; \(a = y - x\) is smooth, so \(v \mapsto f(v + a)\) is sc-smooth Chapter4/RecentreisScSmooth_add_const, non-zero at \(x\), with support in \(B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U\). The argument stops at \(E_\infty\): translation by a vector \(a \notin E_m\) is not even sc⁰, since it sends \(0 \in E_m\) out of \(E_m\) Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwisenot_isSc0_add_const. On M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert spaces both readings hold at every point Chapter5/BumpFunctionsMPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert. Open: whether the weak reading gives a bump function non-zero at a non-smooth point, on an sc-Banach space or an M-polyfold; a counterexample would need an \(E_0\) without \(C^1\) bump functions.

theorem theorem_3_57_dim (hf : B.IsScFredholmSection f)
    (hall : ∀ x, IsZeroAt P f x → B.IsGoodPositionGermTame f x) :
    solutionSet P f = ⋃ n, solutionSetDim PX P f n ∧
    (∀ n m, n ≠ m → Disjoint (solutionSetDim PX P f n) (solutionSetDim PX P f m)) ∧
    (∀ n, solutionSetDim PX P f n = solutionSet P f ∩ solutionSetDimOpen PX P f n) ∧
    (∀ n, ∃ F : Set X, IsClosed F ∧ solutionSetDim PX P f n = solutionSet P f ∩ F) ∧
    ∀ n, (solutionSetDim PX P f n).Nonempty →
      ∃ hsub : PX.IsSubMPolyfold (solutionSetDim PX P f n),
        haveI := PX.paracompactSpace_subtype (solutionSetDim PX P f n)

theorem theorem_4_22 (hP : P.IsTame) {A : Set X} (hA : P.IsSmoothSubmanifold A)
    [ParacompactSpace A] {x : X} (hgp : P.IsGeneralPositionAt A x) :
    ∃ ψ : MChart X, P.IsChart ψ ∧ ∃ hx : x ∈ ψ.source, ψ x = 0 ∧
      ∃ (R : ScRetraction ψ.model.E ψ.model.C) (n : ℕ) (Wq : ScBanach)
        (T : ScIso ψ.model.E ((ScBanach.const (Fin n → ℝ)).prod Wq)),
        R.retract = ψ.model.O ∧ ψ.model.C = T 0 ⁻¹' quadrant n Wq 0 ∧ R.IsTameWith T ∧
      ∃ U : Set X, IsOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ U ⊆ ψ.source ∧
        -- (1)
        P.degIndex x = n ∧
        {F | (ψ.model.toMPolyfold ⟨_, ψ.mapsTo_model x hx⟩).IsFace F ∧
          (⟨ψ x, ψ.mapsTo_model x hx⟩ : ψ.model.O) ∈ F}.encard = (P.degIndex x : ℕ∞) ∧
        -- (2)
        (∀ a : A, (a : X) ∈ U → (subPolyfold hA.isSubMPolyfold).degIndex a = P.degIndex a) ∧
        -- (3)
        (∀ a ∈ U ∩ A, P.IsGeneralPositionAt A a) ∧
        -- (4)
        ∀ σ : Finset (Fin n), ∃ (Fc : σ → Set (ψ.model.E 0)) (G : Set (ψ.model.E 0)),
          (∀ i, R.IsRetractFace (Fc i) ∧ (0 : ψ.model.E 0) ∈ Fc i ∧ Fc i ⊆ coordHyper T i) ∧
          IsOpen G ∧ (0 : ψ.model.E 0) ∈ G ∧ x ∈ ψ.cornerPreimage G Fc ∧
          ψ.cornerPreimage G Fc ⊆ U ∧
          ∃ hF : P.IsSubMPolyfold (ψ.cornerPreimage G Fc),
            haveI := P.paracompactSpace_subtype (ψ.cornerPreimage G Fc)
